title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午我
皇上登極之四年也天下復當大
比士監察御史李良臣祗承
上命巡按廣西方攬轡出燕衞道
荆襄兢兢然懼弗逮馳檄所
司以粤壤寔遐且僻賓興彝
===
典其維先事之圖所司將御
史檄緘儀列省延聘儒臣無
何御史至彰程貞紀旣備益
虔期於登崇俊良以仰副
聖天子寤寐求賢至意先是總督
兩廣右都御史兼兵部左侍
郎劉燾恢弘治敎山海底寧
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午，我皇上登極之四年也。天下復當大比士。監察御史李良臣祗承上命，巡按廣西，方攬轡出燕衞，道荆襄，兢兢然懼弗逮，馳檄所司，以粤壤寔遐且僻，賓興彝典，其維先事之圖。所司將御史檄，緘儀列省，延聘儒臣。無何，御史至，彰程貞紀，旣備益虔，期於登崇俊良，以仰副聖天子寤寐求賢至意。先是，總督兩廣右都御史兼兵部左侍郎劉燾恢弘治敎，山海底寧。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

The gengwu year of Longqing was the fourth year since our Emperor ascended the throne. Throughout the realm, the time had again come for the triennial examination of scholars. Investigating Censor Li Liangchen reverently received the imperial command to make an inspection tour of Guangxi. Just as he took up the reins and departed from Yan and Wei [?], traveling by way of Jing and Xiang, he was deeply apprehensive that he might fall short in his duties. He dispatched urgent instructions to the responsible officials: since the lands of Yue were indeed distant and secluded, advance preparations must be made for the established ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy scholars. Acting upon the censor’s instructions, the responsible officials sent formal invitations and ceremonial gifts to the various provinces [?], inviting Confucian scholars to serve as examiners. Before long, the censor arrived. He made the regulations clear and set discipline in order; with preparations complete, he became still more scrupulous. His aim was to advance and honor men of outstanding ability and virtue, thereby fulfilling the sagely Son of Heaven’s earnest desire to seek worthy men, waking and sleeping.

Previously, Liu Tao, Supreme Commander of Guangdong and Guangxi, Right Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Left Vice Minister of War, had extended good governance and moral instruction, bringing peace to the mountains and coastal regions.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今提督兩廣兵部左侍郎右
僉都御史李遷揆文奮武綱
紀聿新巡撫廣西右僉都御
史殷正茂秉憲敷文甄陶素
洽八桂之士咸得專志明經
挾藝待問屆期御史申飭試
事以燧及敎諭陳冠司考試
===
學正鐵世材敎諭宋邦達林
獻芹梁幹陳三俊同考試提
調則左布政使郭應聘左參
政楊銓監試則按察使萬思
謙僉事楊文明簾以外曁百
執事咸慎簡以從已迺進提
學副使隂武卿所簡士一千
punctuated: 今提督兩廣兵部左侍郎右僉都御史李遷，揆文奮武，綱紀聿新；巡撫廣西右僉都御史殷正茂，秉憲敷文，甄陶素洽。八桂之士咸得專志明經，挾藝待問。屆期，御史申飭試事，以燧及敎諭陳冠司考試，學正鐵世材、敎諭宋邦達、林獻芹、梁幹、陳三俊同考試。提調則左布政使郭應聘、左參政楊銓；監試則按察使萬思謙、僉事楊文明。簾以外曁百執事，咸慎簡以從。已迺進提學副使隂武卿所簡士一千
translation_en:
Li Qian, now supervising military affairs in Liangguang and serving as Left Vice Minister of War and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, oversees civil learning and invigorates military affairs, renewing order and discipline. Yin Zhengmao, Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, upholds the laws and promotes learning; his efforts to cultivate talent have long been widely felt. The scholars of Bagui could thus devote themselves wholeheartedly to mastering the Classics and await examination equipped with their literary skills.

When the appointed time arrived, the censor reiterated the examination regulations and appointed Sui and Chen Guan, a School Instructor, as Examiners. Tie Shicai, a School Director, and Song Bangda, Lin Xianqin, Liang Gan, and Chen Sanjun, School Instructors, served as Associate Examiners. Guo Yingpin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yang Quan, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner, served as Proctors. Wan Siqian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Yang Wenming, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, supervised the examination. The personnel outside the curtain, together with all other functionaries, were carefully selected to assist. Then they admitted the one thousand candidates selected by Yin Wuqing, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而略邊幅重本實而厭英華
雖隆雅敦朴確有古風亦未
必其通方達變盡宜於今而
傳於後也顧光明俊偉之業
非徒質直者所能成而樂聲
名喜詩書者又或鮮持執而
不足以遺大投艱惟本質而
===
濟之以文則碩輔奇勳胥此
出矣廣右古百粵地灕波桂
嶺蜿嬗磅礴清淑之氣于焉
鬱積人生其間率多悃愊直
抗無澆漓委靡之習蓋得之
天者甚厚自古然也我
國家以禮樂道化鼓鑄寰宇
punctuated:
而略邊幅，重本實而厭英華。雖隆雅敦朴，確有古風，亦未必其通方達變，盡宜於今而傳於後也。顧光明俊偉之業，非徒質直者所能成；而樂聲名、喜詩書者，又或鮮持執，而不足以遺大投艱。惟本質而濟之以文，則碩輔奇勳胥此出矣。
廣右古百粵地，灕波桂嶺，蜿嬗磅礴，清淑之氣于焉鬱積。人生其間，率多悃愊直抗，無澆漓委靡之習，蓋得之天者甚厚，自古然也。我國家以禮樂道化鼓鑄寰宇
translation_en:
…and give little attention to outward refinements, valuing substance while disdaining literary brilliance. Although they esteem refinement and cultivate simplicity, truly possessing the spirit of antiquity, it does not necessarily follow that they comprehend general principles and adapt to changing circumstances, fully meeting the needs of the present and leaving something worthy of transmission to posterity. Yet illustrious and outstanding achievements cannot be accomplished by plain uprightness alone. Those who delight in reputation and esteem poetry and books, on the other hand, may lack steadfast convictions and prove unequal to being entrusted with great responsibilities and difficult undertakings. Only when substance forms the foundation and literary cultivation complements it will great ministers and extraordinary accomplishments alike emerge.
Guangyou was anciently the land of the Hundred Yue. The waters of the Li and the ridges of Gui wind and extend in majestic abundance [?]; here pure and beneficent vital energies gather densely. People born among them are generally sincere, upright, and unyielding, free of habits of insincerity and listlessness. Their endowment from Heaven is indeed generous, and has been so since antiquity. Our dynasty, through rites, music, and moral transformation, molds all beneath Heaven…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
文敎所被無遠弗届廣右人士
涵濡旣久蒸蒸嚮風而自奮
於同文之世者衆矣茲適大
比縱觀其所爲文類能採道
德之華掇仁義之精經術文
采寖與中土相埒夫士之悃
愊直抗天眞未斲固近道之
===
===
質大受之基也而又飾以文
學如此是猶楩楠豫章斲以
斧斤裹以藻繡必稱乎清廟
明堂之用昆吾干將淬以清
水斂以越砥何難于斷蛟剸
犀之功也哉由是知廣右之
士必將足以鳴世無疑矣且
punctuated: 文敎所被，無遠弗届。廣右人士涵濡旣久，蒸蒸嚮風，而自奮於同文之世者衆矣。茲適大比，縱觀其所爲文，類能採道德之華，掇仁義之精，經術文采寖與中土相埒。夫士之悃愊直抗，天眞未斲，固近道之質、大受之基也。而又飾以文學如此，是猶楩楠豫章，斲以斧斤，裹以藻繡，必稱乎清廟明堂之用；昆吾干將，淬以清水，斂以越砥，何難于斷蛟剸犀之功也哉！由是知廣右之士必將足以鳴世，無疑矣。且
translation_en: …wherever its civilizing instruction extends, no place is too distant to be reached. The scholars of Guangyou have long been steeped in its influence. Increasingly drawn to its example, many have roused themselves to exertion in this age of a shared written culture. Now, on the occasion of the triennial Provincial Examination, a broad survey of their compositions shows that they generally gather the finest blossoms of the Way and virtue and select the essence of benevolence and righteousness. Their learning in the Classics and literary accomplishment are gradually coming to rival those of the central regions. These scholars’ sincerity and upright resolve, their innate genuineness still unhewn, are indeed qualities close to the Way and a foundation for shouldering great responsibilities. When further adorned with literary learning of this kind, they resemble fine timber—pian, nan, and camphor—hewn with axes and hatchets and clothed in ornate embroidery, certain to be fit for use in the pure ancestral temple and the Hall of Enlightenment. Or they resemble the swords Kunwu and Ganjiang, quenched in clear water and honed on whetstones from Yue: what difficulty could they have in cutting down dragons and cleaving rhinoceroses? From this we know beyond doubt that the scholars of Guangyou will surely distinguish themselves in the world. Moreover, …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以天時地理人事稽之則茲
歲固氣運之獨盛者蓋廣右
輿地當天下西南西屬金而
南屬火歲在庚午庚爲金而
午爲火金以肅殺爲義有武
道焉火以光明爲象有文道
焉然金非能自爲用也必鍛
===
之以火而後可以成器武非
可以獨用也必綏之以文而
後可以成治要皆相須而不
可缺者也茲地自成化以來
人習承平武備稍弛遂致醜
夷漸違聲教今
天子惻然南顧
punctuated: 以天時、地理、人事稽之，則茲歲固氣運之獨盛者。蓋廣右輿地當天下西南，西屬金而南屬火。歲在庚午，庚爲金而午爲火。金以肅殺爲義，有武道焉；火以光明爲象，有文道焉。然金非能自爲用也，必鍛之以火而後可以成器；武非可以獨用也，必綏之以文而後可以成治。要皆相須而不可缺者也。茲地自成化以來，人習承平，武備稍弛，遂致醜夷漸違聲教。今天子惻然南顧
translation_en: …examining the timing of Heaven, the configuration of the land, and human affairs, this year is indeed one in which cosmic forces and fortune are exceptionally flourishing. Guangyou lies in the southwest of the realm: the west corresponds to metal, and the south to fire. This is the gengwu year: geng corresponds to metal, and wu to fire. Metal signifies stern killing and thus embodies the martial way; fire symbolizes radiance and thus embodies the civil way. Yet metal cannot become useful by itself: it must be forged with fire before it can become an implement. Nor can martial force be employed alone: it must be tempered by civil cultivation before orderly government can be achieved. In essence, each depends upon the other, and neither can be dispensed with. Since the Chenghua reign, the people of this region have grown accustomed to peace, and military preparedness has gradually slackened. Consequently, the odious barbarians have increasingly defied imperial authority and instruction. Now the Son of Heaven, moved with concern, turns his gaze southward…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
特命重臣爲經略計武功固期震
矣而又適當掄才之期所得
多士足以彰英華而賛治化
文武竝茂與地之西南歲之
庚午相爲符應其士之彬彬
稱盛也有由然矣爾諸士當
氣運之隆沐賓興之典毋徒
曰此足爲紆青拖紫服冕乗
軒之階也必即其飾之文者
篤之爲德行效之爲事功無
事則用文以綏太平如火之
足以長物有事則用武以戡
禍亂如金之足以收物斯無
負
punctuated: 特命重臣爲經略計，武功固期震矣，而又適當掄才之期，所得多士足以彰英華而賛治化。文武竝茂，與地之西南、歲之庚午相爲符應，其士之彬彬稱盛也有由然矣。爾諸士當氣運之隆，沐賓興之典，毋徒曰此足爲紆青拖紫、服冕乗軒之階也。必即其飾之文者，篤之爲德行，效之爲事功。無事則用文以綏太平，如火之足以長物；有事則用武以戡禍亂，如金之足以收物。斯無負
translation_en:
…has specially commissioned a senior minister to devise strategic plans, so that military achievements may indeed inspire awe. This also happens to coincide with the time for selecting talent, and the many scholars obtained are sufficient to display outstanding gifts and assist the work of governance and moral transformation. Civil and military accomplishments flourish together, corresponding auspiciously with this region’s position in the southwest and the year’s designation as gengwu. There is thus good reason why its scholars, combining refinement with substance, are acclaimed as flourishing.
You scholars, living at a time of ascendant fortune and receiving the favor of the ceremony for honoring and recommending worthy men, must not merely say that this suffices as a stepping-stone to wearing blue and purple insignia, donning ceremonial caps, and riding in dignitaries’ carriages. You must take the literary cultivation that adorns you, deepen it into virtuous conduct, and give it practical expression in service and achievement. In peaceful times, employ civil arts to preserve great peace, just as fire enables things to grow; in times of trouble, employ martial force to quell calamity and disorder, just as metal enables things to be gathered in. Thus you will not fail…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盛時而亦有光斯典矣若脩之
家而用則鑿言於靜而庸或
違是巨樗液樠而被之翬文
曷堪負棟頑鈆鼓冶而鏤以
螭章奚逃缺折又何取于文
之足以鳴世也幷以是爲諸
士勗是舉也鎮守總兵官征
蠻將軍右都督俞大猷振揚
武衞雅重章縫副使鄭一龍
應存卓陳其樂邵惟中左叅
議龔大器僉事金柱皆綜理
于外共襄盛舉左叅將黃應
甲右叅將王世科遊擊將軍
丁山署都指揮僉事錢鳳翔
punctuated:
盛時，而亦有光斯典矣。若脩之家而用則鑿，言於靜而庸或違，是巨樗液樠而被之翬文，曷堪負棟？頑鈆鼓冶而鏤以螭章，奚逃缺折？又何取于文之足以鳴世也？幷以是爲諸士勗。
是舉也，鎮守總兵官、征蠻將軍、右都督俞大猷，振揚武衞，雅重章縫；副使鄭一龍、應存卓、陳其樂、邵惟中，左叅議龔大器，僉事金柱，皆綜理于外，共襄盛舉。左叅將黃應甲、右叅將王世科、遊擊將軍丁山、署都指揮僉事錢鳳翔
translation_en:
…this flourishing age, and would also bring distinction to this ceremony. But if what one cultivates at home proves unsuitable in practice, and what one says in quiet circumstances sometimes conflicts with one’s conduct [?], this is like a great, sap-exuding tree of heaven clothed in the patterned plumage of a pheasant: how could it bear a roof beam? If base lead is smelted and engraved with coiling-dragon designs, how could it escape chipping and breaking? What value, then, is there in literary accomplishment sufficient to win renown in the world? I offer these words also as an exhortation to the scholars.
For this examination, Yu Dayou, Regional Commander, General Who Subdues the Man, and Right Chief Military Commissioner, upheld military protection and had long esteemed Confucian scholars. Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zheng Yilong, Ying Cunzhuo, Chen Qile, and Shao Weizhong; Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Gong Daqi; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Jin Zhu all managed affairs outside the examination compound and jointly assisted this grand undertaking. Left Assistant Regional Commander Huang Yingjia, Right Assistant Regional Commander Wang Shike, Mobile Corps Commander Ding Shan, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Qian Fengxiang…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史李良臣〔直雷貴州普安衛籍直隸江陰縣人乙丑進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使郭應聘〔君賓福建莆田縣人庚戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政楊銓〔朝明直隸華亭縣人丙辰進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使萬思謙〔益甫江西南昌縣人丁未進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事楊文明〔仲謨江西南昌縣人壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
江西贛州府儒學教授王燧〔時用直隸丹徒縣人丙午貢士〕
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教諭陳冠〔子加直隸長洲縣人己酉貢士〕
同考試官
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正鐵世材〔用卿雲南永昌衛籍浙江杭州衛人甲子貢士〕
江西九江府湖口縣儒學教諭宋邦達〔士充福建莆田縣人辛酉貢士〕
湖廣荆州府松滋縣儒學教諭林獻芹〔曉忠廣東東莞縣人甲子貢士〕
福建建寧府政和縣儒學教諭梁幹〔秉楨廣東東莞縣人戊午貢士〕
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學教諭陳三俊〔懋績廣東南海縣人壬子貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年廣西鄉試

監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史李良臣〔直雷，貴州普安衛籍，直隸江陰縣人，乙丑進士〕。

提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使郭應聘〔君賓，福建莆田縣人，庚戌進士〕。
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政楊銓〔朝明，直隸華亭縣人，丙辰進士〕。

監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使萬思謙〔益甫，江西南昌縣人，丁未進士〕。
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事楊文明〔仲謨，江西南昌縣人，壬戌進士〕。

考試官
江西贛州府儒學教授王燧〔時用，直隸丹徒縣人，丙午貢士〕。
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教諭陳冠〔子加，直隸長洲縣人，己酉貢士〕。

同考試官
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正鐵世材〔用卿，雲南永昌衛籍，浙江杭州衛人，甲子貢士〕。
江西九江府湖口縣儒學教諭宋邦達〔士充，福建莆田縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
湖廣荆州府松滋縣儒學教諭林獻芹〔曉忠，廣東東莞縣人，甲子貢士〕。
福建建寧府政和縣儒學教諭梁幹〔秉楨，廣東東莞縣人，戊午貢士〕。
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學教諭陳三俊〔懋績，廣東南海縣人，壬子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangxi Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Longqing (1570)

Supervising Official
Li Liangchen, Regional Inspecting Censor for Guangxi. His courtesy name was Zhilei [?]; he was registered with Pu’an Guard in Guizhou and was a native of Jiangyin County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the yichou year.

Proctors
Guo Yingpin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Junbin; he was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.
Yang Quan, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Chaoming; he was a native of Huating County, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.

Examination Supervisors
Wan Siqian, Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Yifu; he was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:

舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直樊遲退見子夏
曰鄉也吾見於夫子而問知子曰舉直
錯諸枉能使枉者直何謂也子夏曰富
哉言乎
誠則明矣明則誠矣
思天下之民匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤
者若己推而内之溝中其自任以天下
===
之重如此
易
象曰地中有水師君子以容民畜衆
安節之亨承上道也
唯幾也故能成天下之務
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖
人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。樊遲退，見子夏，曰：「鄉也吾見於夫子而問知，子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。』何謂也？」子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」

誠則明矣，明則誠矣。

思天下之民，匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤者，若己推而内之溝中。其自任以天下之重如此。

易

安節之亨，承上道也。

唯幾也，故能成天下之務。

離也者，明也。萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。

He thought that if, among all the people under Heaven, a single man or woman failed to receive the blessings of Yao and Shun, it was as though he himself had pushed them into a ditch. Such was the weight of responsibility for all under Heaven that he took upon himself.

Li means brightness. All things become visible to one another; it is the trigram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern: this practice is surely derived from this trigram.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
總目皆分曹綜緝甄明科部例之宋梁
孰優也夫六經修自仲尼厄於秦火古
今惜之漢唐宋藝文志簡編最爲博洽
然說者謂六經未嘗亡而遞考歷代所
載之書十已亡其六七此又何說也抑
吾儒博綜羣籍當必有窮本知要之學
不繫於篇帙之存亡與多士其詳著于
篇以爲稽古考文者采焉
問粵西自入中國版圖迄漢聲教漸被繇
===
是英才挺生代有作者乃今究觀人物
之林蓋有世業春秋持論識大體者有
擊猺有功民咸頌德者有保障南土無
愧竇融者有淑問得竟人稱爲皐陶者
有不畏彊禦立收常侍暴客者有條對
水旱明于陰陽大義者斯皆漢氏之良
也在唐則持節者開擴化外掇科者抗
言謝歸糾義者助平交趾斯寥寥矣宋
之人材最著故有雄才壯猷受知英主
punctuated:
總目皆分曹綜緝，甄明科部，例之宋梁，孰優也？夫六經修自仲尼，厄於秦火，古今惜之。漢唐宋藝文志，簡編最爲博洽。然說者謂六經未嘗亡，而遞考歷代所載之書，十已亡其六七，此又何說也？抑吾儒博綜羣籍，當必有窮本知要之學，不繫於篇帙之存亡與？多士其詳著于篇，以爲稽古考文者采焉。
問：粵西自入中國版圖，迄漢聲教漸被，繇是英才挺生，代有作者。乃今究觀人物之林，蓋有世業春秋、持論識大體者，有擊猺有功、民咸頌德者，有保障南土、無愧竇融者，有淑問得竟、人稱爲皐陶者，有不畏彊禦、立收常侍暴客者，有條對水旱、明于陰陽大義者，斯皆漢氏之良也。在唐則持節者開擴化外，掇科者抗言謝歸，糾義者助平交趾，斯寥寥矣。宋之人材最著，故有雄才壯猷、受知英主
translation_en:
…The general catalogues all compile and organize their contents by category, clearly distinguishing their subject divisions. Compared with those of the Song and Liang dynasties, which are superior? The Six Classics were edited by Zhongni [Confucius] and suffered the calamity of the Qin book burning, lamented in ancient and modern times alike. The bibliographical treatises of the Han, Tang, and Song histories are exceptionally comprehensive in the writings they record. Yet some say that the Six Classics were never lost, whereas, on examining successively the books recorded under each dynasty, six or seven out of every ten have already disappeared. How, then, is this to be explained? Or must we Confucian scholars, in our broad study of the assembled writings, possess a learning that probes their foundations and grasps their essentials, independent of whether their volumes survive or perish? You candidates should set this out fully in your essays, so that those who investigate antiquity and examine its writings may draw upon them.
Question: After Yuexi [Guangxi] entered the territory of China, civilizing instruction gradually spread there, reaching it by Han times. Thereafter outstanding talents arose, with accomplished men appearing in every generation. Surveying this company of notable figures today, we find one whose family specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals and whose arguments showed an understanding of the larger issues; one who won distinction fighting the Yao and whose virtue all the people praised; one who defended the southern lands and bore comparison with Dou Rong; one whose good reputation was brought to fulfillment [?] and whom people called Gao Yao; one who did not fear the powerful and immediately arrested the violent retainers of a Palace Attendant; and one who submitted itemized responses concerning floods and droughts, displaying a clear understanding of the great principles of yin and yang. These were all worthy men of the Han. Under the Tang, an envoy bearing the credentials of authority extended imperial influence beyond the bounds of civilization; a successful examination candidate spoke out boldly and took his leave to return home; and a man who rallied loyal forces helped pacify Jiaozhi. These were but a few. The Song was most distinguished for its men of talent; thus there was one whose outstanding abilities and grand designs won the recognition of an enlightened ruler…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直樊遲退見子夏
曰鄉也吾見於夫子而問知子曰舉直
錯諸枉能使枉者直何謂也子夏曰富
哉言乎
洪敷誥
同考試官教諭梁批場中作富哉言乎毎難著語獨
此作瑩徹含畜且論舉錯有關治道取之豈徒以其文耶
===
考試官教諭陳批典雅純正宜式多士
考試官教授王批說理明盡
聖人一言盡仁知之道而惟賢者識其大也蓋
仁知合一聖言之所以為大也子夏因遲之問
而嘆之也有以哉夫子之告樊遲意以愛人知
人仁知之理固然也子有疑焉盍觀用舍之道
乎彼天下有直者焉知而舉之與天下共舉之
也有枉者焉知而錯之與天下共錯之也斯則
道之所在吾以道公是非而天下以榮以辱位
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。」樊遲退，見子夏，曰：「鄉也，吾見於夫子而問知。子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。』何謂也？」子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」

洪敷誥

同考試官教諭梁批：場中作「富哉言乎」，毎難著語。獨此作瑩徹含畜，且論舉錯有關治道，取之豈徒以其文耶？

考試官教諭陳批：典雅純正，宜式多士。

考試官教授王批：說理明盡。

聖人一言盡仁知之道，而惟賢者識其大也。蓋仁知合一，聖言之所以為大也。子夏因遲之問而嘆之也，有以哉！夫子之告樊遲，意以愛人知人，仁知之理固然也。子有疑焉，盍觀用舍之道乎？彼天下有直者焉，知而舉之，與天下共舉之也；有枉者焉，知而錯之，與天下共錯之也。斯則道之所在，吾以道公是非，而天下以榮以辱，位
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Raise the upright and place them above the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.” Fan Chi withdrew and went to see Zixia. He said, “Earlier I went to see the Master and asked about wisdom. The Master said, ‘Raise the upright and place them above the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.’ What does this mean?” Zixia said, “How rich these words are!”

Hong Fugao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: In this examination, candidates writing on “How rich these words are!” generally find it difficult to express themselves. This essay alone is lucid and full of implied meaning. Moreover, its discussion of promotion and rejection bears upon the Way of government. Could its selection have been merely for its literary qualities?

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Refined, elegant, pure, and correct; it should serve as a model for the many scholars.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Its exposition of principle is clear and exhaustive.

In a single utterance the sage fully expressed the Way of benevolence and wisdom, yet only a worthy person could recognize its greatness. Indeed, the unity of benevolence and wisdom is what makes the sage’s words great. Zixia had good reason to exclaim in admiration when Fan Chi questioned him! In addressing Fan Chi, the Master meant that loving others and knowing others are the inherent principles of benevolence and wisdom. If you have doubts, why not consider the Way of employing and setting aside men? There are upright men in the world: to recognize and promote them is to join with all under Heaven in promoting them. There are crooked men: to recognize and reject them is to join with all under Heaven in rejecting them. Herein lies the Way. I apply the Way to judge impartially what is right and wrong, and those under Heaven thereby receive honor or disgrace; rank …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
蓋知此理之謂明誠固明之真焉耳苟至明察
其幾有見于萬境之皆徹則反躬踐其實庶幾
于一真之自如善吾明矣而身之誠者不由于
外鑠也知吾致矣而意之誠者無俟于他求也
明之所至誠亦至焉殆與聖人之至誠同其道
矣所謂賢人之教者非耶是知誠則明者性盡
而教無不立也明則誠者教行而性亦可盡也
性教殊名而天人一致誠之者奚容以自諉乎
大抵誠明本一理性教無二機而所以統之者
===
心也故吾性之知爲良知吾性之能爲良能此
誠即此明也此明亦此誠也而命之爲性脩之
爲教特隨在而異其名耳君子大其心以體之
則合天人通性教而一以貫之矣夫然後足以
語盡性之學
思天下之民匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤
者若已推而內之溝中其自任以天下
之重如此
彭啓忠
punctuated:
蓋知此理之謂明，誠固明之真焉耳。苟至明察其幾，有見于萬境之皆徹，則反躬踐其實，庶幾于一真之自如。善吾明矣，而身之誠者不由于外鑠也；知吾致矣，而意之誠者無俟于他求也。明之所至，誠亦至焉，殆與聖人之至誠同其道矣。所謂賢人之教者非耶？是知誠則明者，性盡而教無不立也；明則誠者，教行而性亦可盡也。性教殊名，而天人一致，誠之者奚容以自諉乎？大抵誠明本一理，性教無二機，而所以統之者，心也。故吾性之知爲良知，吾性之能爲良能，此誠即此明也，此明亦此誠也。而命之爲性，脩之爲教，特隨在而異其名耳。君子大其心以體之，則合天人，通性教，而一以貫之矣。夫然後足以語盡性之學。
思天下之民，匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤者，若已推而內之溝中，其自任以天下之重如此。
彭啓忠
translation_en:
For knowing this principle is what is called illumination; sincerity is simply the genuine substance of illumination. If one attains the utmost illumination and discerns the subtle beginnings, perceiving all circumstances with complete clarity, then one turns back upon oneself to put this reality into practice, approaching a state in which undivided genuineness operates spontaneously. Once I understand goodness, sincerity in my person does not come from something imposed from outside. Once I extend my knowledge to the utmost, sincerity of intention need not await any further search elsewhere. Wherever illumination reaches, sincerity also reaches: this surely follows the same Way as the utmost sincerity of the sage. Is this not what is called the teaching of the worthy?
Thus we know that when sincerity leads to illumination, one's nature is fully realized and teaching is established in every respect; when illumination leads to sincerity, teaching is put into practice and one's nature can likewise be fully realized. Nature and teaching differ in name, yet Heaven and humanity are at one. How could those striving for sincerity excuse themselves from this responsibility? In general, sincerity and illumination are fundamentally one principle, and nature and teaching do not operate through two distinct processes. What unifies them is the mind. Thus the knowing inherent in my nature is innate knowledge, and the capacity inherent in my nature is innate ability. This sincerity is precisely this illumination, and this illumination is likewise this sincerity. What Heaven confers is called nature, and its cultivation is called teaching: the names merely differ according to the aspect concerned. If the gentleman enlarges his mind to embody this, he unites Heaven and humanity, connects nature and teaching, and threads them together with a single principle. Only then is he qualified to discuss the learning that fully realizes human nature.
“He reflected that, among the people of the world, if any ordinary man or woman failed to receive the beneficence of Yao and Shun, it was as though he himself had pushed them into a ditch. Such was the weight of responsibility for the world that he took upon himself.”
Peng Qizhong

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
濟天下之溺視宇宙之事爲分內之事也盡斯
民而知覺之而後其責始塞焉畝畝藏脩之時
萬物一體之懷已素具矣敢曰天下至大也非
一己所能獨任而欲諉之於人耶詩書誦說之
日父母天下之心已素存矣敢曰天下之民至
眾也非一人所能兼濟而不以任之於己耶吁
惟其所志者大則所以自視者必不小惟其所
任者重則所以自待者必不輕割烹要湯之說
何其妄歟大抵人有不爲而後可以有爲尹當
===
耕莘之時惟知以堯舜之道自樂而萬鍾千駟
不足以動其中者志定故也故幡然而起以堯
舜君民爲己任而卒成撥亂反正之功豈偶然
哉宋儒謂伊尹格天事業始於一介取與信矣
是故君子貴辨志之學
易
象曰地中有水師君子以容民畜眾
朱寬
同考試官教諭梁批體認容民畜眾精確明切奇特
punctuated:
濟天下之溺，視宇宙之事爲分內之事也。盡斯民而知覺之，而後其責始塞焉。畝畝藏脩之時，萬物一體之懷已素具矣。敢曰天下至大也，非一己所能獨任，而欲諉之於人耶？詩書誦說之日，父母天下之心已素存矣。敢曰天下之民至眾也，非一人所能兼濟，而不以任之於己耶？吁！惟其所志者大，則所以自視者必不小；惟其所任者重，則所以自待者必不輕。割烹要湯之說，何其妄歟！大抵人有不爲，而後可以有爲。尹當耕莘之時，惟知以堯舜之道自樂，而萬鍾千駟不足以動其中者，志定故也。故幡然而起，以堯舜君民爲己任，而卒成撥亂反正之功，豈偶然哉？宋儒謂伊尹格天事業始於一介取與，信矣！是故君子貴辨志之學。
易
象曰：「地中有水，師；君子以容民畜眾。」
朱寬
同考試官教諭梁批：「體認容民畜眾，精確明切，奇特。」
translation_en:
…to rescue all under Heaven from drowning, regarding the affairs of the universe as matters within his own responsibility. Only after awakening all these people to understanding would he have fully discharged that responsibility. While pursuing learning and self-cultivation in the fields [?], he already cherished the conviction that all things form one body. Would he dare say that the world is so vast that he alone could not shoulder its burdens, and therefore seek to shift them onto others? While reciting and expounding the Odes and Documents, he already harbored the resolve to act as a parent to all under Heaven. Would he dare say that the people of the world are so numerous that one person could not aid them all, and therefore decline to assume responsibility for them himself? Ah! Precisely because his aspirations were great, his estimation of himself could not be small; precisely because his responsibilities were weighty, he could not treat himself lightly. How absurd is the claim that he sought access to Tang by cutting up meat and cooking!

In general, only by refusing to do certain things can a person become capable of accomplishment. When Yi Yin was plowing at Shen, he knew only to delight in the Way of Yao and Shun. Neither a stipend of ten thousand measures of grain nor a thousand teams of four horses could stir his heart, because his resolve was settled. Thus he decisively arose, taking as his own responsibility the task of making his ruler and people like those of Yao and Shun, and ultimately achieved the work of quelling disorder and restoring proper rule. Could this have happened by chance? The Song Confucians said that Yi Yin’s Heaven-moving achievements began with his scrupulousness over even the smallest act of taking or giving. True indeed! Thus the gentleman values the learning through which one discerns one’s aspirations.

Book of Changes

The Image says: “Within the earth there is water: the Army. The gentleman accordingly embraces the people and nurtures the multitude.”

Zhu Kuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “His understanding of embracing the people and nurturing the multitude is precise, clear, and pertinent—exceptional.”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
見不猶夫萬物之相見矣乎謂之曰蓋取諸此
信乎觀萬物而識化工之神因氣化而得法天
之治後天之離其合天人而一之者乎而圖位
之妙可知矣雖然天道以離爲用而必役之以
坤蓋氣之盛也不節則過焉故得坤以成其冲
和也聖人以明照四方苟明之過焉則傷于察
故有其明而不自用其明者亦所以培元氣而
代天工也書曰明作有功惇大成裕固敷政法
天竝行不悖之道也斯又繼離者之所當知
===
書
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋批辭旨春融渾厚虞廷都俞氣
象宛然在目
考試官教諭陳批詞理精到
考試官教授王批典則可誦
聖君總敕羣臣欲其敬以相天事焉蓋庶官所
治皆天事也敬以相之臣職其無忝乎帝舜所
punctuated:
見，不猶夫萬物之相見矣乎？謂之曰：「蓋取諸此。」信乎，觀萬物而識化工之神，因氣化而得法天之治。後天之離，其合天人而一之者乎？而圖位之妙可知矣。雖然，天道以離爲用，而必役之以坤。蓋氣之盛也，不節則過焉，故得坤以成其冲和也。聖人以明照四方，苟明之過焉，則傷于察。故有其明而不自用其明者，亦所以培元氣而代天工也。《書》曰：「明作有功，惇大成裕。」固敷政法天竝行不悖之道也。斯又繼離者之所當知。

書

帝曰：「咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。」

史著勳

同考試官教諭宋批：「辭旨春融渾厚，虞廷都俞氣象宛然在目。」

考試官教諭陳批：「詞理精到。」

考試官教授王批：「典則可誦。」

聖君總敕羣臣，欲其敬以相天事焉。蓋庶官所治，皆天事也。敬以相之，臣職其無忝乎？帝舜所
translation_en:
…appear—is this not like the myriad things coming into view together? Of this it is said: “It was presumably taken from this.” Indeed, by observing the myriad things, one recognizes the wondrous power of creation; through the transformations of vital energy, one grasps how to govern in accordance with Heaven. Does not Li in the Later Heaven arrangement unite Heaven and humanity as one? Thus the subtle significance of its position in the diagram can be understood. Nevertheless, although the Way of Heaven employs Li, it must regulate it through Kun. For vital energy at its height will become excessive unless restrained; hence it requires Kun to achieve balanced harmony. The sage illuminates the four quarters with his discernment, but if that discernment becomes excessive, it does harm through over-scrutiny. Thus, possessing discernment without insisting on exercising it oneself is also a means of nurturing primal vital energy and carrying out Heaven’s work on its behalf. The Book of Documents says: “Intelligent action brings achievement; sincerity and magnanimity produce ample well-being.” These are indeed ways of administering government and modeling oneself on Heaven that proceed together without conflict. This, too, is something those who succeed to Li should understand.

Book of Documents

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
見不猶夫萬物之相見矣乎謂之曰蓋取諸此
信乎觀萬物而識化工之神因氣化而得法天
之治後天之離其合天人而一之者乎而圖位
之妙可知矣雖然天道以離為用而必役之以
坤蓋氣之盛也不節則過焉故得坤以成其冲
和也聖人以明照四方苟明之過焉則傷于察
故有其明而不自用其明者亦所以培元氣而
代天工也書曰明作有功惇大成裕固敷政法
天並行不悖之道也斯又繼離者之所當知
===
書
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋 批 辭旨春融渾厚虞廷都俞氣
象宛然在目
考試官教諭陳 批 調理精到
考試官教授王 批 典則可誦
聖君總勑羣臣欲其敬以相天事焉蓋庶官所
治皆天事也敬以相之臣職其無忝乎帝舜所
punctuated:
見，不猶夫萬物之相見矣乎？謂之曰「蓋取諸此」。信乎！觀萬物而識化工之神，因氣化而得法天之治。後天之離，其合天人而一之者乎！而圖位之妙可知矣。雖然，天道以離為用，而必役之以坤。蓋氣之盛也，不節則過焉，故得坤以成其冲和也。聖人以明照四方，苟明之過焉，則傷于察，故有其明而不自用其明者，亦所以培元氣而代天工也。《書》曰：「明作有功，惇大成裕。」固敷政法天並行不悖之道也。斯又繼離者之所當知。

translation_en:
…manifestation—is it not like the mutual manifestation of the myriad things? Of this it is said, “It was probably taken from this.” How true! By observing the myriad things, one recognizes the wondrous workings of creation; through the transformations of vital energy, one discovers governance modeled on Heaven. Does not Li in the Later Heaven arrangement unite Heaven and humanity as one? Thus one can understand the subtlety of the positions in the diagram. Nevertheless, although the Way of Heaven operates through Li, it must employ Kun. When vital energy flourishes, it becomes excessive unless restrained; hence it requires Kun to achieve balanced harmony. The sage illuminates the four quarters with his discernment. If that discernment becomes excessive, however, it causes harm through over-scrutiny. Thus, possessing discernment without relying exclusively upon it is also a means of nourishing primal vital energy and carrying out Heaven’s work on its behalf. The Book of Documents says: “Through clear understanding in action, there is achievement; through generosity and breadth, there is abundance.” These are indeed mutually compatible ways of administering government and modeling oneself on Heaven. This, too, is what those who follow Li must understand.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以總勅羣臣者意曰人君之所畏者惟天而已
而所賴以事天者惟臣而已咨汝二十有二人
也詔之官聯固有崇卑之異秩而辨其官守實
皆天事之攸關者也是必恪共乃職而有嚴有
翼于以克相乎上帝之宜敬爾有官而無怠無
荒于以奉若乎上天之載四岳敬於內治也而
羣牧亦敬於外治焉兢兢然合志以贊化工俾
天職之分布於所司者日奏咸熈之績斯已矣
百揆敬于統理也而庶官亦敬于分理焉業業
===
然一德以調元化俾天事之責成於有位者日
見明作之功斯已矣勲庸之舊著者當因夫天
功之既亮而敬以圖厥終也蓋造化無全能而
待人以成其能雖欽翼以承之猶恐範圍之用
未弘也可以怠心處之乎責任之方新者當成
夫天功之初亮而敬以虞其始也蓋天道無全
功而待人以成其功雖祗慎以圖之猶恐有相
之道未盡也可以慢心乘之乎是則敬以盡職
而因以事天信乎臣道有關於天道也爾羣臣
punctuated: 以總勅羣臣者，意曰：「人君之所畏者惟天而已，而所賴以事天者惟臣而已。咨汝二十有二人也！詔之官聯，固有崇卑之異秩，而辨其官守，實皆天事之攸關者也。是必恪共乃職，而有嚴有翼，于以克相乎上帝之宜；敬爾有官，而無怠無荒，于以奉若乎上天之載。四岳敬於內治也，而羣牧亦敬於外治焉，兢兢然合志以贊化工，俾天職之分布於所司者，日奏咸熈之績斯已矣。百揆敬于統理也，而庶官亦敬于分理焉，業業然一德以調元化，俾天事之責成於有位者，日見明作之功斯已矣。勲庸之舊著者，當因夫天功之既亮，而敬以圖厥終也。蓋造化無全能，而待人以成其能，雖欽翼以承之，猶恐範圍之用未弘也，可以怠心處之乎？責任之方新者，當成夫天功之初亮，而敬以虞其始也。蓋天道無全功，而待人以成其功，雖祗慎以圖之，猶恐有相之道未盡也，可以慢心乘之乎？是則敬以盡職，而因以事天，信乎臣道有關於天道也。爾羣臣
translation_en:
…in issuing his general admonition to the assembled ministers, his meaning was: “What the ruler stands in awe of is Heaven alone; those on whom he relies to serve Heaven are his ministers alone. Ah, you twenty-two men! In appointing you to your associated offices, there are indeed differences of rank, high and low; yet, when your official responsibilities are distinguished, all concern the affairs of Heaven. You must therefore discharge your duties with reverent care, solemn and attentive, so as to assist in what accords with the Lord on High. Be reverent in your offices, neither idle nor neglectful, so as obediently to carry out the workings of Heaven above. Let the Four Mountains be reverent in governing within, and the regional governors likewise be reverent in governing without. With vigilant care, unite your purposes to assist the work of transformation, so that Heaven’s duties, distributed among the responsible offices, may daily yield the achievement of universal prosperity. That is all that is required. Let the Chief Minister be reverent in overseeing the whole, and the various officials likewise be reverent in administering their respective charges. With watchful care, unite in virtue to harmonize the primal transformation, so that Heaven’s affairs, entrusted for their accomplishment to those holding office, may daily display the results of enlightened action. That is all that is required.

“Those whose meritorious service has long been manifest should build upon Heaven’s work already assisted, and reverently plan for its completion. For the creative and transforming powers cannot accomplish everything unaided: they await human beings to fulfill their capacity. Even when we uphold them with reverence and care, we still fear that our work of ordering and encompassing their operations is not sufficiently extensive. Can we approach this with an idle heart? Those whose responsibilities are newly assumed should bring to fulfillment Heaven’s work that they have begun to assist, and reverently take thought for its beginning. For the Way of Heaven does not accomplish its work unaided: it awaits human beings to complete that work. Even when we plan with reverence and caution, we still fear that the means of assisting it have not been fully realized. Can we undertake this with a negligent heart? Thus, through reverence you fulfill your duties and thereby serve Heaven. Truly, the Way of the minister bears upon the Way of Heaven. You assembled ministers…”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盍亦是務乎嘗觀易以財成輔相歸之元后而
此以亮天功者責之臣何耶蓋君道有心而無
爲而岳牧九官之臣所賴以理庶職猶之天道
無心而成化而四時五行之吏所資以成歲功
也然則帝舜之命君道也亦天道也厥後皐陶
陳知人之謨而亦以人代天工責之有虞之君
臣交儆以事天者固如此
先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則知小人之依
伍睿
===
同考試官教諭宋批周公告成王本旨發明精切
錄之以式
考試官教諭陳批鬯達
考試官教授王批雅飭有文
大臣原君子恤民之故見無逸之所自也夫民
之所重者稼穡也君子知其難而體之奚暇以
自逸耶周公告成王意若曰天下之事未始不
成於勤而荒於逸者也君子所以能無逸者何
哉誠以君位至逸也稼穡至艱難也惟不知其
punctuated:
盍亦是務乎？嘗觀《易》以財成輔相歸之元后，而此以亮天功者責之臣，何耶？蓋君道有心而無爲，而岳牧九官之臣所賴以理庶職，猶之天道無心而成化，而四時五行之吏所資以成歲功也。然則帝舜之命，君道也，亦天道也。厥後皐陶陳知人之謨，而亦以人代天工責之有虞之君。臣交儆以事天者，固如此。
先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
伍睿
同考試官教諭宋批：周公告成王本旨，發明精切，錄之以式。
考試官教諭陳批：鬯達。
考試官教授王批：雅飭有文。
大臣原君子恤民之故，見無逸之所自也。夫民之所重者稼穡也，君子知其難而體之，奚暇以自逸耶？周公告成王，意若曰：天下之事，未始不成於勤而荒於逸者也。君子所以能無逸者何哉？誠以君位至逸也，稼穡至艱難也。惟不知其
translation_en:
…should you not also devote yourselves to this? I have observed that the Book of Changes assigns to the sovereign the work of regulating and completing, assisting and supporting Heaven and Earth; yet here responsibility for bringing Heaven’s work to completion is laid upon ministers. Why is this? The ruler’s Way has conscious purpose yet acts without contrivance, and the ministers—the regional overseers, provincial governors, and nine chief officials—depend upon it to administer their various offices. Likewise, Heaven’s Way has no conscious purpose yet accomplishes transformation, and its functionaries—the four seasons and five phases—draw upon it to complete the year’s work. Thus Emperor Shun’s command embodies both the ruler’s Way and Heaven’s Way. Later, Gao Yao presented his counsel on understanding men, likewise charging the ruler of Yu with having men perform Heaven’s work in its stead. Such, indeed, was the mutual admonition through which ruler and minister served Heaven.
“First understand the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then take ease; thus you will understand what the common people depend upon.”
Wu Rui
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “The essential meaning of the Duke of Zhou’s admonition to King Cheng is elucidated with precision and penetration. Recorded here to serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Fluent and clear.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Refined, well ordered, and possessed of literary elegance.”
The great minister traces the reasons why the ruler shows solicitude for the people, revealing the source of his freedom from idle ease. What matters most to the people is sowing and reaping. If the ruler understands their hardships and takes them to heart, what leisure has he to indulge himself in ease? In admonishing King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou meant something like this: affairs throughout the realm invariably succeed through diligence and fall into neglect through ease. How is it that the ruler can refrain from idle ease? Truly, it is because the ruler’s position affords the greatest ease, while sowing and reaping involve the greatest hardship. It is only through not understanding their…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
難而遽享乎逸始有忽民依而自肆者矣君子
則心存於民隱而預識乎百畝之憂慮切於民
生而周知乎三農之務時而東作也不必身親
乎耕稼而先天下以達其勤動之故者昭然若
所備嘗焉時而西成也不必下同乎穡人而先
天下以察其胼胝之勞者確然若所親見焉由
是而居大君之位以享天下之逸也有不知小
民之依乎吾知居於深宮者此心也既灼見乎
畒畝艱難之實則履乎帝位者亦此心也自洞
===
察夫烝民粒食之源知小人之依於稼也而我
稼之未同何以立斯民之大命乎則夫思艱圖
易以作天下之依者蓋有不遑寧處者矣矧敢
縱逸乎哉知小人之依於穡也而穡事之未成
何以貽斯民之率育乎則夫事制曲防以開天
下之麗者蓋有惟日孜孜者矣况敢逸豫乎哉
夫古之居君位者始於憂勤而終於逸樂此所
以稱無逸者歸之也吾王其監之哉抑論書戒
無逸詩陳豳風姬公固惓惓以農事詔王矣迺
punctuated:
難而遽享乎逸，始有忽民依而自肆者矣。君子則心存於民隱，而預識乎百畝之憂；慮切於民生，而周知乎三農之務。時而東作也，不必身親乎耕稼，而先天下以達其勤動之故者，昭然若所備嘗焉；時而西成也，不必下同乎穡人，而先天下以察其胼胝之勞者，確然若所親見焉。由是而居大君之位，以享天下之逸也，有不知小民之依乎？吾知居於深宮者此心也，既灼見乎畒畝艱難之實，則履乎帝位者亦此心也，自洞察夫烝民粒食之源。知小人之依於稼也，而我稼之未同，何以立斯民之大命乎？則夫思艱圖易，以作天下之依者，蓋有不遑寧處者矣，矧敢縱逸乎哉！知小人之依於穡也，而穡事之未成，何以貽斯民之率育乎？則夫事制曲防，以開天下之麗者，蓋有惟日孜孜者矣，况敢逸豫乎哉！夫古之居君位者，始於憂勤而終於逸樂，此所以稱無逸者歸之也。吾王其監之哉！

抑論《書》戒無逸，《詩》陳豳風，姬公固惓惓以農事詔王矣，迺
translation_en:
…the hardship and hastily enjoy ease: only then do they neglect what sustains the people and indulge themselves. The gentleman keeps the people’s sufferings in his heart and understands beforehand the anxieties of tending a hundred mu of land; deeply concerned for their livelihood, he knows thoroughly the tasks of farming. When spring cultivation begins, he need not personally undertake plowing and planting: his understanding, ahead of all under Heaven, of what their exertions entail is as clear as though he had experienced it all himself. When the autumn harvest comes, he need not descend to work alongside the harvesters: his perception, ahead of all under Heaven, of the toil that calluses their hands and feet is as certain as though he had witnessed it himself. Thus, when he occupies the sovereign’s position and enjoys the ease afforded by all under Heaven, could he fail to know what sustains the common people? I know that this is the heart he possesses while dwelling deep within the palace. Having clearly perceived the actual hardships of the fields, he retains that same heart upon occupying the imperial throne, and naturally understands fully the source of the grain that feeds the multitude.

He knows that the common people depend on planting. If our crops have not yet been gathered, how can he secure the very lives of these people? Thus, to consider difficulties and devise ways to ease them, becoming a support for all under Heaven, surely leaves him no leisure to rest peacefully. How could he dare indulge in ease? He knows that the common people depend on harvesting. If the harvest is not yet complete, how can he ensure that these people are all nourished? Thus, to regulate affairs and take precautions in every detail, providing all under Heaven with something to depend upon, surely requires tireless diligence each day. How could he dare give himself to idle pleasure?

Now, those who occupied the ruler’s position in antiquity began with anxious diligence but ended in ease and pleasure. This is why the exhortation to be without ease was addressed to them [?]. May our king take warning from this!

Furthermore, the Documents warns against ease, and the Odes sets forth the Airs of Bin. The Duke of Zhou indeed earnestly instructed the king through the tasks of farming. Yet …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
孟子以竝耕爲害治何也蓋人君以心勞天下
則易故民依不可忽以形勞天下則難故農事
不可兼此其意各有攸當而識治體者當辨之
於早矣後世忘祖德而忽民艱舍憂勤而縱逸
樂者其無以豳風無逸之說告之與
詩
經營四方告成于王
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批〔體格莊嚴詞語精錬於經營告〕
〔成意發揮詳盡殆志存立功者與〕
考試官教諭陳批〔條鬯〕
考試官教授王批〔莊重〕
===
詩人美大將必自其攘夷奏功者言之也蓋大
將有事於外者王命也夫既攘夷而成功矣得
不入告於王哉詩人敘其事以美之也若曰王
者之治以內順外威爲盛人臣之職以攘外安
內爲功彼淮夷侵陵而興師薄伐虎既受成于
王矣使其經營之未就抑將何以告其成乎今
punctuated:
孟子以竝耕爲害治，何也？蓋人君以心勞天下則易，故民依不可忽；以形勞天下則難，故農事不可兼。此其意各有攸當，而識治體者當辨之於早矣。後世忘祖德而忽民艱，舍憂勤而縱逸樂者，其無以《豳風》《無逸》之說告之與？

詩
「經營四方，告成于王。」
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批〔體格莊嚴，詞語精錬，於經營告成意發揮詳盡，殆志存立功者與？〕
考試官教諭陳批〔條鬯。〕
考試官教授王批〔莊重。〕

詩人美大將，必自其攘夷奏功者言之也。蓋大將有事於外者，王命也。夫既攘夷而成功矣，得不入告於王哉？詩人敘其事以美之也。若曰：「王者之治，以內順外威爲盛；人臣之職，以攘外安內爲功。彼淮夷侵陵，而興師薄伐，虎既受成于王矣。使其經營之未就，抑將何以告其成乎？今
translation_en:
…why, then, did Mengzi regard a ruler’s farming alongside the people as harmful to government? For a ruler, to labor for the realm with his mind makes governing easy; hence he must not neglect the people’s means of support. To labor for the realm with his body makes governing difficult; hence he cannot undertake farming as an additional occupation. Each teaching thus has its appropriate application, and those who understand the essentials of government should distinguish them early. As for later rulers who forget their ancestors’ virtue and disregard the people’s hardships, abandoning anxious diligence to indulge in ease and pleasure—has no one admonished them with the teachings of the Airs of Bin and Against Ease?

Book of Odes
“He brought order to the four quarters and reported his accomplishment to the king.”
Peng Qizhong
Associate Examiner Tie, School Instructor, comments: 〔The composition is dignified in form, its language refined and concise. It develops fully and thoroughly the meaning of bringing order and reporting accomplishment. Might its author aspire to render meritorious service?〕
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔Well ordered and lucid.〕
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔Dignified and weighty.〕

When the poet praises a great commander, he necessarily speaks of his repelling foreign peoples and achieving success. For a great commander’s undertaking beyond the royal domain is performed at the king’s command. Having repelled the foreigners and achieved success, how could he fail to enter court and report to the king? The poet recounts his deeds to praise him. It is as though he says: “A king’s government flourishes through obedience within and awe abroad; a minister’s service achieves merit through repelling threats from without and securing peace within. When those Huai peoples encroached, troops were raised to attack them, and Hu had already received his charge from the king. Had his efforts to bring order remained unfinished, how could he have reported their accomplishment? Now …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
虎也奉天討以徂征而式固謀猷期得乎萬全
之道遵廟謨以制勝而式遏寇虐冀成夫底定
之休四方之疆宇莫非王土也悉心於恢拓之
圖而侵者復焉荒者闢焉務俾有利于社稷斯
已矣四方之人民莫非王臣也殫力於綏懷之
略而渙者萃之來者安之務俾有益于生靈斯
已矣如是而成功也能不爲王告哉蓋始焉簡
書之授王固欲觀厥成也玆大懟旣殄而憖迺
丕績用敷奏於天子之庭昔焉推轂之遣王固
===
欲求厥寧也玆大敵旣克而以奏膚公用對揚
乎一人之命以其恢拓之功從而上聞焉則知
土宇版章無改於舊而天王一統之業自是其
永保乎以其綏懷之功從而上達焉則知萬方
攸同不失其初而九重南顧之憂自是其可釋
乎吁召虎之經營也以定王國之事也不爲倖
功其告成也以佐天子之忠也非爲希寵其眞
可謂中興之賢佐者歟抑吾于是而見馭夷之
道也淮夷倡亂召公討之不玩寇不黷武而惟
punctuated:
虎也奉天討以徂征，而式固謀猷，期得乎萬全之道；遵廟謨以制勝，而式遏寇虐，冀成夫底定之休。四方之疆宇，莫非王土也，悉心於恢拓之圖，而侵者復焉，荒者闢焉，務俾有利于社稷斯已矣。四方之人民，莫非王臣也，殫力於綏懷之略，而渙者萃之，來者安之，務俾有益于生靈斯已矣。如是而成功也，能不爲王告哉？蓋始焉簡書之授，王固欲觀厥成也。玆大懟旣殄，而憖迺丕績，用敷奏於天子之庭。昔焉推轂之遣，王固欲求厥寧也。玆大敵旣克，而以奏膚公，用對揚乎一人之命。以其恢拓之功，從而上聞焉，則知土宇版章無改於舊，而天王一統之業，自是其永保乎！以其綏懷之功，從而上達焉，則知萬方攸同不失其初，而九重南顧之憂，自是其可釋乎！

吁！召虎之經營也，以定王國之事也，不爲倖功；其告成也，以佐天子之忠也，非爲希寵。其眞可謂中興之賢佐者歟！抑吾于是而見馭夷之道也。淮夷倡亂，召公討之，不玩寇，不黷武，而惟
translation_en:
…Hu undertook his expedition to carry out Heaven’s punishment, securing his plans in the hope of finding a course that would ensure complete success. He followed the court’s strategic counsels to achieve victory, checking the enemy’s violence in the hope of bringing about the blessing of lasting peace. All territory within the four quarters was the king’s land. He devoted himself wholeheartedly to plans for its recovery and expansion: occupied lands were recovered, and wastelands opened up. His sole aim was to benefit the altars of soil and grain. All the people within the four quarters were the king’s subjects. He exerted himself fully in measures to pacify them and win their allegiance: he gathered those who had scattered and settled those who came to submit. His sole aim was to benefit the people. Having achieved success in this way, could he fail to report it to the king? When the written commands were first conferred, the king certainly wished to see their fulfillment. Now that the great foe had been destroyed, he set forth his mighty achievements [?] before the Son of Heaven’s court. When the king had earlier sent him off, ceremonially pushing his chariot wheels, he certainly sought the restoration of peace. Now that the great enemy had been overcome, Hu reported his great accomplishments, thereby answering and extolling the sovereign’s command. When his achievements in recovering and expanding the realm were reported to the throne, it became clear that the territory and its registers [?] remained as of old. Surely the Heavenly King’s unified dominion could henceforth be preserved forever! When his achievements in pacifying the people and winning their allegiance were communicated to the throne, it became clear that all regions were united as they had been at the beginning. Surely the sovereign’s anxious concern for the south could henceforth be laid to rest!

Ah! Shao Hu’s endeavors were directed toward securing the affairs of the royal realm; he did not seek success through mere luck. His report of success arose from his loyalty in assisting the Son of Heaven; he was not seeking favor. Could he not truly be called a worthy minister of the dynastic restoration? Here, moreover, I perceive the proper way to govern the Yi peoples. When the Huai Yi rose in rebellion, the Duke of Shao attacked them. He neither took the enemy lightly nor resorted recklessly to arms, but solely…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
在于經營信乎老成持重正易所謂師貞丈人
吉也是以有顯允之方叔而獫狁之難襄有赫
赫之南仲而昆夷之患息故誦是詩者雖嘉穆
公之功而宣王得人之盛不亦尤可美歟
思文后稷克配彼天立我烝民莫匪爾極
貽我來牟帝命率育無此疆爾界陳常
于時夏
李宜春
同考試官教諭陳批發揮題意明徹而詞更整潔
===
是深於詩者
考試官教諭陳批義精詞雅讀之灑然
考試官教授王批詞理瑩粹
詩人頌聖祖與天合德而必本其養民之極功
焉夫承天意以養民而教因以行焉聖祖之功
亦偉矣此其德之所以配天也歟此周人尊祖
配天之詩也意謂必有天下之大德斯可享天
下之大報我周南郊之祭人知以稷配天矣而
豈知其德之有同於天乎惟我后稷先天以開
punctuated:
在于經營。信乎，老成持重，正《易》所謂「師貞，丈人吉」也。是以有顯允之方叔，而獫狁之難襄；有赫赫之南仲，而昆夷之患息。故誦是詩者，雖嘉穆公之功，而宣王得人之盛，不亦尤可美歟？
「思文后稷，克配彼天。立我烝民，莫匪爾極。貽我來牟，帝命率育。無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。」
李宜春
同考試官教諭陳批：「發揮題意明徹，而詞更整潔，是深於詩者。」
考試官教諭陳批：「義精詞雅，讀之灑然。」
考試官教授王批：「詞理瑩粹。」
詩人頌聖祖與天合德，而必本其養民之極功焉。夫承天意以養民，而教因以行焉，聖祖之功亦偉矣。此其德之所以配天也歟？此周人尊祖配天之詩也。意謂必有天下之大德，斯可享天下之大報。我周南郊之祭，人知以稷配天矣，而豈知其德之有同於天乎？惟我后稷，先天以開
translation_en:
…lies in careful planning and management. Truly, seasoned experience and sober judgment are precisely what the Book of Changes means by “In leading an army, be steadfast; for a mature man, good fortune.” Thus, with the illustrious and trustworthy Fang Shu, the troubles caused by the Xianyun were overcome; with the glorious Nan Zhong, the menace of the Kunyi subsided. Therefore, although those who recite this ode praise Duke Mu’s achievements, is not King Xuan’s outstanding success in obtaining worthy men still more deserving of admiration?
“Ah, cultivated Hou Ji, you were worthy to be Heaven’s counterpart. You established our multitude of people; none failed to find their highest standard in you. You bequeathed wheat and barley to us; at the Lord on High’s command, you nourished all. Without distinctions between this border and that boundary, you spread the enduring norms throughout this land of Xia.”
Li Yichun
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor: “The meaning of the topic is developed clearly and thoroughly, and the language is especially well ordered and polished. This is someone with a profound understanding of the Odes.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, an Instructor: “The meaning is refined and the language elegant. Reading it leaves one refreshed.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, a Professor: “The language and reasoning are lucid and pure.”
The poet praises the sage ancestor for uniting his virtue with Heaven’s, necessarily grounding this praise in his supreme achievement of nourishing the people. By carrying out Heaven’s intention to nourish the people, he also enabled moral instruction to take effect. Great indeed were the sage ancestor’s achievements! Was this not why his virtue made him worthy to be Heaven’s counterpart? This is an ode in which the people of Zhou honor their ancestor by associating him with Heaven in sacrifice. Its meaning is that only one who possesses the greatest virtue under Heaven may receive the greatest recompense under Heaven. At our Zhou sacrifice in the southern suburb, people know that Ji is associated with Heaven; but do they understand how his virtue was identical with Heaven’s? Our Hou Ji alone anticipated Heaven in opening up…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人而經緯之章合貞觀以竝運因地以盡利而
彌綸之績與造化而同流蘊之爲文德之精者
卽乾元於穆之體也發之爲文治之華者卽天
道高明之用也此其德眞足以配天矣然果何
以見之蓋民生有欲不能以自遂也稷則教之
稼穡開天下粒食之原而利興於當時澤被於
後世矣孰非其至德耶惟天惠民不能以自致
也稷則貽我來牟承上帝率育之命而天雖無
爲稷代有終矣孰非其成能耶由是生養遂則
===
禮義之心自生無有疆界之殊而以正君臣以
篤父子彝倫攸叙之風達之天下矣洪荒之世
不奕然爲文明之會乎民生厚則正德之功自
奮無有彼此之限而各尊其尊各親其親人紀
肇脩之化徧於中國矣顓蒙之俗不燁然爲聲
教之都乎吁后稷上承帝命之命是能爲天地
立心矣下開教養之端是能爲生民立命矣此
其德不謂之至德乎而南郊之配夫孰曰不宜
抑論周人郊而祀天以后稷之文德配至明堂
punctuated: 人，而經緯之章合貞觀以竝運；因地以盡利，而彌綸之績與造化而同流。蘊之爲文德之精者，卽乾元於穆之體也；發之爲文治之華者，卽天道高明之用也。此其德眞足以配天矣。然果何以見之？蓋民生有欲，不能以自遂也，稷則教之稼穡，開天下粒食之原，而利興於當時，澤被於後世矣，孰非其至德耶？惟天惠民，不能以自致也，稷則貽我來牟，承上帝率育之命，而天雖無爲，稷代有終矣，孰非其成能耶？由是生養遂，則禮義之心自生，無有疆界之殊，而以正君臣，以篤父子，彝倫攸叙之風達之天下矣。洪荒之世，不奕然爲文明之會乎？民生厚，則正德之功自奮，無有彼此之限，而各尊其尊，各親其親，人紀肇脩之化徧於中國矣。顓蒙之俗，不燁然爲聲教之都乎？吁！后稷上承帝命之命，是能爲天地立心矣；下開教養之端，是能爲生民立命矣。此其德不謂之至德乎？而南郊之配，夫孰曰不宜？抑論周人郊而祀天，以后稷之文德配，至明堂
translation_en:
…humanity, and the ordered patterns of his work moved in concert with Heaven and Earth’s enduring order. Drawing upon the land to realize all its benefits, his comprehensive achievements flowed together with the processes of creation and transformation. What lay within as the essence of his civil virtue was the very substance of Heaven’s primal, profound majesty; what manifested outwardly as the splendor of his civil governance was the very operation of the Way of Heaven in its loftiness and illumination. His virtue truly sufficed to make him Heaven’s sacrificial companion. Yet how can this actually be seen?

The people have desires in sustaining their lives but cannot fulfill them unaided. Ji therefore taught them sowing and reaping, opening the way for all under Heaven to subsist on grain. Benefits arose in his own time, and his bounty extended to later generations. Which of these was not an expression of his consummate virtue? Heaven bestows blessings upon the people, yet these cannot reach them unaided. Ji therefore bequeathed wheat and barley to us, carrying out the Lord on High’s command to nurture all. Though Heaven acted without deliberate effort, Ji brought its work to completion on its behalf. Which of these was not his fulfillment of Heaven’s capacities?

Thus, once their sustenance and nurture were secured, a sense of ritual propriety and righteousness arose naturally. Without distinction of territorial boundaries, the relationship between ruler and minister was rectified and that between father and son strengthened; the practice of duly ordering the constant human relationships spread throughout the world. Did the age of primordial wilderness not become a splendid era of civilization? Once the people’s livelihood was abundant, efforts to rectify virtue arose of themselves. Without distinction between here and there, each honored those whom they ought to honor and cherished their own kin. The transforming influence through which human relationships first came to be cultivated spread throughout the Central Lands. Did benighted customs not give way to a resplendent center of moral instruction?

Ah! Above, Hou Ji received the command of the imperial command [?], and thus could establish a heart for Heaven and Earth. Below, he initiated the teaching and nurture of the people, and thus could establish a secure life for the living. Should his virtue not be called consummate virtue? Who, then, could say it was unfitting for him to be Heaven’s sacrificial companion at the southern suburban altar? Moreover, to discuss the matter further: the people of Zhou sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar, associating Hou Ji with Heaven on account of his civil virtue; as for the Hall of Light…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則配以文王亦曰文之所以爲文與天之所以
爲天一也然則不有文德不足以配天明矣周
人制禮精義於此可以想見明於其義則仁孝
之道備而尊親之化行此夫子所謂治國其如
視諸斯也讀詩者當自得之
春秋
冬十有二月齊侯鄭伯盟于石門〔隱公三年〕
秦延緒
===
同考試官教諭林批此題傳意甚略作者類失之膚
淺此篇意思清婉而豐腴深得聖人公世之志
考試官教諭陳批辭義森嚴
考試官教授王批莊重典雅
春秋惡諸侯之講信所以志大道之公也此見
聖人之志公天下者也特盟之私自石門始矣
是以見惡於春秋吾聞常事不書春秋例也石
門之盟亦常事爾而何以書蓋自敬信孚于虞
夏卓乎無以尚也而誥誓肇於商周則旣浸以
punctuated:
則配以文王，亦曰文之所以爲文與天之所以爲天，一也。然則不有文德，不足以配天，明矣。周人制禮精義，於此可以想見。明於其義，則仁孝之道備，而尊親之化行。此夫子所謂「治國其如視諸斯也」。讀詩者當自得之。
春秋
冬十有二月，齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門。〔隱公三年〕
秦延緒
同考試官教諭林批：此題傳意甚略，作者類失之膚淺。此篇意思清婉而豐腴，深得聖人公世之志。
考試官教諭陳批：辭義森嚴。
考試官教授王批：莊重典雅。
春秋惡諸侯之講信，所以志大道之公也。此見聖人之志公天下者也。特盟之私自石門始矣，是以見惡於春秋。吾聞常事不書，春秋例也。石門之盟亦常事爾，而何以書？蓋自敬信孚于虞夏，卓乎無以尚也，而誥誓肇於商周，則旣浸以
translation_en:
…then King Wen was associated with Heaven in sacrifice. This likewise means that what made Wen truly Wen—the Cultured King—and what makes Heaven truly Heaven are one. Thus it is clear that without civil virtue one cannot be associated with Heaven in sacrifice. Here we may discern the profound meaning of the Zhou people's establishment of ritual. When this meaning is understood, the way of benevolence and filial piety is complete, and the transforming influence of honoring one's elders and loving one's parents prevails. This is what the Master meant by saying, “Governing a state would be like looking at this”—his palm. Readers of the Book of Odes should grasp this for themselves.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In winter, in the twelfth month, the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen.” 〔Third year of Duke Yin〕
Qin Yanxu
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The commentaries explain the meaning of this topic only very briefly, and writers generally fall into superficiality. This essay's thought is lucid and graceful, yet rich and full; it profoundly grasps the Sage's aspiration to make the world a common possession.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The language and argument are imposing and rigorous.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Dignified, classically refined, and elegant.
The Spring and Autumn Annals condemns the feudal lords' pledging of good faith in order to record the impartiality of the Great Way. Here we see the Sage's aspiration to make all under Heaven a common possession. The pursuit of private interests through bilateral covenants began at Shimen; hence its condemnation in the Spring and Autumn Annals. I have heard that not recording ordinary occurrences is a rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals. The covenant at Shimen was also merely an ordinary occurrence: why, then, was it recorded? For reverence and trust prevailed in the time of Yu and Xia, standing so high that nothing could surpass them; but when proclamations and oaths first appeared under Shang and Zhou, already there was a gradual…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
薄矣况盟又豈盛世之事哉使齊鄭苟能以信
而相諭則斯盟也將焉用之徒以結援於鄭僖
謂不詔言於神將無以固其約矣而不知言不
由衷盟無益也徒欲致驩於宋莊謂不締交於
齊將無以遂其私矣而不知君子屢盟亂是用
長也是果王法之所得為乎聖人於此有感焉
蓋以于郲之盟蔑雖嘗惡之然猶以為自魯要
之爾天下未必其皆魯也今齊也鄭也乃特起
為斯役焉吾知今日離以二明日參以三而天
===
下之不為魯者無幾矣噫安得信孚於不言之
表使有虞之休風復見於今日邪于宋之盟宿
雖常病之然猶以為自隱欲之爾諸侯未必其
皆隱也今僖也莊也乃相率為斯舉焉將見爾
惟我詐我惟爾虞而諸侯之不為齊鄭者無幾
矣噫安得敬存於不令之餘而使有夏之善俗
不專美於前耶世道已衰也而以盛世期之人
心不古也而以古道望之三代之英雖未之逮
而大道之行則其所素志者矣故盟雖常事而
punctuated: 薄矣，况盟又豈盛世之事哉！使齊鄭苟能以信而相諭，則斯盟也，將焉用之？徒以結援於鄭，僖謂不詔言於神，將無以固其約矣，而不知言不由衷，盟無益也。徒欲致驩於宋，莊謂不締交於齊，將無以遂其私矣，而不知君子屢盟，亂是用長也。是果王法之所得為乎？聖人於此有感焉。蓋以于郲之盟蔑，雖嘗惡之，然猶以為自魯要之爾，天下未必其皆魯也。今齊也，鄭也，乃特起為斯役焉。吾知今日離以二，明日參以三，而天下之不為魯者無幾矣。噫！安得信孚於不言之表，使有虞之休風復見於今日邪？于宋之盟宿，雖常病之，然猶以為自隱欲之爾，諸侯未必其皆隱也。今僖也，莊也，乃相率為斯舉焉。將見爾惟我詐，我惟爾虞，而諸侯之不為齊鄭者無幾矣。噫！安得敬存於不令之餘，而使有夏之善俗不專美於前耶？世道已衰也，而以盛世期之；人心不古也，而以古道望之。三代之英雖未之逮，而大道之行則其所素志者矣。故盟雖常事，而
translation_en:
…had grown thin. How much less could covenants belong to an age of flourishing rule! If Qi and Zheng could truly reach mutual understanding through good faith, what use would they have for this covenant? Intent only on securing support from Zheng, Duke Xi thought that unless he proclaimed his words before the spirits, he could not make the agreement firm. He did not understand that when words do not come from the heart, a covenant is of no benefit. Intent only on winning the favor of Song, Duke Zhuang thought that unless he forged ties with Qi, he could not achieve his private ends. He did not understand that when gentlemen repeatedly swear covenants, disorder thereby grows. Could such conduct really be permitted under the laws of the true king? At this the Sage was moved.

As for the covenant at Mie involving Lai [?], although he had condemned it, he still considered that Lu alone had sought it; not everyone under Heaven would necessarily behave like Lu. Now Qi and Zheng had independently undertaken this business. I know that today they will join in pairs, tomorrow in threes, until few under Heaven will remain who do not behave like Lu. Alas! How might trust prevail beyond the need for words, so that the admirable ways of the age of Yu might appear again today?

As for the covenant with Song at Su, although he had always deplored it, he still considered that Duke Yin alone had desired it; not all the regional lords would necessarily behave like Yin. Now Duke Xi and Duke Zhuang had led one another into this undertaking. We shall see you deceiving me and me deceiving you, until few regional lords remain who do not behave like Qi and Zheng. Alas! How might reverence endure without the need for commands, so that the fine customs of Xia would no longer belong exclusively to the glorious past?

The ways of the world had already declined, yet he expected of it the flourishing rule of antiquity. Human hearts were no longer as in ancient times, yet he looked to them to follow the ancient Way. Although he had not attained the excellence of the Three Dynasties, the practice of the Great Way was what he had always aspired to. Thus, although covenants were commonplace affairs, …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
經必書之豈特爲齊鄭慮焉已哉抑論司盟周
制也孔子周人也以周人而變周制然則從周
之說非歟蓋聖人作春秋爲百王法其本則自
正人心始盟可惡也亦可革也雖變周之制何
惑焉是從周者遵時之義道以守經也變周者
復古之志道以達權也故曰聖人隨時變易以
從道又何相悖之有哉
衞人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕公會晉侯宋公
衞侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
===
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕
張文錦
同考試官教諭林批〔發揮二臣引過讓善典明切當經義之最優者〕
考試官教諭陳批〔清新〕
考試官教授王批〔蒼健〕
春秋以忠教天下而於過稱巳善稱君者有取
焉夫忠者人臣事君之道也衞晉之大夫有焉
punctuated:
經必書之，豈特爲齊鄭慮焉已哉？抑論司盟，周制也；孔子，周人也。以周人而變周制，然則從周之說非歟？蓋聖人作《春秋》，爲百王法，其本則自正人心始。盟可惡也，亦可革也，雖變周之制，何惑焉？是從周者，遵時之義，道以守經也；變周者，復古之志，道以達權也。故曰：「聖人隨時變易以從道。」又何相悖之有哉？

衞人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕。公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕。
張文錦
同考試官教諭林批〔發揮二臣引過讓善，典明切當，經義之最優者。〕
考試官教諭陳批〔清新。〕
考試官教授王批〔蒼健。〕

《春秋》以忠教天下，而於過稱巳、善稱君者有取焉。夫忠者，人臣事君之道也，衞、晉之大夫有焉。
translation_en:
…the Classic invariably records them. Could its concern have been merely for Qi and Zheng? Yet consider the office of Supervisor of Covenants: this was an institution of Zhou, and Confucius was a man of Zhou. If, as a man of Zhou, he altered Zhou institutions, was his declaration that he followed Zhou therefore wrong? The sage composed the Spring and Autumn Annals as a model for a hundred generations of kings, and its foundation lay in beginning by rectifying human hearts. Covenants were objectionable and could also be abolished. Even if this changed Zhou institutions, what grounds were there for doubt? Following Zhou expressed the duty to accord with one's times: through the Way, one upheld constant principles. Changing Zhou expressed the resolve to restore antiquity: through the Way, one exercised discretionary judgment. Thus it is said, “The sage changes with the times in order to follow the Way.” How could these courses contradict each other?

“The men of Wei came to Chen's rescue.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕 “The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
Zhang Wenjin
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Expounds how the two ministers took blame upon themselves and yielded credit to others; classically grounded and lucid [?], precise and apt—the finest of the essays on the meaning of the Classics.〕
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔Fresh and clear.〕
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔Vigorous and forceful.〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals teaches loyalty to all under Heaven, and commends those who ascribe faults to themselves and good deeds to their rulers. Loyalty is the way in which a minister serves his ruler; the grand officers of Wei and Jin possessed it…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
春秋得不取之以敎天下之爲人臣者乎粤自
匪躬之義微而凡便於身圖者苟有過也非惟
文之且將諉之矣求其引爲已責者誰歟吾於
衞得一人焉興救陳之師以干清丘之盟固孔
達之過亦衞侯之過也晉使之來岌岌乎社稷
之幾危矣達則曰先君之約不敢背也大國之
討不敢亢也一時辱國之罪毅然當之而不辭
惟知任其事而未常有其身所謂食焉而不避
其難者是矣傳曰過則稱已非孔達其誰與歸
===
耶自讓德之道喪而凡急於邀功者苟有善也
非惟伐之且將攘之矣求其推以與人者誰歟
吾於晉得一人焉成蕭魚之會以致鄭樂之歸
固魏絳之善亦晉侯之善也金石之賜藹藹乎
上下之胥慶矣絳則曰戎狄之和國之福也諸
侯之合君之靈也八年輔國之勳退然讓之而
不居惟知代其終而未嘗有其成所謂不敢貪
天功爲已力者是矣傳曰善則稱君非魏絳又
誰與歸耶于其引過於已也可以見忘已之公
punctuated:
《春秋》得不取之，以敎天下之爲人臣者乎？粤自匪躬之義微，而凡便於身圖者，苟有過也，非惟文之，且將諉之矣。求其引爲已責者，誰歟？吾於衞得一人焉。興救陳之師，以干清丘之盟，固孔達之過，亦衞侯之過也。晉使之來，岌岌乎社稷之幾危矣。達則曰：「先君之約，不敢背也；大國之討，不敢亢也。」一時辱國之罪，毅然當之而不辭，惟知任其事，而未常有其身，所謂食焉而不避其難者是矣。傳曰：「過則稱已。」非孔達，其誰與歸耶？

自讓德之道喪，而凡急於邀功者，苟有善也，非惟伐之，且將攘之矣。求其推以與人者，誰歟？吾於晉得一人焉。成蕭魚之會，以致鄭樂之歸，固魏絳之善，亦晉侯之善也。金石之賜，藹藹乎上下之胥慶矣。絳則曰：「戎狄之和，國之福也；諸侯之合，君之靈也。」八年輔國之勳，退然讓之而不居，惟知代其終，而未嘗有其成，所謂不敢貪天功爲已力者是矣。傳曰：「善則稱君。」非魏絳，又誰與歸耶？于其引過於已也，可以見忘已之公
translation_en:
…Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to commend them, thereby instructing all under Heaven who serve as ministers? Ever since the principle of disregarding oneself in service grew weak, those who scheme for their own advantage, whenever they commit a fault, not only cover it up but seek to shift the blame. Who among them accepts it as his own responsibility? In Wei I find one such man. Raising an army to rescue Chen, thereby violating the covenant of Qingqiu, was indeed the fault of Kong Da, but also that of the Marquis of Wei. When the envoy from Jin arrived, the state stood perilously close to ruin. Yet Kong Da said: “I dare not betray our former lord’s agreement; I dare not resist the great state’s punitive demand.” He resolutely accepted, without demur, the guilt of having disgraced his state on that occasion. He knew only to shoulder his responsibility, never to spare himself. He was what is meant by one who draws sustenance from a state and does not evade its dangers. The Commentary says: “For faults, take the blame oneself.” If not Kong Da, to whom could these words apply?

Ever since the way of yielding credit for virtue was lost, those eager to claim merit, whenever there is a good achievement, not only boast of it but seek to appropriate it. Who among them passes the credit to another? In Jin I find one such man. Bringing the meeting at Xiaoyu to a successful conclusion, and thereby securing the presentation of musicians from Zheng, was indeed the achievement of Wei Jiang, but also that of the Marquis of Jin. The gift of bells and sounding stones filled ruler and ministers alike with shared rejoicing. Yet Wei Jiang said: “Peace with the Rong and Di is the good fortune of the state; the union of the feudal lords is due to my lord’s numinous power.” He modestly yielded the credit for eight years of service to the state, claiming none for himself. He knew only to bring the work to completion on his ruler’s behalf, never to claim its success as his own. He was what is meant by one who dares not covet Heaven’s accomplishment and call it his own effort. The Commentary says: “For good achievements, credit the ruler.” If not Wei Jiang, to whom else could these words apply? In taking faults upon oneself, one may discern the impartiality of self-forgetfulness…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉于其推善於君也可以見尊君之義焉春秋
於二子均之有取焉其所以作臣之忠者何其
至哉噫此華元子反不明人臣之義而擅平上
之功所以不免聖人之惡也巳雖然孔達棄信
罪固不可得而辭矣用人以至於誤國伊誰之
咎歟若魏絳相君之功固云偉矣及其辭樂又
曰抑臣願君安其樂而思其終頌不忘規非賢
而能之乎以此而觀則晋悼之賞不廢典其賢
於衞穆成勞之報也遠矣
===
禮記
禮樂順天地之情達神明之德降興上下
之神而凝是精粗之體領父子君臣之
節是故大人舉禮樂則天地將爲昭焉
徐雱
考試官敎諭陳批禮樂合造化與賛化之妙極
難形容此作得旨而詞氣渾融可以觀所養矣
考試官敎授王批通暢
記者極言禮樂之妙而因著聖人之賛化也蓋
punctuated:
焉。于其推善於君也，可以見尊君之義焉。《春秋》於二子均之有取焉，其所以作臣之忠者何其至哉！噫！此華元、子反不明人臣之義，而擅平上之功，所以不免聖人之惡也巳。雖然，孔達棄信，罪固不可得而辭矣；用人以至於誤國，伊誰之咎歟？若魏絳相君之功，固云偉矣。及其辭樂，又曰：「抑臣願君安其樂而思其終。」頌不忘規，非賢而能之乎？以此而觀，則晋悼之賞不廢典，其賢於衞穆成勞之報也遠矣。

《禮記》
「禮樂順天地之情，達神明之德，降興上下之神，而凝是精粗之體，領父子君臣之節。是故大人舉禮樂，則天地將爲昭焉。」
徐雱

考試官敎諭陳批：「禮樂合造化與賛化之妙，極難形容。此作得旨，而詞氣渾融，可以觀所養矣。」
考試官敎授王批：「通暢。」

記者極言禮樂之妙，而因著聖人之賛化也。蓋
translation_en:
…therein. In his crediting his ruler with good deeds, one can discern the righteousness of honoring the ruler. The Spring and Autumn Annals finds something commendable in both men: how fully it seeks to foster loyalty in ministers! Alas! Hua Yuan and Zifan failed to understand the duties of a minister and arrogated to themselves their rulers’ credit for making peace [?]; hence they could not escape the Sage’s condemnation. Nevertheless, Kong Da broke faith, and certainly could not disclaim his guilt. But whose fault was it to employ someone to the point of bringing harm upon the state? As for Wei Jiang, his achievements in assisting his ruler were indeed great. When declining the gift of music, he further said: “Yet your servant wishes that you, my lord, may enjoy this music in peace while considering how matters will end.” To praise without forgetting to admonish—could anyone but a worthy man accomplish this? Seen in this light, Duke Dao of Jin observed the established norms in bestowing his reward; he far surpassed Duke Mu of Wei in rewarding accomplished service.

Book of Rites
“Rites and music accord with the dispositions of Heaven and Earth, give expression to the potency of the spirits, bring down and raise up the spirits above and below, consolidate the forms of the subtle and the gross, and regulate the proper relations between father and son, ruler and minister. Thus, when the great man puts rites and music into practice, Heaven and Earth will become manifest.”
Xu Pang

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The subtle workings through which rites and music accord with creation and assist its transforming processes are exceedingly difficult to describe. This composition grasps their purport, and its language and spirit form a harmonious whole. From it one can discern the author’s self-cultivation.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Clear and fluent.”

The writer of the Record describes to the fullest the subtle workings of rites and music, thereby revealing how the sage assists the transforming processes of creation. For…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂與造化相爲流通也聖人舉之而化昭焉
不可以其爲用之妙哉今夫禮樂之在天下也
固能管乎人情矣然豈儀文聲容之謂乎蓋嘗
有以觀其深矣彼天地之情廣大而不可象此
其俲之蓋兩儀肇和序之端而同和同節者成
其能也神明之德微妙而不可測此其達之蓋
屈伸秘藏用之機而敦和別宜者顯諸仁也通
乎幽明之故而和敬之感孚則上下之神昭格
矣貫乎道器之全而制作之大備則精粗之體
===
凝會矣紀綱人道之大端而合情飾貌之下父
子君臣之節所由領矣是蓋禮樂之妙用所該
雖甚廣要皆造化之事也然則欲贊化育之道
舍禮樂其何以哉是故大人有見於此則必仰
觀俯察處至序以制禮而經曲之悉備有以昭
著其散殊之文玩至和以作樂而情文之兼該
有以發揚其不息之妙無聲無體之呈露固成
象成形者之所由彰也凡夫氣化之未周者將
自此以幽贊之矣極和極順之顯設固竝育竝
punctuated: 禮樂與造化相爲流通也，聖人舉之而化昭焉，不可以其爲用之妙哉？今夫禮樂之在天下也，固能管乎人情矣，然豈儀文聲容之謂乎？蓋嘗有以觀其深矣。彼天地之情，廣大而不可象，此其俲之，蓋兩儀肇和序之端，而同和同節者成其能也。神明之德，微妙而不可測，此其達之，蓋屈伸秘藏用之機，而敦和別宜者顯諸仁也。通乎幽明之故，而和敬之感孚，則上下之神昭格矣；貫乎道器之全，而制作之大備，則精粗之體凝會矣；紀綱人道之大端，而合情飾貌之下，父子君臣之節所由領矣。是蓋禮樂之妙用所該，雖甚廣，要皆造化之事也。然則欲贊化育之道，舍禮樂其何以哉？是故大人有見於此，則必仰觀俯察，處至序以制禮，而經曲之悉備，有以昭著其散殊之文；玩至和以作樂，而情文之兼該，有以發揚其不息之妙。無聲無體之呈露，固成象成形者之所由彰也。凡夫氣化之未周者，將自此以幽贊之矣。極和極順之顯設，固竝育竝
translation_en: …ritual and music communicate reciprocally with the creative transformations of the cosmos. When the sage puts them into practice, those transformations become manifest. Can this not be attributed to the wondrous efficacy of their operation [?]? Now ritual and music in the world can assuredly govern human feelings. Yet could this refer merely to ceremonial forms and the sounds and gestures of performance? Let us examine their deeper significance. The inherent dispositions of Heaven and Earth are vast and cannot be represented in images; ritual and music emulate them. Heaven and Earth initiate harmony and order, while those who share in their harmony and measure bring their capacities to fulfillment. The power of spiritual beings is subtle and unfathomable; ritual and music give it expression. Contraction and expansion conceal the workings of latent efficacy, while those who foster harmony and distinguish what is fitting manifest it through benevolence. When the principles of the unseen and visible realms are penetrated, and the influence of harmony and reverence inspires a response, the spirits above and below arrive in manifest presence. When the Way and concrete things are comprehended in their entirety, and the great work of instituting ritual and music is complete, the subtle and gross aspects of existence coalesce. When the cardinal principles of human relationships are ordered, through bringing feelings into accord and giving outward conduct its proper form, the distinctions between father and son and between ruler and minister are thereby governed. Thus, although the wondrous operation of ritual and music embraces an exceedingly broad range, all of it ultimately concerns cosmic creation and transformation. If one wishes to assist the process of transformation and nurture, then, what means could there be apart from ritual and music? Therefore, the great man, perceiving this, must observe above and investigate below. Grounding himself in the utmost order, he establishes ritual; with its general principles and detailed prescriptions fully provided, he makes manifest its patterns of differentiation. Contemplating the utmost harmony, he creates music; embracing both inward feeling and outward form, he gives expression to its ceaseless wonders. The disclosure of what has neither sound nor bodily form is precisely what makes manifest that which takes on images and shapes. Wherever transformation through vital energy has not fully reached, ritual and music will henceforth lend it unseen assistance. The manifest establishment of consummate harmony and consummate accord is indeed the means by which things are nurtured together and …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
行之所由宣也凡夫玄工之不逮者將緣是以
默助之矣夫天地之化育必禮樂以昭宣如此
則天地且不能違矣而况於人乎此其所以能
管乎人情也雖然制作者其具也中和者其本
也天子能建中和之極則至樂無聲而天下化
至禮不讓而天下治雖無制作亦可也苟為無
本則雖欲盡制抑末矣其如禮樂何哉而又何
治情宣化之足云故程子謂禮樂只是和序其
亦探本之論與
===
百官得其宜萬事得其序
徐雱
考試官敎授王批規格俊雅而意更明暢讀之
令人躍然
考試官敎諭陳批典雅切實
用人行政之皆善人君養盛所致也夫治天下
有本身之謂也今人無可適而政無可間其君
正莫不正乎記者之意若曰君身為萬化之原
朝廷立四方之極故觀天子之德配天地而可
punctuated:
行之所由宣也，凡夫玄工之不逮者，將緣是以默助之矣。夫天地之化育，必禮樂以昭宣如此，則天地且不能違矣，而况於人乎？此其所以能管乎人情也。雖然，制作者其具也，中和者其本也。天子能建中和之極，則至樂無聲而天下化，至禮不讓而天下治，雖無制作亦可也。苟為無本，則雖欲盡制，抑末矣，其如禮樂何哉？而又何治情宣化之足云？故程子謂禮樂只是和序，其亦探本之論與？

百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
徐雱
考試官敎授王批：規格俊雅，而意更明暢，讀之令人躍然。
考試官敎諭陳批：典雅切實。

用人行政之皆善，人君養盛所致也。夫治天下有本，身之謂也。今人無可適，而政無可間，其君正，莫不正乎？記者之意若曰：君身為萬化之原，朝廷立四方之極。故觀天子之德配天地，而可
translation_en:
… are thereby enabled to proceed together. Wherever the mysterious workings of creation fall short, these will silently assist them. If the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth require rites and music to make them manifest in this way, then even Heaven and Earth cannot contravene them, much less human beings. This is why they can govern human feelings. Yet institutional forms are their instruments; centrality and harmony are their foundation. If the Son of Heaven can establish the highest standard of centrality and harmony, then perfect music, without sound, transforms all under Heaven, and perfect ritual, without acts of deference, brings order to all under Heaven. Even without instituting forms, this would be possible. If the foundation is lacking, however, even an attempt to institute every form would concern only the branches. What could this accomplish for rites and music? How could one even speak of regulating feelings and spreading transformation? Thus Master Cheng said that rites and music are simply harmony and order. Is this not also a judgment that probes their foundation?

“All officials obtain their proper places, and all affairs attain their proper order.”
Xu Pang 徐雱
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “The structure is accomplished and elegant, and the meaning still more lucid and fluent. Reading it makes one’s spirits leap.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Classically elegant, pertinent, and substantial.”

That both the employment of men and the conduct of government are good results from the ruler’s fully developed self-cultivation. Governing all under Heaven has a foundation: the ruler’s own person. Now, if no fault can be found with those employed [?], and no criticism made of the administration, is this not because, when the ruler is upright, none fail to be upright? The recorder’s meaning seems to be this: the ruler’s person is the source of all transformation, and the court establishes the standard for the four quarters. Thus, observing that the Son of Heaven’s virtue matches Heaven and Earth, one can …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以知化理之周矣彼先王設官分職以佐天下
之治固嘗建百官矣未易使之皆宜也今天子
隨在養德則元首之明自足以端股肱之則度
德叙位而百僚效靖共之節因能授任而多士
輸勵翼之誠以之登庸廊廟而為邇臣與必能
寅亮弘化而足以承事一人也以之服采邦國
而為遠臣與必能綜理庶務而足以宣力四方
也蓋人臣本有當然之分而又得明君以表儀
之夫固各盡其當然而協諸義矣百官孰有不
===
宜者乎先王敷典成務以盡天下之蹟固嘗有
萬事矣未易使之皆序也今天子養德之備則
元首之明自足以致庶事之康推行以漸貞百
度而有常施為當可熙庶績而不亂以大綱則
舉焉正體統而建之為維皇之極者昭如也以
萬目則張焉脩紀法而敷之為下土之式者秩
如也蓋政事本有自然之等而又得明君以總
攬之夫固各循其自然而歸諸理矣萬事孰有
不序者乎夫百官得宜則任官惟賢而事益理
punctuated:
以知化理之周矣。彼先王設官分職，以佐天下之治，固嘗建百官矣，未易使之皆宜也。今天子隨在養德，則元首之明自足以端股肱之則。度德叙位，而百僚效靖共之節；因能授任，而多士輸勵翼之誠。以之登庸廊廟而為邇臣與，必能寅亮弘化，而足以承事一人也；以之服采邦國而為遠臣與，必能綜理庶務，而足以宣力四方也。蓋人臣本有當然之分，而又得明君以表儀之，夫固各盡其當然而協諸義矣。百官孰有不宜者乎？
先王敷典成務，以盡天下之蹟，固嘗有萬事矣，未易使之皆序也。今天子養德之備，則元首之明自足以致庶事之康。推行以漸，貞百度而有常；施為當可，熙庶績而不亂。以大綱則舉焉，正體統而建之為維皇之極者昭如也；以萬目則張焉，脩紀法而敷之為下土之式者秩如也。蓋政事本有自然之等，而又得明君以總攬之，夫固各循其自然而歸諸理矣。萬事孰有不序者乎？夫百官得宜，則任官惟賢而事益理
translation_en:
…one may thereby know how comprehensive his transforming influence and governance are. The former kings established offices and apportioned duties to assist in governing all under Heaven. They certainly instituted the various offices, yet ensuring that all were fittingly filled was no easy matter. Now, when the Son of Heaven cultivates virtue in every circumstance, the discernment of the head is itself sufficient to set right the standards of his ministers, his limbs. He assesses virtue and assigns rank, and the assembled officials demonstrate their steadfast, respectful devotion; he entrusts responsibilities according to ability, and the many officers offer their sincere efforts in his support. When he advances them to service at court as ministers close to him, they can assuredly assist him with reverence and extend his transforming influence, adequately serving the One Man. When he employs them in the domains as ministers far from him, they can assuredly manage the many affairs of government and exert themselves in service throughout the realm. Ministers inherently have duties proper to their stations; with an enlightened ruler also setting them an example, each fully discharges what he ought to do and accords with righteousness. Which of the officials, then, would fail to be fittingly placed?
The former kings promulgated statutes and accomplished their tasks, bringing the undertakings of all under Heaven to completion. They certainly had myriad affairs to attend to, yet ensuring that all were ordered was no easy matter. Now, when the Son of Heaven is complete in his cultivation of virtue, the discernment of the head is itself sufficient to bring all affairs to a sound condition. Measures are implemented gradually, setting the many institutions right and giving them constancy; actions suit their circumstances, bringing the many undertakings to flourishing accomplishment without disorder. The main cord of the net is raised: the proper ordering of government is rectified and established as the sovereign’s supreme standard, clear for all to see. Its myriad meshes are spread: regulations and laws are put in order and promulgated as models for the lands below, each in its proper sequence. Government affairs inherently have their natural gradations; with an enlightened ruler also overseeing them as a whole, each follows its natural course and accords with principle. Which of the myriad affairs, then, would fail to be ordered? When all officials are fittingly placed, only the worthy are appointed to office, and affairs become increasingly well governed…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬事得序則位事惟能而官益勸此其相須以
有成而天子之所以治天下參天地也與雖然
養德在君而所以成君之德者又在臣也蓋人
臣能將順匡救而使吾君動皆合宜行已有序
則禮義全而君德備所以贊化育而參天地者
亦自我得之矣否則君心不正則非禮之禮非
義之義日滋也其如用人行政何噫孟子有格
君心之責望大人其意微矣
第貳場
===
論
爲天下國家有九經
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批九經之要本在一誠誠卽人之
生理而爲仁此天人一貫之道也促作獨能發之其眞
探本之論歟
考試官敎諭陳批見理精徹立論古雅
考試官敎授王批議論正大
人君有天下國家之責必欲有以治之非可以
punctuated:
萬事得序，則位事惟能而官益勸。此其相須以有成，而天子之所以治天下、參天地也與！雖然，養德在君，而所以成君之德者又在臣也。蓋人臣能將順匡救，而使吾君動皆合宜，行已有序，則禮義全而君德備，所以贊化育而參天地者，亦自我得之矣。否則，君心不正，則非禮之禮、非義之義日滋也，其如用人行政何？噫！孟子有格君心之責望大人，其意微矣！

第貳場

論

爲天下國家有九經

彭啓忠

同考試官學正鐵批：九經之要，本在一誠。誠卽人之生理而爲仁，此天人一貫之道也。促作獨能發之，其眞探本之論歟！

考試官敎諭陳批：見理精徹，立論古雅。

考試官敎授王批：議論正大。

人君有天下國家之責，必欲有以治之，非可以
translation_en:
…When all affairs are properly ordered, only the capable are assigned duties, and officials are further encouraged to exert themselves. These two conditions depend on each other for their realization: surely this is how the Son of Heaven governs all under Heaven and forms a triad with Heaven and Earth! Nevertheless, cultivating virtue rests with the ruler, while bringing the ruler’s virtue to completion rests also with his ministers. If ministers support what is good in him and correct and remedy his faults, ensuring that every action of their ruler is appropriate and his conduct is orderly, then ritual propriety and righteousness will be complete, and the ruler’s virtue fully developed. The means of assisting the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth, and forming a triad with them, will thus also derive from us. Otherwise, if the ruler’s heart is not upright, purported propriety that is no propriety and purported righteousness that is no righteousness will multiply daily. What then can be done about appointing men and administering government? Ah! Mencius expected great men to shoulder the responsibility of rectifying the ruler’s heart. Profound indeed was his meaning!

Second Session

Discourse

“There Are Nine Guiding Principles for Governing All under Heaven, States, and Families”

Peng Qizhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Tie, Instructor of a Departmental Confucian School: The essentials of the nine guiding principles are rooted in sincerity alone. Sincerity is the generative principle of human life and constitutes benevolence: this is the Way that runs throughout Heaven and humanity. This composition [?] alone succeeds in bringing it to light. Is this not truly a discourse that probes the root?

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor of a County Confucian School: His perception of principle is precise and penetrating; his argument is classically elegant.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor of a Prefectural Confucian School: The argument is upright and broad in scope.

A ruler bears responsibility for all under Heaven, the state, and the family, and must seek the means to govern them. This cannot be accomplished by…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
徒法為也亦惟道之本諸身者運之而已矣古
今之言治者必曰道道固未有不出乎身者出
乎身而施之家推之國達之天下雖行之萬世
而不易可也斯則經之所由名也經即道也道
一而已矣而曰九經自為天下國家言也是故
由吾身以及于家國天下曰脩身也尊賢也親
親也敬大臣也體羣臣也子庶民也來百工也
柔遠人也懷諸侯也以天下國家而約之吾身
則曰所以行之者一也此夫子告魯哀公之言
===
雖所以推廣文武之政而實所以立萬世君道
之準也今夫人君一身至寡也天下國家至大
也天下國家之人至眾也賢者親者大臣羣臣
庶民百工遠人諸侯其所以取足于我者又紛
然至不一也以至寡之身握至大之勢御至眾
之人而欲一其至不一之情豈智術法令之所
能為哉無亦因其自有之理而我有以應之因
其各足之分而我有以與之而已必我有以應
之與之而後可則不求諸身而求諸天下國家
punctuated:
徒法為也，亦惟道之本諸身者運之而已矣。古今之言治者必曰道，道固未有不出乎身者。出乎身而施之家，推之國，達之天下，雖行之萬世而不易可也。斯則經之所由名也。經即道也，道一而已矣，而曰九經，自為天下國家言也。是故，由吾身以及于家國天下，曰脩身也，尊賢也，親親也，敬大臣也，體羣臣也，子庶民也，來百工也，柔遠人也，懷諸侯也。以天下國家而約之吾身，則曰「所以行之者一也」。此夫子告魯哀公之言，雖所以推廣文武之政，而實所以立萬世君道之準也。

今夫人君一身至寡也，天下國家至大也，天下國家之人至眾也。賢者、親者、大臣、羣臣、庶民、百工、遠人、諸侯，其所以取足于我者，又紛然至不一也。以至寡之身，握至大之勢，御至眾之人，而欲一其至不一之情，豈智術法令之所能為哉？無亦因其自有之理，而我有以應之；因其各足之分，而我有以與之而已。必我有以應之、與之而後可，則不求諸身而求諸天下國家，
translation_en:
…be accomplished by laws alone; it requires only putting into operation the Way that is rooted in one’s own person. Those who have spoken of government, past and present, invariably speak of the Way, and the Way has never failed to proceed from one’s own person. Proceeding from oneself, it is applied to the family, extended to the state, and carried throughout the world. It may be practiced for ten thousand generations without alteration. This is why these principles are called constant norms. Constant norms are simply the Way, and the Way is one. Yet they are called the nine constant norms when considered in terms of governing the world, the state, and the family. Thus, proceeding from oneself to the family, the state, and the world, they are: cultivating oneself; honoring the worthy; cherishing one’s kin; respecting the great ministers; showing consideration for the assembled officials; treating the common people as one’s children; attracting the various artisans; treating people from afar with gentleness; and cherishing the feudal lords.
