Truth and falsehood became so confused that they could no longer be disentangled. The men of Qin then took advantage of this, and the calamity of burying scholars and burning books arose. Can the blame for this be laid solely upon…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
咎乎秦皇哉則諸儒恣辯博而忘反約之
過也漢興懲亡秦之敝除挾書之律然干
戈甫釋表章未遑迄乎孝武廣求異書而
嗣世相承崇重經籍於是劉歆總羣書而
奏七略曰輯略曰六藝略曰諸子略曰詩
賦略曰兵書略曰術數略曰方技略條貫
粲然固西京之選也而猶有遺議者以六
經聖人之至教而歆迺次之於輯略則非
矣光武中興篤好文雅而明章繼軌敦尚
===
儒術於是班固傅毅等依七略而為書部
自輯略而六藝略以至方技略舊貫昭然
亦東京之盛也而猶有遺憾者以間有七
略之所無而班氏迺益之以已見則躓矣
降自晉魏隋陳之間雖時代更異趣舎不
倫而好事之君慕古之士亦未甞不以撰
述為意故縹囊緗帙采遺亡於秘書寶軸
錦標函圖籍於別殿誠更僕未易數也以
宋梁言之王儉撰七志於武帝之世如曰
punctuated:
咎乎秦皇哉？則諸儒恣辯博而忘反約之過也。漢興，懲亡秦之敝，除挾書之律。然干戈甫釋，表章未遑。迄乎孝武，廣求異書，而嗣世相承，崇重經籍。於是劉歆總羣書而奏《七略》，曰輯略，曰六藝略，曰諸子略，曰詩賦略，曰兵書略，曰術數略，曰方技略，條貫粲然，固西京之選也。而猶有遺議者，以六經聖人之至教，而歆迺次之於輯略，則非矣。

光武中興，篤好文雅，而明、章繼軌，敦尚儒術。於是班固、傅毅等依《七略》而為書部，自輯略而六藝略，以至方技略，舊貫昭然，亦東京之盛也。而猶有遺憾者，以間有《七略》之所無，而班氏迺益之以已見，則躓矣。

降自晉魏隋陳之間，雖時代更異，趣舎不倫，而好事之君、慕古之士，亦未甞不以撰述為意。故縹囊緗帙，采遺亡於秘書；寶軸錦標，函圖籍於別殿，誠更僕未易數也。以宋梁言之，王儉撰《七志》於武帝之世，如曰
translation_en:
…blame the Qin emperor alone? It was also the fault of the scholars, who indulged in wide-ranging disputation and forgot to return to essentials. When the Han arose, it took warning from the abuses of fallen Qin and abolished the statute prohibiting possession of books. Yet warfare had only just ceased, and there had been no leisure to bring learning into prominence. Under Emperor Xiaowu, unusual books were sought far and wide, and succeeding generations continued to honor the classics and other writings. Liu Xin then surveyed the collected books and submitted the Seven Summaries (Qilüe): the General Summary, the Summary of the Six Arts, the Summary of the Masters, the Summary of Poetry and Rhapsodies, the Summary of Military Writings, the Summary of Numbers and Techniques, and the Summary of Medical and Other Practical Arts. Its organization was brilliantly clear: it was indeed an outstanding achievement of the Western Han. Yet grounds for criticism remained. The Six Classics contain the sages’ highest teachings, and Xin was wrong to place them after the General Summary.

When Guangwu restored the dynasty, he devoted himself to refined learning; Emperors Ming and Zhang followed his example and earnestly esteemed Confucian learning. Ban Gu, Fu Yi, and others accordingly organized books into divisions following the Seven Summaries. From the General Summary to the Summary of the Six Arts, and on through the Summary of Medical and Other Practical Arts, the old arrangement was clearly preserved. This too was a flourishing achievement of the Eastern Han. Yet grounds for regret remained: there were occasional items absent from the Seven Summaries, and Ban stumbled by supplementing it with his own views [?].

Coming down through the times of Jin, Wei, Sui, and Chen, although the ages changed and preferences differed, rulers eager to undertake such projects and scholars who admired antiquity always took an interest in compilation and writing. Thus, with pale-blue book bags and light-yellow wrappers, they gathered lost writings into the palace collections; with precious scroll rollers and brocade labels, they stored maps and books in subsidiary palace halls. Truly, even if one changed attendants while recounting them, they could scarcely all be enumerated. Taking Song and Liang as examples, Wang Jian compiled the Seven Classifications (Qizhi) in the reign of Emperor Wu, with headings such as…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
經典曰諸子曰文翰曰軍書曰陰陽曰術
藝曰圖譜是已阮孝緒著七錄於普通之
中如曰經典曰記傳曰子兵曰文集曰技
術曰佛錄曰道錄是已之二子者遞相祖
述整比卷帙非不自附於作者之林也而
一病於文義之淺近一病於辭義之割裂
例之兩漢風斯下矣況於聖經乎以唐宋
言之玄宗命殷踐猷等脩羣書四部爰別
經史子集之名仁宗命王堯臣等作崇文
===
總目悉倣開元四部之例之諸臣者分曹
綜緝甄明科部非不馳聲於翰墨之苑也
而唐則失之浩繁宋則失之缺略方之宋
梁且未優矣況於史漢乎由是觀之六經
脩於仲尼厄於秦火即得之屋壁所藏口
耳所授者其不絕如綫爾漢唐宋諸書連
篇累帙藏在石室播之寰宇固宜家傳而
人誦之矣鄭夾漈氏迺謂秦人焚書而書
存而歐陽永叔所見唐四庫書目百不存
punctuated: 經典、曰諸子、曰文翰、曰軍書、曰陰陽、曰術藝、曰圖譜，是已。阮孝緒著《七錄》於普通之中，如曰經典、曰記傳、曰子兵、曰文集、曰技術、曰佛錄、曰道錄，是已。之二子者，遞相祖述，整比卷帙，非不自附於作者之林也，而一病於文義之淺近，一病於辭義之割裂。例之兩漢，風斯下矣，況於聖經乎？以唐宋言之，玄宗命殷踐猷等脩羣書四部，爰別經史子集之名；仁宗命王堯臣等作《崇文總目》，悉倣開元四部之例。之諸臣者，分曹綜緝，甄明科部，非不馳聲於翰墨之苑也，而唐則失之浩繁，宋則失之缺略。方之宋梁，且未優矣，況於史漢乎？由是觀之，六經脩於仲尼，厄於秦火，即得之屋壁所藏、口耳所授者，其不絕如綫爾。漢唐宋諸書，連篇累帙，藏在石室，播之寰宇，固宜家傳而人誦之矣。鄭夾漈氏迺謂秦人焚書而書存，而歐陽永叔所見唐四庫書目，百不存
translation_en:
…the Classics, the Masters, Literary Writings, Military Writings, Yin and Yang, Technical Arts, and Charts and Genealogies: these were the categories. Ruan Xiaoxu compiled the Seven Catalogues (Qi lu) during the Putong era, with such categories as the Classics, Records and Biographies, Masters and Military Writings, Literary Collections, Technical Arts, Buddhist Writings, and Daoist Writings. These two men successively followed earlier models, arranging and collating volumes. It was not that they failed to claim a place among authors; yet one work suffered from shallowness in its textual treatment and meaning, the other from fragmentation of wording and meaning. Compared with the works of the two Han dynasties, their scholarly standards had declined—how much more so compared with the sages’ Classics!

As for the Tang and Song, Emperor Xuanzong ordered Yin Jianyou and others to arrange the collected books into four divisions, distinguishing the categories of Classics, Histories, Masters, and Literary Collections. Emperor Renzong ordered Wang Yaochen and others to compile the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Institute for the Veneration of Literature (Chongwen zongmu), following throughout the precedent of the four divisions of the Kaiyuan era. These officials divided their responsibilities, gathered and compiled the material, and discriminated clearly among its categories and divisions. It was not that they failed to win renown in the literary world; yet the Tang compilation erred through excessive bulk, and the Song compilation through omissions and undue abbreviation. They were not even superior to those of the Song and Liang dynasties—how much less to the Records of the Grand Historian and the History of the Han!

Viewed in this light, the Six Classics were edited by Zhongni [Confucius] and suffered the calamity of the Qin fires. Even the texts recovered from hiding places within house walls or transmitted orally maintained a continuity as tenuous as a thread. The writings of the Han, Tang, and Song, by contrast, extended through countless chapters and volumes, were preserved in stone chambers, and circulated throughout the realm. Surely they should have been handed down in every household and recited by everyone. Yet Zheng Jiaji said that the people of Qin burned books, but the books survived, whereas, of the books in the catalogue of the Tang’s Four Repositories seen by Ouyang Yongshu, out of a hundred there did not survive…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
一焉者豈無其故乎夫六經者聖人傳心
之書也統括羣聖包舉造化易以道吾心
之時書以道吾心之中而詩則道吾心之
性情也禮以道吾心之敬樂以道吾心之
和而春秋則道吾心之是非也文發於心
經傳於後百家同指千古不磨夫繁星至
難數計矣而求之天則明衆流匪可涯測
矣而歸之海則一然則六經者羣書之天
與海也其不亡於秦燼也宜哉歷代典籍
===
皆掇拾以爲考訂之具也勦襲往緒罔知
取裁以采掇爲工者則極意於蒐羅而碔
砆美玉莫辨焉以幷蓄爲富者則取盈於
箱篋而魯魚亥豕莫稽焉言不由衷行之
不遠匪直災木且資覆瓿昔有寶敝帚而
鬻之以千金者卒忘其帚之敝也宋人寶
燕石以爲玉而藏之華匱者旣發藏迺知
其燕石也然則藝文志者歷代之敝帚燕
石爾其不傳於世也有由哉嗟乎千聖一
punctuated: 一焉者，豈無其故乎？夫六經者，聖人傳心之書也。統括羣聖，包舉造化。易以道吾心之時，書以道吾心之中，而詩則道吾心之性情也。禮以道吾心之敬，樂以道吾心之和，而春秋則道吾心之是非也。文發於心，經傳於後，百家同指，千古不磨。夫繁星至難數計矣，而求之天則明；衆流匪可涯測矣，而歸之海則一。然則六經者，羣書之天與海也。其不亡於秦燼也，宜哉！歷代典籍，皆掇拾以爲考訂之具也。勦襲往緒，罔知取裁。以采掇爲工者，則極意於蒐羅，而碔砆美玉莫辨焉；以幷蓄爲富者，則取盈於箱篋，而魯魚亥豕莫稽焉。言不由衷，行之不遠，匪直災木，且資覆瓿。昔有寶敝帚而鬻之以千金者，卒忘其帚之敝也。宋人寶燕石以爲玉而藏之華匱者，旣發藏，迺知其燕石也。然則藝文志者，歷代之敝帚燕石爾。其不傳於世也，有由哉！嗟乎！千聖一
translation_en:
…even one [in a hundred surviving]—could there be no reason for this? The Six Classics are books through which the sages transmit their minds. They encompass all the sages and embrace the workings of creation. The Changes expresses our mind’s responsiveness to the proper time; the Documents expresses our mind’s balanced center; and the Odes expresses our mind’s nature and feelings. The Rites expresses our mind’s reverence; the Music expresses our mind’s harmony; and the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses our mind’s judgments of right and wrong. Their writings issue from the mind, and the classics are transmitted to later generations. The hundred schools share their purport, which remains undiminished through the ages. The myriad stars are exceedingly difficult to count, yet when sought in Heaven they are clear; the many streams cannot be measured to their limits, yet when they return to the sea they become one. Thus the Six Classics are the Heaven and sea of all books. How fitting that they did not perish in the ashes of Qin!

The writings of successive dynasties are all gathered piecemeal to serve as materials for examination and verification. They plagiarize the remnants of earlier works, without knowing how to select and judge. Those who regard compilation as their craft devote all their efforts to collecting, yet cannot distinguish jade-like stone from fine jade. Those who regard indiscriminate accumulation as wealth fill their chests and cases, yet cannot check errors that confuse lu with yu or hai with shi. Words that do not issue from the heart do not travel far. Such writings do more than bring ruin upon wood: they furnish covers for jars. Once there was someone who treasured a worn-out broom and offered it for a thousand pieces of gold, altogether forgetting that his broom was worn out. A man of Song treasured a stone from Yan as jade and stored it in an ornate casket; only after opening his hoard did he discover that it was a stone from Yan. Thus the bibliographical treatises are merely the worn-out brooms and stones from Yan of successive dynasties. There is indeed a reason why their contents have not been transmitted to posterity! Alas! The thousand sages share one…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
道千人一心學者不求之載籍而求之六
經不求之六經之迹而求之作經者之心
窮理以明之居敬以養之弗襍於聲色貨
利之私弗遷於紛華波蕩之感養吾心之
時中卽羲畫未陳墳典未述而易與書固
在也養吾心之和敬卽經曲未制聲容未
作而禮與樂固在也養吾心之是非與性
情則風雅頌之未起褒貶予奪之未彰而
詩與春秋固在也心存則道得道得則文
===
自生以之述作可以翼經而垂訓以之遠
覽可以考古而信今而學之能事畢矣易
曰君子多識前言往行以畜其德軻書曰
君子博學而詳說之將以反說約也愚生
誦法孔孟而漢唐宋所不敢知者故有味
於反約之說執事其以爲何如
第四問
梁岱
同考試官教諭梁批評品往哲如持權衡以較輕重
punctuated:
道，千人一心。學者不求之載籍，而求之六經；不求之六經之迹，而求之作經者之心。窮理以明之，居敬以養之，弗襍於聲色貨利之私，弗遷於紛華波蕩之感。養吾心之時中，卽羲畫未陳、墳典未述，而《易》與《書》固在也；養吾心之和敬，卽經曲未制、聲容未作，而《禮》與《樂》固在也；養吾心之是非與性情，則風雅頌之未起、褒貶予奪之未彰，而《詩》與《春秋》固在也。心存則道得，道得則文自生。以之述作，可以翼經而垂訓；以之遠覽，可以考古而信今，而學之能事畢矣。《易》曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」軻書曰：「君子博學而詳說之，將以反說約也。」愚生誦法孔孟，而漢唐宋所不敢知者，故有味於反約之說。執事其以爲何如？

第四問
梁岱
同考試官教諭梁批：「評品往哲，如持權衡以較輕重。」
translation_en:
…Way; a thousand people share one heart. Students should seek it not in the accumulated writings, but in the Six Classics; not in the traces preserved in the Six Classics, but in the hearts of those who composed them. They should investigate principle to illuminate their hearts and abide in reverence to nurture them, allowing neither the selfish desires for sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit to contaminate them, nor the unsettling allure of worldly splendor to sway them. If I nurture my heart’s capacity to attain the mean appropriate to each moment, then even before Fu Xi’s diagrams were set forth or the ancient canonical writings composed, the Changes and the Documents are already present within it. If I nurture harmony and reverence in my heart, then even before the overarching rules and detailed prescriptions of ritual were established, or music and ceremonial deportment devised, the Rites and the Music are already present within it. If I nurture my heart’s discernment of right and wrong, its nature and feelings, then even before the Airs, Odes, and Hymns arose, or praise and blame, approval and disapproval were made manifest, the Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals are already present within it. When the heart is preserved, the Way is attained; when the Way is attained, literary expression arises of itself. Applied to composition, this can supplement the Classics and transmit instruction to posterity; applied to wide-ranging reading, it can investigate antiquity and substantiate the present. Thus all that learning can accomplish is fulfilled.

The Changes says: “The gentleman acquaints himself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nurturing his virtue.” The book of Meng Ke says: “The gentleman learns broadly and explains in detail, so that he may return to an explanation of the essentials.” This humble student recites and takes as his models Kongzi and Mengzi; the learning of the Han, Tang, and Song is something I dare not claim to understand. Thus I find profound meaning in this teaching of returning to the essentials. What does Your Honor think of this?

Fourth Question
Liang Dai
Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “He assesses the worthy thinkers of the past as though holding a balance to compare their relative weight.”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
道千人一心學者不求之載籍而求之六
經不求之六經之迹而求之作經者之心
窮理以明之居敬以養之弗襍於聲色貨
利之私弗遷於紛華波蕩之感養吾心之
時中卽羲畫未陳墳典未述而易與書固
在也養吾心之和敬卽經曲未制聲容未
作而禮與樂固在也養吾吾心之是非與性
情則風雅頌之未起褒貶予奪之未彰而
詩與春秋固在也心存則道得道得則文
===
自生以之述作可以翼經而垂訓以之遠
覽可以考古而信今而學之能事畢矣易
曰君子多識前言往行以畜其德軻書曰
君子博學而詳說之將以反說約也愚生
誦法孔孟而漢唐宋所不敢知者故有味
於反約之說執事其以爲何如
第四問
梁岱
同考試官教諭梁批評品往哲如持權衡以較輕重
punctuated:
道，千人一心。學者不求之載籍，而求之六經；不求之六經之迹，而求之作經者之心。窮理以明之，居敬以養之，弗襍於聲色貨利之私，弗遷於紛華波蕩之感。養吾心之時中，卽羲畫未陳、墳典未述，而易與書固在也；養吾心之和敬，卽經曲未制、聲容未作，而禮與樂固在也；養吾吾心之是非與性情，則風雅頌之未起、褒貶予奪之未彰，而詩與春秋固在也。心存則道得，道得則文自生。以之述作，可以翼經而垂訓；以之遠覽，可以考古而信今，而學之能事畢矣。易曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」軻書曰：「君子博學而詳說之，將以反說約也。」愚生誦法孔孟，而漢唐宋所不敢知者，故有味於反約之說。執事其以爲何如？

第四問
梁岱
同考試官教諭梁批：「評品往哲，如持權衡以較輕重。
translation_en:
…the Way: a thousand people share one mind. Students should seek it not in written records but in the Six Classics; not in the traces preserved in the Six Classics but in the minds of those who composed them. They should investigate principle to illuminate this mind and abide in reverence to nourish it, neither adulterating it with selfish desires for sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit nor allowing it to be swayed by the glitter and turmoil of the world. If I nourish my mind’s capacity to attain the mean appropriate to each occasion, then even before Fuxi’s diagrams were set forth or the ancient records composed, the Changes and the Documents are already present within it. If I nourish my mind’s harmony and reverence, then even before the general rules and detailed observances of ritual were established or musical sounds and ceremonial movements devised, the Rites and the Music are already present within it. If I nourish my mind’s sense of right and wrong, its nature and feelings [the transcription repeats “my”], then even before the Airs, Odes, and Hymns arose or praise and blame, approval and rejection were made manifest, the Poetry and the Spring and Autumn Annals are already present within it. When the mind is preserved, the Way is attained; when the Way is attained, literary expression arises of itself. Through it, one may compose writings that assist the Classics and transmit instruction to posterity; through it, one may survey broadly, examining antiquity and verifying the present. Then all that learning can accomplish is fulfilled.

The Changes says: “The gentleman acquaints himself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nourishing his virtue.” The book of Meng Ke says: “The gentleman learns broadly and expounds in detail, intending thereby to return to an explanation of the essentials.” I, an unworthy student, recite and take as my models Confucius and Mencius; as for the Han, Tang, and Song, I dare not claim knowledge. Thus I find particular savor in the teaching of returning to the essentials. What do you, honored examiners, think of this?

Fourth Question
Liang Dai

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “His assessment of past worthies is like holding a balance to compare their relative weights…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
銖兩不差且辭復雅健可追漢人手筆
考試官教諭陳批敷對無遺蓋志存尚友者
考試官教授王批論人物而得其心可為斷案
籲俊以光洪猷者熈世之治也奮庸以樹
遠績者哲士之程也盖人材之生何地無
之顧其時之所遭或異而士之致用其器
業若相倍蓰然故夫英度卓識審時圖幾
入足以弼諧化理出足以潤澤生民者斯
大受之才也其若隨世程能效時宣力或
===
陳讜議以毗政或捍疆圉以衛國者斯亦
適用之才善圖治者所當兼收而並蓄者
也審如是則粤西之人才即在往代已可
覩記矧
國家重熈累洽所以丕振而長育之者久矣
則夫潤飾鴻猷光揚駿烈之士超軼往代
豈偶然之故哉執事發策以粤西人才為
問盖欲愚生志其大也竊嘗觀之人才之
生關于氣運而實繋乎風化之轉移故有
punctuated:
銖兩不差，且辭復雅健，可追漢人手筆。
考試官教諭陳批：敷對無遺，蓋志存尚友者。
考試官教授王批：論人物而得其心，可為斷案。
籲俊以光洪猷者，熈世之治也；奮庸以樹遠績者，哲士之程也。盖人材之生，何地無之？顧其時之所遭或異，而士之致用，其器業若相倍蓰然。故夫英度卓識，審時圖幾，入足以弼諧化理，出足以潤澤生民者，斯大受之才也。其若隨世程能，效時宣力，或陳讜議以毗政，或捍疆圉以衛國者，斯亦適用之才，善圖治者所當兼收而並蓄者也。審如是，則粤西之人才，即在往代，已可覩記。矧國家重熈累洽，所以丕振而長育之者久矣，則夫潤飾鴻猷、光揚駿烈之士超軼往代，豈偶然之故哉？執事發策，以粤西人才為問，盖欲愚生志其大也。竊嘗觀之，人才之生關于氣運，而實繋乎風化之轉移，故有
translation_en:
…without an error of even a fraction of an ounce. Moreover, the language is elegant and vigorous, worthy of emulating the writing of Han authors.
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: The response leaves nothing unaddressed; its author evidently aspires to take the worthy men of antiquity as his friends.
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: In discussing historical figures, he grasps their innermost intentions; this may serve as a definitive judgment.
Calling forth outstanding men to bring lustre to great plans is the way to govern an age of prosperity; exerting one’s abilities in service to establish lasting achievements is the course of a wise scholar. Indeed, where are talented men not born? Yet the circumstances of the times they encounter may differ, so that, when scholars put their abilities to use, their capacities and accomplishments seem to differ severalfold. Thus those of exceptional bearing and outstanding discernment, who assess the times and consider the first signs of change, who at court can assist in bringing harmony to government and moral transformation, and in service outside the court can confer benefits upon the people—these are men capable of bearing great responsibilities. Those who display their abilities as their age requires and exert themselves in response to its needs, whether by offering forthright counsel to assist government or by defending the frontiers to protect the state, are likewise men of practical talent. Those adept at seeking good government should recruit and nurture both kinds alike.
If this is indeed so, then the talented men of Yuexi could already be seen and recorded in past ages. How much more so now, when our dynasty has enjoyed successive ages of prosperity and harmonious rule, and has long worked to inspire and nurture them! That men who embellish its grand designs and glorify its magnificent achievements should surpass those of earlier ages can hardly be accidental. You, honoured examiners, have issued a policy question asking about the talented men of Yuexi, evidently wishing this humble student to set his aspirations upon what is great. I have ventured to observe that the emergence of talent is connected with the cycles of vital forces and fortune, but depends in truth upon changes in customs and moral influence. Thus there are…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
賢傳紀之其賢可知矣士燮精核經傳見
稱名流及爲交趾太守爰致疆塲無事民
不失業方之竇融保河西何以過之耶鄧
盛事母至孝矢聲尉曹平覆竟左尚之獄
一以恩意感動片言伏之方之皐陶淑問
豈無其由耶徐徴素行方直不畏疆禦爲
督郵時收致唐衡暴客髡之郡市蓋持節
不撓其英畧有足稱焉養奮博通墳籍一
時名儒當和帝時條對陰陽水旱無少牽
===
合蓋正色敢言其大義有足取焉夫是六
子咸漢才咸出東京無亦光武明章之烈
振作于上者有成效而興起于下者無遺
壤哉唐人雖置桂容邕三管厥後藩鎭竊
據士無寧宇故人才罕稱惟趙觀文掇巍
科而以抗言謝歸庶於見幾之君子乎韋
厥持使節而服生蠻開擴化外于向糾義
兵而助高駢平定交趾斯亦濶乎希矣有
宋鼎建南服文敎易敷士風益奮方建隆
punctuated:
賢傳紀之，其賢可知矣。士燮精核經傳，見稱名流。及爲交趾太守，爰致疆塲無事，民不失業。方之竇融保河西，何以過之耶？鄧盛事母至孝，矢聲尉曹，平覆竟左尚之獄，一以恩意感動，片言伏之。方之皐陶淑問，豈無其由耶？徐徴素行方直，不畏疆禦。爲督郵時，收致唐衡暴客，髡之郡市。蓋持節不撓，其英畧有足稱焉。養奮博通墳籍，一時名儒。當和帝時，條對陰陽水旱，無少牽合。蓋正色敢言，其大義有足取焉。夫是六子，咸漢才，咸出東京，無亦光武、明、章之烈振作于上者有成效，而興起于下者無遺壤哉？

唐人雖置桂、容、邕三管，厥後藩鎭竊據，士無寧宇，故人才罕稱。惟趙觀文掇巍科，而以抗言謝歸，庶於見幾之君子乎？韋厥持使節而服生蠻，開擴化外；于向糾義兵而助高駢平定交趾。斯亦濶乎希矣！

有宋鼎建，南服文敎易敷，士風益奮。方建隆
translation_en:
… recorded in the Biographies of Worthies, their worthiness can be known. Shi Xie examined the classics and their commentaries with precision and was acclaimed among eminent men. When he became Governor of Jiaozhi, he brought peace to the frontier and enabled the people to pursue their livelihoods undisturbed. Compared with Dou Rong’s preservation of Hexi, how could the latter’s achievement surpass his? Deng Sheng served his mother with utmost filial devotion and established a reputation in the judicial office [?]. He fairly reviewed and concluded the case of Zuo Shang [?], moving him entirely through benevolent intentions and securing his submission with a few words. Surely there is reason to compare him with Gao Yao’s judicious questioning? Xu Zheng was habitually upright and feared no powerful aggressor. While serving as an Inspector, he arrested Tang Heng’s violent retainers and had their heads shaved in the commandery marketplace. He maintained his integrity without yielding; his outstanding abilities deserve praise. Yang Fen was deeply versed in ancient writings and was a renowned scholar of his day. During Emperor He’s reign, he submitted itemized answers concerning yin and yang, floods, and droughts, without the slightest strained accommodation. His grave bearing and bold speech reveal a commitment to principle worthy of esteem. These six men were all talents of the Han, all emerging under the Eastern Han. Was this not because the illustrious achievements of Emperors Guangwu, Ming, and Zhang had effectively inspired those below, so that no region failed to produce men of promise?

Although the Tang established the three jurisdictions of Gui, Rong, and Yong, military governors subsequently seized control, leaving scholars no peaceful abode. Hence few men of talent won renown. Zhao Guanwen alone attained distinction in the examinations, then took his leave and returned home after speaking out forthrightly. Was he perhaps a gentleman who discerned the first signs of change? Wei Jue, bearing an envoy’s credentials, brought unsubjugated indigenous peoples into submission and extended rule into lands beyond the reach of imperial civilization. Yu Xiang mustered loyal troops and helped Gao Pian pacify Jiaozhi. Such men, too, were exceedingly rare!

When the Song dynasty was established, literary and moral instruction spread readily through the southern territories, and the spirit of the scholars grew increasingly vigorous. At the time of the Jianlong reign …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
初周渭召試時務受知藝祖即能誅縣吏
之奸弭監軍之叛滅偽國挽筭之籍敡歷
中外聲績赫然可不謂奇士哉而教授廣
州獻本政書十三篇慨然有志復古時則
有若林勳焉張敬夫稱其人才卓然有以
也作牧三州躬操廉介惟以恩信結民夷
心時則有若蔣允濟焉朱元晦稱其遺愛
在人有以也覃光佃幼抱岐嶷著名御史
內肅朝儀外紓邊策其繫國安危若此王
===
世則早掇倫魁增光使節進憂國本退播
英聲其繫時輕重若此知昌化軍而請增
賓興之額減折納之輸者黃齊循良之績
也為講讀官而疏陳謹獨之謨建脩武之
策者陶崇啓沃之功也若馮京三為舉首
號名執政而中立之操始終不變所謂大
臣以道事君者京有之矣宋之人才於斯
為盛洪惟我
國家
punctuated:
初，周渭召試時務，受知藝祖，即能誅縣吏之奸，弭監軍之叛，滅偽國挽筭之籍，敡歷中外，聲績赫然，可不謂奇士哉？而教授廣州，獻本政書十三篇，慨然有志復古，時則有若林勳焉。張敬夫稱其人才卓然，有以也。作牧三州，躬操廉介，惟以恩信結民夷心，時則有若蔣允濟焉。朱元晦稱其遺愛在人，有以也。覃光佃幼抱岐嶷，著名御史，內肅朝儀，外紓邊策，其繫國安危若此。王世則早掇倫魁，增光使節，進憂國本，退播英聲，其繫時輕重若此。知昌化軍而請增賓興之額、減折納之輸者，黃齊循良之績也。為講讀官而疏陳謹獨之謨、建脩武之策者，陶崇啓沃之功也。若馮京三為舉首，號名執政，而中立之操始終不變，所謂大臣以道事君者，京有之矣。宋之人才於斯為盛。
洪惟我國家
translation_en:
…early in that era, Zhou Wei was summoned for examination on current affairs and won the recognition of the dynastic founder. He was then able to punish corrupt county clerks, quell a rebellion by an army supervisor, and abolish the registers of transport levies imposed by the illegitimate regime [?]. Serving successively at court and in the provinces, he achieved conspicuous renown and accomplishments. Can he not be called an extraordinary man? Then there was Lin Xun, who served as an instructor in Guangzhou and presented thirteen chapters of his Book on the Foundations of Government, earnestly aspiring to restore ancient institutions. Zhang Jingfu had good reason to praise his outstanding talent. There was also Jiang Yunji, who governed three prefectures, personally maintained integrity and uprightness, and won the hearts of the common people and indigenous communities solely through kindness and trustworthiness. Zhu Yuanhui had good reason to praise the enduring affection he left among the people.

Qin Guangdian [?] displayed exceptional promise from childhood and became renowned as a censor. Within the court he enforced ceremonial discipline; beyond it he helped resolve frontier difficulties through his policies [?]. Such was his importance to the security of the state. Wang Shize won first place in the examinations early in life and brought distinction to his diplomatic commission. In office he concerned himself with the foundations of the state; in retirement his illustrious reputation spread. Such was his weight in the affairs of his age. While administering Changhua Military Prefecture, Huang Qi requested an increase in the quota for candidates sponsored for the examinations and a reduction in payments commuted from taxes in kind: these were the achievements of a conscientious and benevolent administrator. As a court lecturer and reader, Tao Chong submitted memorials advising vigilance over one’s conduct even when alone and proposing measures to strengthen military preparedness: these were his contributions to enlightening and nourishing the ruler’s understanding. As for Feng Jing, he placed first in three successive examinations and was celebrated as a leading minister, yet his principled impartiality remained unchanged throughout. Jing possessed what is meant by the saying that a great minister serves his ruler according to the Way. In these men, the talent of the Song reached its flourishing height.

Reverently considering our dynasty…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
黜浮敦薄優游桂里以壽考終稱之者謂
其守身如蘧伯玉立朝如文潞公居鄉如
司馬君實信矣蔣冕休休有容由文學入
柄大政卒而受遺定策迎立
眞主銷危疑於未著奠
社稷於乂安者冕等二三大臣之功也稱之者
謂其德業文章如有源之水信知言哉夫
此數君子者樹休烈于當時垂芳聲于後
世炳炳烺烺較之漢唐宋諸臣遠過之矣
===
其諸一節一行之士播在記牒尤有未易
以枚舉者頃歲以來鴻材彙征內而秉衡
握軸外而仗鉞擁旄以及廊署岳牧布列
庶位者濟濟相望晉之履公卿輔弼之任
以翊
國家中興之治其所建樹將必與帝王名世
之佐相後先矣猗與盛哉詩曰思皇多士
生此王國王國克生維周之禎言才賢之
利於國也易曰雲從龍風從虎聖人作而
punctuated:
黜浮敦薄，優游桂里，以壽考終。稱之者謂其守身如蘧伯玉，立朝如文潞公，居鄉如司馬君實，信矣。蔣冕休休有容，由文學入柄大政，卒而受遺定策，迎立眞主，銷危疑於未著，奠社稷於乂安者，冕等二三大臣之功也。稱之者謂其德業文章如有源之水，信知言哉！夫此數君子者，樹休烈于當時，垂芳聲于後世，炳炳烺烺，較之漢唐宋諸臣，遠過之矣。其諸一節一行之士，播在記牒，尤有未易以枚舉者。
頃歲以來，鴻材彙征，內而秉衡握軸，外而仗鉞擁旄，以及廊署岳牧，布列庶位者，濟濟相望。晉之履公卿輔弼之任，以翊國家中興之治，其所建樹，將必與帝王名世之佐相後先矣。猗與盛哉！《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之禎。」言才賢之利於國也。《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而
translation_en:
…He rejected frivolity and strengthened the morally weak, lived at ease in his native Gui, and died at an advanced age. Those who praised him said that in personal conduct he resembled Qu Boyu, in service at court Duke Wen of Lu, and in life in his home community Sima Junshi. Truly so! Jiang Mian was generous and tolerant. Through literary learning he rose to direct the great affairs of government. Ultimately, he received the late emperor’s charge and settled the succession, welcoming and enthroning the rightful sovereign. That danger and uncertainty were dispelled before they became manifest, and that the altars of soil and grain were secured in peace and order, was the achievement of Mian and two or three other great ministers. Those who praised him likened his virtue, accomplishments, and writings to water with a wellspring. These were discerning words indeed! These several gentlemen established splendid achievements in their own time and left a fragrant reputation to posterity, brilliant and resplendent. Compared with the ministers of the Han, Tang, and Song, they far surpassed them. As for men distinguished by a single instance of integrity or a single worthy deed, their deeds are scattered through the records, and they are particularly difficult to enumerate individually.
In recent years, men of outstanding talent have advanced together: at court they hold the balance and direct the pivot of government; outside it they wield battle-axes and command beneath their banners. Together with officials in the government offices and regional administrators, they fill the many posts, an impressive succession of worthy men. As they are promoted to the responsibilities of high ministers and chief advisers, assisting the state’s resurgent governance, their achievements will surely rank alongside those of the illustrious assistants to emperors and kings throughout the ages. Ah, how flourishing! The Book of Odes says: “Splendid are the many worthy men, born in this royal realm. The royal realm can bring them forth: they are the auspicious sign of Zhou.” This speaks of the benefit that talented and worthy men bring to the state. The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and…”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬物覩言人類之神於應也今
聖天子雍熙成化綱紀作人一時名賢際雲龍
之會而應彙征之期者蓋所在嚮風而承
德焉愚也生逢
唐虞之世上嘉臯夔之風竊願友天下之善
士又尚論古之人未敢以一方自限量也
敢以是爲明問復
第五問
彭啓忠
===
同考試官教諭陳批時務策關繫最要是作以任
將達權爲主甚合機宜且議論鑿鑿可行足徵經濟
考試官教諭陳批區畫精詳足占用世之學
考試官教授王批籌畫切中機宜誠達時務者
御夷有常而任將爲急制勝有機而達權
爲要夫人之著能各不同也故爲將者有
偏全之技有攻守之才惟選擇而責成之
使專于其任焉斯則得統御之略矣夫兵
之爲勢無常形也故達權者有伸縮之相
punctuated:
萬物覩，言人類之神於應也。今聖天子雍熙成化，綱紀作人，一時名賢際雲龍之會而應彙征之期者，蓋所在嚮風而承德焉。愚也生逢唐虞之世，上嘉臯夔之風，竊願友天下之善士，又尚論古之人，未敢以一方自限量也。敢以是爲明問復。

第五問
彭啓忠

同考試官教諭陳批：時務策關繫最要，是作以任將達權爲主，甚合機宜，且議論鑿鑿可行，足徵經濟。
考試官教諭陳批：區畫精詳，足占用世之學。
考試官教授王批：籌畫切中機宜，誠達時務者。

御夷有常，而任將爲急；制勝有機，而達權爲要。夫人之著能各不同也，故爲將者有偏全之技，有攻守之才，惟選擇而責成之，使專于其任焉，斯則得統御之略矣。夫兵之爲勢無常形也，故達權者有伸縮之相
translation_en:
…and all things behold him.” This speaks of the wondrous responsiveness of humankind. Now our sage Son of Heaven brings transformation to fruition through harmony and prosperity, establishing order and nurturing men of talent. The eminent worthies of our time encounter the auspicious meeting of cloud and dragon, answering the call to advance together; wherever they are, they turn toward his influence and receive his virtue. Humble as I am, I have been born into an age like that of Tang and Yu, and admire the example of Gao Yao and Kui of old. I venture to hope to befriend the good men of the realm and also to discuss the men of antiquity. I dare not confine my aspirations to a single region. With this I venture to answer your illuminating question.

Fifth Question
Peng Qizhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: This policy essay on current affairs concerns matters of the greatest importance. It centers on appointing generals and exercising discretion, closely fitting the needs of the situation. Its arguments are also definite and practicable, amply demonstrating ability in statecraft.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The planning is precise and thorough, sufficient evidence of learning suited to practical service.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: His plans exactly meet the needs of the situation. He truly understands current affairs.

There are established principles for defending against the non-Chinese peoples, but appointing generals is the urgent task; securing victory depends on opportunities, but understanding how to exercise discretion is essential. People differ in the abilities they display. Thus, among generals, some possess specialized skills and others comprehensive abilities; some have talent for attack and others for defense. Only by selecting them and holding them responsible for results, allowing them sole charge of their assignments, can one grasp the art of command. Military dispositions have no constant form. Thus, those who understand the exercise of discretion have an alternation between expansion and contraction…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
仍有勦撫之相因惟隨時而運用之使萬
全不爽焉斯可幾安攘之圖矣爲將者惟
其剛而弗審誇而無當也故於兵則易視
之其自許也則曰我熟夷地諳夷情也至
使當一隊守一障焉則進退維谷尺寸不
效矣若是者不早擇之可乎治兵者惟其
誕而寡謀泥而不通也故臨事則輕言之
其策敵也不過曰夷强可勦弱可撫也至
使臨大敵制大事焉則措置燾張經理失
===
據矣若此者不豫圖之可乎執事憤土猺
叛亂之久幸重臣
簡命之臨思文武將吏之佐詢必勝久安之畫
爲一方計至審也愚生敢借前籌哉敬以
舊聞者陳焉夫嶺表之有蠻夷也其種落
非一類其窟宅非一隅其侵叛非一日其
詒罹非一方也然今之號最黠而禍最鉅
者莫若近省之土猺焉蓋其枕藉兩江連
亘融洛拒龍門之阿扼都狼之隘地至阻
punctuated:
仍，有勦撫之相因，惟隨時而運用之，使萬全不爽焉，斯可幾安攘之圖矣。爲將者，惟其剛而弗審，誇而無當也，故於兵則易視之。其自許也，則曰：「我熟夷地，諳夷情也。」至使當一隊、守一障焉，則進退維谷，尺寸不效矣。若是者，不早擇之可乎？治兵者，惟其誕而寡謀，泥而不通也，故臨事則輕言之。其策敵也，不過曰：「夷强可勦，弱可撫也。」至使臨大敵、制大事焉，則措置燾張，經理失據矣。若此者，不豫圖之可乎？
執事憤土猺叛亂之久，幸重臣簡命之臨，思文武將吏之佐，詢必勝久安之畫，爲一方計至審也。愚生敢借前籌哉？敬以舊聞者陳焉。夫嶺表之有蠻夷也，其種落非一類，其窟宅非一隅，其侵叛非一日，其詒罹非一方也。然今之號最黠而禍最鉅者，莫若近省之土猺焉。蓋其枕藉兩江，連亘融洛，拒龍門之阿，扼都狼之隘，地至阻
translation_en:
…follow one another, and suppression and pacification likewise succeed one another. Only by employing these methods as circumstances require, ensuring complete success without error, can one hope to achieve security at home and repel external threats. Those who serve as generals, being headstrong without careful judgment and boastful without substance, take warfare lightly. In their self-estimation they say, “I know the terrain of the indigenous peoples well and understand their circumstances.” Yet when put in command of a unit or charged with defending a stockade, they can neither advance nor retreat and accomplish nothing whatsoever. Can we afford not to screen such men early? Those who direct military affairs, being extravagant in their claims but deficient in planning, rigid and inflexible, speak lightly when faced with events. Their strategy against the enemy amounts to no more than saying, “When the indigenous peoples are strong, they can be suppressed; when weak, they can be pacified.” Yet when made to confront a major enemy or decide great affairs, their dispositions become confused [?], and their management loses its foundation. Can we afford not to plan for this beforehand?
You, sir, are indignant at the prolonged rebellion of the local Yao and welcome the arrival of a high minister specially commissioned by the emperor. You consider how civil and military officers might assist him and inquire into plans for certain victory and lasting peace: your deliberations on behalf of this region are most careful. Dare I, an ignorant student, presume to lay strategic plans before you? I respectfully present what I have previously heard. As for the indigenous peoples beyond the mountains in Lingbiao, their tribes are of more than one kind, their strongholds occupy more than one corner, their incursions and rebellions have lasted more than a single day, and the calamities they cause affect more than one region. Yet among those now reputed the most cunning and responsible for the greatest harm, none compare with the local Yao near the provincial capital. Their territory rests upon Liangjiang and stretches through Rong and Luo; they hold the slopes of Longmen and control the defile of Dulang. The terrain is exceedingly rugged…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也左連三鎮右達九寨背永寶綏靖之陰
達荔永藤峽之交穴至衆也往者抗王師
戕二將繼則掠省帑斃藩臣窺覦
靖邸侵竊縣治患至無巳也
聖天子軫念南顧而重臣握符矣計重糧餉至
內帑給儲矣然承制而專决一方建纛而總
握羣略者重臣之事也至運謀畫於帷幄
定進止於封郊宣恩威於燮伐奮勇力於
戰陣者文武諸吏之職也執事所謂欽承
===
威命而興師有期又云兵無常形而謀貴豫定
蓋率兵者將而兵勝以謀也制勝者謀而
謀成貴豫也兵志有之曰將者國之輔也
輔周則國强夫將必以周為輔矧今之土
傜地險而穴衆非可以一師一隊徑指而
直搗之者是所以分命諸將不可不擇之
精也又曰伐謀為上野戰為下夫兵之所
伐在謀矧今之土猺為患又至無巳非可
一朝一夕草薙而禽獮之者是所以相機
punctuated:
也。左連三鎮，右達九寨，背永寶綏靖之陰，達荔永藤峽之交，穴至衆也。往者抗王師，戕二將；繼則掠省帑，斃藩臣，窺覦靖邸，侵竊縣治，患至無巳也。聖天子軫念南顧，而重臣握符矣；計重糧餉，至內帑給儲矣。然承制而專决一方，建纛而總握羣略者，重臣之事也。至運謀畫於帷幄，定進止於封郊，宣恩威於燮伐，奮勇力於戰陣者，文武諸吏之職也。執事所謂「欽承威命而興師有期」，又云「兵無常形而謀貴豫定」，蓋率兵者將，而兵勝以謀也；制勝者謀，而謀成貴豫也。
兵志有之，曰：「將者，國之輔也；輔周，則國强。」夫將必以周為輔，矧今之土傜，地險而穴衆，非可以一師一隊徑指而直搗之者，是所以分命諸將不可不擇之精也。又曰：「伐謀為上，野戰為下。」夫兵之所伐在謀，矧今之土猺為患又至無巳，非可一朝一夕草薙而禽獮之者，是所以相機
translation_en:
…such is the terrain. To the left they connect with the Three Garrisons, and to the right they reach the Nine Stockades; behind them lie the shaded sides of Yong, Bao, Sui, and Jing [?], and they extend to the meeting of Li, Yong, and Teng Gorge [?]. Their strongholds are exceedingly numerous. Previously they resisted the imperial armies and slew two commanders; subsequently they plundered the provincial treasury, killed a provincial official, cast covetous eyes upon the residence of the Prince of Jing, and encroached upon and seized county seats. The troubles they cause have no end. Our sagely Son of Heaven has taken the south’s plight to heart, and a high minister now holds the tally of military command. So much importance has been attached to provisioning and military pay that even the palace treasury has supplied funds. Yet receiving imperial authorization to exercise independent authority over a region, raising the great command banner, and directing all strategic plans are the high minister’s responsibilities. Devising plans within the command tent, determining advances and withdrawals at the territorial borders, displaying imperial benevolence and might in pacification and punitive warfare [?], and exerting courage and strength in battle are the duties of the civil and military officials. You speak of ‘reverently receiving the august command, with a date fixed for mobilizing the army,’ and also say that ‘warfare has no constant configuration, and plans should therefore be settled in advance.’ It is generals who lead troops, but troops win through planning; it is planning that secures victory, but successful planning depends upon preparation.
A military treatise says: ‘The general is the support of the state; when that support is comprehensive, the state is strong.’ A general must indeed provide comprehensive support. How much more is this so with the present local Yao, whose terrain is rugged and whose strongholds are numerous! They cannot be directly attacked and overrun by a single army or detachment. This is why, when assigning separate commands to the generals, one must select them with the utmost care. It also says: ‘Attacking the enemy’s plans is best; fighting in the open field is inferior.’ Military attacks thus depend upon planning. Moreover, the troubles caused by the local Yao now have no end: they cannot be mown down like grass, captured, and exterminated in a single morning or evening. This is why one must assess the opportunities…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而任將難夫將之難知也然觀其年以知
其強勇試其言以考其智略其至要莫若
稽其行事驗其平生或累立戰功或甞經
陷陣昔人謂兵官非甞試之惡知其能者
則選將之術也若夫羸弱不可以服衆輕
率不可以諏謀其大致在於脂韋夤緣誇
談飾用聽其言則美施於用則疎昔人謂
兵不擇將以卒與敵者則任將之鑑也任
使旣稱謀猷旣周問罪於貫盈之夷發紓
===
夫人神之憤蠢玆土猺安能久逃鈇鉞也
是故曲道相伏險阨相薄至險不足虞也
何者昔者二馬之禍惟其識不遠而謀不
臧者也夫綿綿翼翼不測不克者師之律
也以曲道險阨之途而以無人之境視之
行不遠間諜止不定行幕經隘不搜竊伏
之奸紆道不匝住守之卒使猺突出以截
我也𫝊豈素豫之將耶使其土著之夫結
之有素緝事之役待以殊恩分遣於數月
punctuated:
而任將難。夫將之難知也，然觀其年以知其強勇，試其言以考其智略，其至要莫若稽其行事，驗其平生。或累立戰功，或甞經陷陣，昔人謂「兵官非甞試之，惡知其能」者，則選將之術也。若夫羸弱不可以服衆，輕率不可以諏謀，其大致在於脂韋夤緣，誇談飾用，聽其言則美，施於用則疎。昔人謂「兵不擇將，以卒與敵」者，則任將之鑑也。任使旣稱，謀猷旣周，問罪於貫盈之夷，發紓夫人神之憤，蠢玆土猺，安能久逃鈇鉞也？
是故曲道相伏，險阨相薄，至險不足虞也。何者？昔者二馬之禍，惟其識不遠而謀不臧者也。夫綿綿翼翼，不測不克者，師之律也。以曲道險阨之途，而以無人之境視之，行不遠間諜，止不定行幕，經隘不搜竊伏之奸，紆道不匝住守之卒，使猺突出以截我也，𫝊豈素豫之將耶？使其土著之夫，結之有素，緝事之役，待以殊恩，分遣於數月
translation_en:
…yet appointing commanders is difficult. Although commanders are difficult to assess, one can observe their age to judge their strength and courage, and test their words to examine their intelligence and strategic ability. Most essential, however, is to investigate their deeds and verify their past conduct. Some have repeatedly won distinction in battle; others have charged into enemy formations. As men of old said, “Unless a military officer has been tried, how can one know his ability?” This is the method for selecting commanders. The weak cannot command the obedience of their men, and the rash cannot deliberate on strategy. Such men generally rely on pliant flattery and connections, boastful talk and embellished claims of competence. Their words sound fine, but their performance falls short. As men of old said, “To field troops without selecting their commander is to give soldiers to the enemy.” This is a warning for those who appoint commanders. Once appointments are fitting and plans comprehensive, we may call to account the non-Han peoples whose crimes have reached their full measure and give vent to the indignation of humans and spirits alike. How could these unruly local Yao long escape the executioner's axe?
Thus, even where ambushes confront us along winding roads and forces clash at narrow defiles, the most perilous terrain need not cause apprehension. Why? The disaster that befell the two Ma in former times arose solely from their lack of foresight and their unsound planning. Unremitting vigilance, proceeding cautiously, and not attacking without first assessing the situation: these are the rules governing an army. Yet they treated winding roads and narrow defiles as though they were uninhabited country. On the march they did not send scouts far afield; when halting they did not properly establish their field encampments. Passing through defiles, they did not search out enemies lurking in ambush; along winding roads, they did not post guarding troops all around. They thereby allowed the Yao to burst out and cut them off. Could these have been commanders who prepared beforehand [?]? Had they cultivated ties with local inhabitants well in advance, treated those employed in gathering intelligence with exceptional favor, and dispatched them separately several months…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之先而申覘於臨發之期雖敵人動靜罔
不纖悉周焉行旌所至或布勇士於險巇
或陟高巘以瞭遠如亞夫然將并崤澠之
伏兵而殲之也而反使之據險以扼我者
有是邪故曰是不素豫之將也往者巢穴
之盤惟其始之挫而終之餒者也夫嗶嗶
焞焞如霆如雷者師之法也以盤據紆迴
之區而以天造之險視之外覘之不先備
内應之不先圖出沒不知其所從虛實不
===
知其所措使猺堅壁以制我也是一將之
善謀者邪使其内宅之窟得其地形外宅
之門得其險要多募敢死之士而懸以破
格之賞雖敵人之信息罔有毫髮遺焉分
道而進或犂賊巢於夾攻之頃或執巨魁
於懸購之下如班超然將指西域之名王
而俘之也而反使之恃險以持我者有是
耶故曰是不達權之將也諸猺之跳踉巉
絕而輕越溪澗也其性則然也何者彼非
punctuated: 之先，而申覘於臨發之期，雖敵人動靜，罔不纖悉周焉。行旌所至，或布勇士於險巇，或陟高巘以瞭遠，如亞夫然，將并崤澠之伏兵而殲之也，而反使之據險以扼我者，有是邪？故曰：是不素豫之將也。往者巢穴之盤，惟其始之挫而終之餒者也。夫嗶嗶焞焞，如霆如雷者，師之法也。以盤據紆迴之區，而以天造之險視之，外覘之不先備，内應之不先圖，出沒不知其所從，虛實不知其所措，使猺堅壁以制我也，是一將之善謀者邪？使其内宅之窟得其地形，外宅之門得其險要，多募敢死之士，而懸以破格之賞，雖敵人之信息，罔有毫髮遺焉。分道而進，或犂賊巢於夾攻之頃，或執巨魁於懸購之下，如班超然，將指西域之名王而俘之也，而反使之恃險以持我者，有是耶？故曰：是不達權之將也。諸猺之跳踉巉絕而輕越溪澗也，其性則然也。何者？彼非
translation_en:
…in advance, and had reconnaissance been renewed just before departure, even the enemy’s movements would have been known comprehensively and in the finest detail. Wherever the army’s standards went, brave soldiers could have been stationed at perilous points, or men could have climbed high peaks to watch the distance. Acting like Yafu, they could have annihilated even troops lying in ambush at Xiao and Mian. How, then, could they instead have allowed the enemy to occupy the strategic heights and block us? Thus I say: these were commanders who had made no preparations beforehand.

As for the earlier entrenchment in their strongholds, it was simply a case of our forces suffering a reverse at the outset and losing heart in the end. For an army’s method is to advance with rumbling chariots and blazing force [?], like thunderclaps and rolling thunder. Yet our commanders regarded the winding terrain occupied by the enemy as a natural fortress. They neither arranged external reconnaissance beforehand nor planned for assistance from within. They did not know where the enemy emerged and disappeared, or where its strengths and weaknesses lay, allowing the Yao to control us from behind fortified walls. Is this what it means for a commander to plan well? Had they learned the terrain of the enemy’s inner lairs and the strategic points at the entrances to its outer settlements, recruited many men willing to face death, and offered rewards beyond the ordinary scale, not the slightest scrap of intelligence about the enemy would have escaped them. Advancing along separate routes, they could have razed the rebels’ nests in a pincer attack or seized their chief leaders through posted bounties. Acting like Ban Chao, they could have singled out renowned kings of the Western Regions and taken them captive. How, then, could they instead have allowed the enemy to rely on difficult terrain to hold us in check? Thus I say: these were commanders who did not understand how to adapt to circumstances.

That the various Yao leap about on precipitous cliffs and cross streams and ravines with ease is simply their nature. Why is this? They do not have…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有棟宇之居衣屨之飾生而烙蹠履險若
飛而中國之足弗及之也彼狼兵者雖有
內屬之名實其侏離之類忍饑行鬭跳躍
射生素相類也以蠻夷攻蠻夷固中國之
形也然狼者懷野心者也非惟其頑之難
於教練抑且悍之不便指麾且今之狼與
昔大相懸也異日者官帑之儲峙充而餉
犒之給賜厚是故土兵調至如歸以飽其
欲也今土兵之給既微且薄矣土官又從
===
而朘削之故就調者非梟雄之兵而猶挾
驕蹇之氣也與我兵雜處也視戰勝則爭
我兵之前而善於搜捕視不勝則要求重
賞然後肯赴敵其氣盈而易衰可以一用
而不可再也近者於永安之役而知夫狼
果不可以純用也漢土兼制此自古馭夷
之常法者非邪諸猺之不樂控制而便於
其黨也亦性然也何者彼非有上下之分
官長之素刀耕而食火種以生而中國之
punctuated:
有棟宇之居、衣屨之飾，生而烙蹠，履險若飛，而中國之足弗及之也。彼狼兵者，雖有內屬之名，實其侏離之類，忍饑行鬭、跳躍射生，素相類也。以蠻夷攻蠻夷，固中國之形也。然狼者，懷野心者也。非惟其頑之難於教練，抑且悍之不便指麾。且今之狼與昔大相懸也。異日者，官帑之儲峙充，而餉犒之給賜厚，是故土兵調至如歸，以飽其欲也。今土兵之給既微且薄矣，土官又從而朘削之，故就調者非梟雄之兵，而猶挾驕蹇之氣也。與我兵雜處也，視戰勝則爭我兵之前，而善於搜捕；視不勝則要求重賞，然後肯赴敵。其氣盈而易衰，可以一用而不可再也。近者於永安之役，而知夫狼果不可以純用也。漢土兼制，此自古馭夷之常法者非邪？

諸猺之不樂控制而便於其黨也，亦性然也。何者？彼非有上下之分、官長之素，刀耕而食，火種以生，而中國之
translation_en:
…have dwellings with roof beams or the adornments of clothing and shoes. From birth their soles are seared [?]; they traverse perilous ground as though flying, and the feet of men of the Central Kingdom cannot keep pace with them. Those Lang troops, though nominally subjects of the empire, are in fact of the same alien-speaking kind. Enduring hunger, fighting on the march, leaping about, and shooting game are abilities they have always shared. Using barbarians to attack barbarians is indeed the strategic disposition appropriate to the Central Kingdom. Yet the Lang harbor untamed ambitions. Their obstinacy makes them difficult to train, and their fierceness also makes them difficult to command. Moreover, the Lang of today differ greatly from those of former times. In earlier days, government treasuries held ample reserves, and provisions and rewards were generous. Thus, when native troops arrived in response to a summons, they felt as though they were coming home, since their desires were satisfied. Now the allowances for native troops are meager, and native officials further fleece them. Consequently, those who answer the summons are no longer formidable soldiers, yet they still retain their arrogance and insolence. When serving alongside our troops, if they see victory in prospect, they compete to get ahead of our men and prove adept at searching out and capturing the enemy; if they see no prospect of victory, they demand substantial rewards before they will face the enemy. Their ardor swells but easily subsides: they can be employed once, but not a second time. The recent campaign at Yong’an has shown that one truly cannot rely exclusively on Lang troops. Exercising control through both Han and native forces—is this not the established method of governing barbarians since antiquity?

That the various Yao dislike being held under control and feel at ease among their own groups likewise follows from their nature. Why is this? They have neither distinctions between superior and inferior nor an established tradition of officials and chiefs. They till with knives for their food and plant with fire for their livelihood, while the Central Kingdom’s …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
陳而亟赴之懷古其得破謀之算者與有
如岳飛之討曹成也盛夏興師而賀州以
平彼非有破敵之異術也蓋經畫旣具師
出不意先已破其膽矣况席累勝之威而
馳之飛其有達權之機者與執事謂韓雍
用永保之兵以殲夷脩荔也愚則曰雍玆
役兼兩京江廣之兵與土漢達官之衆也
其首破脩荔次及斷藤磨崖之烈于今賴
之雍其謀斷兼資之大將也夫執事謂王
===
守仁率田州之旅以蕩掃諸徭也愚則曰
守仁玆役兼用湖廣廣東之諸將而加之
永保址歸之士也其銜枚疾走八寨悉平
京觀之偉於今爲烈守仁其智勇具備之
儒將也夫此皆經畫之略豫審於其始而
區處之策克成於其終執事欲倣其已試
之明效則亦擇將定謀勦撫相因恩威並
濟而已矣善謀者潛於九地之下而發於
九天之上敵雖欲知之而不得所以知之
punctuated: 陳而亟赴之，懷古其得破謀之算者與？有如岳飛之討曹成也，盛夏興師，而賀州以平。彼非有破敵之異術也，蓋經畫旣具，師出不意，先已破其膽矣。况席累勝之威而馳之，飛其有達權之機者與？執事謂韓雍用永保之兵以殲夷脩荔也，愚則曰：雍玆役兼兩京江廣之兵與土漢達官之衆也。其首破脩荔，次及斷藤磨崖之烈，于今賴之。雍其謀斷兼資之大將也夫！執事謂王守仁率田州之旅以蕩掃諸徭也，愚則曰：守仁玆役兼用湖廣廣東之諸將，而加之永保址歸之士也。其銜枚疾走，八寨悉平，京觀之偉，於今爲烈。守仁其智勇具備之儒將也夫！此皆經畫之略豫審於其始，而區處之策克成於其終。執事欲倣其已試之明效，則亦擇將定謀，勦撫相因，恩威並濟而已矣。善謀者潛於九地之下，而發於九天之上，敵雖欲知之，而不得所以知之
translation_en:
…arrayed [?] and hastened to meet them. Did Huaigu possess the calculations needed to defeat their plans? Consider, too, Yue Fei’s campaign against Cao Cheng: he mobilized his army in midsummer, and Hezhou was pacified. He possessed no extraordinary art for defeating the enemy. Rather, his preparations were complete, and his troops appeared unexpectedly, breaking the enemy’s courage in advance. Moreover, he pressed forward with the formidable momentum of repeated victories. Did not Yue Fei possess the discernment to adapt to circumstances?

You state that Han Yong used troops from Yongshun and Baojing to annihilate the tribespeople at Xiuli. I would observe that in this campaign Yong also employed troops from the two capitals, Jiangxi, and Huguang, together with contingents under native, Han Chinese, and Mongol officers. His achievements in first taking Xiuli and then Duanteng and Moya continue to benefit us today. Surely Yong was a great general endowed with both strategic foresight and decisiveness!

You state that Wang Shouren led the troops of Tianzhou to sweep away the various Yao groups. I would observe that in this campaign Shouren also employed commanders from Huguang and Guangdong, supplemented by soldiers from Yongshun, Baojing, and Zhigui [?]. His soldiers marched swiftly with gags in their mouths to maintain silence, and all Eight Stockades were pacified. The imposing mounds of enemy corpses remain a testimony to his martial achievement. Surely Shouren was a scholar-general possessed of both wisdom and courage!

In all these cases, strategic preparations were carefully considered at the outset, and measures for managing affairs were successfully carried through at the end. If you wish to emulate their proven success, you need only select commanders and settle plans, make suppression and pacification support one another, and employ benevolence and severity together. Those skilled in planning conceal themselves beneath the ninefold earth and strike from above the ninefold heavens. Though the enemy wishes to understand their plans, he cannot find the means to do so…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者也達變者畫於一時之宜而垂之爲千
百世之久睹其利而不至詒其害者也首
惡可誅也而種類之不可盡者開其歸附
而與其自新可也土司可置也而平衍之
可以居民者參之漢官以制其滋蔓可也
若風霆之迅震而繼之開明之日若雪霜
之栗烈而繼之和煦之春斯柔遠能邇蠻
夷率服之道也敢以爲進取之助何如
punctuated: 者也。達變者，畫於一時之宜，而垂之爲千百世之久，睹其利而不至詒其害者也。首惡可誅也，而種類之不可盡者，開其歸附而與其自新可也。土司可置也，而平衍之可以居民者，參之漢官以制其滋蔓可也。若風霆之迅震，而繼之開明之日；若雪霜之栗烈，而繼之和煦之春。斯柔遠能邇、蠻夷率服之道也。敢以爲進取之助，何如？
translation_en: …such is the case. Those who understand changing circumstances devise plans suited to the needs of a particular moment, yet leave them to endure for hundreds and thousands of generations, securing their benefits without bequeathing their harms. The chief evildoers may be executed, but since their peoples cannot be utterly eliminated, it is fitting to open a path for them to submit and allow them to reform themselves. Native offices may be established, but in level, open areas suitable for settlement, it is fitting to intersperse Han officials among them to curb the unchecked expansion of their power. Let the swift shock of wind and thunder be followed by bright sunshine; let the bitter severity of snow and frost be followed by a mild, warming spring. This is the way to conciliate those afar, win over those nearby, and bring the Man and Yi peoples into willing submission. I venture to offer these proposals as an aid to your undertaking. What do you think?

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
隆慶庚午秋八月廣西鄉試
事竣御史李良臣率諸大夫
若執事勸饗諸士工歌鹿鳴
繼之南山諸什將馳賢書貢
天府顧冦以執事宜序末簡序曰
始冦膺聘檄道衡山也則前
===
睹九嶷諸峰邏逫橫亘踰永
而南狀若奔驥望之嘆曰兹
其爲嶺粤之始鍾也夫既入
境清湘縈帶文嶂矗空遶以
三江峙以八桂巉絶明秀寰
中罕儷聳然異之曰兹其爲
天地之奧區也夫既鎖院畢
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

隆慶庚午秋八月，廣西鄉試事竣，御史李良臣率諸大夫若執事，勸饗諸士。工歌《鹿鳴》，繼之《南山》諸什。將馳賢書貢天府，顧冦以執事宜序末簡。序曰：

始冦膺聘檄，道衡山也，則前睹九嶷諸峰邏逫橫亘，踰永而南，狀若奔驥。望之嘆曰：「兹其爲嶺粤之始鍾也夫！」既入境，清湘縈帶，文嶂矗空，遶以三江，峙以八桂，巉絶明秀，寰中罕儷。聳然異之曰：「兹其爲天地之奧區也夫！」既鎖院畢
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the gengwu year of the Longqing reign (1570), upon completion of the Guangxi Provincial Examination, Censor Li Liangchen led the assembled officials and examination staff in entertaining the candidates at a banquet. The musicians sang “The Deer Call,” followed by “Southern Mountain” and other odes. As the list of worthy men was about to be dispatched to the imperial government to present them for advancement, he turned to me, Kou, considering that, as one of those serving at the examination, I should write a postface on its final pages. The postface reads:

When I, Kou, first received the official invitation and traveled by way of Hengshan, I saw ahead of me the peaks of Jiuyi stretching across the landscape in winding succession [?]. They extended southward beyond Yong, resembling galloping steeds. Gazing at them, I exclaimed: “Surely this is where the vital energies of Ling and Yue first gather!” Once I entered the territory, the clear Xiang River wound like a sash, and patterned mountain walls towered into the sky. Encircled by the Three Rivers and flanked by the Eight Gui, it was precipitous and splendidly clear, with few equals in the world. Awestruck by its extraordinary beauty, I said: “Surely this is one of Heaven and Earth’s hidden realms!” Once we had been sequestered in the examination compound and completed…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
試閱其文詞根極理要弗鶩
葩藻七篇論對言人人殊咸
稽傳註明性術也肅然三復
之曰玆其大羹玄酒之遺敦
尚典雅而緣以辭采者夫何
粤西産才若是富也往讀王
制稱天子之田南不盡衡山
===
然則粤西者固三代之所不
能仁太樸眞元渾淪而未斲
詩書禮樂湮鬱而未伸者與
夫
天地泰而羣賢生
聖人作而萬物覩神龍襄首則雲
氣追隨葳鳳呈苞則珍禽聚
punctuated: 試，閱其文詞，根極理要，弗鶩葩藻。七篇論對，言人人殊，咸稽傳註，明性術也。肅然三復之曰：「玆其大羹玄酒之遺，敦尚典雅而緣以辭采者夫！何粤西産才若是富也！」往讀《王制》，稱天子之田，南不盡衡山。然則粤西者，固三代之所不能仁，太樸眞元渾淪而未斲，詩書禮樂湮鬱而未伸者與！夫天地泰而羣賢生，聖人作而萬物覩。神龍襄首，則雲氣追隨；葳鳳呈苞，則珍禽聚
translation_en:
…the examination completed, I read their compositions. They reached to the roots of essential principles, without pursuing florid ornament. In the seven essays of argument and response, each candidate expressed himself differently, yet all consulted the commentaries and annotations, making clear their intellectual dispositions and methods of learning. With deep respect I read them repeatedly and said: “Here survives the legacy of the unseasoned sacrificial broth and the ‘dark wine’ of plain water: a firm esteem for classical refinement, embellished with literary grace! How is it that western Guangxi produces talent in such abundance?” I once read in “Royal Regulations” (Wang zhi) that the Son of Heaven’s domain did not extend southward to encompass Mount Heng. Thus western Guangxi was indeed a place beyond the reach of the benevolent rule of the Three Dynasties, where primal simplicity and original vitality remained whole and unhewn, and where the Poetry, Documents, rites, and music lay submerged and had yet to flourish!

Now, when Heaven and Earth are in harmony, worthy men arise in multitude; when the sage appears, all things come into view. When the divine dragon raises its head, clouds follow; when the majestic phoenix displays its luxuriant plumage [?], rare birds gather…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
底績用裨賛襄而潤皇猷者
也故行業著于當世聲稱浹
乎于玆今之談者則云虞夏
商周之士之進也或以事舉
或以德庸或云夢協或云卜
徵匪專之于言誠是也我
國家令制聚士而甄陶諸學宮
===
稽行於有司而賓興之於三
歲蓋非徒曰以試得之以言
揚之爾也顧視虞夏商周之
辨才有同符焉者今諸士之
自獻其言也述虞夏叙商周
舍性術弗陳外傳註弗演鏘
然可觀矣然言華也行實也
punctuated: 底績，用裨賛襄而潤皇猷者也。故行業著于當世，聲稱浹乎于玆。今之談者則云：「虞夏商周之士之進也，或以事舉，或以德庸，或云夢協，或云卜徵，匪專之于言。」誠是也！我國家令制，聚士而甄陶諸學宮，稽行於有司，而賓興之於三歲，蓋非徒曰以試得之、以言揚之爾也。顧視虞夏商周之辨才，有同符焉者。今諸士之自獻其言也，述虞夏，叙商周，舍性術弗陳，外傳註弗演，鏘然可觀矣。然言華也，行實也。
translation_en: …bring achievements to fruition, rendering assistance and enhancing the imperial enterprise. Thus their conduct and accomplishments were manifest in their own age, and their renown has spread down to the present. Those who discuss the matter today say: “When men of learning advanced under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, some were recommended for their accomplishments, others employed for their virtue; some, it is said, matched a dream, while others were confirmed by divination. Advancement did not depend exclusively on words.” This is indeed so! Under our dynasty’s excellent regulations, men of learning are gathered and molded in the schools; the responsible officials examine their conduct, and every three years they are honored as guests and recommended for advancement. This surely does not mean merely selecting them through examinations and promoting them for their words. Compared with the discernment of talent under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, this accords with the same principles. Now, in presenting their compositions, these men recount Yu and Xia and relate Shang and Zhou. They set forth nothing apart from human nature and its cultivation [?], and expound nothing beyond the commentaries and annotations. Their words ring out splendidly and merit attention. Yet words are the blossom; conduct is the fruit.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸士者如其攄心以發言心
罔弗孚卽行以稽言行罔弗
成矣茲魁以是爲諸士望之
也夫士而不以禹臯伊傅箕
望之業待其身匪善致身者
也士而不以虞夏商周之盛
事其君匪能致君者也諸士
===
行矣將以言對
大廷揚敷納明烈訓者繼自今
若曰
明盛間值川岳匪虛旣已應毓秀
而慶遭逢也所持以終身者
惟敏顧于言弗懈於行用是
無忝昔人不媿賢科已矣抑
punctuated: 諸士者，如其攄心以發言，心罔弗孚；卽行以稽言，行罔弗成矣。茲魁以是爲諸士望之也。夫士而不以禹臯伊傅箕望之業待其身，匪善致身者也；士而不以虞夏商周之盛事其君，匪能致君者也。諸士行矣，將以言對大廷，揚敷納明烈訓者，繼自今。若曰：「明盛間值，川岳匪虛，旣已應毓秀而慶遭逢也，所持以終身者，惟敏顧于言，弗懈於行，用是無忝昔人，不媿賢科已矣。」抑
translation_en:
If you gentlemen express your hearts in your words, your hearts will invariably prove sincere; if you test your words against your conduct, your conduct will invariably attain fulfillment. This is what Kui hopes for you gentlemen. A scholar who does not expect of himself achievements like those of Yu, Gao, Yi, Fu, Ji, and Wang is not adept at fulfilling his own potential. A scholar who does not serve his sovereign with the aim of attaining the flourishing rule of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou cannot bring his sovereign to fulfillment. Go forth, gentlemen! You will present your words in response at the imperial court; from this time onward, you will carry forward the illustrious teachings concerning the presentation and reception of counsel [?].

You might say: “We have encountered an enlightened and flourishing age; the mountains and rivers have not nurtured talent in vain. Having answered to their nurturing of excellence, we rejoice in this fortunate encounter. What we must uphold throughout our lives is simply to attend diligently to our words and remain unflagging in our conduct, thereby bringing no dishonor upon the men of old and proving worthy of this examination for selecting the worthy.” Yet …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
愚竊尚有懼焉顧玆文章桂
嶺之巉絶而亦有夷酋異物
之竊爲憑依也清湘三水之
明秀而亦有炎風蒸嵐之因
以時作也諸士者間或有言
馳于心行違于始則醇駁且
不相掩他日人將訾之其於
===
明盛之值川岳之鍾胥有負焉則
使斯錄也不幾爲弗信之書
與故冠之願與諸士勗之也
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教
諭陳冠謹序
punctuated:
愚竊尚有懼焉。顧玆文章，桂嶺之巉絶，而亦有夷酋異物之竊爲憑依也；清湘三水之明秀，而亦有炎風蒸嵐之因以時作也。諸士者間或有言馳于心、行違于始，則醇駁且不相掩。他日人將訾之，其於明盛之值、川岳之鍾，胥有負焉。則使斯錄也，不幾爲弗信之書與？故冠之願與諸士勗之也。
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教諭陳冠謹序。
translation_en:
…Yet I humbly still harbor a fear. Consider the patterned splendor here: the Guiling mountains are steep and lofty, yet tribal chieftains and strange creatures secretly find refuge in them; the Qingxiang and Sanshui waters [?] are clear and lovely, yet scorching winds and steaming mountain mists also arise there from time to time. If any of you gentlemen should let your words outrun your convictions, or your conduct depart from your initial resolve, then your merits will not conceal your flaws. In days to come, people will censure you: you will have failed both the enlightened and flourishing age you have encountered and the gifts bestowed upon you by these rivers and mountains. Would this not make this examination record almost an untrustworthy book? Thus I, Guan, wish to join you gentlemen in taking this admonition to heart.
Preface respectfully composed by Chen Guan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午我
皇上登極之四年也天下復當大
比士監察御史李良臣祗承
上命巡按廣西方攬轡出燕衞道
荆襄兢兢然懼弗逮馳檄所
司以粤壤寔遐且僻賓興彝
===
典其維先事之圖所司將御
史檄縅儀列省延聘儒臣無
何御史至彰程貞紀既備益
虔期於登崇俊良以仰副
聖天子寤寐求賢至意先是總督
兩廣右都御史兼兵部左侍
郎劉燾恢弘治教山海厎寧
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午，我皇上登極之四年也。天下復當大比士。監察御史李良臣祗承上命，巡按廣西，方攬轡出燕，衞道荆襄，兢兢然懼弗逮，馳檄所司，以粤壤寔遐且僻，賓興彝典，其維先事之圖。所司將御史檄縅儀列省，延聘儒臣。無何，御史至，彰程貞紀，既備益虔，期於登崇俊良，以仰副聖天子寤寐求賢至意。先是，總督兩廣右都御史兼兵部左侍郎劉燾恢弘治教，山海厎寧。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

The gengwu year of the Longqing reign was the fourth year since our emperor ascended the throne. Throughout the realm, it was again time for the triennial examination of scholars. Investigating Censor Li Liangchen, reverently receiving the imperial command to inspect Guangxi, had only just taken up the reins and departed from Yan, traveling by way of Jing and Xiang [?]. Deeply anxious lest he fall short of his charge, he dispatched an urgent directive to the responsible officials. Since the lands of Yue were indeed distant and remote, advance preparations must be made for the established ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy scholars. The responsible officials conveyed the censor’s directive to the various provinces with the requisite formalities [?], inviting Confucian scholars to serve.

Before long, the censor arrived. He clarified the regulations and set discipline in order; with preparations complete, he became still more scrupulous. His aim was to advance and honor outstanding men of worth, thereby fulfilling the sage emperor’s earnest desire to seek worthy men, waking and sleeping. Previously, Liu Tao, Supreme Commander of Guangdong and Guangxi, Right Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Left Vice Minister of War, had greatly extended good government and moral instruction, bringing peace to the mountains and seas…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今提督兩廣兵部左侍郎右
僉都御史李遷揆文奮武綱
紀聿新巡撫廣西右僉都御
史殷正茂秉憲敷文甄陶素
洽八桂之士咸得專志明經
挾藝待問屆期御史申飭試
事以燧及敎諭陳冠司考試
===
學正鐵世材敎諭宋邦達林
獻芹梁幹陳三俊同考試提
調則左布政使郭應聘左參
政楊銓監試則按察使萬思
謙僉事楊文明簾以外暨百
執事咸愼簡以從已乃進提
學副使陰武卿所簡士一千
punctuated: 今提督兩廣兵部左侍郎右僉都御史李遷，揆文奮武，綱紀聿新；巡撫廣西右僉都御史殷正茂，秉憲敷文，甄陶素洽。八桂之士咸得專志明經，挾藝待問。屆期，御史申飭試事，以燧及敎諭陳冠司考試，學正鐵世材、敎諭宋邦達、林獻芹、梁幹、陳三俊同考試。提調則左布政使郭應聘、左參政楊銓，監試則按察使萬思謙、僉事楊文明。簾以外暨百執事，咸愼簡以從。已乃進提學副使陰武卿所簡士一千
translation_en:
Now Li Qian, Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Left Vice Minister of War, and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, has ordered civil affairs and invigorated military affairs, renewing discipline and administration. Yin Zhengmao, Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, has upheld the laws and spread literary learning; his work of selecting and cultivating talent has long been effective. The scholars of Bagui could all devote themselves to mastering the Classics, ready with their learning to answer the examination questions.

When the appointed time arrived, the Censor reiterated the instructions for conducting the examination. He appointed me, Sui, and Chen Guan, an Instructor, as Examiners, and Tie Shicai, a School Director, together with the Instructors Song Bangda, Lin Xianqin, Liang Gan, and Chen Sanjun, as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Guo Yingpin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yang Quan, Left Administration Vice Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Wan Siqian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Yang Wenming, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. Those serving outside the curtain separating the examiners from the other staff, along with all the functionaries, were carefully selected to assist. Then the candidates selected by Yin Wuqing, Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were admitted, numbering one thousand…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
四百有奇鎖院三試之遵
制拔其雋五十有五人竝錄其文
之優者以
獻燧以職事宜序諸簡端謹稽
首颺言曰士之致用於天下
也莫重乎文質之相成故論
士者恒憂其相勝而難於有
===
濟何者文勝之士類多樂聲
名喜詩書然其弊也則競藻
絢而乏雅致視仁義道德或
視為繪飾之資而不求實用
於世何補也若質之勝者悃
愊以為心直抗以為氣渾然
天真無所雕琢然或尚簡素
punctuated:
四百有奇，鎖院三試之，遵制拔其雋五十有五人，竝錄其文之優者以獻。燧以職事宜序諸簡端，謹稽首颺言曰：
士之致用於天下也，莫重乎文質之相成。故論士者恒憂其相勝而難於有濟。何者？文勝之士，類多樂聲名，喜詩書，然其弊也，則競藻絢而乏雅致，視仁義道德，或視為繪飾之資，而不求實用，於世何補也？若質之勝者，悃愊以為心，直抗以為氣，渾然天真，無所雕琢，然或尚簡素
translation_en:
…four hundred and more [completing the total of one thousand four hundred and more candidates]. The examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions. In accordance with the imperial regulations, fifty-five outstanding candidates were selected, and their superior compositions were also transcribed for presentation to the throne. Since my official duties require me, Sui, to place a preface at the beginning of this record, I reverently bow my head to the ground and declare:
For scholars to render useful service in the world, nothing matters more than the mutual completion of literary refinement and substantive character. Thus, those who assess scholars constantly worry that one will overpower the other, making effective accomplishment difficult. Why is this? Scholars in whom literary refinement predominates generally delight in reputation and enjoy poetry and books. Yet their failing is to vie in ornate brilliance while lacking cultivated profundity. They regard benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue—or regard them merely as resources for embellishment—without seeking their practical application. What benefit do they bring to the world? As for those in whom substantive character predominates, their hearts are sincere and their spirits upright and unyielding. Entirely natural and uncontrived, they are free of artificial embellishment. Yet some prize simplicity and plainness…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而略邊幅重本實而厭英華
雖隆雅敦朴確有古風亦未
必其通方達變盡宜於今而
傳於後也顧光明俊偉之業
非徒質直者所能成而樂聲
名喜詩書者又或鮮持執而
不足以遺大投艱惟本質而
===
濟之以文則碩輔竒勳胥此
出矣廣右古百粤地灕波桂
嶺蜿嬗磅礴清淑之氣于焉
鬱積人生其間率多悃愊直
抗無澆漓委靡之習蓋得之
天者甚厚自古然也我
國家以禮樂道化鼓鑄寰宇
punctuated:
而略邊幅，重本實而厭英華，雖隆雅敦朴，確有古風，亦未必其通方達變，盡宜於今而傳於後也。顧光明俊偉之業，非徒質直者所能成；而樂聲名、喜詩書者，又或鮮持執，而不足以遺大投艱。惟本質而濟之以文，則碩輔竒勳胥此出矣。
廣右古百粤地，灕波桂嶺，蜿嬗磅礴，清淑之氣于焉鬱積。人生其間，率多悃愊直抗，無澆漓委靡之習，蓋得之天者甚厚，自古然也。我國家以禮樂道化鼓鑄寰宇，
translation_en:
…and neglect outward decorum, valuing substantial foundations while disdaining refined expression. Although they esteem cultivated conduct and prize simplicity, and certainly possess the spirit of antiquity, they may not necessarily understand how to adapt to changing circumstances, be wholly suited to the present, or leave something worthy of transmission to posterity. Yet brilliant and outstanding achievements cannot be accomplished by straightforward sincerity alone. Those who delight in reputation and love poetry and books, meanwhile, may lack firm resolve and thus be unfit to be entrusted with great responsibilities and difficult undertakings. Only when substance forms the foundation and refinement complements it will eminent ministers and extraordinary accomplishments alike emerge.
Guangyou was anciently the land of the Hundred Yue. The waters of the Li and the ridges of Gui wind and spread in imposing grandeur [?]; here pure and beneficent vital energies gather in abundance. Those born amid them are generally sincere and forthright, free from habits of shallowness and lassitude. Their endowment from Heaven is indeed generous, and this has been so since antiquity. Our dynasty, through rites, music, and moral transformation, molds all under Heaven…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
文敎所被無遠弗届廣右人士
涵濡旣久蒸蒸嚮風而自奮
於同文之世者衆矣玆適大
比縱觀其所爲文類能採道
德之華掇仁義之精經術文
采寖與中土相埒夫士之悃
愊直抗天眞未斲固近道之
===
質大受之基也而又飾以文
學如此是猶楩楠豫章斲以
斧斤裹以藻繡必稱乎清廟
明堂之用昆吾干將淬以清
水斂以越砥何難于斷蛟剸
犀之功也哉由是知廣右之
士必將足以鳴世無疑矣且
punctuated: 文敎所被，無遠弗届。廣右人士涵濡旣久，蒸蒸嚮風，而自奮於同文之世者衆矣。玆適大比，縱觀其所爲文，類能採道德之華，掇仁義之精，經術文采寖與中土相埒。夫士之悃愊直抗，天眞未斲，固近道之質、大受之基也。而又飾以文學如此，是猶楩楠豫章，斲以斧斤，裹以藻繡，必稱乎清廟明堂之用；昆吾干將，淬以清水，斂以越砥，何難于斷蛟剸犀之功也哉？由是知廣右之士必將足以鳴世，無疑矣。且……
translation_en:
…Wherever its civilizing instruction reaches, no place is too distant to receive it. The scholars of Guangyou have long been steeped in this influence. Increasingly drawn to its example, many have exerted themselves in this age of a shared written culture. Now, on the occasion of the triennial Provincial Examination, a broad survey of their compositions shows that they generally can gather the blossoms of the Way and virtue and select the essence of benevolence and righteousness. Their classical learning and literary accomplishment are gradually coming to equal those of the central regions.

These scholars’ sincerity and upright resolve, their natural genuineness as yet unhewn, indeed constitute an innate disposition close to the Way and a foundation for bearing great responsibilities. Adorned, moreover, with literary learning such as this, they resemble fine pian, nan, and camphor timber: hewn with axes and hatchets and clothed in ornate embroidery, it will surely be fit for use in the pure ancestral temple and the Hall of Light. Or they resemble the swords Kunwu and Ganjiang: quenched in clear water and honed on whetstones from Yue, what difficulty would they have in cleaving dragons and slicing through rhinoceroses? From this we know beyond doubt that the scholars of Guangyou will surely be capable of winning renown in the world. Furthermore…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以天時地理人事稽之則兹
歲固氣運之獨盛者蓋廣右
輿地當天下西南西屬金而
南屬火歲在庚午庚為金而
午為火金以肅殺為義有武
道焉火以光明為象有文道
焉然金非能自為用也必鍛
===
之以火而後可以成器武非
可以獨用也必綏之以文而
後可以成治要皆相須而不
可缺者也兹地自成化以來
人習承平武備稍弛遂致醜
夷漸違聲教今
天子惻然南顧
punctuated: 以天時地理人事稽之，則兹歲固氣運之獨盛者。蓋廣右輿地當天下西南，西屬金而南屬火。歲在庚午，庚為金而午為火。金以肅殺為義，有武道焉；火以光明為象，有文道焉。然金非能自為用也，必鍛之以火而後可以成器；武非可以獨用也，必綏之以文而後可以成治。要皆相須而不可缺者也。兹地自成化以來，人習承平，武備稍弛，遂致醜夷漸違聲教。今天子惻然南顧，
translation_en: …examining it in terms of heavenly timing, earthly geography, and human affairs, this year is indeed one of exceptional flourishing in the workings of cosmic fortune. Guangyou occupies the southwest of the realm: the west corresponds to metal, and the south to fire. This is the gengwu year: geng corresponds to metal, and wu to fire. Metal signifies stern killing and thus embodies the martial way; fire takes brightness as its image and thus embodies the civil way. Yet metal cannot become useful of itself: it must be forged with fire before it can become an implement. Nor can military force be employed alone: it must be tempered by civil cultivation before orderly government can be achieved. In essence, the two depend upon one another, and neither can be dispensed with. Since the Chenghua reign, the people of this region have grown accustomed to peace, and military preparedness has gradually slackened. Consequently, the odious barbarians have increasingly defied the court’s authority and civilizing instruction. Now the Son of Heaven, moved by concern, turns his gaze southward…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
特命重臣爲經略計武功固期震
矣而又適當掄才之期所得
多士足以彰英華而賛治化
文武竝茂與地之西南歲之
庚午相爲符應其士之彬彬
稱盛也有由然矣爾諸士當
氣運之隆沐賓興之典毋徒
===
曰此足爲紆青拖紫服冕乗
軒之階也必即其飾之文者
篤之爲德行效之爲事功無
事則用文以綏太平如火之
足以長物有事則用武以戡
禍亂如金之足以收物斯無
負
punctuated: 特命重臣爲經略計，武功固期震矣。而又適當掄才之期，所得多士足以彰英華而賛治化。文武竝茂，與地之西南、歲之庚午相爲符應，其士之彬彬稱盛也有由然矣。爾諸士當氣運之隆，沐賓興之典，毋徒曰：「此足爲紆青拖紫、服冕乗軒之階也。」必即其飾之文者，篤之爲德行，效之爲事功。無事則用文以綏太平，如火之足以長物；有事則用武以戡禍亂，如金之足以收物。斯無負
translation_en:
…has specially commissioned a high minister to devise plans for strategic administration; military achievements are indeed expected to inspire awe. Moreover, this happens to coincide with the time for selecting talent. The many scholars obtained through this selection are sufficient to display outstanding refinement and assist government and moral transformation. Civil and military accomplishments flourish together, corresponding auspiciously to this southwestern region and the gengwu year. There is thus good reason why its scholars, combining refinement and substance, are acclaimed as flourishing.
You scholars, living at a height of auspicious fortune and receiving the honor of the ceremonial selection of worthy men, must not merely say: “This is sufficient as a stepping-stone to trailing blue and purple insignia, wearing ceremonial caps, and riding in dignitaries’ carriages.” You must take the literary cultivation that adorns you, deepen it into virtuous conduct, and give it practical effect in accomplishments. In peaceful times, employ civil arts to sustain peace, just as fire enables things to grow; in times of trouble, employ military force to quell calamity and disorder, just as metal enables things to be gathered in. Thus you will not fail…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盛時而亦有光斯典矣若脩之
家而用則鑿言於靜而庸或
違是巨樗液樠而被之翬文
曷堪負棟頑鉛鼓冶而鏤以
螭章奚逃缺折又何取于文
之足以鳴世也幷以是爲諸
士勗是舉也鎮守總兵官征
===
蠻將軍右都督俞大猷振揚
武衛雅重章縫副使鄭一龍
應存卓陳其樂邵惟中左叅
議龔大器僉事金柱皆綜理
于外共襄盛舉左叅將黃應
甲右叅將王世科遊擊將軍
丁山署都指揮僉事錢鳳翔
punctuated:
盛時，而亦有光斯典矣。若脩之家而用則鑿，言於靜而庸或違，是巨樗液樠而被之翬文，曷堪負棟？頑鉛鼓冶而鏤以螭章，奚逃缺折？又何取于文之足以鳴世也？幷以是爲諸士勗。
是舉也，鎮守總兵官征蠻將軍右都督俞大猷振揚武衛，雅重章縫。副使鄭一龍、應存卓、陳其樂、邵惟中，左叅議龔大器，僉事金柱，皆綜理于外，共襄盛舉。左叅將黃應甲、右叅將王世科、遊擊將軍丁山、署都指揮僉事錢鳳翔
translation_en:
…this flourishing age, and would also bring honor to this ceremony. If what one cultivates at home proves unsuitable in practice, and what one says in quiet moments is perhaps contradicted by one’s conduct [?], this is like a great, useless tree oozing resin, yet clothed in the splendid plumage of a pheasant: how could it support a roof beam? Or like base lead smelted and cast, then engraved with coiling dragons: how could it escape chipping and breaking? What value, then, is there in literary accomplishment sufficient to win renown in the world? I offer these words also as an exhortation to the scholars.
For this examination, Yu Dayou, Regional Commander, General Who Subdues the Man, and Chief Military Commissioner of the Right, invigorated the military defenses and held Confucian scholars in lasting esteem. Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zheng Yilong, Ying Cunzhuo, Chen Qile, and Shao Weizhong, Left Administration Assistant Gong Daqi, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Jin Zhu all managed affairs outside the examination compound and jointly assisted this grand undertaking. Left Assistant Regional Commander Huang Yingjia, Right Assistant Regional Commander Wang Shike, Mobile Corps Commander Ding Shan, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Qian Fengxiang…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
董龍王德懋皆捍禦于外與
有勤勞左布政使周寀右叅
政余敬中曹天祐以遷秩行
皆虔恭始事快覩人文者也
法得備書
江西贛州府儒學教授王燧
謹序
punctuated:
董龍、王德懋皆捍禦于外，與有勤勞。左布政使周寀、右叅政余敬中、曹天祐以遷秩行，皆虔恭始事，快覩人文者也，法得備書。
江西贛州府儒學教授王燧謹序。
translation_en:
…Dong Long and Wang Demao all provided defense outside and shared in the labors. Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhou Cai and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners Yu Jingzhong and Cao Tianyou departed upon promotion; all had attended reverently to the undertaking at its inception and rejoiced to witness the flourishing of literary culture. By convention, they may all be recorded here in full.
Preface respectfully written by Wang Sui, Professor of the Confucian School of Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年廣西鄕試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史李良臣〔直甫貴州普安衛籍直隸藍山縣人乙丑進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使郭應聘〔君賓福建莆田縣人庚戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政楊銓〔朝明直隸華亭縣人丙辰進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使萬思謙〔益甫江西南昌縣人丁未進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事楊文明〔仲謨江西南昌縣人壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
江西贛州府儒學教授王燧〔時用直隸丹徒縣人丙午貢士〕
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教諭陳冠〔子加直隸長洲縣人已酉貢士〕
同考試官
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正鐵世材〔用卿雲南永昌衛籍浙江杭州衛人甲子貢士〕
江西九江府湖口縣儒學教諭宋邦達〔士充福建莆田縣人辛酉貢士〕
湖廣荆州府松滋縣儒學教諭林獻芹〔獻忠廣東東莞縣人甲子貢士〕
福建建寧府政和縣儒學教諭梁幹〔秉楨廣東東莞縣人戊午貢士〕
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學教諭陳三俊〔懋績廣東南海縣人壬子貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年廣西鄕試

監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史李良臣〔直甫，貴州普安衛籍，直隸藍山縣人，乙丑進士〕。

提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使郭應聘〔君賓，福建莆田縣人，庚戌進士〕。
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政楊銓〔朝明，直隸華亭縣人，丙辰進士〕。

監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使萬思謙〔益甫，江西南昌縣人，丁未進士〕。
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事楊文明〔仲謨，江西南昌縣人，壬戌進士〕。

考試官
江西贛州府儒學教授王燧〔時用，直隸丹徒縣人，丙午貢士〕。
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教諭陳冠〔子加，直隸長洲縣人，已酉貢士〕。

同考試官
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正鐵世材〔用卿，雲南永昌衛籍，浙江杭州衛人，甲子貢士〕。
江西九江府湖口縣儒學教諭宋邦達〔士充，福建莆田縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
湖廣荆州府松滋縣儒學教諭林獻芹〔獻忠，廣東東莞縣人，甲子貢士〕。
福建建寧府政和縣儒學教諭梁幹〔秉楨，廣東東莞縣人，戊午貢士〕。
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學教諭陳三俊〔懋績，廣東南海縣人，壬子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangxi Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Longqing (1570)

Supervising Official
Li Liangchen, Investigating Censor on a surveillance tour of Guangxi, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in Pu'an Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Lanshan County, Zhili [?]. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yichou year.

Proctors
Guo Yingpin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Junbin, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.
Yang Quan, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Chaoming, was a native of Huating County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.

Examination Invigilators
Wan Siqian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Yifu, was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Yang Wenming, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Zhongmo, was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.

Examiners
Wang Sui, Instructor at the Confucian School of Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Shiyong, was a native of Dantu County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingwu year.
Chen Guan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Zijia, was a native of Changzhou County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar of the jiyou [?] year.

Associate Examiners
Tie Shicai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Yongqing, was registered in Yongchang Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Hangzhou Guard, Zhejiang. He was a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.
Song Bangda, Instructor at the Confucian School of Hukou County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Shichong, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.
Lin Xianqin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Songzi County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Xianzhong, was a native of Dongguan County, Guangdong, and a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.
Liang Gan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Zhenghe County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, courtesy name Bingzhen, was a native of Dongguan County, Guangdong, and a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Chen Sanjun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Maoji, was a native of Nanhai County, Guangdong, and a tribute scholar of the renzi year.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
廣西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷王化〔德成浙江桐鄉縣人監生〕
廣西等處提刑按察司經歷司知事王元吉〔汝旋浙江餘姚縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
桂林府知府馬濂〔濬卿直隸無錫縣人庚戌進士〕
梧州府知府陸一鵬〔應程浙江餘姚縣人丙辰進士〕
潯州府知府陳復升〔以見福建長樂縣人丙辰進士〕
受卷官
平樂府知府陳子佐〔道諟福建惠安縣人丙辰進士〕
===
南寧府知府林喬相〔廷翰福建晉江縣人壬戌進士〕
思恩軍民府知府張志淑〔在旌浙江臨海縣人甲午貢士〕
桂林府同知黎楚〔子立廣東番禺縣籍順德縣人丙午貢士〕
平樂府同知蔡萬〔一之福建晉江縣人己未進士〕
彌封官
慶遠府同知何世彥〔汝實雲南賓川州籍江西安縣人丙午貢士〕
桂林府推官王頤〔觀生湖廣沔陽衛籍直隸潜山縣人戊辰進士〕
桂林府全州知州方沆〔子及福建莆田縣人戊辰進士〕
梧州府容縣知縣張學顏〔子的廣東瓊山縣人乙丑進士〕
punctuated:
印卷官：
廣西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷王化〔德成，浙江桐鄉縣人，監生〕。
廣西等處提刑按察司經歷司知事王元吉〔汝旋，浙江餘姚縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：
桂林府知府馬濂〔濬卿，直隸無錫縣人，庚戌進士〕。
梧州府知府陸一鵬〔應程，浙江餘姚縣人，丙辰進士〕。
潯州府知府陳復升〔以見，福建長樂縣人，丙辰進士〕。

受卷官：
平樂府知府陳子佐〔道諟，福建惠安縣人，丙辰進士〕。

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直樊遲退見子夏
曰鄉也吾見於夫子而問知子曰舉直
錯諸枉能使枉者直何謂也子夏曰富
哉言乎
誠則明矣明則誠矣
思天下之民匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤
者若己推而內之溝中其自任以天下
===
之重如此
易
象曰地中有水師君子以容民畜衆
安節之亨承上道也
唯幾也故能成天下之務
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖
人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。樊遲退，見子夏，曰：「鄉也吾見於夫子而問知。子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。』何謂也？」子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」

誠則明矣，明則誠矣。

思天下之民，匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤者，若己推而內之溝中。其自任以天下之重如此。

易

象曰：「地中有水，師。君子以容民畜衆。」

安節之亨，承上道也。

唯幾也，故能成天下之務。

離也者，明也。萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.” Fan Chi withdrew and saw Zixia. He said, “Earlier I went to see the Master and asked about wisdom. The Master said, ‘Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.’ What does this mean?” Zixia said, “How rich in meaning these words are!”

Sincerity brings illumination; illumination brings sincerity.

He thought that if any man or woman among the people of the world had not received the blessings of Yao and Shun, it was as though he himself had pushed them into a ditch. Such was the weight of responsibility for the world that he took upon himself.

Book of Changes

The Image says: “Within the earth there is water: the Army hexagram. Thus the gentleman embraces the people and nurtures the multitude.”

The success of being at ease within limitations comes from following the way of those above.

Only through discerning the incipient signs of things can one accomplish the affairs of the world.

Li means brightness. All things become visible to one another; it is the hexagram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of the world and turns toward the light to govern, taking his model from this.

Book of Documents

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
九州攸同四隩既宅九山刋旅九川滌源
九澤既陂四海會同六府孔修庶土交
正底慎財賦咸則三壤成賦中邦
一曰貌二曰言三曰視四曰聽五曰思
先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則知小人之依
詩
九月肅霜十月滌場朋酒斯饗
夜如何其夜鄉晨庭燎有煇君子至止言
===
觀其旂
經營四方告成于王
思文后稷克配彼天立我烝民莫匪爾極
貽我來牟帝命率育無此疆爾界陳常
于時夏
春秋
冬十有二月齊侯鄭伯盟于石門〔隱公三年〕
遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕十有一月壬戌晉侯及

帝曰：「咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。」

夜如何其？夜鄉晨，庭燎有煇。君子至止，言觀其旂。
經營四方，告成于王。
思文后稷，克配彼天。立我烝民，莫匪爾極。貽我來牟，帝命率育。無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。

冬，十有二月，齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門。〔隱公三年〕
