translation_en:
The Emperor said: “Ah! You twenty-two men, be reverent! Assist in accomplishing Heaven’s work.”
The nine provinces were brought into accord; the lands in all four quarters were made habitable. The nine mountain ranges had their paths cleared and sacrifices offered; the nine rivers were cleared to their sources; the nine marshes were embanked. All within the Four Seas were united, and the six storehouses of resources were thoroughly put in order. The various lands were duly assessed in relation to one another, and resources and levies were carefully regulated. All followed the three grades of soil in determining the levies of the central realm.
The first is demeanor; the second, speech; the third, sight; the fourth, hearing; the fifth, thought.
First understand the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then take your ease; thus you will understand what the common people depend upon for their livelihood.
Book of Odes
In the ninth month the frost bites; in the tenth month they clear the threshing ground. With paired jars of wine they hold a feast.
How far has the night advanced? The night approaches dawn; the courtyard torches glow. The lords have arrived; behold their banners!
He set the four quarters in order and reported his achievement to the king.
Ah, cultured Hou Ji, worthy to be paired with Heaven! You established our teeming people; none fails to take you as the standard. You bequeathed us wheat and barley; at the Supreme Lord’s command, you nourished all. Without distinguishing this boundary from that border, you spread the enduring rule throughout this land of Xia.
Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, in the twelfth month, the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen. 〔Third year of Duke Yin.〕
They then attacked Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 In the eleventh month, on the renxu day, the Marquis of Jin and …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
秦伯戰于韓獲晉侯〔僖公十有五年〕
衞人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕公會晉侯宋公
衞侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔襄公十〕
〔有一年〕
春王正月季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋
人衞人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人
薛人杞人小邾人會吳于向〔襄公十有〕
〔四年〕
===
禮記
虞夏商周有師保有疑丞設四輔及三公
不必備唯其人語使能也
禮樂僨天地之情達神明之德降興上下
之神而凝是精粗之體領父子君臣之
節是故大人舉禮樂則天地將爲昭焉
百官得其宜萬事得其序
天地四方者男子之所有事也故必先有
志於其所有事然後敢用穀也
punctuated:
秦伯戰于韓，獲晉侯。〔僖公十有五年〕
衞人救陳。〔宣公十有二年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔襄公十〕〔有一年〕
春，王正月，季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衞人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人，會吳于向。〔襄公十有〕〔四年〕

禮記
虞、夏、商、周有師保，有疑丞，設四輔及三公，不必備，唯其人，語使能也。
禮樂僨天地之情，達神明之德，降興上下之神，而凝是精粗之體，領父子君臣之節。是故大人舉禮樂，則天地將爲昭焉，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
天地四方者，男子之所有事也。故必先有志於其所有事，然後敢用穀也。
translation_en:
…and the Earl of Qin fought at Han; the Marquis of Jin was captured. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xi.〕
The men of Wei came to Chen’s rescue. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh〕〔year of Duke Xiang.〕
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, Jisun Su and Shu Lao joined Shi Gai of Jin, men of Qi, Song, and Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, Xue, Qi, and Lesser Zhu to meet with Wu at Xiang. 〔Fourteenth〕〔year of Duke Xiang.〕

Record of Rites
Under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou there were Preceptors and Guardians, Counselors and Assistants. The Four Aides and the Three Dukes were established, but these offices did not all have to be filled: what mattered was finding the right people. This speaks of employing the capable.
Rites and music [encompass?] the essential nature of Heaven and Earth, give expression to the potency of spiritual beings, bring down and raise up the spirits above and below, unite the forms of the subtle and the gross, and govern the proper relationships between father and son and between ruler and minister. Thus, when the great man puts rites and music into practice, Heaven and Earth will thereby become manifest, the hundred officials will each find their proper place, and all affairs will find their proper order.
Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters are the spheres in which a man has duties to perform. Therefore, he must first set his mind upon those duties before he dares to consume grain.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
文武維后書稱乃武乃文為天下君蓋
文以致太平武以戡禍亂其道不可偏
廢也周之盛王訪範叙疇卜洛作誥車
攻簡閱吉日蒐獮傳之至今以為稱美
者可得聞其詳歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝廓清區夏禮備樂和
成祖文皇帝汛掃夷荒論經討藝
文德武功古今獨盛迨我
世宗肅皇帝入承
===
大統
謨烈重光誠如昔人所謂文武並用長久之道
也我
皇上正位嗣服丕闡
鴻猷如建元一
詔制並典謨
郊社一議祀從周禮與首
臨太學日
御經筵皆以隆稽古右文之治也頒
punctuated: 「文武維后」，《書》稱「乃武乃文」為天下君，蓋文以致太平，武以戡禍亂，其道不可偏廢也。周之盛王，訪範叙疇，卜洛作誥，《車攻》簡閱，《吉日》蒐獮，傳之至今以為稱美者，可得聞其詳歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝廓清區夏，禮備樂和；成祖文皇帝汛掃夷荒，論經討藝，文德武功，古今獨盛。迨我世宗肅皇帝入承大統，謨烈重光，誠如昔人所謂「文武並用，長久之道」也。我皇上正位嗣服，丕闡鴻猷。如建元一詔，制並典謨；郊社一議，祀從周禮；與首臨太學，日御經筵，皆以隆稽古右文之治也。頒
translation_en:
…“Civil and martial qualities make a sovereign”; the Book of Documents speaks of being “both martial and cultured” as ruler of all under Heaven. Civil governance brings about great peace, while military power quells calamity and disorder: neither way may be neglected. The illustrious kings of Zhou consulted about the Great Plan and set its categories in order, divined the site at Luo and composed proclamations, inspected troops as described in “Chariots Are Sturdy,” and conducted hunts as described in “Auspicious Day.” These deeds have been transmitted to the present as worthy of praise. May we hear their particulars?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao cleared and pacified the Chinese realm, perfected ritual, and brought music into harmony. Emperor Chengzu Wen swept clean the distant lands of non-Chinese peoples, discussed the classics, and investigated the classical arts. Their civil virtue and military achievements were unrivaled, past or present. When our Emperor Shizong Su succeeded to the imperial line, his plans and accomplishments renewed that glory. This was truly what men of old called “employing civil and military means together—the way to enduring rule.”

Our present emperor has taken his rightful position and succeeded to the imperial charge, magnificently unfolding his grand designs. His edict inaugurating the reign era rivaled the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents in its composition; his deliberation on the suburban sacrifices and the sacrifices to the altars of soil established worship in accordance with the Rites of Zhou. Together with his first visit to the Imperial University and his daily attendance at the Classics Colloquium, these all serve to exalt a government that examines antiquity and honors civil learning. Promulgating…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖諭以飭邊圉采羣議以
簡邊才與
躬親大閱
勅理軍儲均以粛詰戎訓武之規也
聖文
神武章顯炳耀固人人可得而揄揚矣其與
祖宗竝古盛王果相符合歟諸士子涵濡
德化必有明于文武之道可爲
今日獻助者願詳陳之將以轉
===
聞于
上
問斯道之在天下未甞一日而無統自孔
子敘書斷自唐虞故稽斯道之統者必
昉于堯舜若精一執中之傳帝王之心
法無以加矣嗣是而禹湯文武下逮孔
子遞相傳授所見于孟子終篇之敘與
韓愈原道之論有灼鑑矣然孟子謂堯
舜之道竝傳于湯而禹之見知但爲聞
punctuated:
聖諭以飭邊圉，采羣議以簡邊才，與躬親大閱，勅理軍儲，均以粛詰戎訓武之規也。聖文神武，章顯炳耀，固人人可得而揄揚矣。其與祖宗竝古盛王果相符合歟？諸士子涵濡德化，必有明于文武之道、可爲今日獻助者，願詳陳之，將以轉聞于上。

問：斯道之在天下，未甞一日而無統。自孔子敘書，斷自唐虞，故稽斯道之統者，必昉于堯舜。若精一執中之傳，帝王之心法無以加矣。嗣是而禹、湯、文、武，下逮孔子，遞相傳授，所見于孟子終篇之敘與韓愈原道之論，有灼鑑矣。然孟子謂堯舜之道竝傳于湯，而禹之見知但爲聞
translation_en:
…sacred instructions to put the frontier defenses in order, soliciting opinions to select capable men for frontier service, personally conducting a grand military review, and ordering the management of military provisions: all these measures serve to enforce rigorous standards for military preparedness and martial training. His Majesty’s sagely civil accomplishments and divine martial prowess shine forth brilliantly; everyone can indeed extol them. But do they truly accord with those of his ancestors and the flourishing sage kings of antiquity? You candidates have been steeped in his transforming virtue. Surely some among you understand the Way of civil and military governance and can offer useful assistance at this time. Please set forth your views in detail, so that they may be forwarded to His Majesty.

Question: Since this Way has existed in the world, not a single day has passed without its line of transmission. When Confucius arranged the Book of Documents, he began with Tang and Yu—the reigns of Yao and Shun. Thus those who investigate the transmission of this Way must begin with Yao and Shun. As for the transmitted teaching to remain discerning and single-minded and to hold fast to the Mean, nothing can surpass it as the teaching of the mind for emperors and kings. Thereafter, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, down to Confucius, transmitted it in succession. The account in the concluding chapter of the Mencius and the discussion in Han Yu’s Inquiry into the Way provide clear testimony to this. Yet Mencius says that the Way of both Yao and Shun was transmitted to Tang, while Yu’s knowledge through seeing was merely knowledge through hearing…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知之自得湯之傳者文王而已而武且
不與也原道則謂堯傳于舜舜傳于禹
禹傳于湯湯傳于文武互有不同何歟
萊朱散宜生之徒言行略無可見孟子
乃亦及之說者謂見知不過爲聞知之
羽翼不必其人之名世也然禹亦以見
知列焉豈禹果無得統之傳歟若謂見
知聞知果有軒輊于其間也則見知文
武之道者莫如周公矣乃置之不言而
===
===
顧及于宜生也抑又何歟繼孔子者孟
子古今無異論矣然謂顏氏曾氏獨得
其宗何無與于統與將謂顏曾見知于
孔子則孟子宜居于聞知矣其叙以見
知自命何歟孟子之後建圖屬書默契
道體如濂溪者誠足以嗣統矣而伊川
乃直屬之明道謂孟子之後一人斯豈
無其故歟繼周程者莫如朱子元儒亦
嘗以集諸儒之大成許之矣顧今爲良
punctuated: 知之自得。湯之傳者，文王而已，而武且不與也。《原道》則謂堯傳于舜，舜傳于禹，禹傳于湯，湯傳于文武，互有不同，何歟？萊朱、散宜生之徒，言行略無可見，孟子乃亦及之。說者謂見知不過爲聞知之羽翼，不必其人之名世也。然禹亦以見知列焉，豈禹果無得統之傳歟？若謂見知、聞知果有軒輊于其間也，則見知文武之道者莫如周公矣，乃置之不言，而顧及于宜生也，抑又何歟？繼孔子者，孟子，古今無異論矣。然謂顏氏、曾氏獨得其宗，何無與于統與？將謂顏、曾見知于孔子，則孟子宜居于聞知矣，其叙以見知自命，何歟？孟子之後，建圖屬書、默契道體如濂溪者，誠足以嗣統矣。而伊川乃直屬之明道，謂孟子之後一人，斯豈無其故歟？繼周、程者，莫如朱子。元儒亦嘗以集諸儒之大成許之矣。顧今爲良
translation_en:
…personal attainment through knowledge acquired by hearing [?]. The one who received Tang’s transmission was King Wen alone; even King Wu was not included. Yet Inquiry into the Way states that Yao transmitted it to Shun, Shun to Yu, Yu to Tang, and Tang to Kings Wen and Wu. Why do these accounts differ?

Virtually nothing can be found concerning the words and deeds of such men as Lai Zhu and San Yisheng, yet Mengzi mentions them too. Commentators say that those who knew through seeing merely assisted those who knew through hearing, and need not themselves have been figures renowned in their age. Yet Yu is also listed among those who knew through seeing. Could Yu really have failed to receive the transmission of the succession to the Way? If knowing through seeing and knowing through hearing truly differ in rank, then no one surpassed the Duke of Zhou in knowing the Way of Kings Wen and Wu through seeing. Why, then, does Mengzi leave him unmentioned, yet mention Yisheng?

That Mengzi succeeded Kongzi is a judgment undisputed from antiquity to the present. Yet it is said that Master Yan and Master Zeng alone grasped the essential teaching. Why, then, have they no share in this succession? If one argues that Yan and Zeng knew through seeing Kongzi, then Mengzi ought to belong among those who knew through hearing. Why does he describe himself in his account as one who knew through seeing?

After Mengzi, a man such as Lianxi, who composed a diagram and writings and tacitly apprehended the substance of the Way, was surely worthy to continue the succession. Yet Yichuan assigned it directly to Mingdao, calling him the one man since Mengzi. Surely there was a reason for this? No one surpassed Master Zhu as successor to Zhou and the Cheng brothers. Scholars of the Yuan also praised him for bringing together the great achievements of the various Confucian masters. Yet those today who pursue the learning of innate knowing …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知之學者又若于陸氏有取何歟諸士
平日仰止既有定見折衷必有定說願
爲我告焉
問學者所以稽往轍訓來禩者必考信於
典籍粤自書契既造載籍蔚興唐虞而
上厥有五典三墳夏商以來爰著九丘
八索至周方策大備國家之所職掌學
士大夫之所誦習彬彬然稱盛矣然仲
尼刪述六經垂世立教而墳典丘索多
===
刪而不錄焉豈盡荒誕而無足采與抑
他固有說與秦政不綱燔滅文章以愚
黔首漢興學校廣求異書西漢則有總
羣書而奏七略者東漢則有依七略而
爲書部者其校讎討論諸賢可得聞其
槩乎逮六朝唐宋諸君雖趣舍不倫而
亦多重圖籍宋有別撰七志者梁有更
爲七錄者皆遞相祖述整比卷帙例之
兩漢何似也唐修羣書四部宋作崇文
punctuated:
知之學者，又若于陸氏有取，何歟？諸士平日仰止，既有定見，折衷必有定說，願爲我告焉。

問：學者所以稽往轍、訓來禩者，必考信於典籍。粤自書契既造，載籍蔚興，唐虞而上，厥有五典三墳；夏商以來，爰著九丘八索。至周，方策大備，國家之所職掌，學士大夫之所誦習，彬彬然稱盛矣。然仲尼刪述六經，垂世立教，而墳典丘索多刪而不錄焉，豈盡荒誕而無足采與？抑他固有說與？秦政不綱，燔滅文章，以愚黔首。漢興學校，廣求異書，西漢則有總羣書而奏七略者，東漢則有依七略而爲書部者，其校讎討論，諸賢可得聞其槩乎？逮六朝唐宋，諸君雖趣舍不倫，而亦多重圖籍。宋有別撰七志者，梁有更爲七錄者，皆遞相祖述，整比卷帙，例之兩漢何似也？唐修羣書四部，宋作崇文
translation_en:
…those who pursue the learning of innate knowing nevertheless seem to find something worth adopting in Master Lu’s teachings. Why is this? You gentlemen already have settled views concerning those whom you habitually admire; surely you also have definite conclusions for adjudicating these matters. I ask you to explain them to me.

Question: Scholars, in examining the paths of the past and providing instruction for future years, must establish what is trustworthy through the canonical writings and other records. Ever since writing was invented, written records have flourished. From the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and earlier, there were the Five Canons and Three Tombs; from the Xia and Shang onward, the Nine Mounds and Eight Cords appeared. By the Zhou, written records were abundantly complete. Those in the charge of the state and those recited and studied by scholars and scholar-officials displayed a flourishing literary culture. Yet when Zhongni edited and transmitted the Six Classics, establishing teachings for later generations, he excluded much of the Tombs, Canons, Mounds, and Cords. Were these entirely fantastical, with nothing worth selecting? Or was there some other explanation?

The government of Qin abandoned proper order and burned and destroyed writings to keep the common people ignorant. The Han established schools and sought out uncommon books far and wide. Under the Western Han, someone brought the collected books together and submitted the Seven Epitomes; under the Eastern Han, someone arranged books into divisions following the Seven Epitomes. May I hear from you gentlemen an outline of their work in collating texts and critically examining them?

By the Six Dynasties, Tang, and Song, although rulers differed in what they favored and rejected, many valued maps and books. Under the Song, someone separately compiled the Seven Treatises; under the Liang, someone in turn produced the Seven Records. Each successively followed earlier models, arranging and ordering the volumes. How did these compare with the work of the two Han dynasties? The Tang compiled the Four Divisions of Collected Books, and the Song produced the Chongwen…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
總目皆分曹綜緝甄明科部例之宋梁
孰優也夫六經修自仲尼厄於秦火古
今惜之漢唐宋藝文志簡編最爲博洽
然說者謂六經未嘗亡而遞考歷代所
載之書十已亡其六七此又何說也抑
吾儒博綜羣籍當必有窮本知要之學
不繫於篇帙之存亡與多士其詳著于
篇以爲稽古考文者采焉
問粵西自入中國版圖迨漢聲敎漸被繇
===
是英才挺生代有作者乃今究觀人物
之林蓋有世業春秋持論識大體者有
擊猺有功民咸頌德者有保障南土無
愧竇融者有淑問得竟人稱爲臯陶者
有不畏彊禦立收常侍暴客者有條對
水旱明于陰陽大義者斯皆漢氏之良
也在唐則持節者開擴化外掇科者抗
言謝歸糾義者助平交趾斯寥寥矣宋
之人材最著故有雄才壯猷受知英主
punctuated:
總目，皆分曹綜緝，甄明科部，例之宋梁，孰優也？夫六經修自仲尼，厄於秦火，古今惜之。漢唐宋藝文志，簡編最爲博洽，然說者謂六經未嘗亡，而遞考歷代所載之書，十已亡其六七，此又何說也？抑吾儒博綜羣籍，當必有窮本知要之學，不繫於篇帙之存亡與？多士其詳著于篇，以爲稽古考文者采焉。
問：粵西自入中國版圖，迨漢聲敎漸被，繇是英才挺生，代有作者。乃今究觀人物之林，蓋有世業春秋，持論識大體者；有擊猺有功，民咸頌德者；有保障南土，無愧竇融者；有淑問得竟，人稱爲臯陶者；有不畏彊禦，立收常侍暴客者；有條對水旱，明于陰陽大義者。斯皆漢氏之良也。在唐則持節者開擴化外，掇科者抗言謝歸，糾義者助平交趾，斯寥寥矣。宋之人材最著，故有雄才壯猷，受知英主
translation_en:
…General Catalogue: in both undertakings, scholars were assigned to separate groups to compile the works comprehensively and distinguish their subject divisions clearly. Compared with the compilations of the Song and Liang dynasties, which were superior? The Six Classics were edited by Zhongni [Confucius] and suffered disaster in the Qin book burning, a loss lamented in ancient and modern times. The bibliographical treatises of the Han, Tang, and Song histories are exceptionally comprehensive in their coverage of writings. Yet some maintain that the Six Classics were never lost, whereas successive examination of the books recorded under the various dynasties shows that six or seven out of ten have already disappeared. How, then, is this to be explained? Or must we Confucian scholars, in our comprehensive study of books, possess a learning that probes their foundations and grasps their essentials, independent of the survival or loss of particular volumes? You candidates should set this out fully in your essays, so that those who investigate antiquity and examine its writings may draw upon them.
Question: After western Yue [Guangxi] entered the territory of China, the civilizing influence of imperial teaching gradually reached it by Han times. Outstanding talents consequently emerged, and every age produced men of achievement. Now, surveying these ranks of notable men closely, we find one who pursued the study of the Spring and Autumn Annals as a family tradition and showed an understanding of larger principles in his arguments; one whose meritorious campaigns against the Yao won universal praise for his virtue among the people; one who safeguarded the southern lands and could stand comparison with Dou Rong; one whose fine reputation reached fulfillment [?], whom people called Gao Yao; one who did not fear the powerful and immediately arrested a violent retainer of a Palace Attendant; and one who submitted itemized responses concerning floods and droughts, displaying a clear understanding of the great principles of yin and yang. These were all worthy men of the Han. Under the Tang, a bearer of the imperial credentials extended imperial influence into lands beyond its civilizing reach; a successful examination candidate spoke out boldly and took his leave to return home; and a man who rallied loyal forces helped pacify Jiaozhi. Such men were few indeed. The Song was most distinguished for its talented men: thus there was one whose outstanding abilities and grand designs won the recognition of an enlightened ruler…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聲績獨光于中外者有獻書議政作牧
遺思竝見褒于大儒者有少稱神童進
爲名御史者有疏陳廟謨退無忝于倫
魁者有知昌化著循良之績者有爲講
讀多啓沃之功者而三爲舉首裒然號
名執政尤有中立不倚之操焉可得而
悉數其人歟
國家景運隆興鴻彦輩出或疏停夷貢以寬
民力或臨鑿庾嶺以裨綱運或討邊夷
===
而滇人沐其猷或懲席寵而黔酋伏其
法或躋樞筦而時以文學稱或列上卿
而人以完名羨或崇勛勁節退居東湖
或醇德清風令終桂里或柄大政定大
策而奠安社稷之功居多之數君子者
雖所樹立不同然皆炳灼顯著斯
列聖煕洽之鍾而粤壤羽儀之表也諸士亦嘗
稽其名實否乎願品列之以觀尚友之
學
punctuated:
聲績獨光于中外者，有獻書議政、作牧遺思，竝見褒于大儒者，有少稱神童、進爲名御史者，有疏陳廟謨、退無忝于倫魁者，有知昌化、著循良之績者，有爲講讀、多啓沃之功者，而三爲舉首、裒然號名執政，尤有中立不倚之操焉。可得而悉數其人歟？
國家景運隆興，鴻彦輩出。或疏停夷貢以寬民力，或臨鑿庾嶺以裨綱運，或討邊夷而滇人沐其猷，或懲席寵而黔酋伏其法，或躋樞筦而時以文學稱，或列上卿而人以完名羨，或崇勛勁節、退居東湖，或醇德清風、令終桂里，或柄大政、定大策，而奠安社稷之功居多。之數君子者，雖所樹立不同，然皆炳灼顯著，斯列聖煕洽之鍾，而粤壤羽儀之表也。諸士亦嘗稽其名實否乎？願品列之，以觀尚友之學。
translation_en:
…whose reputation and achievements shone with exceptional brilliance both within the court and beyond it. There were those who submitted writings to discuss government and left fond memories through their service as prefects, earning praise on both counts from great Confucian scholars; those acclaimed as child prodigies who advanced to become renowned investigating censors; those who presented memorials on court policy and, in retirement, remained worthy of their distinction as foremost examination graduates; those who governed Changhua and established a record of benevolent administration; and those who served as court lecturers and readers and did much to enlighten the sovereign. One who placed first in the examinations three times and rose to prominence as a celebrated chief councillor displayed, above all, an integrity that remained upright and impartial. Could all these men possibly be enumerated?
With the glorious flourishing of our dynasty’s auspicious fortunes, outstanding worthies have emerged in succession. Some memorialized to halt tribute missions from foreign peoples, easing the burdens on the populace; some supervised the cutting of a passage through the Yu Ridge to facilitate convoy transport; some campaigned against frontier peoples, and the people of Yunnan benefited from their plans; some punished those who presumed upon imperial favor, and the chieftains of Guizhou submitted to their law. Some rose to high military office and were acclaimed in their time for literary learning; some ranked among the high ministers and were admired for their untarnished reputations. Some, distinguished by great merit and steadfast integrity, retired to Donghu; some, possessed of pure virtue and an unblemished reputation, ended their days honorably in their native Guangxi. Some wielded the highest authority and settled great questions of policy, contributing especially much to securing the altars of soil and grain. Although these gentlemen differed in what they accomplished, all were illustrious and distinguished. They embodied the accumulated blessings of the successive sage emperors’ harmonious rule and stood as exemplary figures of the Guangxi region. Have you gentlemen ever examined their reputations and actual achievements? Please assess and enumerate them, so that we may see your learning in taking the worthy men of the past as friends.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
問嶺表疆域土猺叛服不常爲患非一日
矣今
皇上軫念南服
特簡重臣兼發
內帑俾興問罪之師誠地方一大幸也文武
將吏欽承
威命師出有期第兵無常形謀貴豫定容可不
熟爲之計乎夫曲道相伏險阨相薄雖
有長技將安所施則我師有過險之虞
===
矣當其未入也何以使敵不得據險以
扼我耶巢穴盤據徑路紆廻一夫當關
誰與爲敵在彼有負險之守矣及其既
入也何以使敵不得恃險以持我耶或
謂調狼兵以制諸猺從其素所畏也又
有謂狼難敎練惟善搜剿而不長于捍
禦狼可純用否與或謂立土司以控諸
猺欲其有所屬也又有謂民近縣治猶
可馴擾而未可以盡棄土司可純任否
punctuated: 問：嶺表疆域，土猺叛服不常，爲患非一日矣。今皇上軫念南服，特簡重臣，兼發內帑，俾興問罪之師，誠地方一大幸也。文武將吏欽承威命，師出有期。第兵無常形，謀貴豫定，容可不熟爲之計乎？夫曲道相伏，險阨相薄，雖有長技，將安所施？則我師有過險之虞矣。當其未入也，何以使敵不得據險以扼我耶？巢穴盤據，徑路紆廻，一夫當關，誰與爲敵？在彼有負險之守矣。及其既入也，何以使敵不得恃險以持我耶？或謂調狼兵以制諸猺，從其素所畏也。又有謂狼難敎練，惟善搜剿，而不長于捍禦。狼可純用否與？或謂立土司以控諸猺，欲其有所屬也。又有謂民近縣治，猶可馴擾，而未可以盡棄。土司可純任否
translation_en:
Question: In the territory south of the mountains, the local Yao alternate unpredictably between rebellion and submission; they have caused trouble for many a day. Now His Majesty, concerned for the southern domains, has specially selected a high minister and also released funds from the imperial treasury to launch a punitive expedition. This is indeed a great blessing for the region. The civil and military commanders and officials reverently obey his august command, and a date has been set for the army’s departure. Yet warfare has no fixed form, and plans are best settled in advance. Can we fail to deliberate thoroughly upon this undertaking?

On winding paths, enemies lie in ambush; at dangerous defiles, opposing forces press upon one another. Even if we possess particular military strengths, where can we employ them? Our army thus faces the danger of traversing difficult terrain. Before it enters, how can we prevent the enemy from occupying the defiles to block us? They are entrenched in their lairs, and the paths twist and turn. With a single man holding a pass, who can stand against him? The enemy thus has defensive positions protected by difficult terrain. Once our army has entered, how can we prevent the enemy from relying on that terrain to hold us in check?

Some propose deploying lang troops to subdue the various Yao groups, employing those whom they have always feared. Others say that lang troops are difficult to instruct and train: they excel only at searching out and destroying the enemy, but are not adept at defense. Can we rely exclusively on lang troops? Some propose establishing native officials to control the various Yao groups, intending thereby to place them under an authority. Others say that people living near county seats can still be brought under orderly rule and should not all be relinquished. Can responsibility be entrusted exclusively to native officials…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與昔人有輕騎至壁賊衆迎降者有盛
夏行師大破賀州者有用來保之兵而
殲夷脩荔劇寇者有率田州之旅而蕩
掃斷藤諸猺者其所以經略於先區畫
於後已試之明效抑可倣而行之與爾
諸士負桑梓之憂於制禦之方講之必
熟尚明言之以爲進取之助
punctuated: 與？昔人有輕騎至壁，賊衆迎降者；有盛夏行師，大破賀州者；有用來保之兵，而殲夷脩荔劇寇者；有率田州之旅，而蕩掃斷藤諸猺者。其所以經略於先、區畫於後，已試之明效，抑可倣而行之與？爾諸士負桑梓之憂，於制禦之方講之必熟，尚明言之，以爲進取之助。
translation_en: …? In former times, some rode with light cavalry to the enemy’s fortifications, where the rebels came out to surrender; some campaigned in high summer and won a great victory at Hezhou; some employed the troops of Laibao [?] to annihilate the formidable bandits of Xiu and Li; and some led the forces of Tianzhou to sweep away the various Yao groups at Duanteng. Might their methods of strategic planning beforehand and arranging affairs afterward, whose effectiveness has already been demonstrated, be emulated and put into practice? You scholars bear concern for your native country and must have thoroughly studied methods of controlling and defending against these adversaries. Set these forth clearly, so that they may aid our advance.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人五十五名
第一名洪敷誥臨桂縣學生易
第二名彭啓忠南寧府學生詩
第三名史著勳桂林府學增廣生書
第四名秦延緒臨桂縣學生春秋
第五名徐雱臨桂縣學生禮記
第六名朱寬臨桂縣學生易
第七名伍睿全州學生書
===
第八名李宜春臨桂縣學增廣生詩
第九名梁岱南寧府學生易
第十名鄧一元灌陽縣學生詩
第十一名張言馬平縣學增廣生書
第十二名張文錦古田縣學增廣生春秋
第十三名吳大有柳州府學生詩
第十四名陳善政柳州府學生書
第十五名蔣增全州學生禮記
第十六名莊宇毅容縣儒學訓導易
punctuated:
中式舉人五十五名。

第一名，洪敷誥，臨桂縣學生，易。
第二名，彭啓忠，南寧府學生，詩。
第三名，史著勳，桂林府學增廣生，書。
第四名，秦延緒，臨桂縣學生，春秋。
第五名，徐雱，臨桂縣學生，禮記。
第六名，朱寬，臨桂縣學生，易。
第七名，伍睿，全州學生，書。
第八名，李宜春，臨桂縣學增廣生，詩。
第九名，梁岱，南寧府學生，易。
第十名，鄧一元，灌陽縣學生，詩。
第十一名，張言，馬平縣學增廣生，書。
第十二名，張文錦，古田縣學增廣生，春秋。
第十三名，吳大有，柳州府學生，詩。
第十四名，陳善政，柳州府學生，書。
第十五名，蔣增，全州學生，禮記。

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直樊遲退見子夏
曰鄉也吾見於夫子而問知子曰舉直
錯諸枉能使枉者直何謂也子夏曰富
哉言乎
洪敷誥
同考試官教諭梁批場中作富哉言乎毎難著語獨
此作瑩徹含畜且論舉錯有關治道取之豈徒以其文耶
===
考試官教諭陳批典雅純正宜式多士
考試官教授王批說理明盡
聖人一言盡仁知之道而惟賢者識其大也蓋
仁知合一聖言之所以為大也子夏因遲之問
而嘆之也有以哉夫子之告樊遲意以愛人知
人仁知之理固然也子有疑焉盍觀用舎之道
乎彼天下有直者焉知而舉之與天下共舉之
也有枉者焉知而錯之與天下共錯之也斯則
道之所在吾以道公是非而天下以榮以辱位
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。」樊遲退，見子夏，曰：「鄉也，吾見於夫子而問知。子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。』何謂也？」子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」

洪敷誥

同考試官教諭梁批：場中作「富哉言乎」，毎難著語。獨此作瑩徹含畜，且論舉錯有關治道，取之豈徒以其文耶？

考試官教諭陳批：典雅純正，宜式多士。

考試官教授王批：說理明盡。

聖人一言，盡仁知之道，而惟賢者識其大也。蓋仁知合一，聖言之所以為大也。子夏因遲之問而嘆之也，有以哉！夫子之告樊遲，意以愛人知人，仁知之理固然也。子有疑焉，盍觀用舎之道乎？彼天下有直者焉，知而舉之，與天下共舉之也；有枉者焉，知而錯之，與天下共錯之也。斯則道之所在，吾以道公是非，而天下以榮以辱；位
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.” Fan Chi withdrew and met Zixia, saying: “Earlier I went to see the Master and asked about wisdom. The Master said, ‘Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.’ What does this mean?” Zixia said: “How rich these words are!”

Hong Fugao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: In the examination hall, candidates writing on “How rich these words are!” generally find it difficult to give the phrase adequate expression. This composition alone is lucid and rich in implication. Moreover, its discussion of promoting and setting aside men bears upon the Way of government. Could its selection have been merely for its literary merits?

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Classical and elegant, pure and correct; it should serve as a model for the many scholars.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Its exposition of principle is clear and exhaustive.

In a single utterance the sage fully expressed the Way of benevolence and wisdom, yet only a worthy man recognized its greatness. For the unity of benevolence and wisdom is what makes the sage’s words great. Zixia had good reason to express his admiration upon hearing Fan Chi’s question! In instructing Fan Chi, the Master meant that loving others and knowing others are indeed the principles of benevolence and wisdom. If you have doubts about this, why not consider the Way of employing men and setting them aside? There are upright men in the world: to recognize and promote them is to promote them together with all under Heaven. There are crooked men: to recognize and set them aside is to set them aside together with all under Heaven. Thus, where the Way is concerned, I use the Way to judge right and wrong impartially, and thereby those under Heaven receive honor or disgrace; as for official position …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之所在吾以位公進退而天下以勸以懲謂不
能使枉者直乎是夫子之言已合仁知而一之
矣何遲猶未之達也乃退而問於子夏焉蓋徒
知舉錯爲知人之事而不知化枉兼愛人之仁
矣子夏聞而嘆之曰富哉言乎蓋語此而遺彼
者辭之及也有盡言近而指遠者意之貫也無
窮今觀夫子之言舉直者官人之哲也而因以
化枉則言不止於知焉帝王所以弘錫類之機
者在是矣洋洋乎其天下之至言耶錯枉者絀
===
惡之明也而因可使直則知不足以盡焉帝王
所以溥曲成之化者寓是矣優優乎其天下之
善言耶吁一仁知也自夫子發之寓其意於用
舍之間自子夏聞之會其理於言辭之表遲也
可以自悟矣抑考知人則哲能官人安民則惠
黎民懷之是仁知之道固帝王致治之要也然
理本一致機實相通知人而因以化人知之未
始不仁也愛人而不必徧愛仁之未始不知也
仁知交相爲用而聖人舉錯之化益明矣學者
punctuated:
之所在，吾以位公進退，而天下以勸以懲，謂不能使枉者直乎？是夫子之言已合仁知而一之矣，何遲猶未之達也？乃退而問於子夏焉。蓋徒知舉錯爲知人之事，而不知化枉兼愛人之仁矣。子夏聞而嘆之曰：「富哉言乎！」蓋語此而遺彼者，辭之及也有盡；言近而指遠者，意之貫也無窮。今觀夫子之言，舉直者，官人之哲也，而因以化枉，則言不止於知焉。帝王所以弘錫類之機者在是矣，洋洋乎其天下之至言耶！錯枉者，絀惡之明也，而因可使直，則知不足以盡焉。帝王所以溥曲成之化者寓是矣，優優乎其天下之善言耶！

吁！一仁知也，自夫子發之，寓其意於用舍之間；自子夏聞之，會其理於言辭之表。遲也可以自悟矣。抑考「知人則哲，能官人；安民則惠，黎民懷之」，是仁知之道固帝王致治之要也。然理本一致，機實相通。知人而因以化人，知之未始不仁也；愛人而不必徧愛，仁之未始不知也。仁知交相爲用，而聖人舉錯之化益明矣。學者
translation_en:
…where rank is concerned, I use rank impartially in advancing and dismissing men, so that all under Heaven receive encouragement or admonition. Can one say that this cannot make the crooked straight? Thus the Master's words already unite benevolence and wisdom as one. Why had Chi still not understood them? He therefore withdrew and questioned Zixia. He knew only that promoting and setting aside men were matters of discerning people; he did not understand that transforming the crooked also embraced the benevolence of loving people. Hearing this, Zixia exclaimed: “How rich these words are!” When speech addresses one thing and omits another, its reach is limited; when words concern what is near but point to what is distant, their meaning extends without end. Now consider the Master's words: promoting the upright shows the discernment needed to appoint men to office. Yet when this also transforms the crooked, his words extend beyond wisdom alone. Here lies the means by which emperors and kings spread goodness to others of their kind. How vast—are these not the most consummate words in all under Heaven? Setting aside the crooked shows the clear judgment needed to dismiss the wicked. Yet when this can also make them upright, wisdom alone cannot encompass its meaning. Here resides the means by which emperors and kings extend their transforming influence, bringing each to fulfillment according to its particular circumstances. How ample—are these not the finest words in all under Heaven?

Ah! Benevolence and wisdom are one. When the Master expressed this, he lodged his meaning in the employment and dismissal of men; when Zixia heard it, he grasped the principle beyond the words themselves. Chi could thereby come to understand it for himself. Moreover, consider the saying: “To discern men is to be wise, and thus able to appoint men to office; to bring peace to the people is to be benevolent, and the common people cherish such a ruler.” The way of benevolence and wisdom is indeed essential to how emperors and kings achieve good government. Yet their principle is fundamentally one, and their workings are interconnected. To discern people and thereby transform them: such wisdom is never without benevolence. To love people without necessarily loving everyone indiscriminately: such benevolence is never without wisdom. Benevolence and wisdom work through one another, and the transforming influence of the sage's promotions and dismissals becomes all the clearer. Those who study…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
合而觀之始得
誠則明矣明則誠矣
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋批發明天人一致之旨詳盡無遺
可謂實學有得者矣宜錄之
考試官教諭陳批清順不凡
考試官教授王批理精詞暢
中庸申言誠明合一之妙勉人以求誠也蓋誠
之與明本一貫之理也故觀於終之極致又豈
===
可以異視哉中庸望人以求誠也意謂天人之
分雖異而性教之歸則同是故自誠而明者非
曰既誠而猶有俟于明也蓋純此理之謂誠明
特誠之精焉耳苟真實無妄者既完于降衷之
初則真知不眩者自通于於穆之表誠之復焉
實體之渾涵合萬物於兼照也誠之通焉實用
之流行斯萬理於無遺也誠之所至明自至焉
殆與天道之貞觀一其機矣所謂聖人之性者
非耶自明而誠者非曰既明而終有歉于誠也
punctuated:
合而觀之，始得。
誠則明矣，明則誠矣。
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋批：發明天人一致之旨，詳盡無遺，可謂實學有得者矣，宜錄之。
考試官教諭陳批：清順不凡。
考試官教授王批：理精詞暢。
中庸申言誠明合一之妙，勉人以求誠也。蓋誠之與明，本一貫之理也。故觀於終之極致，又豈可以異視哉？中庸望人以求誠也，意謂天人之分雖異，而性教之歸則同。是故自誠而明者，非曰既誠而猶有俟于明也。蓋純此理之謂誠，明特誠之精焉耳。苟真實無妄者既完于降衷之初，則真知不眩者自通于於穆之表。誠之復焉，實體之渾涵，合萬物於兼照也；誠之通焉，實用之流行，斯萬理於無遺也。誠之所至，明自至焉，殆與天道之貞觀一其機矣。所謂聖人之性者，非耶？自明而誠者，非曰既明而終有歉于誠也。
translation_en:
…Only by considering them together can one attain understanding.

“Sincerity brings illumination; illumination brings sincerity.”

Shi Zhuxun

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “He elucidates the purport of the unity of Heaven and humanity thoroughly, leaving nothing out. He may indeed be said to have gained understanding through substantial learning. This should be selected.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Clear and fluent, and out of the ordinary.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Precise in principle and flowing in expression.”

The Doctrine of the Mean further explains the subtle unity of sincerity and illumination, encouraging people to seek sincerity. Sincerity and illumination are fundamentally governed by one continuous principle. Thus, viewed at their ultimate culmination, how could they be regarded as different? The Doctrine of the Mean hopes that people will seek sincerity. Its meaning is that, although Heaven and humanity are distinct, nature and instruction converge upon the same end.

Thus, proceeding from sincerity to illumination does not mean that, once sincere, one must still await illumination. Sincerity means being pure in this principle; illumination is simply the refined essence of sincerity. If what is true and free from falsity is already complete at the initial bestowal of our inmost nature, then true knowledge, free from confusion, naturally penetrates beyond the profound mystery. In sincerity’s return, its real substance embraces all things within its comprehensive illumination; in sincerity’s free operation, its real functioning flows forth, encompassing every principle without omission [?]. Wherever sincerity reaches, illumination naturally reaches as well: its workings are virtually one with the constant manifestation of the Way of Heaven. Is this not what is called the nature of the sage? Proceeding from illumination to sincerity does not mean that, once illuminated, one must ultimately remain deficient in sincerity.…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
蓋知此理之謂明誠固明之真焉耳苟至明察
其幾有見于萬境之皆徹則反躬踐其實庶幾
于一真之自如善吾明矣而身之誠者不由于
外鑠也知吾致矣而意之誠者無俟于他求也
明之所至誠亦至焉殆與聖人之至誠同其道
矣所謂賢人之教者非耶是知誠則明者性盡
而教無不立也明則誠者教行而性亦可盡也
性教殊名而天人一致誠之者奚容以自諉乎
大抵誠明本一理性教無二機而所以統之者
===
心也故吾性之知爲良知吾性之能爲良能此
誠卽此明也此明亦此誠也而命之爲性脩之
爲教特隨在而異其名耳君子大其心以體之
則合天人通性教而一以貫之矣夫然後足以
語盡性之學
思天下之民匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤
者若已推而內之溝中其自任以天下
之重如此
彭啓忠
punctuated:
蓋知此理之謂明，誠固明之真焉耳。苟至明察其幾，有見于萬境之皆徹，則反躬踐其實，庶幾于一真之自如。善吾明矣，而身之誠者不由于外鑠也；知吾致矣，而意之誠者無俟于他求也。明之所至，誠亦至焉，殆與聖人之至誠同其道矣。所謂賢人之教者，非耶？是知誠則明者，性盡而教無不立也；明則誠者，教行而性亦可盡也。性教殊名，而天人一致，誠之者奚容以自諉乎？大抵誠明本一理，性教無二機，而所以統之者，心也。故吾性之知爲良知，吾性之能爲良能。此誠卽此明也，此明亦此誠也。而命之爲性，脩之爲教，特隨在而異其名耳。君子大其心以體之，則合天人、通性教，而一以貫之矣。夫然後足以語盡性之學。

思天下之民，匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤者，若已推而內之溝中，其自任以天下之重如此。

彭啓忠
translation_en:
…For understanding this principle is called illumination; sincerity is simply the genuineness of illumination. If, through utmost illumination, one discerns the subtle beginnings and perceives all circumstances with complete clarity, then one turns back upon oneself and puts this into practice, approaching a state of undivided genuineness that comes naturally. Once I have understood goodness, sincerity in my person does not result from something imposed from outside; once I have extended my knowledge fully, sincerity in my intentions requires no further seeking elsewhere. Wherever illumination reaches, sincerity also reaches: its way is surely the same as the sage’s utmost sincerity. Is this not what is meant by the teaching through which one becomes worthy?

Thus we know that becoming illuminated through sincerity means fully realizing one’s nature, so that teaching is established in every respect; becoming sincere through illumination means putting teaching into practice, so that one’s nature can likewise be fully realized. Nature and teaching have different names, but Heaven and humanity are of one accord. How, then, could those striving for sincerity excuse themselves from the task? In general, sincerity and illumination are fundamentally one principle, and nature and teaching do not operate through two different processes. What unifies them is the mind. Thus the knowing inherent in my nature is innate knowledge, and the capacity inherent in my nature is innate ability. This sincerity is precisely this illumination, and this illumination is also precisely this sincerity. What is conferred is called nature; its cultivation is called teaching. These are merely different names according to the aspect concerned. If the gentleman enlarges his mind to embody this, he unites Heaven and humanity, links nature and teaching, and comprehends them through a single thread. Only then is he qualified to discuss the learning that fully realizes one’s nature.

“Thinking of the people of the world, if any ordinary man or woman had not received the blessings of Yao and Shun, he felt as though he himself had pushed them into a ditch. Such was the weight of responsibility for the world that he took upon himself.”

Peng Qizhong

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正鐵批〔伊尹自任澤民意思發揮清暢〕
〔雋永是深知尹之心者錄之〕
考試官教諭陳批〔發明親切〕
考試官教授王批〔詞意貫徹〕
觀聖人憂天下之心其所自任者大矣蓋天生
聖人為天下計也尹以天下為已責肯自貶以
求行其道耶孟氏推之以曉萬章所以辨要湯
之惑也若曰聖人之任天下也以道其憂天下
也以心伊尹以天民自待矣其為心果何如耶
===
蓋尹既以堯舜之道樂諸已必思以堯舜之澤
被諸人故其為心也舉斯世斯民之衆咸欲濟
之而無遺雖匹夫匹婦之微所以憂之為甚切
一有不被其澤是吾之道有未行也誠若由已
之溺而思所以拯其危者不容以不亟矣一有
不獲其所是吾之責有未盡也誠若溝中之納
而思所以措之安者不能以自遑矣尹之為心
如此是其心先天下之憂視一人之身為天下
之身也躋斯世而唐虞之而後其願始慰焉道
punctuated:
同考試官學正鐵批〔伊尹自任澤民意思，發揮清暢，〕〔雋永，是深知尹之心者，錄之。〕
考試官教諭陳批〔發明親切。〕
考試官教授王批〔詞意貫徹。〕
觀聖人憂天下之心，其所自任者大矣。蓋天生聖人，為天下計也。尹以天下為已責，肯自貶以求行其道耶？孟氏推之以曉萬章，所以辨要湯之惑也。若曰：聖人之任天下也以道，其憂天下也以心。伊尹以天民自待矣，其為心果何如耶？
蓋尹既以堯舜之道樂諸已，必思以堯舜之澤被諸人。故其為心也，舉斯世斯民之衆，咸欲濟之而無遺。雖匹夫匹婦之微，所以憂之為甚切。一有不被其澤，是吾之道有未行也，誠若由已之溺，而思所以拯其危者，不容以不亟矣。一有不獲其所，是吾之責有未盡也，誠若溝中之納，而思所以措之安者，不能以自遑矣。尹之為心如此，是其心先天下之憂，視一人之身為天下之身也。躋斯世而唐虞之，而後其願始慰焉。道
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Tie, School Instructor: 〔The idea that Yi Yin took upon himself the responsibility of bringing blessings to the people is developed clearly and fluently,〕〔with enduring savor. This writer deeply understands Yi Yin’s heart. Selected for inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔The exposition is apt and direct.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: 〔The language and ideas are coherent throughout.〕
When we consider the sage’s concern for all under Heaven, how great is the responsibility he takes upon himself! Heaven brings forth sages for the sake of all under Heaven. Yi Yin regarded the world as his own responsibility: would he willingly debase himself to secure the practice of his Way? Mengzi expounded this to enlighten Wan Zhang, thereby dispelling the mistaken belief that Yi Yin sought Tang’s favor. It is as though he said: the sage undertakes responsibility for all under Heaven through the Way, and cares for all under Heaven with his heart. Yi Yin regarded himself as one of Heaven’s people. What, then, was his heart truly like?
Since Yi Yin delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun within himself, he necessarily wished to extend the blessings of Yao and Shun to others. Thus, in his heart, he wished to aid the entire multitude of people in his age, leaving none behind. Even for an ordinary man or woman of humble standing, his concern was deeply earnest. If even one person failed to receive those blessings, he thought, “My Way has yet to be fully put into practice.” It was truly as though he himself had caused that person to drown; his efforts to find a means of rescue from danger could admit no delay. If even one person failed to find a proper place, he thought, “My responsibility has yet to be fully discharged.” It was truly as though he himself had thrust that person into a ditch; in thinking how to bring that person to safety, he could allow himself no repose. Such was Yi Yin’s heart. His heart anticipated the sorrows of all under Heaven, and he regarded his own person as belonging to all under Heaven. Only after raising his age to the condition of the reigns of Tang Yao and Yu Shun would his aspiration find fulfillment. The Way…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
濟天下之溺視宇宙之事爲分內之事也盡斯
民而知覺之而後其責始塞焉甽畝藏脩之時
萬物一體之懷已素具矣敢曰天下至大也非
一已所能獨任而欲諉之於人耶詩書誦說之
日父母天下之心已素存矣敢曰天下之民至
衆也非一人所能兼濟而不以任之於已耶吁
惟其所志者大則所以自視者必不小惟其所
任者重則所以自待者必不輕割烹要湯之說
何其妄歟大抵人有不爲而後可以有爲尹當
===
耕莘之時惟知以堯舜之道自樂而萬鍾千駟
不足以動其中者志定故也故幡然而起以堯
舜君民爲已任而卒成撥亂反正之功豈偶然
哉宋儒謂伊尹格天事業始於一介取與信矣
是故君子貴辨志之學
易
象曰地中有水師君子以容民畜衆
朱寬
同考試官教諭梁 批 體認容民畜衆精確明切萬選
punctuated:
濟天下之溺，視宇宙之事爲分內之事也。盡斯民而知覺之，而後其責始塞焉。甽畝藏脩之時，萬物一體之懷已素具矣，敢曰天下至大也，非一已所能獨任，而欲諉之於人耶？詩書誦說之日，父母天下之心已素存矣，敢曰天下之民至衆也，非一人所能兼濟，而不以任之於已耶？吁！惟其所志者大，則所以自視者必不小；惟其所任者重，則所以自待者必不輕。割烹要湯之說，何其妄歟！大抵人有不爲，而後可以有爲。尹當耕莘之時，惟知以堯舜之道自樂，而萬鍾千駟不足以動其中者，志定故也。故幡然而起，以堯舜君民爲已任，而卒成撥亂反正之功，豈偶然哉？宋儒謂伊尹格天事業始於一介取與，信矣！是故君子貴辨志之學。

易
象曰：「地中有水，師。君子以容民畜衆。」
朱寬
同考試官教諭梁批：「體認容民畜衆，精確明切，萬選
translation_en:
…rescues all under Heaven from drowning, regarding the affairs of the universe as matters within his own duty. Only after awakening all these people to understanding would his responsibility be fulfilled. While living in seclusion and cultivating himself amid the fields, he already possessed the conviction that all things form one body. Would he dare say that the world was too vast for him alone to shoulder its burdens, and seek to shift them onto others? While reciting and discussing the Odes and the Documents, he already harbored the resolve to act as a parent to all under Heaven. Would he dare say that the people of the world were too numerous for one person to aid them all, and therefore decline to take responsibility himself? Ah! Because his aspirations were great, his estimation of himself could not be small; because his responsibilities were weighty, his expectations of himself could not be slight. How absurd is the claim that he sought access to Tang by butchering and cooking!

In general, only by refusing to do certain things can a person accomplish others. When Yi Yin was plowing at Shen, he knew only to delight in the Way of Yao and Shun. Neither a stipend of ten thousand zhong of grain nor a thousand teams of four horses could stir his heart, because his resolve was fixed. Thus he rose decisively, taking as his own responsibility the transformation of ruler and people according to the example of Yao and Shun, and ultimately accomplished the work of ending disorder and restoring proper rule. Could this have been accidental? The Song Confucians said that Yi Yin’s Heaven-moving achievements began with his scruples about accepting or giving even the smallest thing. True indeed! For this reason, the gentleman values the learning that clarifies his resolve.

Book of Changes
The Image Commentary says: “Within the earth there is water: The Army. The gentleman accordingly embraces the people and nurtures the multitude.”
Zhu Kuan
Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of embracing the people and nurturing the multitude is precise, clear, and incisive. Selected from ten thousand [?]…”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
詞氣清爽可為多士式矣
考試官教諭陳批詞理明暢高薦允宜
考試官教授王批詞不煩而意足
易具寓兵之象君子有足兵之政焉夫兵不外
于民也君子政在容民而兵寓焉其善於體師
者乎今夫坤象為地坎象為水地中有水則是
大順之內至險伏焉至靜之中不測藏焉師之
象也君子體之以為水固險也而不外于地兵
雖眾也又寧有外于民乎於是大其撫字之恩
===
而囿黎庶于安全因以寓夫即戎之勢擴其怙
冒之澤而阜羣生于樂育有以豫乎敵愾之資
制之田里教之樹畜凡以厚民之生也而有勇
之眾於此畜焉不出乎深耕易耨之中所以為
折衝禦侮者有其具矣出入相友守望相助凡
以奠民之居也而有制之兵由此畜焉不越乎
同溝共井之外所以為攻堅擊銳者有其人矣
當其無事則比閭族黨之夫此民也亦此兵也
而所養皆所用未有被吾之惠而不捍吾之患
punctuated:
詞氣清爽，可為多士式矣。
考試官教諭陳批：詞理明暢，高薦允宜。
考試官教授王批：詞不煩而意足。
易具寓兵之象，君子有足兵之政焉。夫兵不外于民也，君子政在容民，而兵寓焉，其善於體師者乎！今夫坤象為地，坎象為水，地中有水，則是大順之內至險伏焉，至靜之中不測藏焉，師之象也。君子體之，以為水固險也，而不外于地；兵雖眾也，又寧有外于民乎？於是大其撫字之恩，而囿黎庶于安全，因以寓夫即戎之勢；擴其怙冒之澤，而阜羣生于樂育，有以豫乎敵愾之資。制之田里，教之樹畜，凡以厚民之生也，而有勇之眾於此畜焉。不出乎深耕易耨之中，所以為折衝禦侮者有其具矣。出入相友，守望相助，凡以奠民之居也，而有制之兵由此畜焉。不越乎同溝共井之外，所以為攻堅擊銳者有其人矣。當其無事，則比閭族黨之夫，此民也，亦此兵也，而所養皆所用，未有被吾之惠而不捍吾之患
translation_en:
…The diction and tone are clear and fresh; this can serve as a model for the many candidates.
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: The diction and reasoning are lucid and fluent. A high recommendation is entirely fitting.
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: The wording is economical, yet the meaning is fully conveyed.
The Book of Changes contains an image of keeping military forces within the populace; the gentleman accordingly has a policy for ensuring sufficient troops. Soldiers do not exist apart from the people. The gentleman’s government consists in embracing the people, and military forces reside among them. Is this not skill in embodying the meaning of Shi, the Army hexagram?
Now Kun represents earth, and Kan represents water. Water within the earth means that the utmost danger lies concealed within the utmost compliance, and the unfathomable is hidden within the utmost stillness. This is the image of the Army. The gentleman embodies it, considering that water is indeed dangerous, yet does not exist apart from the earth. Though soldiers are numerous, how could they exist apart from the people? Thus he extends his nurturing kindness, keeping the common people in safety, and thereby incorporates the capacity to take up arms. He enlarges his protective beneficence and enables all the people to flourish under his joyful nurture, thereby preparing the resources for confronting the enemy.
He regulates their fields and settlements and teaches them planting and animal husbandry. All this enriches the people’s livelihood, while a courageous host is nurtured therein. Without going beyond deep plowing and diligent weeding, the means to repel attacks and resist aggression are already in place. They befriend one another in their comings and goings and assist one another in keeping watch. All this secures the people’s homes, while a disciplined army is nurtured thereby. Without going beyond those who share irrigation ditches and well-field units, the men needed to assault strong positions and strike elite troops are already available.
In peaceful times, the men organized into neighborhood groups—bi, lü, zu, and dang—are these same people and these same soldiers. All those nurtured are those employed in service. Never has there been anyone who received my bounty yet failed to defend me against calamity…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者也及其有事則伍兩卒旅之衆此兵也亦此
民也而所用皆所養未有沐吾之仁而不用吾
之命者也是民雖非爲衆而容衆實以容民而
畜矣其與地中有水者何異哉吁君子其善于
體師之象矣抑是成周之制也卒乘起於井田
軍法寓於蒐狩國無養兵之費民無徵調之煩
所以建久安長治之道者良有由也後世作丘
甲履畝稅兵農始分而爲二焉踐卒材官之紛
紜府兵彍騎之迭變其於畜衆之義大相遠矣
===
安得舉容民之政而行之乎
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖
人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
洪敷誥
同考試官教諭梁批順題發揮不求雕刻而典雅春
融洗脫俗套且以南面嚮明串講尤爲灼見錄之
考試官教諭陳批融粹精切深於易學者
考試官教授王批精潔
punctuated:
者也。及其有事，則伍兩卒旅之衆，此兵也，亦此民也，而所用皆所養，未有沐吾之仁而不用吾之命者也。是民雖非爲衆，而容衆實以容民而畜矣。其與地中有水者何異哉？吁！君子其善于體師之象矣！抑是成周之制也，卒乘起於井田，軍法寓於蒐狩，國無養兵之費，民無徵調之煩，所以建久安長治之道者，良有由也。後世作丘甲，履畝稅，兵農始分而爲二焉。踐卒材官之紛紜，府兵彍騎之迭變，其於畜衆之義大相遠矣。安得舉容民之政而行之乎？

離也者，明也。萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。

洪敷誥

同考試官教諭梁批：順題發揮，不求雕刻，而典雅春融，洗脫俗套；且以南面嚮明串講，尤爲灼見。錄之。

考試官教諭陳批：融粹精切，深於易學者。

考試官教授王批：精潔。
translation_en:
…there are none who do so. When trouble arises, the men organized into squads, platoons, companies, and battalions are soldiers, yet they are also these same people. Those we employ are all those we have nurtured: none who have received our benevolence will fail to obey our commands. Although these people do not constitute a military host for its own sake [?], the host is indeed nurtured by embracing the people. How does this differ from water within the earth? Ah! How well the gentleman embodies the image of the Army hexagram!

This, moreover, was the system of the perfected Zhou order. Infantry and chariot forces arose from the well-field system, and military discipline was incorporated into seasonal hunts. The state incurred no expense in maintaining troops, and the people suffered no vexation from conscription and mobilization. There was sound reason why this established the way to lasting peace and enduring order. In later ages, armor levies were imposed on land units and taxes assessed by the mu; soldiers and farmers then began to separate into two groups. Amid the proliferation of rotating-service soldiers [?] and trained fighting men, and the successive transformations of the militia system and expanded cavalry forces, the principle of nurturing the host became remote indeed. How might we put into practice the government that embraces the people?

“Li means brightness. All things become visible to one another; it is the trigram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern: he takes his model from this.”

Hong Fugao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: He develops the meaning in accordance with the topic, seeking no elaborate ornamentation, yet achieving classical elegance and the warmth of spring, free of conventional formulas. Moreover, his connected exposition of ‘facing south’ and ‘turning toward the light’ shows particularly clear insight. Selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Harmonious, pure, refined, and precise—the work of someone deeply versed in the study of the Book of Changes.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Refined and clean.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
大傳釋後天之離顯於造化而成於治功也蓋
離位乎南化之所由顯也然則聖人之治天下
謂不有取於此哉說卦論物之隨帝以出也至
此蓋謂帝不可見也而必見于物物不自見也
而相見乎離是豈無謂哉蓋離也者適維新之
會而彰明盛之休有明之義焉萬物至此則始
出者悉呈其象而發榮滋長之勢煥乎其莫掩
也潔齊者皆流其形而宣著盛大之機勃乎其
愈彰也所以然者離位正南四時之氣盛於夏
===
而此有以當其會五行之用著于火而此有以
司其權夫固物之所由相見而離之所以爲明
也聖人之治不有取爾乎吾見恭己以正南面
體統于此乎尊也而向離明之地因以顯夫文
明之治功禮樂明備天地將爲之昭矣正位以
臨天下皇極于是乎建也而御陽明之方于以
敷乎休明之治教經緯有章人文自爲之煥矣
其在造化則帝歷于南而光輝之象以著其在
聖化則位向乎南而丕顯之治以昭萬民之利
punctuated:
大傳釋後天之離，顯於造化而成於治功也。蓋離位乎南，化之所由顯也。然則聖人之治天下，謂不有取於此哉？《說卦》論物之隨帝以出也，至此蓋謂帝不可見也，而必見于物；物不自見也，而相見乎離。是豈無謂哉？蓋離也者，適維新之會，而彰明盛之休，有明之義焉。萬物至此，則始出者悉呈其象，而發榮滋長之勢，煥乎其莫掩也；潔齊者皆流其形，而宣著盛大之機，勃乎其愈彰也。所以然者，離位正南，四時之氣盛於夏，而此有以當其會；五行之用著于火，而此有以司其權。夫固物之所由相見，而離之所以爲明也。
聖人之治，不有取爾乎？吾見恭己以正南面，體統于此乎尊也，而向離明之地，因以顯夫文明之治功。禮樂明備，天地將爲之昭矣。正位以臨天下，皇極于是乎建也，而御陽明之方，于以敷乎休明之治教。經緯有章，人文自爲之煥矣。其在造化，則帝歷于南，而光輝之象以著；其在聖化，則位向乎南，而丕顯之治以昭。萬民之利
translation_en:
The Great Commentary explains the Li trigram in the Later Heaven arrangement: it manifests itself in the processes of creation and transformation and finds fulfillment in the achievements of government. Li occupies the south, where transformation becomes manifest. Can it then be said that the sage draws nothing from this in governing the realm? The Discussion of the Trigrams describes how things emerge in accordance with the Lord on High. At this point, its meaning is that the Lord on High cannot be seen, yet necessarily becomes visible through things; things do not make themselves visible, but become mutually visible in Li. Surely this is not without significance! Li marks the moment of renewal and displays the blessings of luminous abundance; hence its meaning of brightness. When the myriad things reach this stage, those just emerging all reveal their appearance, and their burgeoning growth shines forth irrepressibly. Those that have become pure and well ordered all unfold their forms, and their impulse toward manifest abundance grows ever more vigorously apparent. This is because Li occupies due south: the vital energies of the four seasons flourish in summer, and Li presides over their convergence; the workings of the Five Phases become manifest in fire, and Li exercises authority over them. This is indeed how things become mutually visible and why Li signifies brightness.
Does not the sage’s government draw upon this? I see him compose himself reverently and take his proper place facing south, thereby exalting the dignity of sovereign order. Facing the region of Li’s brightness, he thus manifests the achievements of enlightened government. With rites and music clearly established and fully provided, Heaven and Earth will shine because of them. He takes his rightful position to preside over the realm, thereby establishing the sovereign standard. Ruling from the direction of yang brightness, he spreads the governance and instruction of an auspicious, enlightened reign. With the warp and weft of government duly patterned, human culture naturally shines forth. In creation and transformation, the Lord on High passes through the south, and the image of radiance becomes manifest; in the sage’s transforming influence, his position faces south, and resplendent government shines forth. The benefit to the myriad people…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
見不猶夫萬物之相見矣乎謂之曰蓋取諸此
信乎觀萬物而識化工之神因氣化而得法天
之治後天之離其合天人而一之者乎而圖位
之妙可知矣雖然天道以離為用而必役之以
坤蓋氣之盛也不節則過焉故得坤以成其冲
和也聖人以明照四方苟明之過焉則傷于察
故有其明而不自用其明者亦所以培元氣而
代天工也書曰明作有功惇大成裕固敷政法
天竝行不悖之道也斯又繼離者之所當知
===
書
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋批辭旨春融渾厚虞廷都俞氣
象宛然在目
考試官教諭陳批詞理精到
考試官教授王批典則可誦
聖君總敕羣臣欲其敬以相天事焉蓋庶官所
治皆天事也敬以相之臣職其無忝乎帝舜所
punctuated:
見，不猶夫萬物之相見矣乎？謂之曰「蓋取諸此」，信乎！觀萬物而識化工之神，因氣化而得法天之治，後天之離，其合天人而一之者乎！而圖位之妙可知矣。雖然，天道以離為用，而必役之以坤，蓋氣之盛也，不節則過焉，故得坤以成其冲和也。聖人以明照四方，苟明之過焉，則傷于察，故有其明而不自用其明者，亦所以培元氣而代天工也。《書》曰：「明作有功，惇大成裕。」固敷政法天竝行不悖之道也。斯又繼離者之所當知。

書
帝曰：「咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。」
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋批：「辭旨春融渾厚，虞廷都俞氣象宛然在目。」
考試官教諭陳批：「詞理精到。」
考試官教授王批：「典則可誦。」

聖君總敕羣臣，欲其敬以相天事焉。蓋庶官所治，皆天事也。敬以相之，臣職其無忝乎！帝舜所
translation_en:
…being seen by the myriad people—is this not like the myriad things becoming visible to one another? To say, “They probably took this as their model,” is indeed justified! By observing the myriad things, one recognizes the wondrous workings of creation; through the transformations of qi, one discovers how to govern in imitation of Heaven. Does not Li in the Later Heaven arrangement unite Heaven and humanity as one? Thus one can understand the subtlety of the positions in the diagram. Nevertheless, although the Way of Heaven operates through Li, it must employ Kun to regulate it. For qi at its height will become excessive unless restrained; with Kun, it attains balanced harmony. The sage illuminates the four quarters with his insight, but if that insight becomes excessive, it does harm through over-scrutiny. Thus, possessing insight without relying exclusively upon it is also a means of nurturing primordial qi and performing Heaven’s work on its behalf. The Book of Documents says, “Enlightened action brings achievement; generosity and greatness produce ample ease.” These are indeed complementary ways of administering government and modeling oneself on Heaven. This, too, is what those who carry forward the work of Li should understand.

Book of Documents
The Emperor said: “Ah! You twenty-two men, be reverent! Thereby assist in accomplishing Heaven’s work.”
Shi Zhuxun
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “The language and meaning have the warmth of spring and are full and substantial. The atmosphere of approving exchanges at Shun’s court appears vividly before one’s eyes.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The language and reasoning are precise and thoroughly developed.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Classical and exemplary, worthy of recitation.”

The sage ruler issued a collective admonition to his ministers, wishing them to assist reverently in Heaven’s affairs. For all that the various officials administer is Heaven’s business. If they assist in it reverently, surely they will not disgrace their duties as ministers! As for Emperor Shun’s …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以總勅羣臣者意曰人君之所畏者惟天而已
而所賴以事天者惟臣而已咨汝二十有二人
也詔之官聯固有崇卑之異秩而辨其官守實
皆天事之攸關者也是必恪共乃職而有嚴有
翼于以克相乎上帝之宜敬爾有官而無怠無
荒于以奉若乎上天之載四岳敬於內治也而
羣牧亦敬於外治焉兢兢然合志以賛化工俾
天職之分布於所司者日奏咸熈之績斯巳矣
百揆敬于統理也而庶官亦敬于分理焉業業
===
然一德以調元化俾天事之責成於有位者日
見明作之功斯巳矣勳庸之舊著者當因夫天
功之既亮而敬以圖厥終也蓋造化無全能而
待人以成其能雖欽翼以承之猶恐範圍之用
未弘也可以怠心處之乎責任之方新者當成
夫天功之初亮而敬以虔其始也蓋天道無全
功而待人以成其功雖祗慎以圖之猶恐有相
之道未盡也可以慢心乘之乎是則敬以盡職
而因以事天信乎臣道有關於天道也爾羣臣
punctuated: 以總勅羣臣者，意曰：「人君之所畏者，惟天而已；而所賴以事天者，惟臣而已。咨！汝二十有二人也，詔之官聯，固有崇卑之異秩；而辨其官守，實皆天事之攸關者也。是必恪共乃職，而有嚴有翼，于以克相乎上帝之宜；敬爾有官，而無怠無荒，于以奉若乎上天之載。四岳敬於內治也，而羣牧亦敬於外治焉，兢兢然合志以賛化工，俾天職之分布於所司者，日奏咸熈之績，斯巳矣。百揆敬于統理也，而庶官亦敬于分理焉，業業然一德以調元化，俾天事之責成於有位者，日見明作之功，斯巳矣。勳庸之舊著者，當因夫天功之既亮，而敬以圖厥終也。蓋造化無全能，而待人以成其能，雖欽翼以承之，猶恐範圍之用未弘也，可以怠心處之乎？責任之方新者，當成夫天功之初亮，而敬以虔其始也。蓋天道無全功，而待人以成其功，雖祗慎以圖之，猶恐有相之道未盡也，可以慢心乘之乎？是則敬以盡職，而因以事天，信乎臣道有關於天道也。爾羣臣
translation_en:
…in issuing his general injunction to the assembled ministers, his meaning was: “What a ruler stands in awe of is Heaven alone; those upon whom he relies to serve Heaven are his ministers alone. Ah, you twenty-two men! In the coordinated offices to which you have been appointed [?], there are indeed distinctions of higher and lower rank; yet, when we distinguish the duties of each office, all are in fact bound up with Heaven’s affairs. You must therefore discharge your duties with scrupulous reverence, solemnly and cautiously, so that you may assist in fulfilling what the Lord on High ordains. Be reverent in your offices, neither indolent nor negligent, so that you may obediently carry out the work of Heaven above.

“The Four Chiefs must be reverent in governing within, and the regional governors must likewise be reverent in governing without. Vigilantly uniting their purposes to assist the work of transformation, they must ensure that the duties of Heaven distributed among their respective charges daily yield achievements of universal prosperity: that is all. The Chief Minister must be reverent in overall administration, and the various officials must likewise be reverent in administering their particular responsibilities. Cautiously united in virtue to harmonize the primal process of transformation, they must ensure that Heaven’s affairs, entrusted for fulfillment to those holding office, daily show the results of enlightened action: that is all.

“Those whose meritorious service has long been manifest should build upon the assistance already rendered to Heaven’s work and reverently seek to bring it to completion. For the creative and transforming powers of nature cannot exercise their capacities fully by themselves, but await human beings to bring those capacities to fulfillment. Even when we support them with reverence and caution, we still fear that our work of ordering and encompassing them has not been sufficiently extensive. Can we approach this with an indolent mind?

“Those whose responsibilities are newly assumed should bring to fulfillment the assistance just begun for Heaven’s work, reverently and devoutly attending to its inception. For the Way of Heaven cannot complete its work by itself, but awaits human beings to bring that work to fulfillment. Even when we pursue it with reverence and care, we still fear that we have not exhausted the ways of assisting it. Can we undertake this with a negligent mind?

“Thus, through reverence you fulfill your duties and thereby serve Heaven. Truly, the way of the minister is bound up with the Way of Heaven. You assembled ministers…”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盍亦是務乎甞觀易以財成輔相歸之元后而
此以亮天功者責之臣何耶蓋君道有心而無
為而岳牧九官之臣所賴以理庶職猶之天道
無心而成化而四時五行之吏所資以成歲功
也然則帝舜之命君道也亦天道也厥後皐陶
陳知人之謨而亦以人代天工責之有虞之君
臣交儆以事天者固如此
先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則知小人之依
伍睿
===
同考試官教諭宋批周公告成王本旨發明精切錄之以式
考試官教諭陳批鬯達
考試官教授王批雅飭有文
大臣原君子恤民之故見無逸之所自也夫民
之所重者稼穡也君子知其難而體之奚暇以
自逸耶周公告成王意若曰天下之事未始不
成於勤而荒於逸者也君子所以能無逸者何
哉誠以君位至逸也稼穡至艱難也惟不知其
punctuated:
盍亦是務乎？甞觀《易》以財成輔相歸之元后，而此以亮天功者責之臣，何耶？蓋君道有心而無為，而岳牧九官之臣所賴以理庶職；猶之天道無心而成化，而四時五行之吏所資以成歲功也。然則帝舜之命，君道也，亦天道也。厥後皐陶陳知人之謨，而亦以人代天工責之有虞之君，臣交儆以事天者固如此。
先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
伍睿
同考試官教諭宋批：周公告成王本旨，發明精切，錄之以式。
考試官教諭陳批：鬯達。
考試官教授王批：雅飭有文。
大臣原君子恤民之故，見無逸之所自也。夫民之所重者，稼穡也。君子知其難而體之，奚暇以自逸耶？周公告成王，意若曰：「天下之事，未始不成於勤而荒於逸者也。君子所以能無逸者何哉？誠以君位至逸也，稼穡至艱難也。惟不知其
translation_en:
…should you not also devote yourselves to this? I have observed that the Book of Changes assigns to the sovereign the work of regulating and assisting the processes of Heaven and Earth, whereas here the responsibility for accomplishing Heaven’s work is placed upon ministers. Why is this? The ruler’s Way acts with intention yet without direct intervention; it is what the ministers—the regional overseers, governors, and nine chief officials—rely upon in administering their various duties. Similarly, Heaven’s Way brings about transformation without intention; it is what its officers, the four seasons and five phases, draw upon to complete the year’s work. Thus Emperor Shun’s charge expresses both the ruler’s Way and Heaven’s Way. Later, when Gao Yao presented his counsel on discerning men’s abilities, he likewise charged the ruler of Youyu with having men perform Heaven’s work in its stead. Such indeed was the mutual admonition through which ruler and ministers served Heaven.
“First understand the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then take ease; thus you will know what the common people depend upon.”
Wu Rui
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “The essential purport of the Duke of Zhou’s admonition to King Cheng is elucidated with precision and insight. Recorded here to serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Fluent and clear.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Elegant, disciplined, and accomplished in expression.”
The great minister traced the reasons for the noble ruler’s solicitude for the people, revealing the source of his refusal to indulge in ease. What the people prize is sowing and reaping. When the noble ruler understands their hardships and takes them to heart, what leisure has he to indulge himself? In admonishing King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou meant something like this: “The affairs of the world have always been accomplished through diligence and ruined through indulgence in ease. How is it that the noble ruler can refrain from such indulgence? Truly, the ruler’s position affords the greatest ease, while sowing and reaping entail the greatest hardship. It is only through failing to understand their…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
難而遽享乎逸始有忽民依而自肆者矣君子
則心存於民隱而預識乎百畝之憂慮切於民
生而周知乎三農之務時而東作也不必身親
乎耕稼而先天下以達其勤動之故者昭然若
所備嘗焉時而西成也不必下同乎穡人而先
天下以察其胼胝之勞者確然若所親見焉由
是而居大君之位以享天下之逸也有不知小
民之依乎吾知居於深宮者此心也既灼見乎
畎畝艱難之實則履乎帝位者亦此心也自洞
===
察夫烝民粒食之源知小人之依於稼也而我
稼之未同何以立斯民之大命乎則夫思艱圖
易以作天下之依者蓋有不遑寧處者矣矧敢
縱逸乎哉知小人之依於穡也而穡事之未成
何以貽斯民之率育乎則夫事制曲防以開天
下之麗者蓋有惟日孜孜者矣况敢逸豫乎哉
夫古之居君位者始於憂勤而終於逸樂此所
以稱無逸者歸之也吾王其監之哉抑論書戒
無逸詩陳豳風姬公固惓惓以農事詔王矣迺
punctuated:
難而遽享乎逸，始有忽民依而自肆者矣。君子則心存於民隱，而預識乎百畝之憂；慮切於民生，而周知乎三農之務。時而東作也，不必身親乎耕稼，而先天下以達其勤動之故者，昭然若所備嘗焉。時而西成也，不必下同乎穡人，而先天下以察其胼胝之勞者，確然若所親見焉。由是而居大君之位，以享天下之逸也，有不知小民之依乎？吾知居於深宮者此心也，既灼見乎畎畝艱難之實，則履乎帝位者亦此心也，自洞察夫烝民粒食之源。知小人之依於稼也，而我稼之未同，何以立斯民之大命乎？則夫思艱圖易，以作天下之依者，蓋有不遑寧處者矣，矧敢縱逸乎哉！知小人之依於穡也，而穡事之未成，何以貽斯民之率育乎？則夫事制曲防，以開天下之麗者，蓋有惟日孜孜者矣，况敢逸豫乎哉！夫古之居君位者，始於憂勤而終於逸樂，此所以稱無逸者歸之也。吾王其監之哉！

抑論《書》戒無逸，《詩》陳豳風，姬公固惓惓以農事詔王矣，迺
translation_en:
…the hardship, and hastily enjoy ease: only then do rulers neglect what the people depend upon and give themselves free rein. The gentleman, however, keeps the people’s sufferings in his heart and understands beforehand the anxieties of tending a hundred mu of land; his concern for their livelihood is earnest, and he knows thoroughly the tasks of farming. When spring cultivation begins, he need not personally plow and sow: his understanding, ahead of all under Heaven, of what their toil entails is as clear as though he had experienced it all himself. When the autumn harvest comes, he need not descend to work alongside the harvesters: his recognition, ahead of all under Heaven, of the labor that calluses their hands and feet is as certain as though he had witnessed it himself. Thus, when he occupies the position of sovereign and enjoys the ease afforded by all under Heaven, could he fail to know what the common people depend upon? I know that the heart dwelling within the secluded palace, once it clearly perceives the actual hardships of the fields, is the very same heart that occupies the imperial throne. It will naturally discern the source of the grain that feeds the multitude. Knowing that the common people depend upon planting, he asks: “If our crops have not yet come together [?], how can I secure the very lives of these people?” Thus, in contemplating difficulties and devising ways to ease them, so as to become the support of all under Heaven, he has no leisure to rest peacefully. How would he dare indulge in ease? Knowing that the common people depend upon harvesting, he asks: “If the harvest is not yet complete, how can I enable all these people to be nourished?” Thus, in regulating affairs and taking precautions in every detail, so as to provide all under Heaven with something to rely upon, he works diligently every day. How would he dare surrender to idle pleasure? Those who occupied the ruler’s position in antiquity began with anxious diligence but ended in idle enjoyment. This is why the praise of freedom from ease is attributed to them [?]. May our king take warning from this!

Furthermore, the Book of Documents warns against ease, while the Book of Odes presents the Airs of Bin. The Duke of Zhou indeed earnestly instructed the king through agricultural affairs. Yet …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
孟子以竝耕爲害治何也蓋人君以心勞天下
則易故民依不可忽以形勞天下則難故農事
不可兼此其意各有攸當而識治體者當辨之
於早矣後世忘祖德而忽民艱舍憂勤而縱逸
樂者其無以豳風無逸之說告之與
詩
經營四方告成于王
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批體格莊嚴詞語精鍊於經營告
===
成意發揮詳盡殆志存立功者與
考試官教諭陳批條鬯
考試官教授王批莊重
詩人美大將必自其攘夷奏功者言之也蓋大
將有事於外者王命也夫旣攘夷而成功矣得
不入告於王哉詩人敘其事以美之也若曰王
者之治以內順外威爲盛人臣之職以攘外安
內爲功彼淮夷侵陵而興師薄伐虎旣受成于
王矣使其經營之未就抑將何以告其成乎今
punctuated:
孟子以竝耕爲害治，何也？蓋人君以心勞天下則易，故民依不可忽；以形勞天下則難，故農事不可兼。此其意各有攸當，而識治體者當辨之於早矣。後世忘祖德而忽民艱，舍憂勤而縱逸樂者，其無以《豳風》《無逸》之說告之與？
詩
經營四方，告成于王。
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批：體格莊嚴，詞語精鍊，於經營告成意發揮詳盡，殆志存立功者與？
考試官教諭陳批：條鬯。
考試官教授王批：莊重。
詩人美大將，必自其攘夷奏功者言之也。蓋大將有事於外者，王命也。夫旣攘夷而成功矣，得不入告於王哉？詩人敘其事以美之也。若曰：王者之治，以內順外威爲盛；人臣之職，以攘外安內爲功。彼淮夷侵陵，而興師薄伐，虎旣受成于王矣。使其經營之未就，抑將何以告其成乎？今
translation_en:
…why, then, did Mencius regard ploughing alongside the people as harmful to government? For a ruler to toil mentally for the realm makes governing easy; hence he must not neglect what sustains the people. To toil physically for the realm makes governing difficult; hence he cannot also undertake agricultural work. Each of these teachings has its proper application, and those who understand the principles of government should distinguish them early. As for later rulers who forget their ancestors’ virtue and disregard the people’s hardships, abandoning anxious diligence and indulging in ease and pleasure—should they not be admonished with the teachings of the Airs of Bin and Against Idleness?
Book of Odes
“He brought order to the four quarters and reported his achievement to the king.”
Peng Qizhong
Comment by Associate Examiner Tie, an Instructor: “The structure and style are dignified, the language refined. The meaning of bringing order and reporting achievement is developed fully and in detail. Surely this is someone whose ambition is to render meritorious service?”
Comment by Examiner Chen, an Instructor: “Orderly and lucid.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, a Professor: “Dignified and grave.”
When the poet praises a great commander, he necessarily speaks of his achievements in repelling the alien peoples. For a great commander undertakes affairs abroad at the king’s command. Once he has repelled the alien peoples and achieved success, how could he fail to come to court and report to the king? The poet recounts his deeds to praise him. It is as though he were saying: the government of a king flourishes through obedience within and awe abroad; the service of a minister achieves merit by repelling threats abroad and securing peace within. When the Huai peoples invaded and encroached, troops were raised to attack them, and Hu had already received the king’s plan of action. Had his efforts to bring order remained unfinished, how could he have reported their accomplishment? Now…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
虎也奉天討以徂征而式固謀猷期得乎萬全
之道遵廟謨以制勝而式遏冦虐兾成夫底定
之休四方之疆宇莫非王土也悉心於恢拓之
圖而侵者復焉荒者闢焉務俾有利于社稷斯
已矣四方之人民莫非王臣也殫力於綏懷之
略而渙者萃之來者安之務俾有益于生靈斯
已矣如是而成功也能不爲王告哉蓋始焉簡
書之授王固欲觀厥成也兹大憝旣殄而懋廼
丕績用敷奏於天子之庭昔焉推轂之遣王固
===
欲求厥寧也兹大敵旣克而以奏膚公用對揚
乎一人之命以其恢拓之功從而上聞焉則知
土宇版章無改於舊而天王一統之業自是其
永保乎以其綏懷之功從而上達焉則知萬方
攸同不失其初而九重南顧之憂自是其可釋
乎吁召虎之經營也以定王國之事也不爲倖
功其告成也以佐天子之忠也非爲希寵其眞
可謂中興之賢佐者歟抑吾于是而見馭夷之
道也淮夷倡亂召公討之不玩冦不黷武而惟
punctuated: 虎也奉天討以徂征，而式固謀猷，期得乎萬全之道；遵廟謨以制勝，而式遏冦虐，兾成夫底定之休。四方之疆宇，莫非王土也，悉心於恢拓之圖，而侵者復焉，荒者闢焉，務俾有利于社稷斯已矣。四方之人民，莫非王臣也，殫力於綏懷之略，而渙者萃之，來者安之，務俾有益于生靈斯已矣。如是而成功也，能不爲王告哉？蓋始焉簡書之授，王固欲觀厥成也。兹大憝旣殄，而懋廼丕績，用敷奏於天子之庭。昔焉推轂之遣，王固欲求厥寧也。兹大敵旣克，而以奏膚公，用對揚乎一人之命。以其恢拓之功，從而上聞焉，則知土宇版章無改於舊，而天王一統之業，自是其永保乎！以其綏懷之功，從而上達焉，則知萬方攸同不失其初，而九重南顧之憂，自是其可釋乎！吁！召虎之經營也，以定王國之事也，不爲倖功；其告成也，以佐天子之忠也，非爲希寵。其眞可謂中興之賢佐者歟！抑吾于是而見馭夷之道也。淮夷倡亂，召公討之，不玩冦，不黷武，而惟
translation_en:
…Hu undertook the campaign to carry out Heaven’s punishment, firmly establishing his plans in the hope of securing complete success. Following the court’s strategic counsels to achieve victory, he checked the raiders’ violence, hoping to accomplish the glorious work of pacification. The territories in all four directions were all the king’s land. He devoted himself wholeheartedly to plans for their recovery and expansion: occupied lands were recovered, and waste lands opened up. His sole concern was to benefit the altars of soil and grain. The people in all four directions were all the king’s subjects. He exerted himself fully in measures to pacify them and win their allegiance: those who had scattered were gathered together, and those who came over were settled in peace. His sole concern was to benefit the people. Having thus achieved success, how could he fail to report it to the king?

When the written orders were first conferred, the king certainly wished to see the undertaking completed. Now that the great malefactors had been destroyed and his mighty achievements brought to fruition, he duly reported them in the Son of Heaven’s court. When the king had earlier dispatched him, ceremonially pushing his chariot wheels, he certainly sought to secure peace. Now that the great enemy had been defeated and a great accomplishment achieved, he duly acknowledged and extolled the sovereign’s command. When his achievements in recovering and expanding the territory were reported to the throne, it became clear that the realm’s territorial boundaries [?] remained as of old. Could not the Heavenly King’s unified dominion henceforth be preserved forever? When his achievements in pacification and winning allegiance were communicated to the throne, it became clear that the myriad regions were united as they had originally been. Could not the sovereign’s anxiety as he looked south from the palace’s ninefold enclosures henceforth be dispelled?

Ah! Shao Hu’s conduct of the campaign served to settle the affairs of the royal realm; he was not seeking success through luck. His report of victory expressed his loyalty in assisting the Son of Heaven; he was not seeking favor. Truly, could he not be called a worthy minister of the restoration? Moreover, here I discern the way to govern the Yi peoples. When the Huai Yi stirred up rebellion, the Duke of Shao campaigned against them. He neither took the enemy lightly nor resorted recklessly to arms, but solely…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
在于經營信乎老成持重正易所謂師貞丈人
吉也是以有顯允之方叔而獫狁之難襄有赫
赫之南仲而昆夷之患息故誦是詩者雖嘉穆
公之功而宣王得人之盛不亦尤可美歟
思文后稷克配彼天立我烝民莫匪爾極
貽我來牟帝命率育無此疆爾界陳常
于時夏
李宜春
同考試官教諭陳批發揮題意明徹而詞更整潔
===
是深於詩者
考試官教諭陳批義精詞雅讀之灑然
考試官教授王批詞理瑩粹
詩人頌聖祖與天合德而必本其養民之極功
焉夫承天意以養民而教因以行焉聖祖之功
亦偉矣此其德之所以配天也歟此周人尊祖
配天之詩也意謂必有天下之大德斯可享天
下之大報我周南郊之祭人知以稷配天矣而
豈知其德之有同於天乎惟我后稷先天以開
punctuated:
在于經營，信乎老成持重，正《易》所謂「師貞，丈人吉」也。是以有顯允之方叔，而獫狁之難襄；有赫赫之南仲，而昆夷之患息。故誦是詩者，雖嘉穆公之功，而宣王得人之盛，不亦尤可美歟？
「思文后稷，克配彼天。立我烝民，莫匪爾極。貽我來牟，帝命率育。無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。」
李宜春
同考試官教諭陳批：發揮題意明徹，而詞更整潔，是深於詩者。
考試官教諭陳批：義精詞雅，讀之灑然。
考試官教授王批：詞理瑩粹。
詩人頌聖祖與天合德，而必本其養民之極功焉。夫承天意以養民，而教因以行焉，聖祖之功亦偉矣！此其德之所以配天也歟？此周人尊祖配天之詩也。意謂必有天下之大德，斯可享天下之大報。我周南郊之祭，人知以稷配天矣，而豈知其德之有同於天乎？惟我后稷，先天以開
translation_en:
…lies in careful planning. Truly, this is the prudence and steadiness of a seasoned elder, precisely what the Book of Changes calls: “In conducting an army, be steadfast; for a venerable leader, good fortune.” Thus, with the illustrious and trustworthy Fang Shu, the troubles caused by the Xianyun were overcome; with the resplendent Nan Zhong, the menace of the Kunyi ceased. Hence, although those who recite this poem praise the achievements of Duke Mu [?], is King Xuan’s outstanding success in obtaining worthy men not still more deserving of admiration?
“Ah, cultured Hou Ji, worthy to be paired with Heaven! You established our teeming people; none failed to find their standard in you. You bequeathed us wheat and barley; at the Lord’s command, you nourished all. Without distinctions between this territory and that boundary, you set forth the constant rule throughout this land of Xia.”
Li Yichun
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “His exposition of the topic’s meaning is clear and thorough, and his language is especially orderly and polished. Here is someone deeply versed in the Poetry.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The meaning is refined and the language elegant; reading it leaves one refreshed.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “The language and reasoning are lucid and pure.”
The poet praises the sage ancestor for matching Heaven in virtue, necessarily grounding this praise in his supreme achievement of nourishing the people. By carrying out Heaven’s intent to nourish the people, he also enabled moral instruction to take effect. Great indeed were the sage ancestor’s achievements! Is this not why his virtue entitled him to be paired with Heaven? This is a poem in which the people of Zhou honor their ancestor by pairing him with Heaven in sacrifice. Its meaning is that only one possessing the greatest virtue under Heaven may receive the greatest recompense under Heaven. At our Zhou sacrifice in the southern suburb, people know that Ji is paired with Heaven; but do they understand how his virtue accorded with Heaven’s? Our Hou Ji alone acted in advance of Heaven to open up…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人而經緯之章合貞觀以竝運因地以盡利而
彌綸之績與造化而同流蘊之爲文德之精者
卽乾元於穆之體也發之爲文治之華者卽天
道高明之用也此其德眞足以配天矣然果何
以見之蓋民生有欲不能以自遂也稷則教之
稼穡開天下粒食之原而利興於當時澤被於
後世矣孰非其至德耶惟天惠民不能以自致
也稷則貽我來牟承上帝率育之命而大雖無
爲稷代有終矣孰非其成能耶由是生養遂則
===
禮義之心自生無有疆界之殊而以正君臣以
篤父子彝倫攸叙之風達之天下矣洪荒之世
不奕然爲文明之會乎民生厚則正德之功自
奮無有彼此之限而各尊其尊各親其親人紀
肇修之化徧於中國矣顓蒙之俗不燁然爲聲
教之都乎吁后稷上承帝命之命是能爲天地
立心矣下開教養之端是能爲生民立命矣此
其德不謂之至德乎而南郊之配夫孰曰不宜
抑論周人郊而祀天以后稷之文德配至明堂
punctuated: 人，而經緯之章合貞觀以竝運；因地以盡利，而彌綸之績與造化而同流。蘊之爲文德之精者，卽乾元於穆之體也；發之爲文治之華者，卽天道高明之用也。此其德眞足以配天矣。然果何以見之？蓋民生有欲，不能以自遂也，稷則教之稼穡，開天下粒食之原，而利興於當時，澤被於後世矣，孰非其至德耶？惟天惠民，不能以自致也，稷則貽我來牟，承上帝率育之命，而大雖無爲，稷代有終矣，孰非其成能耶？由是生養遂，則禮義之心自生，無有疆界之殊，而以正君臣，以篤父子，彝倫攸叙之風達之天下矣。洪荒之世，不奕然爲文明之會乎？民生厚，則正德之功自奮，無有彼此之限，而各尊其尊，各親其親，人紀肇修之化徧於中國矣。顓蒙之俗，不燁然爲聲教之都乎？吁！后稷上承帝命之命，是能爲天地立心矣；下開教養之端，是能爲生民立命矣。此其德不謂之至德乎？而南郊之配，夫孰曰不宜？抑論周人郊而祀天，以后稷之文德配，至明堂
translation_en:
…humankind, and the ordered pattern of his work operated together with Heaven’s constant manifestation; drawing upon the earth to realize its benefits fully, his all-encompassing achievements flowed together with the processes of creation. What he stored within as the essence of cultivated virtue was the very substance of Heaven’s primal, profound majesty; what he expressed outwardly as the splendor of civil governance was the very operation of the Way of Heaven in its loftiness and brilliance. His virtue truly sufficed to make him Heaven’s companion in sacrifice. Yet how, indeed, can this be demonstrated? People have desires in their lives but cannot fulfill them unaided. Ji therefore taught them sowing and reaping, opening the source of grain nourishment for all under Heaven. Its benefits arose in his own time, and its blessings extended to later generations. Was any of this not an expression of his consummate virtue? Heaven bestows benefits upon the people but cannot bring them about unaided. Ji therefore bequeathed to us wheat and barley, receiving the command of the Lord on High to nurture all. Though the Great One [?] acts without purposeful action, Ji brought the work to completion on its behalf. Was any of this not his fulfillment of Heaven’s capacities?

Thus, once people’s livelihood and nourishment were secured, a disposition toward ritual propriety and righteousness arose of itself. Without distinctions of territorial boundaries, the relationship between ruler and minister was set right, and that between father and son was strengthened. The practice of putting the enduring human relationships in order spread throughout the world. Did the age of primordial wilderness not become a splendid gathering of civilization? Once people’s livelihood was abundant, the work of rectifying virtue advanced of itself. Without distinctions between one group and another, each honored those whom they should honor and cherished those whom they should cherish. The transforming influence that first established the human relationships spread throughout the Central Lands. Did benighted customs not give way to a radiant center of moral instruction?

Ah! Above, Hou Ji received the command of the Lord’s command [?], and thus could establish the heart of Heaven and Earth; below, he initiated instruction and nourishment, and thus could establish the destiny of the people. Should this virtue of his not be called consummate virtue? And who could say it was unfitting for him to be Heaven’s companion in the sacrifice at the southern suburban altar? Furthermore, consider how the people of Zhou sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar, associating Hou Ji with Heaven on account of his cultivated virtue; as for the Hall of Light…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則配以文王亦曰文之所以爲文與天之所以
爲天一也然則不有文德不足以配天明矣周
人制禮精義於此可以想見明於其義則仁孝
之道備而尊親之化行此夫子所謂治國其如
視諸斯也讀詩者當自得之
春秋
冬十有二月齊侯鄭伯盟于石門〔隱公三年〕
秦延緒
===
同考試官教諭林批此題傳意甚略作者類失之膚
淺此篇意思清婉而豐腴深得聖人公世之志
考試官教諭陳批辭義森嚴
考試官教授王批莊重典雅
春秋惡諸侯之講信所以志大道之公也此見
聖人之志公天下者也特盟之私自石門始矣
是以見惡於春秋吾聞常事不書春秋例也石
門之盟亦常事爾而何以書蓋自敬信孚于虞
夏卓乎無以尚也而誥誓肇於商周則旣浸以
punctuated:
則配以文王，亦曰文之所以爲文，與天之所以爲天，一也。然則不有文德，不足以配天，明矣。周人制禮精義，於此可以想見。明於其義，則仁孝之道備，而尊親之化行。此夫子所謂「治國其如視諸斯也」。讀詩者當自得之。
春秋
冬十有二月，齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門。〔隱公三年〕
秦延緒
同考試官教諭林批：此題傳意甚略，作者類失之膚淺。此篇意思清婉而豐腴，深得聖人公世之志。
考試官教諭陳批：辭義森嚴。
考試官教授王批：莊重典雅。
春秋惡諸侯之講信，所以志大道之公也。此見聖人之志公天下者也。特盟之私，自石門始矣，是以見惡於春秋。吾聞常事不書，春秋例也。石門之盟亦常事爾，而何以書？蓋自敬信孚于虞夏，卓乎無以尚也；而誥誓肇於商周，則旣浸以
translation_en:
…then King Wen was associated with Heaven in sacrifice. This likewise means that what made Wen truly “cultured” and what makes Heaven truly Heaven are one. It is therefore clear that without cultural virtue one cannot be associated with Heaven in sacrifice. Here we can discern the profound principles underlying the Zhou people's establishment of ritual. When these principles are understood, the Way of benevolence and filial devotion is complete, and the transforming influence of honoring the honored and cherishing one's kin takes effect. This is what the Master meant when he said, “Governing the state would be like looking at this here.” Readers of the Book of Odes should grasp this for themselves.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In winter, in the twelfth month, the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng covenanted at Shimen.” 〔Third year of Duke Yin〕
Qin Yanxu
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The commentarial explanation of this topic is very brief, and writers generally fall into superficiality. This essay is lucid and graceful in its ideas, yet rich and full, profoundly grasping the sage's aspiration to make the world serve the common good.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The language and reasoning are rigorously ordered and commanding.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Dignified, classically refined, and elegant.
The Spring and Autumn Annals condemns the feudal lords' pledging of good faith in order to set forth the impartiality of the Great Way. Here we see the sage's aspiration to make all under Heaven serve the common good. The pursuit of private interests through bilateral covenants began at Shimen; hence its condemnation in the Spring and Autumn Annals. I have heard that omitting ordinary affairs is a rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals. The covenant at Shimen was also merely an ordinary affair; why, then, was it recorded? Reverence and trust prevailed in the times of Yu and Xia, reaching a height beyond which nothing could rise. But when proclamations and oaths first appeared under Shang and Zhou, there had already gradually begun to…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
薄矣况盟又豈盛世之事哉使齊鄭苟能以信
而相諭則斯盟也將焉用之徒以結援於鄭僖
謂不詔言於神將無以固其約矣而不知言不
由衷盟無益也徒欲致讎於宋莊謂不締交於
齊將無以遂其私矣而不知君子屢盟亂是用
長也是果王法之所得爲乎聖人於此有感焉
蓋以于邾之盟蔑雖甞惡之然猶以爲自魯要
之爾天下未必其皆魯也今齊也鄭也乃特起
爲斯役焉吾知今日離以二明日參以三而天
===
下之不爲魯者無幾矣噫安得信孚於不言之
表使有虞之休風復見於今日邪于宋之盟宿
雖常病之然猶以爲自隱欲之爾諸侯未必其
皆隱也今僖也莊也乃相率爲斯舉焉將見爾
惟我詐我惟爾虞而諸侯之不爲齊鄭者無幾
矣噫安得敬存於不令之餘而使有夏之善俗
不專美於前耶世道已衰也而以盛世期之人
心不古也而以古道望之三代之英雖未之逮
而大道之行則其所素志者矣故盟雖常事而
punctuated: 薄矣，况盟又豈盛世之事哉？使齊鄭苟能以信而相諭，則斯盟也將焉用之？徒以結援於鄭，僖謂不詔言於神，將無以固其約矣，而不知言不由衷，盟無益也。徒欲致讎於宋，莊謂不締交於齊，將無以遂其私矣，而不知君子屢盟，亂是用長也。是果王法之所得爲乎？聖人於此有感焉。蓋以于邾之盟蔑，雖甞惡之，然猶以爲自魯要之爾，天下未必其皆魯也。今齊也，鄭也，乃特起爲斯役焉。吾知今日離以二，明日參以三，而天下之不爲魯者無幾矣。噫！安得信孚於不言之表，使有虞之休風復見於今日邪？于宋之盟宿，雖常病之，然猶以爲自隱欲之爾，諸侯未必其皆隱也。今僖也，莊也，乃相率爲斯舉焉。將見爾惟我詐，我惟爾虞，而諸侯之不爲齊鄭者無幾矣。噫！安得敬存於不令之餘，而使有夏之善俗不專美於前耶？世道已衰也，而以盛世期之；人心不古也，而以古道望之。三代之英，雖未之逮，而大道之行，則其所素志者矣。故盟雖常事，而
translation_en:
…had grown thin. How much less could sworn covenants belong to an age of flourishing rule! If Qi and Zheng could truly reach an understanding through good faith, what use would there be for this covenant? Intent merely on securing Zheng’s support, Duke Xi of Qi thought that unless he proclaimed his words to the spirits, he could not make their agreement firm. He did not understand that when words do not come from the heart, a covenant is of no benefit. Intent merely on pursuing his enmity against Song, Duke Zhuang of Zheng thought that unless he established an alliance with Qi, he could not achieve his private ends. He did not understand that when gentlemen repeatedly swear covenants, disorder thereby grows. Was this indeed something permitted under the laws of the true king? At this the Sage was moved.
As for the covenant with Zhu at Mie, although he had disapproved of it, he could still regard it as something Lu itself had sought: not every state under Heaven would necessarily behave like Lu. Now, however, Qi and Zheng had taken it upon themselves to undertake this affair. I know that today two will form a separate grouping, and tomorrow a third will join them; few states under Heaven will then remain unlike Lu. Alas! How might trust prevail beyond the need for words, so that the splendid ways of the age of Yu might appear again today?
