As for the covenant with Song at Su, although he had deplored it, he could still regard it as something Duke Yin himself had desired: not every regional lord would necessarily behave like Duke Yin. Now, however, Duke Xi and Duke Zhuang had followed one another in taking this action. We shall see you deceiving me and me outwitting you; few regional lords will then remain unlike those of Qi and Zheng. Alas! How might reverence endure without commands, so that the fine customs of Xia would no longer be a glory belonging exclusively to the past?
The ways of the world had already declined, yet he expected of them the standards of a flourishing age; people’s hearts were no longer as in antiquity, yet he looked to them to follow the ancient Way. Though he had not lived to witness the glorious age of the Three Dynasties, the practice of the Great Way was what he had always aspired to. Thus, although covenants were ordinary affairs, yet…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
經必書之豈特爲齊鄭慮焉已哉抑論司盟周
制也孔子周人也以周人而變周制然則從周
之說非歟蓋聖人作春秋爲百王法其本則自
正人心始盟可惡也亦可革也雖變周之制何
惑焉是從周者遵時之義道以守經也變周者
復古之志道以達權也故曰聖人隨時變易以
從道又何相悖之有哉
衞人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕公會晉侯宋公
衞侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
===
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕
張文錦
同考試官教諭林 批 發揮二臣引過讓善典明切當
經義之最優者
考試官教諭陳 批 清新
考試官教授王 批 蒼健
春秋以忠教天下而於過稱已善稱君者有取
焉夫忠者人臣事君之道也衞晉之大夫有焉
punctuated:
經必書之，豈特爲齊鄭慮焉已哉？抑論司盟，周制也；孔子，周人也。以周人而變周制，然則從周之說非歟？蓋聖人作《春秋》，爲百王法，其本則自正人心始。盟可惡也，亦可革也，雖變周之制，何惑焉？是從周者，遵時之義，道以守經也；變周者，復古之志，道以達權也。故曰：「聖人隨時變易以從道。」又何相悖之有哉？
衞人救陳。〔宣公十有二年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔襄公十有一年〕
張文錦
同考試官教諭林批：發揮二臣引過讓善，典明切當，經義之最優者。
考試官教諭陳批：清新。
考試官教授王批：蒼健。
《春秋》以忠教天下，而於過稱已、善稱君者有取焉。夫忠者，人臣事君之道也。衞、晉之大夫有焉。
translation_en:
…the Classic invariably records them. Could its concern have been confined to Qi and Zheng? Yet consider the office of Director of Covenants: this was an institution of Zhou, and Confucius was a man of Zhou. If a man of Zhou altered Zhou institutions, does that mean his declaration that he followed Zhou was mistaken? The sage composed the Spring and Autumn Annals to provide a model for a hundred generations of kings; its foundation lay in first rectifying people’s hearts. Covenants were objectionable and could also be abolished. Even if this changed a Zhou institution, what cause was there for perplexity? Following Zhou expressed the duty to accord with the times: through the Way, one upheld constant principles. Changing Zhou expressed the aspiration to restore antiquity: through the Way, one exercised discretion. Thus it is said, “The sage changes with the times in order to follow the Way.” How could these courses contradict each other?
“The men of Wei came to the aid of Chen.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕 “The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
Zhang Wenjin
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Expounds how the two ministers assumed blame and yielded credit to others. Classically grounded and lucid [?], precise and apt—the finest of the essays on the meaning of the Classics.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Fresh and clear.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Mature and vigorous.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals teaches loyalty to all under Heaven, and commends those who attribute faults to themselves and good deeds to their rulers. Loyalty is the Way by which a minister serves his ruler. The grandees of Wei and Jin possessed it…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
春秋得不取之以敎天下之爲人臣者乎粤自
匪躬之義微而凡便於身圖者苟有過也非惟
文之且將諉之矣求其引爲己責者誰歟吾於
衛得一人焉興救陳之師以干清丘之盟固孔
達之過亦衛侯之過也晉使之來岌岌乎社稷
之幾危矣達則曰先君之約不敢背也大國之
討不敢亢也一時辱國之罪毅然當之而不辭
惟知任其事而未常有其身所謂食焉而不避
其難者是矣傳曰過則稱己非孔達其誰與歸
===
耶自讓德之道喪而凡急於邀功者苟有善也
非惟伐之且將攘之矣求其推以與人者誰歟
吾於晉得一人焉成蕭魚之會以致鄭樂之歸
固魏絳之善亦晉侯之善也金石之賜藹藹乎
上下之胥慶矣絳則曰戎狄之和國之福也諸
侯之合君之靈也八年輔國之勳退然讓之而
不居惟知代其終而未嘗有其成所謂不敢貪
天功爲己力者是矣傳曰善則稱君非魏絳又
誰與歸耶于其引過於己也可以見忘己之公
punctuated: 春秋得不取之，以敎天下之爲人臣者乎？粤自匪躬之義微，而凡便於身圖者，苟有過也，非惟文之，且將諉之矣。求其引爲己責者，誰歟？吾於衛得一人焉。興救陳之師，以干清丘之盟，固孔達之過，亦衛侯之過也。晉使之來，岌岌乎社稷之幾危矣！達則曰：「先君之約，不敢背也；大國之討，不敢亢也。」一時辱國之罪，毅然當之而不辭，惟知任其事，而未常有其身，所謂食焉而不避其難者是矣。傳曰：「過則稱己。」非孔達，其誰與歸耶？自讓德之道喪，而凡急於邀功者，苟有善也，非惟伐之，且將攘之矣。求其推以與人者，誰歟？吾於晉得一人焉。成蕭魚之會，以致鄭樂之歸，固魏絳之善，亦晉侯之善也。金石之賜，藹藹乎上下之胥慶矣！絳則曰：「戎狄之和，國之福也；諸侯之合，君之靈也。」八年輔國之勳，退然讓之而不居，惟知代其終，而未嘗有其成，所謂不敢貪天功爲己力者是矣。傳曰：「善則稱君。」非魏絳，又誰與歸耶？于其引過於己也，可以見忘己之公
translation_en:
…How could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to commend them, thereby instructing all under Heaven who serve as ministers? Ever since the principle of selfless service declined, those who scheme for their own advantage, whenever they commit a fault, not only conceal it but also shift the blame. Who among them accepts it as his own responsibility? In Wei I find one such man. Raising an army to rescue Chen, thereby violating the covenant of Qingqiu, was certainly Kong Da’s fault, but it was also the fault of the Marquis of Wei. When the envoy from Jin arrived, the state stood perilously close to disaster! Kong Da declared: “I dare not betray the covenant of our former lord; I dare not resist the punitive demands of the great state.” He resolutely accepted, without evasion, the blame for having brought disgrace upon his state. Knowing only that he must bear responsibility for the affair, he gave no thought to his own person. He was indeed what is meant by one who draws sustenance from a state and does not evade its dangers. The Commentary says: “For faults, take the blame oneself.” If not Kong Da, to whom could this apply?

Ever since the way of yielding credit for virtue was lost, those eager to claim merit, whenever there is a good achievement, not only boast of it but also appropriate it. Who among them yields the credit to others? In Jin I find one such man. Bringing about the meeting at Xiaoyu, which led to the receipt of Zheng’s musicians, was certainly Wei Jiang’s achievement, but it was also that of the Marquis of Jin. The bestowal of bells and sounding stones occasioned warm rejoicing among ruler and subjects alike! Wei Jiang declared: “Peace with the Rong and Di is the state’s good fortune; the union of the feudal lords is due to my lord’s spiritual potency.” The merit of eight years spent supporting the state he modestly yielded, claiming none for himself. He knew only to carry the undertaking through on his lord’s behalf [?], and never claimed its accomplishment as his own. He was indeed what is meant by one who dares not appropriate Heaven’s achievement as the product of his own strength. The Commentary says: “For good achievements, give credit to the ruler.” If not Wei Jiang, to whom else could this apply? In his taking the fault upon himself, one can discern the self-forgetting impartiality…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉于其推善於君也可以見尊君之義焉春秋
於二子均之有取焉其所以作民之忠者何其
至哉噫此華元子反不明人臣之義而擅必上
之功所以不免聖人之惡也已雖然孔達棄信
罪固不可得而辭矣用人以至於誤國伊誰之
咎歟若魏絳相君之功固云偉矣及其辭樂又
曰抑臣願君安其樂而思其終頌不忘規非賢
而能之乎以此而觀則晉悼之賞不廢典其賢
於衛穆成勞之報也遠矣
===
禮記
禮樂偩天地之情達神明之德降興上下
之神而凝是精粗之體領父子君臣之
節是故大人舉禮樂則天地將爲昭焉
徐𩃎
考試官敎諭陳批禮樂合造化與贊化之妙極
難形容此作得旨而詞氣渾融可以觀所養矣
考試官敎授王批通暢
記者極言禮樂之妙而因著聖人之贊化也蓋
punctuated:
焉。于其推善於君也，可以見尊君之義焉。《春秋》於二子均之有取焉，其所以作民之忠者，何其至哉！噫！此華元、子反不明人臣之義，而擅必上之功，所以不免聖人之惡也已。雖然，孔達棄信，罪固不可得而辭矣；用人以至於誤國，伊誰之咎歟？若魏絳相君之功，固云偉矣。及其辭樂，又曰：「抑臣願君安其樂而思其終。」頌不忘規，非賢而能之乎？以此而觀，則晉悼之賞不廢典，其賢於衛穆成勞之報也遠矣。

禮記
禮樂偩天地之情，達神明之德，降興上下之神，而凝是精粗之體，領父子君臣之節。是故大人舉禮樂，則天地將爲昭焉。
徐𩃎
考試官敎諭陳批：「禮樂合造化與贊化之妙，極難形容。此作得旨，而詞氣渾融，可以觀所養矣。」
考試官敎授王批：「通暢。」

記者極言禮樂之妙，而因著聖人之贊化也。蓋
translation_en:
…; in his attributing good deeds to his ruler, one can see his sense of duty in honoring his sovereign. The Spring and Autumn Annals finds something worthy in both men. How consummately it thus inspires loyalty among the people! Alas! Hua Yuan and Zifan failed to understand the duties of a minister and presumptuously claimed their superiors’ achievements [?]; hence they could not escape the Sage’s condemnation. Nevertheless, Kong Da abandoned good faith, and certainly could not deny his guilt. But whose fault was it to employ someone who brought the state to grief? As for Wei Jiang, his achievements in assisting his ruler were indeed great. When he declined the gift of musicians, he further said: “Yet your servant wishes that you, my lord, may enjoy this music in peace while considering how it will end.” To praise without forgetting to admonish—could anyone but a worthy man do this? Viewed in this light, Duke Dao of Jin’s reward upheld established norms; it was far superior to Duke Mu of Wei’s recompense for accomplished service.

Record of Rites
“Rites and music accord with the inherent dispositions of Heaven and Earth and give expression to the potency of spiritual powers. They bring down and raise up the spirits above and below, consolidate the forms of the subtle and the gross, and govern the proper relations between fathers and sons, rulers and ministers. Thus, when the great man puts rites and music into practice, Heaven and Earth will thereby be made manifest.”
Xu 𩃎 [given-name reading uncertain].
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The subtle workings through which rites and music accord with creation and assist its transforming processes are exceedingly difficult to describe. This composition grasps the essential meaning, and its language and tenor form a harmonious whole. From it one can discern the writer’s self-cultivation.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Lucid and fluent.”

The author of the Record fully expounds the subtle workings of rites and music, thereby revealing how the sage assists the transforming processes of creation. For…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂與造化相爲流通也聖人舉之而化昭焉
不可以其爲用之妙哉今夫禮樂之在天下也
固能管乎人情矣然豈儀文聲容之謂乎蓋嘗
有以觀其深矣彼天地之情廣大而不可象此
其偵之蓋兩儀肇和序之端而同和同節者成
其能也神明之德微妙而不可測此其達之蓋
屈神秘藏用之機而敦和别宜者顯諸仁也通
乎幽明之故而和敬之感孚則上下之神昭格
矣貫乎道器之全而制作之大備則精粗之體
===
舉會矣紀綱人道之大端而合情飾貌之下父
子君臣之節所由領矣是蓋禮樂之妙用所該
雖甚廣要皆造化之事也然則欲贊化育之道
舎禮樂其何以哉是故大人有見於此則必仰
觀俯察處至序以制禮而經曲之悉備有以昭
著其散殊之文玩至和以作樂而情文之兼該
有以發揚其不息之妙無聲無體之呈露固成
象成形者之所由彰也凡夫氣化之未周者將
自此以幽贊之矣極和極順之顯設固竝育竝
punctuated:
禮樂與造化相爲流通也，聖人舉之而化昭焉，不可以其爲用之妙哉？今夫禮樂之在天下也，固能管乎人情矣，然豈儀文聲容之謂乎？蓋嘗有以觀其深矣。彼天地之情，廣大而不可象，此其偵之；蓋兩儀肇和序之端，而同和同節者成其能也。神明之德，微妙而不可測，此其達之；蓋屈神秘藏用之機，而敦和别宜者顯諸仁也。通乎幽明之故，而和敬之感孚，則上下之神昭格矣；貫乎道器之全，而制作之大備，則精粗之體舉會矣；紀綱人道之大端，而合情飾貌之下，父子君臣之節所由領矣。是蓋禮樂之妙用所該，雖甚廣，要皆造化之事也。然則欲贊化育之道，舎禮樂其何以哉？

是故大人有見於此，則必仰觀俯察，處至序以制禮，而經曲之悉備，有以昭著其散殊之文；玩至和以作樂，而情文之兼該，有以發揚其不息之妙。無聲無體之呈露，固成象成形者之所由彰也。凡夫氣化之未周者，將自此以幽贊之矣。極和極順之顯設，固竝育竝
translation_en:
…rites and music circulate in mutual communion with the creative transformations of Heaven and Earth. When the sage puts them into practice, those transformations become manifest. Can this not be considered the marvel of their operation [?]? Now, rites and music in the world can certainly govern human feelings. But could they mean merely ceremonial forms, sounds, and outward appearances? Let us consider their deeper significance. The dispositions of Heaven and Earth are vast and cannot be represented in images; rites and music discern them [?]. For the two primal powers originate harmony and order, while that which shares their harmony and their measured order brings their capacities to fulfillment. The efficacy of spiritual powers is subtle and unfathomable; rites and music give it expression. For withdrawal and spiritual activity conceal the workings of their operation [?], while fostering harmony and distinguishing what is fitting make them manifest in benevolence. By penetrating the principles of the unseen and visible realms and making the influence of harmony and reverence sincerely felt, they cause the spirits above and below to come in manifest presence. By comprehending the entirety of the Way and its concrete embodiments, and fully providing the great institutions, they bring together both subtle and gross forms of existence. By ordering the great essentials of the human way, harmonizing feelings, and refining outward demeanor, they regulate the proper relationships between father and son, ruler and minister. Thus, although the marvelous operation of rites and music embraces an exceedingly broad range, all of it ultimately belongs to the work of creation and transformation. If one wishes to assist the process of transformation and nurture, by what means could one do so apart from rites and music?

Therefore, the great man, perceiving this, must look upward and examine what lies below. Grounding himself in perfect order, he institutes rites; their complete provision for both overarching principles and detailed observances makes manifest the patterned distinctions among things. Contemplating perfect harmony, he creates music; its inclusion of both inner feeling and outward form brings forth the marvel of ceaseless activity. The disclosure of what has neither sound nor bodily form is indeed how things that take on images and shapes become manifest. Wherever transformation through vital energy remains incomplete, rites and music will henceforth assist it unseen. The manifest establishment of perfect harmony and perfect accord is indeed that through which things are nurtured together and together…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
行之所由宣也凡夫玄工之不逮者將緣是以
默助之矣夫天地之化育必禮樂以昭宣如此
則天地且不能違矣而况於人乎此其所以能
管乎人情也雖然制作者其具也中和者其本
也天子能建中和之極則至樂無聲而天下化
至禮不讓而天下治雖無制作亦可也苟爲無
本則雖欲盡制抑末矣其如禮樂何哉而又何
治情宣化之足云故程子謂禮樂只是和序其
亦探本之論與
===
百官得其宜萬事得其序
徐豸
考試官敎授王批規格俊雅而意更明暢讀之
令人躍然
考試官敎諭陳批典雅切實
用人行政之皆善人君養盛所致也夫治天下
有本身之謂也今人無可適而政無可間其君
正莫不正乎記者之意若曰君身爲萬化之原
朝廷立四方之極故觀天子之德配天地而可
punctuated:
行之所由宣也。凡夫玄工之不逮者，將緣是以默助之矣。夫天地之化育，必禮樂以昭宣如此，則天地且不能違矣，而况於人乎？此其所以能管乎人情也。雖然，制作者其具也，中和者其本也。天子能建中和之極，則至樂無聲而天下化，至禮不讓而天下治，雖無制作亦可也。苟爲無本，則雖欲盡制，抑末矣，其如禮樂何哉？而又何治情宣化之足云？故程子謂禮樂只是和序，其亦探本之論與！

百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
徐豸
考試官敎授王批：規格俊雅，而意更明暢，讀之令人躍然。
考試官敎諭陳批：典雅切實。

用人行政之皆善，人君養盛所致也。夫治天下有本，身之謂也。今人無可適，而政無可間，其君正，莫不正乎？記者之意若曰：君身爲萬化之原，朝廷立四方之極，故觀天子之德配天地，而可
translation_en:
…is how their proceeding together is made manifest. Wherever the mysterious workings of creation fall short, these will silently assist them. Since the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth must thus be made manifest through rites and music, even Heaven and Earth cannot go against them—how much less can human beings! This is why they can govern human feelings. Nevertheless, institutional arrangements are their instruments; centrality and harmony are their foundation. If the Son of Heaven can establish the highest standard of centrality and harmony, then through supreme music, which has no sound, all under Heaven are transformed; through supreme ritual, which involves no yielding, all under Heaven are governed. Even without institutional arrangements, this would suffice. If the foundation is lacking, however, even an exhaustive effort to establish institutions attends only to the branches. What could this accomplish for rites and music? How could one even speak of governing feelings and making transformation manifest? Thus Master Cheng said that rites and music are simply harmony and order. Surely this, too, is a judgment that probes their foundation!

“The hundred officials obtain their proper places, and all affairs attain their proper order.”
Xu Zhi 徐豸
Examiner Wang, an Education Professor, comments: “The composition is distinguished and elegant in form, and its meaning is still more lucid and fluent. Reading it makes one’s spirits leap.”
Examiner Chen, an Education Instructor, comments: “Refined, pertinent, and substantial.”

Excellence in both employing men and administering government results from the ruler’s abundant self-cultivation. Governing all under Heaven has a foundation: the ruler’s own person. Now, if there is nothing to reproach in the men employed [?] and nothing to criticize in government, is this not because, when the ruler is upright, none fails to be upright? The writer’s meaning seems to be this: the ruler’s person is the source of all transformation, and the court establishes the standard for the four quarters. Thus, observing that the Son of Heaven’s virtue matches Heaven and Earth, one can…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以知化理之周矣彼先王設官分職以佐天下
之治固嘗建百官矣未易使之皆宜也今天子
隨在養德則元首之明自足以端股肱之則度
德叙位而百僚效靖共之節因能授任而多士
輸勵翼之誠以之登庸廊廟而為邇臣與必能
寅亮弘化而足以承事一人也以之服采邦國
而為遠臣與必能綜理庶務而足以宣力四方
也蓋人臣本有當然之分而又得明君以表儀
之夫固各盡其當然而恊諸義矣百官孰有不
===
宜者乎先王敷典成務以盡天下之賾固嘗有
萬事矣未易使之皆序也今天子養德之備則
元首之明自足以致庶事之康推行以漸貞百
度而有常施為當可熈庶績而不亂以大綱則
舉焉正體統而建之為維皇之極者昭如也以
萬目則張焉脩紀法而敷之為下土之式者秩
如也蓋政事本有自然之等而又得明君以總
攬之夫固各循其自然而歸諸理矣萬事孰有
不序者乎夫百官得宜則任官惟賢而事益理
punctuated: 以知化理之周矣。彼先王設官分職，以佐天下之治，固嘗建百官矣，未易使之皆宜也。今天子隨在養德，則元首之明自足以端股肱之則。度德叙位，而百僚效靖共之節；因能授任，而多士輸勵翼之誠。以之登庸廊廟而為邇臣與？必能寅亮弘化，而足以承事一人也。以之服采邦國而為遠臣與？必能綜理庶務，而足以宣力四方也。蓋人臣本有當然之分，而又得明君以表儀之，夫固各盡其當然而恊諸義矣，百官孰有不宜者乎？先王敷典成務，以盡天下之賾，固嘗有萬事矣，未易使之皆序也。今天子養德之備，則元首之明自足以致庶事之康。推行以漸，貞百度而有常；施為當可，熈庶績而不亂。以大綱則舉焉，正體統而建之為維皇之極者昭如也；以萬目則張焉，脩紀法而敷之為下土之式者秩如也。蓋政事本有自然之等，而又得明君以總攬之，夫固各循其自然而歸諸理矣，萬事孰有不序者乎？夫百官得宜，則任官惟賢而事益理
translation_en:
…one may thereby know how comprehensive his transforming influence and governance are. The former kings established offices and apportioned duties to assist in governing all under Heaven. They certainly instituted the hundred offices, yet it was no easy matter to ensure that all were suitably filled. Now, when the Son of Heaven cultivates his virtue in every circumstance, the enlightened head is of itself sufficient to rectify the standards of his limbs—the ministers. He assesses virtue and assigns rank, and all officials display the integrity of devoted, reverent service; he grants responsibilities according to ability, and the many officers offer their sincere efforts to assist him. Are they promoted to service at court as ministers close to him? They will surely assist him reverently and faithfully and extend his transforming influence, proving fully capable of serving the One Man, the sovereign. Are they employed in the regions as ministers far from him? They will surely administer the various affairs comprehensively, proving fully capable of exerting themselves throughout the realm. Ministers already have their proper duties, and they also gain an enlightened ruler to serve as their model. Thus each fully performs what he ought and accords with righteousness. Which of the hundred offices, then, could fail to be suitably filled?

The former kings promulgated statutes and accomplished their tasks, attending exhaustively to the intricate affairs of all under Heaven. They certainly had myriad affairs to manage, yet it was no easy matter to bring them all into order. Now, when the Son of Heaven's cultivation of virtue is complete, the enlightenment of the head is of itself sufficient to bring all affairs to a sound condition. Measures are implemented gradually, setting the various institutions right and giving them constancy; actions accord with what is fitting, bringing the various undertakings to fruition without disorder. As for the main cord of the net, it is raised: the governing order is rectified and established as the sovereign's supreme standard, clear for all to see. As for its myriad meshes, they are spread: regulations and laws are put in good order and promulgated as models for the lands below, each in its proper place. Affairs of government already have their natural gradations, and they also gain an enlightened ruler to oversee them as a whole. Thus each follows its natural course and accords with principle. Which of the myriad affairs, then, could fail to be ordered? When the hundred offices are suitably filled, only the worthy are appointed, and affairs become ever better governed…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬事得序則位事惟能而官益勸此其相須以
有成而天子之所以治天下參天地也與雖然
養德在君而所以成君之德者又在臣也蓋人
臣能將順匡救而使吾君動皆合宜行已有序
則禮義全而君德備所以賛化育而參天地者
亦自我得之矣否則君心不正則非禮之禮非
義之義日滋也其如用人行政何噫孟子有格
君心之責望大人其意微矣
第貳場
===
論
爲天下國家有九經
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批九經之要本在一誠誠即人之
生理而爲仁此天人一貫之道也作獨能發之其真
探本之論歟
考試官教諭陳批見理精徹立論古雅
考試官教授王批議論正大
人君有天下國家之責必欲有以治之非可以
punctuated:
萬事得序，則位事惟能而官益勸。此其相須以有成，而天子之所以治天下、參天地也與！雖然，養德在君，而所以成君之德者又在臣也。蓋人臣能將順匡救，而使吾君動皆合宜，行已有序，則禮義全而君德備，所以賛化育而參天地者，亦自我得之矣。否則，君心不正，則非禮之禮、非義之義日滋也，其如用人行政何？噫！孟子有格君心之責望大人，其意微矣。
第貳場
論
爲天下國家有九經
彭啓忠
同考試官學正鐵批：九經之要，本在一誠。誠即人之生理而爲仁，此天人一貫之道也。作獨能發之，其真探本之論歟！
考試官教諭陳批：見理精徹，立論古雅。
考試官教授王批：議論正大。
人君有天下國家之責，必欲有以治之，非可以
translation_en:
…When all affairs are properly ordered, duties are assigned solely to the capable, and officials become still more diligent. These two depend upon one another for their accomplishment: this is how the Son of Heaven governs the world and forms a triad with Heaven and Earth! Nevertheless, while nurturing virtue rests with the ruler, bringing the ruler’s virtue to completion rests also with his ministers. If ministers can support what is right and correct what is wrong, so that every action of our ruler is fitting and his personal conduct is orderly, ritual propriety and righteousness will be complete, and the ruler’s virtue fully developed. The means of assisting the transforming and nourishing processes of creation and forming a triad with Heaven and Earth will thus also derive from us. Otherwise, if the ruler’s heart is not upright, proprieties that are not truly proper and acts of righteousness that are not truly righteous will multiply daily. What then can be done about employing men and administering government? Ah! Mencius expected great men to assume responsibility for rectifying the ruler’s heart. Profound indeed was his meaning.
Second Session
Discourse
“There Are Nine Guiding Principles for Governing the World, the State, and the Family”
Peng Qizhong
Comment by Associate Examiner Tie, School Director: The essentials of the nine guiding principles are rooted in sincerity alone. Sincerity is the principle of life in human beings and constitutes benevolence; this is the Way that runs through Heaven and humanity alike. This composition alone succeeds in bringing it out. Is this not truly a discourse that probes the root?
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: His perception of principle is precise and penetrating; his argument is classical and elegant.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: The discussion is upright and broad in scope.
The ruler bears responsibility for the world, the state, and the family, and must seek the means to govern them. This cannot be done by…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
徒法爲也亦惟道之本諸身者運之而已矣古
今之言治者必曰道道固未有不出乎身者出
乎身而施之家推之國達之天下雖行之萬世
而不易可也斯則經之所由名也經即道也道
一而已矣而曰九經自爲天下國家言也是故
由吾身以及于家國天下曰脩身也尊賢也親
親也敬大臣也體羣臣也子庶民也來百工也
柔遠人也懷諸侯也以天下國家而約之吾身
則曰所以行之者一也此夫子告魯哀公之言
===
雖所以推廣文武之政而實所以立萬世君道
之準也今夫人君一身至寡也天下國家至大
也天下國家之人至衆也賢者親者大臣羣臣
庶民百工遠人諸侯其所以取足于我者又紛
然至不一也以至寡之身握至大之勢御至衆
之人而欲一其至不一之情豈智術法令之所
能爲哉無亦因其自有之理而我有以應之因
其各足之分而我有以與之而已必我有以應
之與之而後可則不求諸身而求諸天下國家
punctuated:
徒法爲也，亦惟道之本諸身者運之而已矣。古今之言治者必曰道，道固未有不出乎身者。出乎身而施之家，推之國，達之天下，雖行之萬世而不易可也。斯則經之所由名也。經即道也，道一而已矣，而曰九經，自爲天下國家言也。是故由吾身以及于家國天下，曰脩身也、尊賢也、親親也、敬大臣也、體羣臣也、子庶民也、來百工也、柔遠人也、懷諸侯也。以天下國家而約之吾身，則曰所以行之者一也。此夫子告魯哀公之言，雖所以推廣文武之政，而實所以立萬世君道之準也。
今夫人君一身至寡也，天下國家至大也，天下國家之人至衆也。賢者、親者、大臣、羣臣、庶民、百工、遠人、諸侯，其所以取足于我者，又紛然至不一也。以至寡之身，握至大之勢，御至衆之人，而欲一其至不一之情，豈智術法令之所能爲哉？無亦因其自有之理而我有以應之，因其各足之分而我有以與之而已。必我有以應之與之而後可，則不求諸身而求諸天下國家
translation_en:
…be accomplished through laws alone; it requires only putting into operation the Way that is rooted in oneself. Those who have spoken of government, ancient and modern alike, invariably speak of the Way. The Way has never failed to issue from oneself. Issuing from oneself, it is applied to the family, extended to the state, and carried throughout all under Heaven; it may then be practiced for ten thousand generations without alteration. This is why these principles are called constant rules. Constant rules are the Way, and the Way is one and nothing more. Yet they are called the nine constant rules when considered from the standpoint of governing all under Heaven, the state, and the family. Thus, proceeding from oneself to the family, the state, and all under Heaven, they are: cultivating oneself, honoring the worthy, cherishing one's kin, respecting the great ministers, showing sympathetic concern for the body of officials, treating the common people as one's children, attracting the various artisans, treating people from afar with kindness, and winning the allegiance of the feudal lords. When all under Heaven, the state, and the family are brought back to their foundation in oneself, it is said: “That by which these are put into practice is one.” These words, spoken by the Master to Duke Ai of Lu, served to elaborate the government of Kings Wen and Wu, but in truth established the standard for the way of rulership for ten thousand generations.
Now, the ruler's single person is exceedingly small in number; all under Heaven, the state, and the family are exceedingly vast; and their people are exceedingly numerous. The worthy, one's kin, the great ministers, the body of officials, the common people, the various artisans, people from afar, and the feudal lords—the things they look to me to supply are bewilderingly diverse. With a single person, to wield such vast power, govern so many people, and seek to bring unity to their utterly diverse dispositions—could this possibly be accomplished through clever techniques, laws, and commands? Surely it consists simply in following the principles inherent in them and having the means within myself to respond to them, and in following the allotted share sufficient for each and having the means within myself to provide it. Only when I have the means to respond to them and provide for them can this succeed. Thus, to seek this in all under Heaven, the state, and the family instead of in oneself…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也祗見其日鶩于叢脞而不可爲也已誠知夫
天下國家之人即一人也一人之身即天下國
家之身也如是而視吾身如是而視天下國家
使我與天下國家共爲一體元氣充滿流行而
四肢百骸莫不相貫視聽持行罔不相用無有
壅塞凌悖間隔而不通之處是爲大公而無我
大公而無我故能順應而不窮斯吾身與天下
國家竝理之至術也噫身爲本一爲要焉所謂
一者豈出于夫子所言哉夫子前此曰脩身以
===
道脩道以仁仁者人也後此則曰誠身誠者天
之道也自天而言謂之誠自人而言謂之仁誠
非仁之肫肫乎仁非誠之生生乎天道誠也而
其一元之氣運行不息其始萬物者元也其品
物流形爲亨元之流形也其變化旣成萬物爲
利貞即元之變化也曰復其見天地之心曰天
地之大德曰生天地之心何嘗一日而不生物
哉天命流行物與無妄吾身之所自來也屬之
于心則曰人得天地生物之心以爲心然則夫
punctuated:
也，祗見其日鶩于叢脞而不可爲也已。誠知夫天下國家之人即一人也，一人之身即天下國家之身也，如是而視吾身，如是而視天下國家，使我與天下國家共爲一體，元氣充滿流行，而四肢百骸莫不相貫，視聽持行罔不相用，無有壅塞凌悖間隔而不通之處，是爲大公而無我。大公而無我，故能順應而不窮，斯吾身與天下國家竝理之至術也。
噫！身爲本，一爲要焉。所謂一者，豈出于夫子所言哉？夫子前此曰：「脩身以道，脩道以仁，仁者人也。」後此則曰：「誠身。」「誠者，天之道也。」自天而言謂之誠，自人而言謂之仁。誠非仁之肫肫乎？仁非誠之生生乎？天道誠也，而其一元之氣運行不息。其始萬物者，元也；其品物流形爲亨，元之流形也；其變化旣成萬物爲利貞，即元之變化也。曰：「復，其見天地之心。」曰：「天地之大德曰生。」天地之心何嘗一日而不生物哉？天命流行，物與無妄，吾身之所自來也。屬之于心，則曰：「人得天地生物之心以爲心。」然則夫
translation_en:
…one will only find oneself daily pursuing petty details, unable to accomplish anything. Truly understand that the people of the world, the state, and the family are a single person, and that one person’s body is the body of the world, the state, and the family. Regard oneself in this way, and regard the world, the state, and the family in this way, so that oneself and all these together form one body. Its primal vital energy fills it and circulates throughout; its four limbs and hundred bones are all interconnected, and seeing, hearing, grasping, and walking all serve one another. Nowhere is there obstruction, disorder, or separation that prevents communication. This is perfect impartiality without selfishness. Being perfectly impartial and without selfishness, one can respond fittingly without exhaustion. This is the supreme method for bringing both oneself and the world, the state, and the family into order.
Ah! The self is the foundation, and unity is the essential point. Could this so-called unity lie outside what the Master said? Earlier, the Master said: “Cultivate oneself through the Way; cultivate the Way through humaneness. Humaneness is being human.” Later, he spoke of “making oneself sincere” and said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven.” Viewed from Heaven, it is called sincerity; viewed from humanity, it is called humaneness. Is sincerity not the profound earnestness of humaneness? Is humaneness not the ceaseless generation of sincerity? Heaven’s Way is sincerity, and its single primal vital energy circulates without rest. That which initiates the myriad things is origination, yuan. The various things flowing into their forms constitute flourishing, heng: this is origination flowing into form. Their transformation, once it has brought the myriad things to completion, constitutes benefit and constancy, li and zhen: these are the transformations of origination itself. It is said: “In Return, may we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth?” It is also said: “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation.” Has the heart of Heaven and Earth ever gone a single day without generating things? Heaven’s mandate circulates, and things partake of freedom from falsity [?]; this is the source from which our own selves arise. In relation to the heart, it is said: “Human beings receive the heart with which Heaven and Earth generate things, and take it as their own heart.” Thus, the Master…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
子所謂誠與仁者非二也卽所謂一也此理在
人渾然無欲粹然不雜謂之至善能明善則能
誠身誠身卽仁其身也能仁其身則吾身爲德
之聚而達德非三也爲道之管而達道非五也
爲人之存而文武非爲先也故能視天下國家
之人惟我而視我惟人凡人之有所取足于我
者我皆有以順其性平其情不違其所願而與
之各得其所賢者吾有以尊之義之所以盡也
親者吾有以親之仁之所以至也于大臣敬之
===
于羣臣體之庶民子之百工來之遠人諸侯則
柔之懷之何莫而非親親之殺尊賢之等也禮
之所以達也故曰所以行之者一也是爲天下
國家之常經而二帝三王之所不能易者也稽
諸陶唐氏睦族和邦授時釐工莫非經也而實
堯之明德能仁其身爲之稽諸有虞氏齊政輯
瑞詢岳命官莫非經也而實舜之精一能仁其
身爲之夏商以來六事之治五服之制人紀之
脩官刑之儆莫非經也而實禹湯之好善執中
punctuated:
子所謂誠與仁者，非二也，卽所謂一也。此理在人，渾然無欲，粹然不雜，謂之至善。能明善，則能誠身；誠身，卽仁其身也。能仁其身，則吾身爲德之聚，而達德非三也；爲道之管，而達道非五也；爲人之存，而文武非爲先也。故能視天下國家之人惟我，而視我惟人。凡人之有所取足于我者，我皆有以順其性，平其情，不違其所願，而與之各得其所。賢者，吾有以尊之，義之所以盡也；親者，吾有以親之，仁之所以至也。于大臣敬之，于羣臣體之，庶民子之，百工來之，遠人諸侯則柔之懷之，何莫而非親親之殺、尊賢之等也？禮之所以達也。故曰：「所以行之者一也。」是爲天下國家之常經，而二帝三王之所不能易者也。
稽諸陶唐氏，睦族和邦、授時釐工，莫非經也，而實堯之明德能仁其身爲之。稽諸有虞氏，齊政輯瑞、詢岳命官，莫非經也，而實舜之精一能仁其身爲之。夏商以來，六事之治、五服之制、人紀之脩、官刑之儆，莫非經也，而實禹湯之好善執中
translation_en:
…what the Master calls sincerity and benevolence are not two things: they are precisely what he calls the one. This principle, present in human beings, is wholly free of desire, pure and unmixed; it is called the highest good. If one can understand goodness, one can make oneself sincere; making oneself sincere is precisely embodying benevolence. If I can embody benevolence, my person becomes the gathering place of the virtues, and the universally applicable virtues are not three separate things; it becomes the conduit of the Way, and the universally applicable relationships are not five separate things; it constitutes the presence of the requisite person, so that Kings Wen and Wu have no priority [?]. Thus I can regard the people of the world, the state, and the family as myself, and myself as others. Whatever others look to me to provide, I have the means to accord with their natures and bring their feelings into balance, without contravening their wishes, enabling each to find their proper place. I have the means to honor the worthy: through this, righteousness is fulfilled. I have the means to cherish my kin: through this, benevolence reaches its utmost. I respect the great ministers and show consideration for the other ministers; I treat the common people as my children and attract the various artisans; I deal gently with people from afar and cherish the feudal lords. How could any of these fail to express the decreasing degrees of affection for kin and the graded honors accorded to the worthy? Through these, ritual propriety finds universal expression. Hence the saying: “That by which these are put into practice is one.” These are the constant guiding principles for the world, the state, and the family, which even the Two Emperors and Three Kings could not alter.
Consider the ruler of Taotang: bringing harmony to his kin and concord to the states, promulgating the seasons and ordering the various labors—all were applications of these guiding principles. Yet it was truly Yao’s luminous virtue, enabling him to embody benevolence, that accomplished them. Consider the ruler of Youyu: regulating government, collecting the jade tokens, consulting the Chiefs of the Four Mountains, and appointing officials—all were applications of these principles. Yet it was truly Shun’s refined discernment and singleness of purpose, enabling him to embody benevolence, that accomplished them. From the Xia and Shang onward, governance through the six responsibilities, the system of the five service zones, the cultivation of human relationships, and the admonitions concerning punishments for officials—all were applications of these principles. Yet it was truly Yu’s and Tang’s love of goodness and adherence to the mean…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
能仁其身爲之迨周文王以緝熈仁其身故刑
于寡妻以至兄弟以御于家邦振作綱紀而九
經之政行焉武王以執競仁其身故始于治內
暨于治外以至制禮作樂不泄不忘而九經之
政弘焉文武之道即堯舜之道也夫子祖述堯
舜憲章文武而志欲行周公之道亦所以行堯
舜之道行文武之道也春秋之時邪說起而學
術散覇政作而王風微道在夫子而不得爲有
位者之事故自言曰大道之行三代之英丘未
===
之逮也而竊有志焉吁亦悲矣猶有魯哀公之
問非幸邪魯吾父母之邦也周公之後也昔者
魯公之國周公訓以不弛其親不遺大臣不棄
故舊不求備一人魯公以此治其國三年報政
曰尊賢而親親是九經固魯先公之所行也歷
世漸遠不無廢墜吾特從而脩舉之則一變至
道魯爲周公伯禽之魯矣使吾欲道之行而姑
就功利之國孰若從魯之爲易是故不薄其君
之不爲文武問焉必告告焉必盡好學力行知
punctuated:
能仁其身爲之。迨周文王以緝熈仁其身，故刑于寡妻，以至兄弟，以御于家邦，振作綱紀，而九經之政行焉。武王以執競仁其身，故始于治內，暨于治外，以至制禮作樂，不泄不忘，而九經之政弘焉。文武之道，即堯舜之道也。夫子祖述堯舜，憲章文武，而志欲行周公之道，亦所以行堯舜之道、行文武之道也。
春秋之時，邪說起而學術散，覇政作而王風微。道在夫子，而不得爲有位者之事，故自言曰：「大道之行，三代之英，丘未之逮也，而竊有志焉。」吁，亦悲矣！猶有魯哀公之問，非幸邪？魯，吾父母之邦也，周公之後也。昔者魯公之國，周公訓以不弛其親，不遺大臣，不棄故舊，不求備一人。魯公以此治其國，三年報政，曰：「尊賢而親親。」是九經固魯先公之所行也。歷世漸遠，不無廢墜，吾特從而脩舉之，則一變至道，魯爲周公伯禽之魯矣。使吾欲道之行，而姑就功利之國，孰若從魯之爲易？是故不薄其君之不爲文武，問焉必告，告焉必盡。好學、力行、知
translation_en:
…enabled them to embody benevolence in their own persons and thereby accomplish this. When King Wen of Zhou came, he embodied benevolence through continuous cultivation of luminous virtue. Thus he set an example for his wife, extended it to his brothers, and thereby governed his household and state. He reinvigorated the guiding principles and ordering bonds, and government according to the nine guidelines was put into practice. King Wu embodied benevolence through steadfast strength. Thus he began by ordering affairs within and proceeded to those without, ultimately instituting rites and creating music. Without slackening or forgetting, he enlarged the government of the nine guidelines. The Way of Wen and Wu was precisely the Way of Yao and Shun. The Master transmitted the traditions of Yao and Shun and took Wen and Wu as his models. His aspiration to put the Duke of Zhou’s Way into practice was likewise a means of practicing the Way of Yao and Shun and the Way of Wen and Wu.
In the Spring and Autumn period, heterodox teachings arose and learning fragmented; government by hegemons emerged, and the influence of true kingship waned. The Way resided in the Master, yet he could not undertake the work of those holding office. Thus he himself said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—these I, Qiu, came too late to encounter, yet I privately aspire to them.” Alas, how sorrowful! Yet there was still Duke Ai of Lu’s inquiry: was this not fortunate? Lu was the land of my father and mother, the domain of the Duke of Zhou’s descendants. Formerly, when the Duke of Lu went to his state, the Duke of Zhou instructed him not to neglect his relatives, not to disregard his great ministers, not to abandon old associates, and not to demand perfection of any one person. The Duke of Lu governed his state by these principles. After three years, he reported on his government, saying: “I honor the worthy and cherish my kin.” Thus the nine guidelines were indeed practiced by Lu’s founding duke. As successive generations grew more distant, some things inevitably fell into neglect. If I simply restored and implemented them, then with a single transformation Lu would attain the Way and become once again the Lu of the Duke of Zhou and Boqin. If I wished the Way to be practiced, but provisionally turned to a state devoted to achievement and profit, how could that be as easy as proceeding through Lu? Thus the Master did not disdain its ruler for failing to be a Wen or a Wu. Whenever asked, he invariably explained; whenever he explained, he did so fully. Loving learning, striving to act, knowing…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
恥與人一己百人十己千之說皆為哀公設也
而夫子之情亦激矣不然九經之章吾道一以
貫之一言而足何樂乎其詞之費也夫不灼其
形昧者弗覩不烈其聲聵者弗聞灼其形烈其
聲而猶弗覩弗聞如哀公夫子且奈之何噫九
經之義昭然漢以霸蝕唐以夷棄宋未盡行明
而行之不能無待于知人知天者
表
擬宋宣撫使狄青平廣南羣臣賀表〔皇祐〕
===
〔五年〕
洪敷誥
同考試官教諭梁 批狄青崑崙之捷場中能悉
其故實者絕少獨此作敘事詳明摛詞典雅且忠
愛之誠盎然可掬非特四六之工已也
考試官教諭陳 批體裁雅整詞藻煥發
考試官教授王 批駢麗可則
皇祐五年宣撫使狄青大破蠻賊儂智高
于邕州廣南悉平臣某等謹奉
punctuated:
恥與人一己百、人十己千之說，皆為哀公設也，而夫子之情亦激矣。不然，九經之章，「吾道一以貫之」，一言而足，何樂乎其詞之費也？夫不灼其形，昧者弗覩；不烈其聲，聵者弗聞。灼其形，烈其聲，而猶弗覩弗聞，如哀公，夫子且奈之何？噫！九經之義昭然，漢以霸蝕，唐以夷棄，宋未盡行。明而行之，不能無待于知人知天者。

表

擬宋宣撫使狄青平廣南羣臣賀表〔皇祐〕〔五年〕

洪敷誥

同考試官教諭梁批：狄青崑崙之捷，場中能悉其故實者絕少。獨此作敘事詳明，摛詞典雅，且忠愛之誠盎然可掬，非特四六之工已也。

考試官教諭陳批：體裁雅整，詞藻煥發。

考試官教授王批：駢麗可則。

皇祐五年，宣撫使狄青大破蠻賊儂智高于邕州，廣南悉平。臣某等謹奉
translation_en:
…shame, and the teaching that what others accomplish with one effort, one should accomplish with a hundred, and what others accomplish with ten, one should accomplish with a thousand—all were propounded for Duke Ai. The Master's feelings, too, were deeply stirred. Otherwise, for the chapter on the nine guiding principles, the single statement, “My Way is bound together by one thread,” would have sufficed. Why would he have willingly expended so many words? Unless a form shines brightly, the dim-sighted cannot see it; unless a sound is forceful, the deaf cannot hear it. Yet if, even with the form made bright and the sound made forceful, someone still neither sees nor hears—as with Duke Ai—what could the Master do with him? Alas! The meaning of the nine guiding principles is manifest. The Han eroded it through hegemonic rule; the Tang abandoned it through barbarian ways; the Song did not fully put it into practice. To understand and carry it out, we must still await someone who knows human beings and knows Heaven.

Memorial

A Composed Congratulatory Memorial from the Assembled Officials on the Song Pacification Commissioner Di Qing's Pacification of Guangnan 〔Huangyou〕〔fifth year〕

Hong Fugao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: Very few candidates in the examination compound knew all the historical details of Di Qing's victory at Kunlun. This composition alone narrates the events fully and clearly, expressing them in classical and elegant language. Moreover, its sincere loyalty and devotion are so abundant as to be almost tangible. Its merit is more than simply skill in four-and-six parallel prose.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The form is elegant and orderly; the diction is resplendent.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Its elegant parallel prose may serve as a model.

In the fifth year of Huangyou, Pacification Commissioner Di Qing decisively defeated the barbarian rebel Nong Zhigao at Yongzhou, and all Guangnan was pacified. Your servants, so-and-so and the others, respectfully present…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
表稱
賀者伏以
六師雷動隼旟指翼軫以南征五嶺風清
鰲極控湖湘而北奠運
謨猷于帷幄銷氛祲於潢池捷
獻崑崙歡騰河洛臣某等誠懽誠忭稽首頓
首竊惟虞帝嚴猾夏之防士師勅法周官
重攘夷之略司馬專征舞干羽于七旬有
苗來格勤師徒於六月獫狁于襄蓋人主
===
守在四夷用昭文德以威不軌而天王治
大一統當除戎器以戒不虞粵若廣南寔
稱邊徼在虞周尚違聲教至秦漢始入職
方馬援收徵側之勛百蠻褫魄任囂諭蒼
梧之詔列郡歸心迨有唐既疲河北之師
致中葉遂隳日南之績夷酋跋扈勢有類
乎鴟張險阻憑陵衆實同于蟻聚自昔乍
臣而乍叛伊誰七縱而七擒顧
今海內為家豈容榻邊鼾睡
punctuated:
表稱賀者，伏以：六師雷動，隼旟指翼軫以南征；五嶺風清，鰲極控湖湘而北奠。運謨猷于帷幄，銷氛祲於潢池；捷獻崑崙，歡騰河洛。臣某等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。
竊惟虞帝嚴猾夏之防，士師勅法；周官重攘夷之略，司馬專征。舞干羽于七旬，有苗來格；勤師徒於六月，獫狁于襄。蓋人主守在四夷，用昭文德以威不軌；而天王治大一統，當除戎器以戒不虞。粵若廣南，寔稱邊徼。在虞周尚違聲教，至秦漢始入職方。馬援收徵側之勛，百蠻褫魄；任囂諭蒼梧之詔，列郡歸心。迨有唐既疲河北之師，致中葉遂隳日南之績。夷酋跋扈，勢有類乎鴟張；險阻憑陵，衆實同于蟻聚。自昔乍臣而乍叛，伊誰七縱而七擒？顧今海內為家，豈容榻邊鼾睡？
translation_en:
…this memorial offering congratulations. We humbly submit: the Six Armies moved like thunder, their falcon banners pointing toward the constellations Yi and Zhen as they campaigned southward; the winds over the Five Ridges are clear, and the turtle-supported imperial axis commands the Hu-Xiang region, securing the north. Plans were devised within the command tent, and the baleful vapors of rebellion were dispelled from the stagnant pools. Victory at Kunlun was reported; rejoicing surged through the lands of the Yellow and Luo Rivers. We, your servants, are truly joyful and truly delighted; we bow our heads to the ground and kowtow.
We respectfully reflect that the Emperor of Yu rigorously guarded against those who would disturb the Chinese realm, and his Judge enforced the laws. The offices of Zhou gave weight to the strategy of repelling the foreign peoples, and the Minister of War exercised sole command of punitive expeditions. After seventy days of dances with shields and feathers, the Youmiao came to submit; when the troops exerted themselves in the sixth month, the Xianyun were driven off. For a ruler’s defenses lie among the peoples of the four quarters: he makes manifest his civil virtue to overawe the lawless. And the Son of Heaven, governing a realm under unified rule, must put weapons in readiness against unforeseen dangers.
As for Guangnan, it is indeed a frontier region. Under Yu and Zhou it still lay beyond the reach of royal instruction; only under Qin and Han did it enter the empire’s administrative domain. Ma Yuan won merit by subduing Zheng Ce, striking terror into the many southern peoples; Ren Xiao proclaimed an edict to Cangwu [?], and the commanderies gave their allegiance. By the Tang, however, military operations in Hebei had exhausted its forces, so that by the dynasty’s middle period its achievements in Rinan had fallen into ruin. The foreign chieftains grew overbearing, spreading their power like owls spreading their wings; relying on difficult terrain, they acted arrogantly, their multitudes gathering like ants. From ancient times they have alternated between submission and rebellion: who could release them seven times and capture them seven times? Yet now that all within the seas forms one household, how could anyone be allowed to snore beside the imperial couch?

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天佑一德
日靖四方恭惟
〇〇〇〇
文明憲古
睿智沉幾
本忠厚以纘圖
推誠信而懷遠五兵常偃藹然天地之春羣
策畢收沛若江河之決西傾元昊則橫山
涇原之境烽燧不驚北弭契丹則燕雲幽
===
薊之民干戈載戢兆庶共訢於翼戴萬方
盡被乎陶鎔蠢玆儂族之蠻初屬廣源之
種渠魁倡亂始盤據於一方羣黨恊謀遂
蔓延于二廣敢移書而求節鉞輒僭號以
擬
乘輿烏合五千餘人鼓行略地鯨呑六七巨郡
扇虐薰天釜底揚鬐甘效涸鱗之狀轍前
攘臂妄逞怒螳之兇裒鞠狂圖包藏逆釁
雖鬼方未伐奚損商室之中興而密旅不
punctuated:
天佑一德，日靖四方。恭惟〇〇〇〇，文明憲古，睿智沉幾，本忠厚以纘圖，推誠信而懷遠。五兵常偃，藹然天地之春；羣策畢收，沛若江河之決。西傾元昊，則橫山、涇原之境烽燧不驚；北弭契丹，則燕雲、幽薊之民干戈載戢。兆庶共訢於翼戴，萬方盡被乎陶鎔。

蠢玆儂族之蠻，初屬廣源之種。渠魁倡亂，始盤據於一方；羣黨恊謀，遂蔓延于二廣。敢移書而求節鉞，輒僭號以擬乘輿。烏合五千餘人，鼓行略地；鯨呑六七巨郡，扇虐薰天。釜底揚鬐，甘效涸鱗之狀；轍前攘臂，妄逞怒螳之兇。裒鞠狂圖，包藏逆釁。雖鬼方未伐，奚損商室之中興？而密旅不
translation_en:
Heaven aids the one steadfast in virtue, who daily brings peace to the four quarters. We reverently contemplate 〇〇〇〇: enlightened and cultured, taking antiquity as a model; sagacious and discerning, deeply attentive to the subtle beginnings of events. Grounding the continuation of imperial rule in loyalty and generosity, you extend sincerity and trustworthiness to win over distant peoples. The weapons of war lie ever at rest, amid a benevolence like spring throughout heaven and earth; all counsels are accepted, flowing abundantly like rivers bursting through their banks. With Yuanhao brought low in the west, no alarm rises from the beacon towers along the borders of Hengshan and Jingyuan. With the Khitan pacified in the north, weapons are laid aside among the people of Yan, Yun, You, and Ji. The common people rejoice together in supporting their sovereign, and every region receives your transforming influence.

These unruly barbarians of the Nong clan originally belonged to the people of Guangyuan. Their chief instigated rebellion, at first occupying a single region; his followers conspired together, and the trouble then spread throughout Guangdong and Guangxi. He dared send letters seeking the insignia of military command, and presumptuously assumed a title to rival the emperor. Gathering a disorderly host of more than five thousand men, he advanced to the beat of drums and seized territory. Swallowing up six or seven great prefectures, he spread cruelty whose fumes reached heaven. Raising their fins at the bottom of a cauldron, they willingly acted like fish stranded without water; baring their arms before an approaching wheel, they vainly displayed the ferocity of an angry mantis. They nurtured their reckless designs [?] and harbored rebellious intentions. Though Guifang had not yet been attacked, how did that diminish the restoration of the Shang ruling house? Yet the hosts of Mi were not …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
共難釋周文之赫怒上廑
宵旰博訪安攘紓籌策於
九重兼聽輿人之誦聞鼓鼙于四境爰思將帥
之遺迺
命樞貳之重臣俾膺經略之大任
綸綍自天而下
制重登壇牙旗向日而開
命隆專閫鷹鸇奮擊乘雲氣而度斗南貔虎成
羣挾風聲而踰嶺表晡傳蓐食宵下險關
===
嚴陳曙失律之誅三軍股栗鼓費達先登
之勇羣醜魂搖驅精銳以摧其前席卷建
瓴之勢麾蕃落直擣於後刃迎破竹之鋒
彼黨方豕突而狼奔我師咸投石而超距
追亡百里山川震逐北之威俘馘萬人草
木動征西之氣殲厥醜類固我封疆救民
水火之中室家胥慶旋師枕席之上簞食
來迎士已樂乎投戈野咸安於負耒追蹤
銅柱紀不世奇勳奏績
punctuated: 共，難釋周文之赫怒。上廑宵旰，博訪安攘，紓籌策於九重，兼聽輿人之誦；聞鼓鼙于四境，爰思將帥之遺。迺命樞貳之重臣，俾膺經略之大任。綸綍自天而下，制重登壇；牙旗向日而開，命隆專閫。鷹鸇奮擊，乘雲氣而度斗南；貔虎成羣，挾風聲而踰嶺表。晡傳蓐食，宵下險關。嚴陳曙失律之誅，三軍股栗；鼓費達先登之勇，羣醜魂搖。驅精銳以摧其前，席卷建瓴之勢；麾蕃落直擣於後，刃迎破竹之鋒。彼黨方豕突而狼奔，我師咸投石而超距。追亡百里，山川震逐北之威；俘馘萬人，草木動征西之氣。殲厥醜類，固我封疆。救民水火之中，室家胥慶；旋師枕席之上，簞食來迎。士已樂乎投戈，野咸安於負耒。追蹤銅柱，紀不世奇勳；奏績
translation_en:
…failed to show submission, making it difficult to appease King Wen of Zhou’s blazing wrath. This troubled His Majesty, who attended to affairs before dawn and ate only late at night. He sought counsel widely on pacification and repelling aggression, developing strategies within the ninefold palace and also hearing the people’s voiced opinions. Hearing war drums throughout the realm, he recalled the legacy of past commanders. He therefore appointed a high minister serving as deputy in the military administration to undertake the great responsibility of directing the campaign.

The imperial command descended from Heaven, lending solemn authority to his ascent of the general’s platform; the ivory-decorated standard unfurled toward the sun, and the commission bestowed exalted authority to command independently in the field. Hawks and falcons struck fiercely, riding the clouds south of the Dipper; troops fierce as mythical beasts and tigers assembled in hosts, crossing beyond the mountains amid the roaring wind. Orders were relayed at dusk, and the men ate on their bedding [?]; by night they descended through the perilous pass. The stern execution of Chen Shu for violating military discipline made the entire army tremble. The valor of Fei Da [?], first to scale the defenses, stirred the troops and shook the rebels’ souls.

The picked troops were driven forward to crush the enemy’s front, sweeping all before them with the force of water poured from a high roof. Tribal troops were directed to strike straight at the rear, their blades advancing as easily as splitting bamboo. While the enemy bands charged like boars and fled like wolves, our soldiers displayed their strength in stone throwing and long jumping. They pursued the fugitives for a hundred li, making mountains and rivers quake at the might of the pursuit; ten thousand were taken captive or had their ears severed as trophies, and even the vegetation stirred at the spirit of the western expedition. They annihilated those vile bands and secured our frontiers.

The people were rescued from fire and flood, and every household rejoiced. The army returned as peacefully as if resting upon pillows and mats, and people came to welcome it with baskets of food. The soldiers now delighted in laying down their weapons, while those in the countryside could all shoulder their plows in peace. Following the precedent of the bronze pillar, they recorded extraordinary achievements unmatched for generations; they reported their accomplishments…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
玉階彰曠時之偉略是皆
宸衷獨斷明威電照于域中遂令將校同心號
令風行乎閫外固將除兇而翦逆誠非黷
武以窮兵築京觀於邕南翼翼奠華夷之
界限息狼烟于甌駱明明壯百二之山河
臣等敵愾有懷憂時共念勞未伸於汗馬
拊已知慙心嘗切于據鞍聞風思奮仰窺
勝算嘆識
帝王之有真幸際凱旋知
===
仁者之無敵車騎懽呼於重譯衣冠蹈舞于
千班伏願
駿烈覃敷
鴻恩遐曁
乃文乃武用對
帝臣之心
作福作威式敷
皇極之訓右騶虞貍首
瑤圖鞏周道於緜延朝荆楚享氐羌
punctuated:
玉階，彰曠時之偉略。是皆宸衷獨斷，明威電照于域中，遂令將校同心，號令風行乎閫外。固將除兇而翦逆，誠非黷武以窮兵。築京觀於邕南，翼翼奠華夷之界限；息狼烟于甌駱，明明壯百二之山河。臣等敵愾有懷，憂時共念。勞未伸於汗馬，拊已知慙；心嘗切于據鞍，聞風思奮。仰窺勝算，嘆識帝王之有真；幸際凱旋，知仁者之無敵。車騎懽呼於重譯，衣冠蹈舞于千班。
伏願駿烈覃敷，鴻恩遐曁。乃文乃武，用對帝臣之心；作福作威，式敷皇極之訓。右《騶虞》《貍首》，瑤圖鞏周道於緜延；朝荆楚，享氐羌，
translation_en:
…at the jade steps of the throne, displaying a grand strategy unmatched in an age. All this arose from Your Majesty’s sole decision: your brilliant might flashed like lightning throughout the realm, bringing commanders and officers into accord and causing orders to spread like the wind beyond the military headquarters. The purpose was assuredly to eliminate the wicked and cut down rebels, certainly not to indulge in warfare and exhaust military strength. South of Yong, a mound of enemy corpses was raised, firmly establishing the boundary between the Chinese and the foreign peoples; in Ouluo, the beacon smoke of war was extinguished, splendidly strengthening a land whose natural defenses enable two to withstand a hundred.
We, your servants, cherish the resolve to oppose your enemies and share concern for the times. We have yet to render service amid the sweat of warhorses, and, examining ourselves, feel shame. Our hearts have long yearned to mount the saddle; hearing the news, we long to exert ourselves. Looking reverently upon your victorious calculations, we recognize with admiration that you are a true emperor. Fortunate to witness the triumphant return, we know that the benevolent ruler has no rival. Charioteers and cavalry cheer in lands reached through successive interpreters; officials in ceremonial dress dance for joy in their thousand ranks.
We humbly wish that your great achievements may spread everywhere and your abundant grace reach afar. Through both civil and military accomplishments, may you answer the hearts of your imperial servants; in bestowing blessings and wielding authority, may you disseminate the teaching of the August Mean. May you honor the songs Zouyu and Lishou, and may your glorious imperial design perpetuate the Way of Zhou. May you receive the court homage of Jing and Chu and the offerings of the Di and Qiang…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
寶籙寧湯孫於萬年臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖抃躍屛營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
===
史著勳
同考試官教諭宋批我
皇上文武之道匹休
二祖
先皇此策揄揚殆盡而復以
天道望我
皇上一其心以培元氣振神氣其素抱忠愛之誠者歟薦先多士
宜也
考試官教諭陳批我
punctuated:
寶籙寧湯孫於萬年。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、抃躍屛營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叁場，策五道。第一問。
史著勳。
同考試官教諭宋批：我皇上文武之道，匹休二祖、先皇。此策揄揚殆盡，而復以天道望我皇上，一其心以培元氣、振神氣，其素抱忠愛之誠者歟？薦先多士，宜也。
考試官教諭陳批：我
translation_en:
…May the precious register of imperial destiny secure the descendants of Tang for ten thousand years. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Majesty, overcome with joyful excitement and reverent awe. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session: Five Policy Questions. First Question.
Shi Zhuxun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “Our emperor’s civil and military governance equals in glory that of the two founding emperors and the late emperor. This policy essay praises it almost exhaustively, and further invokes the Way of Heaven as the standard to which it hopes our emperor will aspire: to unify his mind, thereby nourishing the primal vital force and invigorating his spiritual energies. Is its author not one who has long cherished sincere loyalty and devotion? It is fitting that he be recommended ahead of the other candidates.”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國家文武一道威德兼隆信足以軼唐虞而媲成周者子能鋪
張惕厲以鳴其盛而純一不息之論更見臣子忠
愛無已之情宜錄以式
考試官教授王批我
皇上嗣統覲揚光烈子能備極榆揚末復進一心之論尤見忠悃
帝王所以敷鬯聲教恢擴弘猷躋熈皞之
休揚乂安之烈者非徒著飾夫文具而取
辦于武功已也要必有至聖之德篤于淵
微至神之幾妙於獨運故其存之也玄遠
===
而不可測其發之也時出而不可窺以化
成天下也而聲教曁于四方以肅將天威
也而弘猷奠於萬世夫是以綏懷戢寧遠
至邇安而帝業以成治道無壅也於戲此
天道也天之道於穆不已者也化工默運
而溫冽之氣通復之序萬物生且成乎其
間矣帝王之道則天者也至德無爲而仁
義之用恩威之布天下和且平於其間矣
是故帝王之文非以致飾於天下也治定
punctuated:
國家文武一道，威德兼隆，信足以軼唐虞而媲成周者。子能鋪張惕厲，以鳴其盛，而純一不息之論，更見臣子忠愛無已之情，宜錄以式。
考試官教授王批：我皇上嗣統，覲揚光烈，子能備極榆揚，末復進一心之論，尤見忠悃。
帝王所以敷鬯聲教、恢擴弘猷、躋熈皞之休、揚乂安之烈者，非徒著飾夫文具而取辦于武功已也。要必有至聖之德篤于淵微，至神之幾妙於獨運。故其存之也，玄遠而不可測；其發之也，時出而不可窺。以化成天下也，而聲教曁于四方；以肅將天威也，而弘猷奠於萬世。夫是以綏懷戢寧，遠至邇安，而帝業以成，治道無壅也。於戲！此天道也。天之道，於穆不已者也。化工默運，而溫冽之氣、通復之序，萬物生且成乎其間矣。帝王之道，則天者也。至德無爲，而仁義之用、恩威之布，天下和且平於其間矣。是故帝王之文，非以致飾於天下也。治定
translation_en:
…Our dynasty unites civil and martial governance in a single Way, with majesty and virtue flourishing together. It is indeed sufficient to surpass Tang Yao and Yu Shun and rival the perfected Zhou. You have elaborated upon its vigilance and diligence to proclaim its grandeur; your discussion of undivided and unceasing dedication further reveals a subject’s inexhaustible loyalty and love. This merits inclusion as a model.
Examiner Wang, an instructor, comments: Our emperor has succeeded to the throne and gloriously carried forward the illustrious achievements of his predecessors [?]. You have praised these to the fullest [?], and at the end further advanced an argument for singleness of mind, especially revealing your heartfelt loyalty.
The means by which emperors and kings spread their civilizing influence and instruction, enlarge their grand designs, attain the blessings of radiant harmony, and magnify the achievements of peaceful rule consist in more than embellishing mere formalities and relying on military accomplishments. They must possess supremely sagely virtue firmly rooted in profound subtlety, and supremely numinous discernment whose workings are wondrously their own. Thus, when held within, it is mysterious, remote, and unfathomable; when expressed, it emerges as circumstances require, and its workings cannot be discerned. Through transforming and perfecting all under Heaven, their civilizing influence and instruction reach the four quarters; through reverently exercising Heaven’s majesty, their grand designs are established for ten thousand generations. In this way they soothe and win allegiance, restrain and pacify: those far away come to them, those nearby dwell securely, imperial achievement is accomplished, and the Way of governance meets no obstruction. Ah! This is the Way of Heaven. The Way of Heaven is profound and unceasing. The work of transformation proceeds silently; amid the forces of warmth and cold and the succession of circulation and return, the myriad things are born and brought to maturity. The Way of emperors and kings takes Heaven as its model. Supreme virtue acts without contrivance; amid the practice of benevolence and righteousness and the dispensing of favor and majesty, all under Heaven becomes harmonious and peaceful. Thus, the civil accomplishments of emperors and kings are not intended merely to ornament the world. When orderly rule is established…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而文斯顯則天下以文贊之其諸天道陽
舒之運而能培國家元氣之長者乎帝王
之武非以立威於天下也亂輯而武斯顯
則天下以武贊之其諸天道陰肅之運而
能揚國家神氣之精者乎故唐堯之大也
書稱之則曰乃武乃文夫堯起諸侯而爲
天子光天下是文武之放勳也然惟帝德
廣運爾堯不自知也周文之盛也詩稱之
則曰文武維后夫文王起岐周而爲西伯
===
顯西土是文武之顯謨也然惟厥德不回
爾文亦不自知也武王之順天應人燮伐
大商武功成焉遂訪箕子叙九疇皇極敷
言之訓而至文于是乎闡矣周公之繼武
相成卜建東都武功寓焉乃作洛誥訓殷
頑畢公保釐之命而文教于是乎著矣至
于宣王紹文武之績成安攘之勳會諸侯
于東都復有周之境土詩人於車攻美其
簡閲焉於吉日美其蒐獮焉蓋兵戢而時
punctuated: 而文斯顯，則天下以文贊之，其諸天道陽舒之運，而能培國家元氣之長者乎？帝王之武，非以立威於天下也。亂輯而武斯顯，則天下以武贊之，其諸天道陰肅之運，而能揚國家神氣之精者乎？故唐堯之大也，書稱之則曰：「乃武乃文。」夫堯起諸侯而爲天子，光天下，是文武之放勳也。然惟帝德廣運爾，堯不自知也。周文之盛也，詩稱之則曰：「文武維后。」夫文王起岐周而爲西伯，顯西土，是文武之顯謨也。然惟厥德不回爾，文亦不自知也。武王之順天應人，燮伐大商，武功成焉，遂訪箕子，叙九疇、皇極敷言之訓，而至文于是乎闡矣。周公之繼武相成，卜建東都，武功寓焉，乃作《洛誥》訓殷頑、畢公保釐之命，而文教于是乎著矣。至于宣王紹文武之績，成安攘之勳，會諸侯于東都，復有周之境土，詩人於《車攻》美其簡閲焉，於《吉日》美其蒐獮焉。蓋兵戢而時
translation_en:
…and civil accomplishment thereby becomes manifest, then all under Heaven praise him for it. Is this not like the expansive movement of Heaven’s yang, capable of nurturing the growth of the state’s vital energy? The martial achievement of emperors and kings is not intended to impose their might upon the world. When disorder has been quelled and martial achievement thereby becomes manifest, all under Heaven praise them for it. Is this not like the stern movement of Heaven’s yin, capable of bringing forth the concentrated spiritual vigor of the state?

Thus, of the greatness of Tang Yao, the Book of Documents says: “Both martial and civil.” Yao rose from among the feudal lords to become Son of Heaven and illuminate the world: this was his far-reaching achievement in both civil and martial affairs. Yet it was simply that his imperial virtue was vast and all-pervading; Yao himself was unaware of it. Of the flourishing virtue of King Wen of Zhou, the Book of Odes says: “Civil and martial was the sovereign.” King Wen rose from Qizhou to become the Earl of the West and bring glory to the western lands: this was his illustrious design in both civil and martial affairs. Yet it was simply that his virtue did not deviate; Wen likewise was unaware of it.

King Wu complied with Heaven and responded to the people, joining forces in an attack on the great Shang, and his martial achievement was accomplished. He then consulted Jizi, who set forth the Nine Categories and the teaching concerning the August Ultimate and its promulgated pronouncements; thus the highest civil accomplishment was made manifest. The Duke of Zhou continued King Wu’s work and assisted King Cheng, choosing by divination the site for the eastern capital and establishing it; martial achievement was embodied therein. He then composed the Announcement concerning Luo to instruct the recalcitrant people of Yin, and the charge to the Duke of Bi to preserve order and govern [?]; thus civil instruction became evident.

King Xuan continued the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu and accomplished the work of securing peace within and repelling enemies without. He assembled the feudal lords at the eastern capital and recovered Zhou’s territory. In Our Chariots Were Well Prepared (Che gong), the poet praised his inspection of the troops; in Auspicious Day (Ji ri), the poet praised his seasonal hunts. For arms are laid aside, yet at appropriate times …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
動動則威備弛則玩玩則無振此宣王之
用文事而飭武功所以爲內順治而外威
嚴也夫文武之用與變推移而張弛之機
隨時以著周之盛王所以爲聖而至今傳
頌之不衰者也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝之開天也混一區宇汎掃腥羶武
功亢矣是故其平江漢也翦吳會也討蜀
越也戡荆湖也以及于元都廓清西南底
定開闢之極功也夷考其渡江
===
登極之詔所謂克當天心受天明命者與然而
簡命儒臣集禮典樂釐正
郊祀升中因吉立臥碑於黌宮也頒
大誥於中外也蓋六合嚮德而遠邇同文矣方
天心厭亂神異潜孚若有以默發
聖心焉一仗劒而羣雄懾服九有頌聲是啟億
萬載之耿光者與帝堯同運非富天下者
也
成祖文皇帝之繼天也起自北平嗣大
punctuated:
動，動則威備；弛則玩，玩則無振。此宣王之用文事而飭武功，所以爲內順治而外威嚴也。夫文武之用，與變推移，而張弛之機，隨時以著，周之盛王所以爲聖，而至今傳頌之不衰者也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝之開天也，混一區宇，汎掃腥羶，武功亢矣。是故其平江漢也，翦吳會也，討蜀越也，戡荆湖也，以及于元都廓清，西南底定，開闢之極功也。夷考其渡江、登極之詔，所謂克當天心、受天明命者與？然而簡命儒臣，集禮典樂，釐正郊祀，升中因吉，立臥碑於黌宮也，頒大誥於中外也，蓋六合嚮德而遠邇同文矣。方天心厭亂，神異潜孚，若有以默發聖心焉。一仗劒而羣雄懾服，九有頌聲，是啟億萬載之耿光者與？帝堯同運，非富天下者也。
成祖文皇帝之繼天也，起自北平，嗣大
translation_en:
…mobilized at the proper time. When mobilized, their might is held in readiness; when discipline slackens, neglect follows, and neglect leaves them unable to rouse themselves. This was how King Xuan employed civil affairs to put military achievements in order, securing orderly government within and imposing majesty abroad. The employment of civil and military measures shifts with changing circumstances, while occasions for tightening and relaxing become apparent as the times require. This is why the flourishing kings of Zhou were sages, and why praise of them has continued undiminished to this day.
We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao inaugurated a new order: he united the realm and swept away the rank and fetid presence of alien rule; his military achievements were supreme. Thus he pacified Jianghan, cut down Wu and Kuaiji, campaigned against Shu and Yue, and subdued Jing and Hu, proceeding to clear the Yuan capital and settle the southwest. These were the consummate achievements of founding a new order. Examining his proclamations on crossing the Yangzi and ascending the throne, do we not find what is meant by fulfilling Heaven’s will and receiving Heaven’s luminous mandate? Yet he also selected and commissioned Confucian ministers, compiled rites and regulated music, rectified the suburban sacrifices, and reported his accomplishments to Heaven, ‘following the auspicious’ [?]. He erected recumbent stelae in the schools and promulgated the Grand Pronouncements throughout the court and the provinces. Thus all within the six directions turned toward his virtue, and near and far shared a common culture. At that time, Heaven’s heart had grown weary of disorder, and supernatural portents secretly corresponded with it, as though silently stirring his sagely heart. Once he took up the sword, the contending heroes submitted in awe, and songs of praise resounded throughout the nine regions. Was this not the inauguration of a radiant glory lasting countless ages? He shared the destiny of Emperor Yao; he was not one who sought to possess the wealth of All under Heaven.
When Emperor Chengzu Wen carried forward Heaven’s work, he arose from Beiping and succeeded to the great…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歷服武烈彰矣是故其戡寧夏也降西戎也
掃幕北也克南交也以至于島夷歸命漲
海靜波皆丕承之偉績也夷考其定鼎金
陵之
詔所謂克相上帝寵綏四方者與然而肇創內
閣崇重儒臣日
御經筵不廢寒暑廣脩纂以訂書籍也
頒大全以訓諸士也蓋臣民仰德而治教休
明矣方
===
天命有在祥異荐徵若有默定大數焉一揮戈
而內難悉平四方頌德是弘億萬載之大
烈者與文武同道不失天下之顯名者也
迨我
世宗肅皇帝之入承
大統也則發明正學而
敬一著箴也闡揚儒術而
五箴釋註也
重幸胄監而
punctuated:
歷服，武烈彰矣。是故其戡寧夏也，降西戎也，掃幕北也，克南交也，以至于島夷歸命，漲海靜波，皆丕承之偉績也。夷考其定鼎金陵之詔，所謂克相上帝、寵綏四方者與？然而肇創內閣，崇重儒臣，日御經筵，不廢寒暑；廣脩纂以訂書籍也，頒《大全》以訓諸士也。蓋臣民仰德，而治教休明矣。方天命有在，祥異荐徵，若有默定大數焉。一揮戈而內難悉平，四方頌德，是弘億萬載之大烈者，與文武同道，不失天下之顯名者也。
迨我世宗肅皇帝之入承大統也，則發明正學而《敬一》著箴也，闡揚儒術而《五箴》釋註也，重幸胄監而
translation_en:
…the imperial mandate, his martial achievements shone forth. Thus his pacification of Ningxia, his subjugation of the western Rong, his sweeping campaigns north of the desert, and his conquest of southern Jiaozhi, extending even to the submission of the island peoples and the stilling of the waves of the distant seas—all were great achievements in carrying forward his inheritance. Upon examining his edict establishing the capital at Jinling, was this not what was meant by “ably assisting the Lord on High and graciously bringing peace to the four quarters”? Moreover, he established the Grand Secretariat and accorded high honor to Confucian officials. He attended the Classics Colloquium daily, suspending it neither in cold nor in heat. He undertook extensive compilation projects to revise books and issued the Great Compendia to instruct scholars. Officials and commoners alike looked up to his virtue, and governance and education flourished in splendor. At that time, Heaven’s mandate had its recipient, and auspicious marvels repeatedly supplied confirmation, as though the great course of destiny had been silently determined. With one brandishing of his spear, all internal troubles were quelled, and the four quarters praised his virtue. Thus he magnified great achievements that would endure for countless ages. He followed the same Way as Kings Wen and Wu and retained his illustrious name throughout the realm.
When our Emperor Shizong, posthumously honored as Su, came to inherit the imperial succession, he elucidated orthodox learning by composing the Admonition on Reverent Unity, and expounded Confucian teachings by providing explanatory annotations to the Five Admonitions. He again visited the Directorate of Education, and…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖諭有紀也克謹禋祀而
欽天有記也皆炳蔚之文也然安南不庭則問
罪興師北虜跳梁則練兵遣將倭奴煽禍
特簡重臣以驅撻之苗夷侵叛爰分閫帥以鎮
壓之法不貸於勳舊刑不弛于僨將親閱
章疏而
離照旁通分任臣工而
乾綱總攬其撫民之仁溫乎若太和之普被
而萬物皆春也其勵精之武凜乎若雷霆
===
之震迅而奸宄讋服也所以培百年之休
運固萬世之治安者眞上與
二祖同符矣我
皇上嗣累葉之洪基紹
列聖之駿烈乾坤合德而文武兼資試即其大
者言之如建元一
詔明定保之原著紹述之美錄忠諫之節寬賦
役之征停織造之使禁珠玉之採皆以爲
民也
punctuated:
聖諭有紀也；克謹禋祀，而欽天有記也。皆炳蔚之文也。然安南不庭，則問罪興師；北虜跳梁，則練兵遣將；倭奴煽禍，特簡重臣以驅撻之；苗夷侵叛，爰分閫帥以鎮壓之。法不貸於勳舊，刑不弛于僨將。親閱章疏，而離照旁通；分任臣工，而乾綱總攬。其撫民之仁，溫乎若太和之普被，而萬物皆春也；其勵精之武，凜乎若雷霆之震迅，而奸宄讋服也。所以培百年之休運、固萬世之治安者，眞上與二祖同符矣。
我皇上嗣累葉之洪基，紹列聖之駿烈，乾坤合德而文武兼資。試即其大者言之，如建元一詔，明定保之原，著紹述之美，錄忠諫之節，寬賦役之征，停織造之使，禁珠玉之採，皆以爲民也。
translation_en:
…there is a record of his sagely instructions; he scrupulously performed the sacrifices, and there is a record of his reverence for Heaven. These are all splendid manifestations of civil accomplishment. Yet when Annan failed to acknowledge his court, he raised an army to call it to account; when the northern barbarians ran rampant, he trained troops and dispatched generals. When the Japanese marauders fomented calamity, he specially selected high ministers to drive them out and chastise them. When the Miao peoples raided and rebelled, he assigned regional commanders to suppress them. The law spared neither meritorious veterans nor longstanding servants, and punishments were not relaxed for commanders whose failures brought disaster. He personally reviewed memorials, and his illumination, like that of the sun, reached everywhere; he apportioned responsibilities among his officials while retaining overall command of sovereign authority. His benevolence in caring for the people was as warming as the universal influence of supreme harmony, bringing spring to all things. His martial vigor in applying himself to government was as awe-inspiring as the swift crash of thunder, causing evildoers to tremble and submit. In nurturing the auspicious fortunes of a century and securing peace and good order for myriad generations, he truly matched the achievements of the two ancestral founders before him.
Our present emperor has inherited the vast foundation established over successive generations and continued the magnificent achievements of the sage emperors. His virtue accords with Heaven and Earth, and he possesses both civil and martial abilities. Let us speak of the greatest instances. With the single edict inaugurating his reign, he clarified the principles of securing and preserving the realm and displayed the excellence of carrying forward his predecessors’ work. He recognized the integrity of loyal remonstrance, eased the exaction of taxes and labor service, discontinued the dispatch of commissioners for imperial textile manufacture, and prohibited the gathering of pearls and jade. All this was for the people.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
郊祀之親俯採禮官之議
幸學之典益隆重道之儀
御經筵則儒臣進講以資啓沃也重科目則表
正文體以挽淳風也皆
聖政之要務是天下之至文也如邊圉少警有
諭誡之辭儲積未充有實邊之
令以六師未振非所以重武衛也
親大閱以激勵之邊才未廣非所以重封疆
也
===
命諸司得薦揚之是詰戎訓武之規即
祖宗之遺也
聖猷神斷淵乎弘深中外諸臣欣逢快覩仰窺
我
皇上文武之德固將鬯
聲教於無外壯
皇猷於無疆者其與隆古盛王先後一道授受
一心猶天之造化生成乎萬物溫冽爲序
通復相成而不自知也草茅之所欲竊有
punctuated:
郊祀之親，俯採禮官之議；幸學之典，益隆重道之儀。御經筵，則儒臣進講以資啓沃也；重科目，則表正文體以挽淳風也。皆聖政之要務，是天下之至文也。如邊圉少警，有諭誡之辭；儲積未充，有實邊之令。以六師未振，非所以重武衛也，親大閱以激勵之；邊才未廣，非所以重封疆也，命諸司得薦揚之。是詰戎訓武之規，即祖宗之遺也。
聖猷神斷，淵乎弘深。中外諸臣欣逢快覩，仰窺我皇上文武之德，固將鬯聲教於無外，壯皇猷於無疆者。其與隆古盛王先後一道，授受一心，猶天之造化生成乎萬物，溫冽爲序，通復相成，而不自知也。草茅之所欲竊有
translation_en:
In personally conducting the suburban sacrifices, Your Majesty graciously adopted the deliberations of the ritual officials; in the ceremony of visiting the state school, you further enhanced the rites honoring the Way. When you attend the Classics Colloquium, Confucian officials deliver lectures to aid in enlightening your mind; in giving weight to the examinations, you set literary composition aright so as to restore unspoiled customs. These are all essential tasks of sagely government: they constitute the highest civil achievement in the realm. When even slight alarms arise on the frontier, you issue admonitory instructions; when reserves are insufficient, you command that the frontier be provisioned. Since the failure to invigorate the Six Armies does not accord with the importance of military protection, you personally conduct a grand review to inspire them. Since an insufficient pool of talent for frontier service does not accord with the importance of defending the borders, you authorize the various offices to recommend and promote such men. These measures for putting the forces in order and training them for war are precisely the legacy of your imperial ancestors.
Your sagely plans and inspired decisions are profound and far-reaching. Officials at court and in the provinces rejoice to encounter and behold them. Reverently contemplating Your Majesty’s civil and martial virtue, they see that you will surely spread your moral influence and instruction everywhere, leaving no place beyond their reach, and extend your imperial designs without limit. You and the illustrious kings of high antiquity follow the same Way in succession, transmitting and receiving it with one mind. This resembles Heaven’s transforming, generating, and nurturing of the myriad things: warmth and cold follow their ordered sequence, advance and return complement one another, without conscious awareness. As for what this humble man of the countryside would venture to…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
獻者無亦以
天道望我
皇上而已上天之運不息而其化有漸生物不
測者其功也而為物不二者其本也故天
道不二而
聖心惟一一則純純則無欲一則恒恒則無息
思
天之民不可下也懷保之政常先焉思
天之臣不可易也激勸之典常隆焉思
===
天之權不可褻也近習之馭常嚴焉思
天之明不可息也經筵之講常重焉順
天命者必揚違
天道者必絀所以培元氣於靈長振神氣於赫
奕者率不外此是道也即
祖宗之道而堯文武宣之所以為文武者統是
矣書曰惟天聰明惟聖時憲愚願以為吾
君告不識可以轉聞于
上否
punctuated: 獻者，無亦以天道望我皇上而已。上天之運不息，而其化有漸；生物不測者，其功也，而為物不二者，其本也。故天道不二，而聖心惟一。一則純，純則無欲；一則恒，恒則無息。思天之民不可下也，懷保之政常先焉；思天之臣不可易也，激勸之典常隆焉；思天之權不可褻也，近習之馭常嚴焉；思天之明不可息也，經筵之講常重焉。順天命者必揚，違天道者必絀。所以培元氣於靈長、振神氣於赫奕者，率不外此。是道也，即祖宗之道，而堯、文、武、宣之所以為文武者，統是矣。《書》曰：「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。」愚願以為吾君告，不識可以轉聞于上否？
translation_en:
…what I would offer is perhaps simply the hope that our Emperor will take the Way of Heaven as his standard. Heaven’s operation never ceases, yet its transforming work proceeds gradually. Bringing forth living things in unfathomable ways is its achievement; being undivided in bringing things into existence is its foundation. Thus the Way of Heaven is undivided, and the sagely mind is single. Singleness brings purity, and purity brings freedom from desire; singleness brings constancy, and constancy brings unceasing activity.

Reflect that Heaven’s people must not be treated as inferior: policies to cherish and protect them must always come first. Reflect that Heaven’s ministers must not be treated lightly: measures to inspire and encourage them must always be generously maintained. Reflect that Heaven’s authority must not be profaned: control of intimate attendants must always be strict. Reflect that Heaven’s illumination must not cease: lectures at the Classics Colloquium must always be accorded importance. Those who follow Heaven’s mandate must be advanced; those who violate Heaven’s Way must be dismissed. The means of nurturing the primal vitality so that it endures, and rousing the spiritual energies to brilliance, lie entirely within these principles. This Way is precisely the Way of the imperial ancestors. It also comprehends all that made Yao, Wen, Wu, and Xuan exemplars of civil and martial virtue.

The Book of Documents says: “Heaven alone is keen of hearing and clear of sight; the sage takes this as his model.” In my ignorance, I wish to offer this counsel to our ruler. Might it be conveyed to His Majesty?

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第二問
洪敷誥
同考試官教諭梁批聖賢道統之傳發明詳盡而
末總歸之天尤為有見乎其潛心斯道而有得者與
考試官教諭陳批知道之言出人意表
考試官教授王批諸說異同剖析獨為明盡
斯道之在天下也有相承之統君子固當
沿其源而遡其流古人之尚論也有不一
之見學者不可執其疑而失其是夫道之
===
有統也前乎千百世之上以承天道而主
斯文後乎千百世之下以繼往聖而興來
學然時有顯晦而道無存亡言有詳略而
聖無加損君子惟當觀其大旨究其意之
所存焉爾豈可據其一而疑之哉今夫道
統之說何所昉乎董子曰道之大原出于
天是天者道統之所自來也傳曰聖人者
道之管是聖人者道統之所由寄也粤自
洪荒以上記載無傳故孔子叙書斷自唐
punctuated:
第二問
洪敷誥
同考試官教諭梁批：聖賢道統之傳，發明詳盡，而末總歸之天，尤為有見。乎其潛心斯道而有得者與！
考試官教諭陳批：知道之言，出人意表。
考試官教授王批：諸說異同，剖析獨為明盡。
斯道之在天下也，有相承之統，君子固當沿其源而遡其流；古人之尚論也，有不一之見，學者不可執其疑而失其是。夫道之有統也，前乎千百世之上，以承天道而主斯文；後乎千百世之下，以繼往聖而興來學。然時有顯晦，而道無存亡；言有詳略，而聖無加損。君子惟當觀其大旨，究其意之所存焉爾，豈可據其一而疑之哉？今夫道統之說，何所昉乎？董子曰：「道之大原出于天。」是天者，道統之所自來也。傳曰：「聖人者，道之管。」是聖人者，道統之所由寄也。粤自洪荒以上，記載無傳，故孔子叙書，斷自唐
translation_en:
Second Question
Hong Fugao
Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “The transmission of the succession of the Way through the sages and worthies is elucidated thoroughly and in detail. The conclusion traces it all back to Heaven, showing particular insight. Surely he is one who has devoted himself to this Way and attained an understanding of it! [?]”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Words displaying knowledge of the Way, surpassing expectations.”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “The similarities and differences among the various explanations are analyzed with exceptional clarity and thoroughness.”
This Way, as it exists in the world, has a continuous succession. The gentleman should indeed follow its source and trace its stream back upstream. In discussing the ancients, opinions differ; students must not cling to what is doubtful and thereby lose what is correct. As for the succession of the Way, those who lived hundreds and thousands of generations earlier received the Way of Heaven and presided over this cultural tradition; those who live hundreds and thousands of generations later carry on the sages of the past and inspire students yet to come. Yet although times have their periods of illumination and obscurity, the Way neither comes into being nor perishes. Although statements may be detailed or brief, sagehood is neither augmented nor diminished. The gentleman should simply consider their general purport and investigate where their meaning lies. How could he seize upon a single point and cast doubt upon the whole?
Now, where did the account of the succession of the Way originate? Master Dong said: “The great source of the Way issues from Heaven.” Thus Heaven is the source from which the succession of the Way comes. A transmitted text says: “The sage is the conduit of the Way.” Thus the sage is the one in whom the succession of the Way is lodged. From remotest antiquity and before, no written records have been transmitted. Hence Confucius, in arranging the Book of Documents, set its beginning at Tang …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
虞者以精一之旨自堯而始也然三代以
上其統每屬之在位之人若堯舜之後有
禹湯禹湯之後有文武文武之後有周公
爲君爲相位各不同要皆達而在上其道
行行者統之所由立也三代以下其統每
屬之無位之士若孔子之後有孟軻孟軻
之後有周程朱子或師或友時各未遇要
皆窮而在下其道明明者統之所由紹也
此其大槩也試舉孟子終篇之疑韓愈原
===
===
道之論及孔門宋儒之緒而悉論之彼自
精一執中承堯之統者舜也原道謂堯以
是傳之舜矣孟子乃以堯舜至湯一舉而
竝言之何也蓋孟子謂斯道大約五百年
而一興故凡肇統于先者均啓嗣聖之緒
初無彼此也非軼舜也視韓所述何有于
軒輊乎祗台德先承舜之統者禹也原道
謂舜以是傳之禹矣孟子乃以禹皐陶爲
見知而不叙諸統何也蓋孟子惟以五百
punctuated:
虞者，以精一之旨自堯而始也。然三代以上，其統每屬之在位之人，若堯舜之後有禹湯，禹湯之後有文武，文武之後有周公。爲君爲相，位各不同，要皆達而在上，其道行，行者統之所由立也。三代以下，其統每屬之無位之士，若孔子之後有孟軻，孟軻之後有周程朱子。或師或友，時各未遇，要皆窮而在下，其道明，明者統之所由紹也。此其大槩也。試舉《孟子》終篇之疑、韓愈《原道》之論及孔門宋儒之緒而悉論之。
彼自精一執中承堯之統者，舜也。《原道》謂堯以是傳之舜矣，《孟子》乃以堯舜至湯一舉而竝言之，何也？蓋《孟子》謂斯道大約五百年而一興，故凡肇統于先者，均啓嗣聖之緒，初無彼此也，非軼舜也。視韓所述，何有于軒輊乎？祗台德先，承舜之統者，禹也。《原道》謂舜以是傳之禹矣，《孟子》乃以禹皐陶爲見知而不叙諸統，何也？蓋《孟子》惟以五百
translation_en:
…Yu, because the teaching of refinement and singleness of mind began with Yao. During the Three Dynasties and earlier, the succession to the Way generally belonged to men holding office: after Yao and Shun came Yu and Tang; after Yu and Tang came Wen and Wu; and after Wen and Wu came the Duke of Zhou. Whether rulers or chief ministers, their positions differed, but all had attained eminence and stood above others. Their Way was put into practice, and it was through this practice that the succession was established. After the Three Dynasties, the succession generally belonged to scholars without office: after Confucius came Meng Ke, and after Meng Ke came Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhu. Whether teachers or friends, none encountered a favorable time for advancement. All remained in straitened circumstances and lowly stations, yet their Way was elucidated, and through this elucidation the succession was continued. Such is the broad outline. Let us examine fully the doubts raised by the final chapter of the Mencius, Han Yu’s argument in Inquiry into the Way, and the lines of transmission among Confucius’s disciples and the Song Confucians.
It was Shun who inherited Yao’s succession through refinement and singleness of mind and by holding fast to the mean. Inquiry into the Way says that Yao transmitted this to Shun. Why, then, does the Mencius speak of Yao and Shun together in a single statement about the period from them to Tang? The Mencius holds that this Way flourishes approximately once every five hundred years. Thus, all who first established the succession equally opened the line for succeeding sages; no distinction between them was intended. Shun was not passed over. Compared with Han Yu’s account, what difference of rank is there? It was Yu who, ‘reverently taking my virtue as his guide,’ inherited Shun’s succession. Inquiry into the Way says that Shun transmitted this to Yu. Why, then, does the Mencius classify Yu and Gao Yao as those who knew the Way through seeing it, without listing them in the succession? This is because the Mencius takes five hundred…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
年為斯道一傳故凡未越百年者均屬見
知之列原無優劣也非略禹也視韓所敘
何有于低昂乎當殷士之來歸親訪洪範
之傳使斯道既蔽而復明者文之後賴有
武王也而孟氏終篇無一言及之若于武
為未與于統者然不知父子迭聖同出一
時稱人世德從其所尊茲敘文而不及武
者豈非以舉父則子可該之意歟觀其他
日敘統于文王之後復繼以不泄不忘之
===
言則可以知孟子敘武之心矣原道所謂
湯以是傳之文武者不既同耶當周命之
方新大衍禮樂之制親覿文考之懿範者
見知莫周公若也孟子乃置之不言而顧
及于宜生之儔若以周公為無得于文王
者然不知交儆以道祗在君臣信史之傳
取其協贊茲周公之不與于見知者豈非
以父子之間而略之歟觀其他日敘統于
武王之後復綴之思兼數語則可以諒孟
punctuated: 年為斯道一傳，故凡未越百年者，均屬見知之列，原無優劣也，非略禹也。視韓所敘，何有于低昂乎？當殷士之來歸，親訪洪範之傳，使斯道既蔽而復明者，文之後賴有武王也。而孟氏終篇無一言及之，若于武為未與于統者然。不知父子迭聖，同出一時，稱人世德，從其所尊。茲敘文而不及武者，豈非以舉父則子可該之意歟？觀其他日敘統于文王之後，復繼以不泄不忘之言，則可以知孟子敘武之心矣。《原道》所謂湯以是傳之文武者，不既同耶？當周命之方新，大衍禮樂之制，親覿文考之懿範者，見知莫周公若也。孟子乃置之不言，而顧及于宜生之儔，若以周公為無得于文王者然。不知交儆以道，祗在君臣；信史之傳，取其協贊。茲周公之不與于見知者，豈非以父子之間而略之歟？觀其他日敘統于武王之後，復綴之思兼數語，則可以諒孟
translation_en:
…years as the interval between transmissions of this Way. Thus all those separated by fewer than a hundred years belong alike among those who knew it through direct acquaintance. There was originally no distinction of superiority or inferiority: this was no slight to Yu. Compared with Han Yu’s account, what difference in standing is there? When the men of Yin came over in allegiance, it was King Wu, following King Wen, who personally inquired into the transmission of the Great Plan and caused this Way, once obscured, to shine again. Yet throughout his chapter Mengzi says not a word about him, as though King Wu had no share in the succession of the Way. This overlooks the fact that father and son were sages in succession, arising in the same era, and that in praising a family’s virtue across generations one follows its most honored member. Does recounting King Wen here without mentioning King Wu not mean that naming the father also includes the son? Elsewhere, when Mengzi recounts the succession after King Wen, he follows it with the words “neither neglecting nor forgetting.” From this we can discern his intention in treating King Wu. Is this not already the same as the statement in On the Origin of the Way that Tang transmitted it to Kings Wen and Wu?

When Zhou’s mandate was newly established and the institutions of ritual and music were greatly elaborated, no one equaled the Duke of Zhou in knowing through direct acquaintance, for he had personally witnessed the exemplary conduct of his illustrious father. Yet Mengzi leaves him unmentioned and instead refers to the likes of Yisheng, as though the Duke of Zhou had received nothing from King Wen. This overlooks the fact that mutual admonition through the Way pertains specifically to ruler and minister, and that trustworthy historical accounts record their cooperative assistance. Is the Duke of Zhou’s exclusion here from those who knew through direct acquaintance not because the father–son relationship allowed him to be passed over? Elsewhere, when Mengzi recounts the succession after King Wu, he appends several phrases beginning with “he thought of embracing [the achievements of the Three Kings].” From this we can understand Meng…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
子叙周公之心矣原道所謂文武以是傳
之周公者不旣合耶要之禹之去堯舜也
武周之去文王也皆在百年之內故禹為
見知非有所劣武周之不得嗣統于文王
非有所遺也由堯舜至湯也由湯至文王
也由文王至孔子也適當乎五百之期故
湯文雖非有加于禹而得以直接乎虞夏
孔子雖非賢於周公而得以直接乎文王
也昔草廬謂伏羲為上古之元堯舜其亨
===
禹湯其利文武周公其貞非有見而云然
乎愚謂道統之所由立者蓋如此自周轍
旣東大道日隱文武周公之緒幾墜于地
矣惟夫子講道于洙泗之濱而一貫之旨
為萬世傳心之脉于時及門之士蓋三千
而得其宗者獨顏氏曾氏也然後世叙統
反不及焉豈非以聖師在上門弟不得以
方其軌歟自列國爭雄權謀相煽孔門仁
義一脉幾于澌絕矣惟孟子壁立于羣雄
punctuated:
子叙周公之心矣。《原道》所謂文武以是傳之周公者，不旣合耶？要之，禹之去堯舜也，武周之去文王也，皆在百年之內。故禹為見知，非有所劣；武周之不得嗣統于文王，非有所遺也。由堯舜至湯也，由湯至文王也，由文王至孔子也，適當乎五百之期。故湯文雖非有加于禹，而得以直接乎虞夏；孔子雖非賢於周公，而得以直接乎文王也。昔草廬謂伏羲為上古之元，堯舜其亨，禹湯其利，文武周公其貞，非有見而云然乎？愚謂道統之所由立者，蓋如此。
自周轍旣東，大道日隱，文武周公之緒幾墜于地矣。惟夫子講道于洙泗之濱，而一貫之旨為萬世傳心之脉。于時及門之士蓋三千，而得其宗者獨顏氏曾氏也。然後世叙統，反不及焉，豈非以聖師在上，門弟不得以方其軌歟？自列國爭雄，權謀相煽，孔門仁義一脉幾于澌絕矣。惟孟子壁立于羣雄
translation_en:
…Mencius’s intent in his account of the Duke of Zhou. Does this not accord with the statement in On the Origin of the Way (Yuan dao) that Kings Wen and Wu transmitted this Way to the Duke of Zhou? In essence, Yu lived within a hundred years of Yao and Shun, as did King Wu and the Duke of Zhou of King Wen. Thus, Yu’s knowing the Way through seeing its exemplars does not imply any inferiority; nor does the exclusion of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou as successors to King Wen in the succession of the Way imply that they were overlooked. From Yao and Shun to Tang, from Tang to King Wen, and from King Wen to Confucius, the intervals corresponded precisely to periods of five hundred years. Thus, although Tang and King Wen did not surpass Yu, they could succeed directly to the traditions of Yu and Xia; although Confucius was not worthier than the Duke of Zhou, he could succeed directly to King Wen. Caolu once said that Fuxi represented the “origination” of high antiquity, Yao and Shun its “flourishing,” Yu and Tang its “benefit,” and Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou its “constancy.” Surely this statement rested on genuine insight? In my humble view, this is how the succession of the Way was established.
After the Zhou royal chariot tracks turned eastward, the Great Way grew more obscure by the day, and the legacy of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou nearly fell to the ground. It was the Master alone who expounded the Way on the banks of the Zhu and Si rivers, making the purport of the single thread running through his teachings the living channel for transmitting the heart-mind through all ages. At that time, some three thousand scholars entered his school, but only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen grasped its essential teaching. Yet later accounts of the succession omitted them. Was this not because, with the sage teacher above them, his disciples could not be ranked alongside him?
