Once the contending states struggled for supremacy and incited one another to schemes and stratagems, the single thread of benevolence and righteousness transmitted by the school of Confucius almost vanished entirely. Mencius alone stood firm as a sheer wall among the contending hegemons…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之中而知言養氣爲吾道赤幟之立則聞
知孔子之道而繼其統者信無踰于孟氏
也然其自敘乃以見知自命豈其志在闢
邪以任之不親則排之不力歟濂溪周子
金井玉淵光風霽月圖書之作默契邃古
不傳之秘晦庵稱其非秦漢諸儒所及當
矣然伊川乃以孟子之後一人歸之明道
非無以也蓋伊川所稱祗以明道闢邪之
功可匹孟子非謂道統之傳輕濂溪爲無
===
得也亦何妨于茂叔之統乎紫陽朱子苦
心極力繭絲牛毛著述之贍大發千聖之
奧許衡稱其集諸儒大成當矣然今爲良
知之學者若于陸氏有取非無故也蓋陸
氏之學務明心朱子之學在窮理故恒情
樂徑悟而憚積累是以厭常而喜新也亦
何損于元晦之統乎要之孔子也顏曾孟
也倡斯道于大亂之後其任之也難此堯
舜湯文之道所以至今不廢也濂溪也程
punctuated:
之中，而知言養氣，爲吾道赤幟之立，則聞知孔子之道而繼其統者，信無踰于孟氏也。然其自敘乃以見知自命，豈其志在闢邪，以任之不親則排之不力歟？濂溪周子，金井玉淵，光風霽月，圖書之作，默契邃古不傳之秘，晦庵稱其非秦漢諸儒所及，當矣。然伊川乃以孟子之後一人歸之明道，非無以也。蓋伊川所稱，祗以明道闢邪之功可匹孟子，非謂道統之傳輕濂溪爲無得也，亦何妨于茂叔之統乎？

紫陽朱子，苦心極力，繭絲牛毛，著述之贍，大發千聖之奧，許衡稱其集諸儒大成，當矣。然今爲良知之學者，若于陸氏有取，非無故也。蓋陸氏之學務明心，朱子之學在窮理，故恒情樂徑悟而憚積累，是以厭常而喜新也，亦何損于元晦之統乎？

要之，孔子也，顏曾孟也，倡斯道于大亂之後，其任之也難，此堯舜湯文之道所以至今不廢也。濂溪也，程
translation_en:
…in their midst, and through understanding words and nurturing his vital energy, raised the crimson banner of our Way. Thus, among those who knew Confucius’s Way through what they heard and continued its succession, surely none surpassed Mengzi. Yet in his own account he described himself as one who knew through direct observation. Was this because his ambition lay in refuting heterodox teachings, and he believed that unless he took this responsibility personally to heart, he could not vigorously repel them?

Master Zhou of Lianxi was like a golden well and a jade pool, a clear breeze and the moon after rain. In composing his diagram and writings, he silently accorded with the untransmitted mysteries of remote antiquity. Hui’an’s judgment that the Confucian scholars of the Qin and Han could not equal him was fitting. Yet Yichuan accorded Mingdao the distinction of being the one man since Mengzi, and this was not without reason. What Yichuan praised was simply that Mingdao’s achievement in refuting heterodox teachings equaled Mengzi’s. He did not mean to belittle Lianxi as having attained nothing in the transmission of the succession of the Way. How, then, could this impair Maoshu’s place in that succession?

Master Zhu of Ziyang devoted painstaking thought and utmost effort to his work. As fine and profuse as cocoon silk and ox hair, his abundant writings brought fully to light the profound teachings of the myriad sages. Xu Heng’s praise that he brought the learning of the various Confucian masters to its fullest synthesis was fitting. Yet those who now pursue the learning of innate moral knowledge seem to find something valuable in Master Lu, and this is not without reason. Master Lu’s learning concentrates on illuminating the mind, while Master Zhu’s learning lies in investigating principle. Ordinary people therefore delight in direct enlightenment and shrink from cumulative effort; thus they tire of the familiar and welcome the new. But how could this diminish Yuanhui’s place in the succession?

In sum, Confucius, Yan Hui, Zengzi, and Mengzi championed this Way after times of great disorder. Difficult indeed was the responsibility they bore. This is why the Way of Yao, Shun, Tang, and King Wen has not fallen into disuse even today. Lianxi and Cheng…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
朱也振絕學于寥廓之餘其見之也卓此
堯舜湯文之道所以千載一日也昔勉齋
謂由孔子而後曾子子思繼其微至孟子
而始著由孟子而後周程張子繼其微至
朱子而始著豈無見而妄言乎愚謂道統
之所由紹者蓋如此竊嘗論之道之傳與
不傳由于人之遇與不遇然有天焉非人
之所能與也不係于見聞之間吾嘗怪夫
孔門諸子若子貢者其悟非不敏其問非
===
不切也然終日侍于夫子之側乃謂性與
天道不可得而聞於戲文章之外豈復有
性與天道哉若回之愚參之魯則無不聞
矣何也蓋天之所與者在顏曾不在賜而
道之所傳者以遇不以見也故自古聖賢
以道相授受者其聞雖在于五百年之後
而其知則在于五百年之先由堯舜以下
逮于程朱皆遇也皆天也不然雖日侍其
側不可謂有所見雖日誦其書不可謂有
punctuated:
朱也，振絕學于寥廓之餘，其見之也卓，此堯舜湯文之道所以千載一日也。昔勉齋謂：「由孔子而後，曾子、子思繼其微，至孟子而始著；由孟子而後，周、程、張子繼其微，至朱子而始著。」豈無見而妄言乎？愚謂道統之所由紹者，蓋如此。
竊嘗論之：道之傳與不傳，由于人之遇與不遇，然有天焉，非人之所能與也，不係于見聞之間。吾嘗怪夫孔門諸子，若子貢者，其悟非不敏，其問非不切也，然終日侍于夫子之側，乃謂性與天道不可得而聞。於戲！文章之外，豈復有性與天道哉？若回之愚、參之魯，則無不聞矣。何也？蓋天之所與者在顏、曾，不在賜，而道之所傳者以遇，不以見也。故自古聖賢以道相授受者，其聞雖在于五百年之後，而其知則在于五百年之先。由堯舜以下，逮于程朱，皆遇也，皆天也。不然，雖日侍其側，不可謂有所見；雖日誦其書，不可謂有
translation_en:
…and Zhu Xi revived a learning whose transmission had been broken, after a long interval of desolation. Their insight was outstanding: this is why the Way of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wen remains the same across a thousand years as in a single day. Mianzhai once said: “After Kongzi, Zengzi and Zisi carried on its tenuous transmission, and only with Mengzi did it become manifest. After Mengzi, Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, and Master Zhang carried on its tenuous transmission, and only with Master Zhu did it become manifest.” Could these have been rash words spoken without insight? In my humble view, such is how the succession of the Way has been continued.
I have ventured to consider this: whether the Way is transmitted depends upon whether people encounter the right circumstances. Yet Heaven is at work here; this is not something human effort can determine, nor does it depend upon what one sees and hears. Among Kongzi’s disciples, I have often wondered about Zigong. His understanding was certainly quick, and his questions certainly searching. Yet, though he attended upon the Master throughout the day, he said that the Master’s teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be heard. Ah! Can there be a human nature and a Way of Heaven apart from the Master’s cultural teachings? Yet Hui, for all his apparent foolishness, and Shen, for all his apparent dullness, heard everything. Why was this? Heaven’s favor rested upon Yan Hui and Zeng Shen, not upon Ci—that is, Zigong—and the transmission of the Way depended upon a providential encounter, not upon seeing someone in person. Thus, among the sages and worthies who have handed down and received the Way since antiquity, although their hearing of it came five hundred years afterward, their understanding reached back five hundred years before. From Yao and Shun down to the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, all depended upon such encounters; all depended upon Heaven. Otherwise, even if one attended upon a sage every day, one could not be said to have seen anything; even if one recited his writings every day, one could not be said to have…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所聞而此心相遇之眞知實有超于耳目
之所不及者矣嗟夫觀道統之絕續一係
于天是又世道升降之一大機也敢以質
于明問
第三問
秦延緒
同考試官敎諭林批以經學守約爲言而考究
詳明議論精確子其博而能約者
考試官敎諭陳批博雅之學精切之論錄之
===
考試官敎授王批宏博淹貫之學於此作見之
文所以載道者也必持精約之論而後可
垂於無窮學所以明道者也必敦反約之
功而後有裨於實用何也道原於天管於
心匪文弗載匪學弗明也工著述者繁文
侈說而不求諸至當則其論畸焉而弗精
是裂乎道者也而奚以垂無窮心訓乎稽
往牒者遠綜博覽而不要其指歸則其功
泛焉而靡約是晦乎道者也而奚以裨身
punctuated:
所聞，而此心相遇之眞知，實有超于耳目之所不及者矣。嗟夫！觀道統之絕續，一係于天，是又世道升降之一大機也。敢以質于明問。

第三問
秦延緒

同考試官敎諭林批：以經學守約爲言，而考究詳明，議論精確，子其博而能約者。
考試官敎諭陳批：博雅之學，精切之論，錄之。
考試官敎授王批：宏博淹貫之學，於此作見之。

文所以載道者也，必持精約之論，而後可垂於無窮；學所以明道者也，必敦反約之功，而後有裨於實用。何也？道原於天，管於心，匪文弗載，匪學弗明也。工著述者，繁文侈說，而不求諸至當，則其論畸焉而弗精，是裂乎道者也，而奚以垂無窮心訓乎？稽往牒者，遠綜博覽，而不要其指歸，則其功泛焉而靡約，是晦乎道者也，而奚以裨身
translation_en:
…anything heard. Yet the true understanding attained when these minds encounter one another indeed transcends what eyes and ears can reach. Alas! Whether the transmission of the Way is broken or continued depends entirely upon Heaven. This, too, is a great turning point in the rise and decline of the world’s moral order. I venture to submit these thoughts in response to your discerning question.

Third Question
Qin Yanxu

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “He speaks of holding to essentials in the study of the Classics, yet his investigations are thorough and clear, and his arguments precise. You are surely one whose breadth of learning enables him to grasp the essentials.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Broad and refined learning; incisive and pertinent argument. Accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Learning of great breadth and comprehensive mastery is evident in this composition.”

Writing is the means of conveying the Way. Only when its arguments are precise and concise can it be handed down for all time. Learning is the means of illuminating the Way. Only through diligent effort to return to the essentials can it contribute to practical use. Why is this? The Way originates in Heaven and is governed within the mind [?]; without writing it cannot be conveyed, and without learning it cannot be illuminated. If those skilled in composition multiply ornate phrases and extravagant explanations without seeking what is entirely fitting, their arguments become distorted and lack precision. This fragments the Way: how could it transmit instruction for the mind for all time [?]? If those who examine records of the past range far in their investigations and read widely without grasping their central purport, their efforts become diffuse and fail to reach the essentials. This obscures the Way: how could it benefit the person …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
心之實乎故善作者會其精而脩文則道
載於文而傳之也遠稽古者反其約以為
學則道明於學而積之也深究其歸則一
心盡之矣心存則道得文為至文學為實
學茲固多識者之要軌而儒生之所當亟
亟以講求者也今夫典籍何昉乎太古之
世其民醇醇其政悶悶上無誥戒之施下
安忘言之化時則人文未闡也粵自篆籀
形製載籍所以蔚興簡竹汗青文墨由是
===
駸發庖羲氏於是造書契以代結繩之政
焉羲黃以降洪荒載闢束帙漸備三皇有
三墳以述大道之要五帝有五典以紀常
道之經是皆先天開人遐哉邈乎弗可尚
也已夏商以來風氣聿開制作迺作述八
索則八卦之奧義悉陳著九丘則九州之
風土具載是皆隨事立教因時有作殆弗
可加也已周人監于夏商方策大備外史
掌三皇五帝之書則國家之所職掌者此
punctuated:
心之實乎？故善作者會其精而脩文，則道載於文而傳之也遠；稽古者反其約以為學，則道明於學而積之也深。究其歸，則一心盡之矣。心存則道得，文為至文，學為實學。茲固多識者之要軌，而儒生之所當亟亟以講求者也。
今夫典籍何昉乎？太古之世，其民醇醇，其政悶悶，上無誥戒之施，下安忘言之化，時則人文未闡也。粵自篆籀形製，載籍所以蔚興；簡竹汗青，文墨由是駸發。庖羲氏於是造書契，以代結繩之政焉。羲黃以降，洪荒載闢，束帙漸備。三皇有《三墳》，以述大道之要；五帝有《五典》，以紀常道之經。是皆先天開人，遐哉邈乎，弗可尚也已！夏商以來，風氣聿開，制作迺作。述《八索》，則八卦之奧義悉陳；著《九丘》，則九州之風土具載。是皆隨事立教，因時有作，殆弗可加也已！周人監于夏商，方策大備。外史掌三皇五帝之書，則國家之所職掌者此
translation_en:
…of practical benefit to one's mind? Thus, those skilled in composition gather together the essentials and refine their writing: the Way is then borne by their writings and transmitted far into the future. Those who investigate antiquity return to its essentials in pursuing learning: the Way is then illuminated through learning and accumulated in depth. Examining their ultimate destination, we find that the mind alone encompasses it all. When the mind is preserved, the Way is attained; writing becomes consummate writing, and learning becomes substantive learning. This is indeed the essential path for those of wide knowledge, and what Confucian scholars should urgently investigate.
Now, where did the canonical writings originate? In highest antiquity, the people were simple and sincere, and government was unobtrusive. Those above issued no admonitions or injunctions; those below rested content in a transforming influence that dispensed with words. At that time, human culture had not yet unfolded. Once seal-script forms were fashioned, written records flourished; with bamboo fashioned into slips and cured by heat, writing rapidly developed. Paoxi thereupon created writing to replace government by knotted cords. From the time of Fuxi and Huangdi onward, the primordial wilderness was opened up, and bound collections of writings gradually became complete. The Three August Ones had the Three Tumuli (Sanfen), which expounded the essentials of the Great Way; the Five Emperors had the Five Canons (Wudian), which recorded the enduring principles of the constant Way. All these anticipated Heaven and enlightened humanity. How remote and distant they were—beyond all surpassing!
From the Xia and Shang onward, the temper of the age opened up, and institutions and compositions arose. The composition of the Eight Cords (Basuo) fully set forth the profound meanings of the Eight Trigrams; the writing of the Nine Mounds (Jiuqiu) comprehensively recorded the local customs and geography of the Nine Provinces. All these established teachings in response to circumstances and produced works suited to their times; scarcely anything could have been added to them! The people of Zhou took Xia and Shang as their models, and their written records became fully comprehensive. The Outer Scribe had charge of the writings of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors: these, then, were what the state held in its official custody…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也楚左史倚相能讀三墳五典八索九丘
則學士大夫之所誦習者此也郁郁之文
六合同風九有共貫後有作者弗可及矣
逮乎叔季縟文勝而實德衰史籍繁而異
說熾仲尼懼覽者之不一也迺明舊章定
禮樂刪詩篇而為三百因魯史而脩春秋
讀易道以黜八索述職方以除九丘討論
墳典斷自唐虞皇姒以來之所著述多刪
而弗錄者豈其書盡無足采哉蓋世遠風
===
遐遺軌失據殘編斷簡贗說亂真故倡竝
耕而治者藉說於神農述陰陽醫方者竊
談乎黃帝他如太素太初之論多涉謬悠
三皇十紀之書咸屬迂誕夫事無徵則聞
者創駭言有證則習者心融此仲尼所以
不能無所折衷也仲尼既歿聖學榛蕪戰
國從衡眾說蠭起挾藝者吐舌而爭談窮
經者分門而肄辯真偽溷淆莫可究詰於
是秦人乘之而坑焚之禍起矣斯豈可獨
punctuated: 也。楚左史倚相能讀《三墳》《五典》《八索》《九丘》，則學士大夫之所誦習者此也。郁郁之文，六合同風，九有共貫，後有作者弗可及矣。逮乎叔季，縟文勝而實德衰，史籍繁而異說熾。仲尼懼覽者之不一也，迺明舊章，定禮樂，刪詩篇而為三百，因魯史而脩《春秋》，讀易道以黜《八索》，述職方以除《九丘》，討論《墳》《典》，斷自唐虞。皇姒以來之所著述，多刪而弗錄者，豈其書盡無足采哉？蓋世遠風遐，遺軌失據，殘編斷簡，贗說亂真。故倡竝耕而治者，藉說於神農；述陰陽醫方者，竊談乎黃帝。他如太素太初之論，多涉謬悠；三皇十紀之書，咸屬迂誕。夫事無徵則聞者創駭，言有證則習者心融，此仲尼所以不能無所折衷也。仲尼既歿，聖學榛蕪，戰國從衡，眾說蠭起。挾藝者吐舌而爭談，窮經者分門而肄辯，真偽溷淆，莫可究詰。於是秦人乘之，而坑焚之禍起矣。斯豈可獨
translation_en:
…such were the works in its charge. Yixiang, the Scribe of the Left in Chu, could read the Three Tombs (San Fen), Five Canons (Wu Dian), Eight Cords (Ba Suo), and Nine Mounds (Jiu Qiu): these, then, were the works that scholars and officials recited and studied. So richly flourishing was this culture that the same customs prevailed throughout the universe, and a common thread united the nine regions. No later author could equal it.

By the age of decline, elaborate literary ornament prevailed while genuine virtue waned; historical writings proliferated while heterodox doctrines flourished. Zhongni (Confucius), fearing that readers would lack a common understanding, clarified the old institutions and established rites and music. He pruned the poems to three hundred and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals from the records of Lu. He read the Way of the Changes to displace the Eight Cords, expounded the Offices of the Regions (Zhi Fang) to supersede the Nine Mounds, and examined the Tombs and Canons, taking the eras of Tang and Yu as his starting point. Of the writings produced since the sovereigns of the Si lineage [?], many were cut and left unrecorded. Was this because those books contained nothing worth selecting? Rather, their age was remote and their customs distant; surviving precedents lacked reliable support, texts remained only in fragments, and spurious accounts were confused with the genuine.

Thus those who advocated governing while tilling alongside the people borrowed authority for their doctrines from Shennong; those who expounded yin and yang and medical prescriptions appropriated the name of Huangdi for their discourse. Other discussions, such as those of the Primal Simplicity and the Primal Beginning, were largely fanciful and erroneous; writings on the Three Sovereigns and the Ten Eras were all far-fetched and extravagant. When events lack corroboration, those who hear of them are startled; when statements have supporting evidence, those who study them find their minds enlightened. This is why Zhongni could not dispense with critical judgment.

After Zhongni died, the learning of the sages became overgrown with weeds. Amid the competing vertical and horizontal alliances of the Warring States, doctrines swarmed forth. Those possessing specialized learning wagged their tongues in contentious discourse; those who explored the classics divided into schools and practiced disputation. Truth and falsehood became so intermingled that no one could fully disentangle them. The men of Qin then took advantage of this, and the calamity of burying scholars and burning books arose. Could this be solely …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
咎乎秦皇哉則諸儒恣辯博而忘反約之
過也漢興懲亡秦之敝除挾書之律然干
戈甫釋表章未遑迄乎孝武廣求異書而
嗣世相承崇重經籍於是劉歆總羣書而
奏七略曰輯略曰六藝略曰諸子略曰詩
賦略曰兵書略曰術數略曰方技略條貫
粲然固西京之選也而猶有遺議者以六
經聖人之至教而歆迺次之於輯略則非
矣光武中興篤好文雅而明章繼軌敦尚
===
儒術於是班固傅毅等依七略而為書部
自輯略而六藝略以至方技略舊貫昭然
亦東京之盛也而猶有遺憾者以間有七
略之所無而班氏迺益之以已見則躓矣
降自晉魏隋陳之間雖時代更異趣舍不
倫而好事之君慕古之士亦未嘗不以撰
述為意故緗囊緗帙采遺亡於秘書寶軸
錦標匵圖籍於別殿誠更僕未易數也以
宋梁言之王儉撰七志於武帝之世如曰
punctuated: 咎乎秦皇哉？則諸儒恣辯博而忘反約之過也。漢興，懲亡秦之敝，除挾書之律。然干戈甫釋，表章未遑。迄乎孝武，廣求異書，而嗣世相承，崇重經籍。於是劉歆總羣書而奏《七略》，曰輯略，曰六藝略，曰諸子略，曰詩賦略，曰兵書略，曰術數略，曰方技略。條貫粲然，固西京之選也。而猶有遺議者，以六經，聖人之至教，而歆迺次之於輯略，則非矣。光武中興，篤好文雅，而明、章繼軌，敦尚儒術。於是班固、傅毅等依《七略》而為書部，自輯略而六藝略，以至方技略，舊貫昭然，亦東京之盛也。而猶有遺憾者，以間有《七略》之所無，而班氏迺益之以已見，則躓矣。降自晉魏隋陳之間，雖時代更異，趣舍不倫，而好事之君、慕古之士，亦未嘗不以撰述為意。故緗囊緗帙，采遺亡於秘書；寶軸錦標，匵圖籍於別殿。誠更僕未易數也。以宋梁言之，王儉撰《七志》於武帝之世，如曰
translation_en:
…blame the Qin emperor alone? Rather, the fault lay with the scholars, who indulged in wide-ranging disputation and forgot to return to essentials. When the Han arose, it took warning from the failings of the fallen Qin and repealed the law against possessing books. Yet warfare had only just ceased, and there had been no leisure to promote learning. By the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, unusual books were sought far and wide, and succeeding generations continued to honor the classics and other writings. Thus Liu Xin surveyed the collected books and submitted his Seven Summaries (Qi lüe): the General Summary, the Summary of the Six Arts, the Summary of the Masters, the Summary of Poetry and Rhapsodies, the Summary of Military Writings, the Summary of Computational and Divinatory Arts, and the Summary of Medical and Other Techniques. Its organization was lucid: it was certainly an outstanding achievement of the Western Han. Yet grounds for criticism remained. The Six Classics contain the sages’ supreme teachings, but Xin placed them after the General Summary: this was wrong.

Emperor Guangwu restored the Han and deeply cherished literary culture. Emperors Ming and Zhang followed his example and earnestly esteemed Confucian learning. Accordingly, Ban Gu, Fu Yi, and others arranged books into divisions following the Seven Summaries. From the General Summary through the Summary of the Six Arts down to the Summary of Medical and Other Techniques, the former organization remained clearly apparent. This, too, was a splendid achievement of the Eastern Han. Yet grounds for regret remained: some items were absent from the Seven Summaries, and Ban added them according to his own judgment [?], thereby stumbling.

Coming down through the periods of Jin, Wei, Sui, and Chen, although the times changed and preferences differed, rulers interested in such pursuits and scholars who admired antiquity never ceased to concern themselves with compilation and writing. Thus, with pale-yellow book bags and wrappers, they gathered lost works into the imperial library; with precious scroll rollers and brocade labels, they stored illustrated works and books in separate palace halls. Truly, one could not readily enumerate them even with successive attendants taking turns. To speak of Song and Liang, Wang Jian compiled the Seven Classifications (Qi zhi) in the reign of Emperor Wu, with headings such as…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
經典曰諸子曰文翰曰軍書曰陰陽曰術
藝曰圖譜是已阮孝緒著七錄於普通之
中如曰經典曰記傳曰子兵曰文集曰枝
術曰佛錄曰道錄是已之二子者遞相祖
述整比卷帙非不自附於作者之林也而
一病於文義之淺近一病於辭義之割裂
例之兩漢風斯下矣況於聖經乎以唐宋
言之玄宗命殷踐猷等脩羣書四部爰別
經史子集之名仁宗命王堯臣等作崇文
===
總目悉倣開元四部之例之諸臣者分曹
綜緝甄明科部非不馳聲於翰墨之苑也
而唐則失之浩繁宋則失之缺略方之宋
梁且未優矣況於史漢乎由是觀之六經
脩於仲尼厄於秦火即得之屋壁所藏口
耳所授者其不絕如綫爾漢唐宋諸書連
篇累帙藏在石室播之寰宇固宜家傳而
人誦之矣鄭夾漈氏迺謂秦人焚書而書
存而歐陽永叔所見唐四庫書目百不存
punctuated:
經典，曰諸子，曰文翰，曰軍書，曰陰陽，曰術藝，曰圖譜，是已。阮孝緒著七錄於普通之中，如曰經典，曰記傳，曰子兵，曰文集，曰枝術，曰佛錄，曰道錄，是已。之二子者，遞相祖述，整比卷帙，非不自附於作者之林也；而一病於文義之淺近，一病於辭義之割裂。例之兩漢，風斯下矣，況於聖經乎？以唐宋言之，玄宗命殷踐猷等脩羣書四部，爰別經史子集之名；仁宗命王堯臣等作《崇文總目》，悉倣開元四部之例。之諸臣者，分曹綜緝，甄明科部，非不馳聲於翰墨之苑也；而唐則失之浩繁，宋則失之缺略。方之宋梁，且未優矣，況於史漢乎？
由是觀之，六經脩於仲尼，厄於秦火，即得之屋壁所藏、口耳所授者，其不絕如綫爾。漢唐宋諸書，連篇累帙，藏在石室，播之寰宇，固宜家傳而人誦之矣。鄭夾漈氏迺謂秦人焚書而書存，而歐陽永叔所見唐四庫書目，百不存
translation_en:
…Classics, Masters, Literary Writings, Military Works, Yin and Yang, Technical Arts, and Charts and Genealogies: these were its categories. Ruan Xiaoxu compiled the Seven Registers during the Putong era, with such categories as Classics, Historical Records and Biographies, Masters and Military Works, Literary Collections, Branch Arts [?], Buddhist Register, and Daoist Register. These two men successively followed earlier models and arranged the volumes in order. They certainly sought a place among the ranks of authors; yet one suffered from shallowness of textual meaning, and the other from fragmentation of language and meaning. Compared with the works of the two Han dynasties, their standards had declined—how much more so compared with the sages’ classics!
As for the Tang and Song, Emperor Xuanzong ordered Yin Jianyou and others to arrange the collected books into four divisions, distinguishing them as Classics, Histories, Masters, and Literary Collections. Emperor Renzong ordered Wang Yaochen and others to compile the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Institute for the Veneration of Literature, following throughout the precedent of the four divisions established during the Kaiyuan era. These officials divided their responsibilities, assembled and edited the materials, and distinguished the categories clearly. They certainly won renown in the literary world; yet the Tang work erred through excessive bulk, and the Song work through omissions and excessive abbreviation. They were not even superior to the works of the Song and Liang dynasties, much less to the Records of the Historian and the History of the Han!
Viewed in this light, the Six Classics were edited by Zhongni and suffered the calamity of the Qin book burning. Even with the recovery of texts hidden within the walls of houses and transmitted orally, their survival hung by a mere thread. The books of the Han, Tang, and Song, by contrast, extended through successive chapters and numerous volumes, were stored in stone chambers, and circulated throughout the realm. Surely they ought to have been handed down in every household and recited by everyone. Yet Zheng Jiaji said that the people of Qin burned books but the books survived, whereas, of the books in the catalogue of the Tang’s Four Repositories that Ouyang Yongshu saw, out of a hundred there did not survive …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
一焉者豈無其故乎夫六經者聖人傳心
之書也統括羣聖包舉造化易以道吾心
之時書以道吾心之中而詩則道吾心之
性情也禮以道吾心之敬樂以道吾心之
和而春秋則道吾心之是非也文發於心
經傳於後百家同指千古不磨夫繁星至
難數計矣而求之天則明衆流匪可涯測
矣而歸之海則一然則六經者羣書之天
與海也其不亡於秦燼也宜哉歷代典籍
===
皆掇拾以爲考訂之具也勦襲往緒罔知
取裁以采掇爲工者則極意於蒐羅而碔
砆美玉莫辨焉以幷蓄爲富者則取盈於
箱篋而魯魚亥豕莫稽焉言不由衷行之
不遠匪直災木且資覆瓿昔有寶敝帚而
鬻之以千金者卒忘其帚之敝也宋人寶
燕石以爲玉而藏之華匱者旣發藏廼知
其燕石也然則藝文志者歷代之敝帚燕
石爾其不傳於世也有由哉嗟乎千聖一
punctuated: 一焉者，豈無其故乎？夫六經者，聖人傳心之書也，統括羣聖，包舉造化。易以道吾心之時，書以道吾心之中，而詩則道吾心之性情也；禮以道吾心之敬，樂以道吾心之和，而春秋則道吾心之是非也。文發於心，經傳於後，百家同指，千古不磨。夫繁星至難數計矣，而求之天則明；衆流匪可涯測矣，而歸之海則一。然則六經者，羣書之天與海也，其不亡於秦燼也宜哉！歷代典籍，皆掇拾以爲考訂之具也。勦襲往緒，罔知取裁；以采掇爲工者，則極意於蒐羅，而碔砆美玉莫辨焉；以幷蓄爲富者，則取盈於箱篋，而魯魚亥豕莫稽焉。言不由衷，行之不遠，匪直災木，且資覆瓿。昔有寶敝帚而鬻之以千金者，卒忘其帚之敝也。宋人寶燕石以爲玉而藏之華匱者，旣發藏，廼知其燕石也。然則藝文志者，歷代之敝帚燕石爾，其不傳於世也有由哉！嗟乎！千聖一
translation_en:
…not even one in a hundred survived—could there be no reason for this? The Six Classics are books through which the sages transmitted their minds. They encompass all the sages and embrace the workings of creation. The Changes expresses our mind’s responsiveness to the times; the Documents expresses our mind’s equilibrium; and the Odes expresses our mind’s nature and feelings. The Rites expresses our mind’s reverence; the Music expresses our mind’s harmony; and the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses our mind’s judgments of right and wrong. Their writings issued from the mind, and their texts were transmitted to later generations. The hundred schools share their purport, which remains undiminished through the ages. The myriad stars are exceedingly difficult to count, yet when sought in Heaven they are clear; the many streams cannot be measured to their limits, yet when they return to the sea they become one. Thus the Six Classics are the Heaven and sea of all books. It is fitting that they did not perish in the ashes of Qin!

The writings of successive dynasties are all gathered as materials for examination and verification. They appropriate and repeat the remnants of earlier writings without knowing how to select and judge. Those who take compilation as their craft devote all their efforts to collecting, yet cannot distinguish jade-like stones from fine jade. Those who regard comprehensive holdings as wealth fill their chests and cases, yet leave scribal confusions—between lu 魯 and yu 魚, or hai 亥 and shi 豕—unchecked. Words that do not issue from the heart do not travel far. Such writings do more than waste the wood of printing blocks: they serve as covers for jars. Once there was someone who treasured a worn-out broom and offered it for sale for a thousand pieces of gold, utterly forgetting how worn it was. A man of Song treasured a stone from Yan as jade and stored it in an ornate casket; only when the casket was opened did he learn that it was merely a stone from Yan. Thus the bibliographical treatises are no more than the worn-out brooms and Yan stones of successive dynasties. There is indeed a reason why their contents have not been transmitted to posterity! Alas! The thousand sages share one…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
道千人一心學者不求之載籍而求之六
經不求之六經之迹而求之作經者之心
窮理以明之居敬以養之弗襍於聲色貨
利之私弗遷於紛華波蕩之感養吾心之
時中即羲畫未陳墳典未述而易與書固
在也養吾心之和敬即經曲未制聲容未
作而禮與樂固在也養吾心之是非與性
情則風雅頌之未起褒貶予奪之未彰而
詩與春秋固在也心存則道得道得則文
===
自生以之述作可以翼經而垂訓以之逺
覽可以考古而信今而學之能事畢矣易
曰君子多識前言往行以畜其德軻書曰
君子博學而詳說之將以反說約也愚生
誦法孔孟而漢唐宋所不敢知者故有味
於反約之說執事其以為何如
第四問
梁岱
同考試官教諭梁批訶品往哲如持權衡以較輕重
punctuated:
道，千人一心。學者不求之載籍，而求之六經；不求之六經之迹，而求之作經者之心。窮理以明之，居敬以養之，弗襍於聲色貨利之私，弗遷於紛華波蕩之感。養吾心之時中，即羲畫未陳、墳典未述，而易與書固在也；養吾心之和敬，即經曲未制、聲容未作，而禮與樂固在也；養吾心之是非與性情，則風雅頌之未起、褒貶予奪之未彰，而詩與春秋固在也。心存則道得，道得則文自生。以之述作，可以翼經而垂訓；以之逺覽，可以考古而信今，而學之能事畢矣。易曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」軻書曰：「君子博學而詳說之，將以反說約也。」愚生誦法孔孟，而漢唐宋所不敢知者，故有味於反約之說。執事其以為何如？
第四問
梁岱
同考試官教諭梁批：訶品往哲，如持權衡以較輕重，
translation_en:
…the Way; a thousand people share one heart. The student should seek it not in the mass of written records, but in the Six Classics; not in the traces preserved in the Six Classics, but in the hearts of those who composed them. Investigate principle to illuminate the heart, and abide in reverence to nurture it. Do not let it be adulterated by selfish desires for sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit, or diverted by the turbulent influence of dazzling worldly attractions. Nurture the heart’s capacity to attain the mean appropriate to each occasion: even before Fuxi’s diagrams were set forth or the ancient canonical records composed, the Changes and the Documents were already inherently present. Nurture harmony and reverence in the heart: even before the principal and detailed rules of ritual were established, or musical sounds and ceremonial forms devised, the Rites and the Music were already inherently present. Nurture the heart’s discernment of right and wrong, its nature and feelings: even before the Airs, Odes, and Hymns arose, or praise and blame, approval and rejection were explicitly expressed, the Poetry and the Spring and Autumn Annals were already inherently present. When the heart is preserved, the Way is attained; when the Way is attained, literary expression arises of itself. Through it, one may compose writings that assist the Classics and transmit instruction to posterity; through it, one may read widely, investigating antiquity and establishing what is trustworthy in the present. Thus all that learning can accomplish is fulfilled. The Changes says: “The gentleman acquaints himself extensively with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nourishing his virtue.” The book of Meng Ke says: “The gentleman learns broadly and expounds in detail, intending thereby to return to an explanation of the essentials.” I, your unworthy student, recite and take as my models Confucius and Mencius; as for the Han, Tang, and Song, I dare not claim knowledge of them. Thus I find much significance in this teaching of returning to the essentials. What is your judgment, honored examiner?
Fourth Question
Liang Dai
Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: In criticizing and appraising [?] the worthy men of the past, he is like someone holding a balance to compare their relative weight…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
銖兩不差且辭復雅健可追漢人手筆
考試官教諭陳批〔敷對無遺蓋志存尚友者〕
考試官教授王批〔論人物而得其心可為斷案〕
顒俊以光洪猷者熈世之治也奮庸以樹
遠績者哲士之程也蓋人材之生何地無
之顧其時之所遭或異而士之致用其器
業若相倍蓰然故夫英度卓識審時圖幾
入足以弼諧化理出足以潤澤生民者斯
大受之才也其若隨世程能效時宣力或
===
陳讜議以毗政或捍疆圉以衛國者斯亦
適用之才善圖治者所當兼收而並蓄者
也審如是則粤西之人才即在往代已可
覩記矧
國家重熈累洽所以丕振而長育之者久矣
則夫潤飾鴻猷光揚駿烈之士超軼往代
豈偶然之故哉執事發策以粤西人才為
問蓋欲愚生志其大也竊甞觀之人才之
生關于氣運而實繫乎風化之轉移故有
punctuated:
銖兩不差，且辭復雅健，可追漢人手筆。
考試官教諭陳批〔敷對無遺，蓋志存尚友者。〕
考試官教授王批〔論人物而得其心，可為斷案。〕
顒俊以光洪猷者，熈世之治也；奮庸以樹遠績者，哲士之程也。蓋人材之生，何地無之？顧其時之所遭或異，而士之致用，其器業若相倍蓰然。故夫英度卓識，審時圖幾，入足以弼諧化理，出足以潤澤生民者，斯大受之才也。其若隨世程能，效時宣力，或陳讜議以毗政，或捍疆圉以衛國者，斯亦適用之才，善圖治者所當兼收而並蓄者也。審如是，則粤西之人才，即在往代已可覩記。矧國家重熈累洽，所以丕振而長育之者久矣，則夫潤飾鴻猷、光揚駿烈之士，超軼往代，豈偶然之故哉？執事發策，以粤西人才為問，蓋欲愚生志其大也。竊甞觀之，人才之生，關于氣運，而實繫乎風化之轉移，故有
translation_en:
…without an error of even a zhu or a liang in the weighing. Moreover, the language is elegant and vigorous, worthy of comparison with the writings of Han authors.
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The response leaves nothing unaddressed; the writer evidently aspires to take the worthies of antiquity as his friends.〕
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔In discussing these figures, he grasps their hearts; this may serve as a definitive judgment.〕
To summon worthy men [?] to bring lustre to grand designs is the way to govern an age into prosperity; to exert oneself in service and establish lasting achievements is the course of a wise scholar. For what place does not produce men of talent? Yet the circumstances they encounter may differ, and when scholars put their abilities to use, their capacities and accomplishments seem to differ twofold or fivefold. Thus, those of outstanding bearing and exceptional discernment, who assess the times and consider incipient developments, who at court can assist in harmonizing transformative government and outside it can benefit the people—these are talents fit for great responsibilities. Those who demonstrate their abilities as the age requires and exert themselves in timely service, whether presenting forthright counsel to assist government or defending the frontiers to protect the state, are likewise talents suited to practical employment. Those skilled in pursuing good government should recruit and nurture both kinds.
If this is indeed so, the talented men of Yuexi can already be identified and recorded in past dynasties. How much more so under our dynasty, with its successive ages of prosperity and accumulated good government, which has long worked to invigorate and nurture them! That scholars who embellish its grand designs and illuminate its magnificent achievements should surpass those of earlier ages can hardly be accidental. You, honoured examiners, have issued a policy question concerning the talented men of Yuexi, surely wishing this humble student to set his aspirations on what is great. I have ventured to observe that the emergence of talent is connected with the workings of cosmic forces and the fortunes of the age, but depends in truth upon changes in customs and moral influence. Thus, when there is…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
時雍風動之俗而後有亮采惠疇之賢有
籲俊尊帝之猷而後有迪知忱恂之哲有
用協丕式之治而後有三宅三俊之材周
之棫樸菁莪譽髦久之而後奔走禦侮疏
附先後諸臣出焉蓋人才作興若斯其難
也人亦有言燕趙之士懷慷慨而宋鄭多
沉畧秦晉之士張果毅而齊魯富聲名嗟
乎斯殆囿于風氣之說未暇究觀化澤者
歟粤西古甌駱之地方其阻于聲教也仁
===
賢隱閟亡可槩見秦人雖并百越置郡而
發謫騷然漢興蕩平南越開拓境土漸涵
及乎世祖始復崇尚風教於是人才彬彬
出矣夷考其時陳元世業春秋議立左氏
學官蓋篤信士也至立朝忠鯁諫止督察
三公復識君人大體昔人謂其克蓋厥考
事新之愆其賢可知矣申朔雅尚儉素不
事紈綺蓋廉靜士也至舉孝廉爲九眞都
尉擊賊有功民無不頌厥德吳人爲著先
punctuated:
時雍風動之俗，而後有亮采惠疇之賢；有籲俊尊帝之猷，而後有迪知忱恂之哲；有用協丕式之治，而後有三宅三俊之材。周之《棫樸》《菁莪》譽髦，久之，而後奔走禦侮、疏附先後諸臣出焉。蓋人才作興，若斯其難也！
人亦有言：燕趙之士懷慷慨，而宋鄭多沉畧；秦晉之士張果毅，而齊魯富聲名。嗟乎！斯殆囿于風氣之說，未暇究觀化澤者歟？粤西，古甌駱之地，方其阻于聲教也，仁賢隱閟，亡可槩見。秦人雖并百越置郡，而發謫騷然。漢興，蕩平南越，開拓境土，漸涵；及乎世祖，始復崇尚風教，於是人才彬彬出矣。
夷考其時，陳元世業《春秋》，議立《左氏》學官，蓋篤信士也。至立朝忠鯁，諫止督察三公，復識君人大體。昔人謂其克蓋厥考事新之愆，其賢可知矣。申朔雅尚儉素，不事紈綺，蓋廉靜士也。至舉孝廉，爲九眞都尉，擊賊有功，民無不頌厥德。吳人爲著先
translation_en:
…customs of harmony, responsive to moral influence, and only then are there worthy men who faithfully discharge their duties and bring concord to their fellows. Only when there is a policy of summoning outstanding men to honor the sovereign are there wise men of understanding and sincerity; only when government accords with the great rule are there men qualified for the three offices and the three classes of outstanding service. Under the Zhou, outstanding men were praised and nurtured, as in the poems “The Oak Trees” and “The Luxuriant Southernwood.” Only after a long time did ministers emerge who hastened to serve, resisted aggression, drew the distant near, attached the people to their ruler, and assisted him in every capacity. Such is the difficulty of fostering talent!
People also say that the men of Yan and Zhao cherish a generous ardor, while Song and Zheng have many men of profound strategic judgment; that the men of Qin and Jin display resolve and courage, while Qi and Lu abound in men of renown. Alas! Are such views perhaps confined to theories of regional temperament, without examining fully the beneficent effects of moral transformation? Western Yue—Guangxi—was anciently the land of Ouluo. When it was cut off from the imperial civilizing influence, humane and worthy men remained hidden, and no general view of them could be obtained. Although the Qin annexed the Hundred Yue and established commanderies, their dispatch of convicts into exile caused widespread turmoil. When the Han arose, it pacified Nanyue, extended its territory, and gradually imbued the region with its influence. With Shizu, the Guangwu Emperor, moral instruction once again came to be esteemed, and cultivated men of talent then began to emerge in abundance.
Examining that period, we find that Chen Yuan continued his family’s study of the Spring and Autumn Annals and advocated establishing an academic post for the Zuo Commentary. He was indeed a man of steadfast conviction. Moreover, serving at court with loyalty and integrity, he remonstrated against subjecting the Three Dukes to supervisory investigation, showing that he also understood the broad principles of rulership. Earlier writers said that he succeeded in redeeming his father’s fault in serving the Xin dynasty. His worthiness is thus evident. Shen Shuo consistently prized frugality and simplicity and did not indulge in fine silks: he was indeed a man of incorruptibility and restraint. Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and appointed Commandant of Jiuzhen, he distinguished himself in suppressing bandits, and all the people praised his virtue. The people of Wu wrote an account of him in the Former…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
賢傳紀之其賢可知矣士燮精核經傳見
稱名流及爲交趾太守爰致疆塲無事民
不失業方之竇融保河西何以過之耶鄧
盛事母至孝矢聲尉曹及覆竟左尚之獄
一以恩意感動片言伏之方之臯陶淑問
豈無其由耶徐徴素行方直不畏疆禦爲
督郵時收致唐衡暴客髠之郡市蓋持節
不撓其英畧有足稱焉養奮博通墳藉一
時名儒當和帝時條對陰陽水旱無少牽
===
合蓋正色敢言其大義有足取焉夫是六
子咸漢才咸出東京無亦光武明章之烈
振作于上者有成效而興起于下者無遺
壤哉唐人雖置桂容邕三管厥後藩鎭竊
據士無寧宇故人才罕稱惟趙觀文掇巍
科而以抗言謝歸庶於見幾之君子乎韋
厥持使節而服生蠻開擴化外于向糾義
兵而助高駢平定交趾斯亦濶乎希矣有
宋鼎建南服文教易敷士風益奮方建隆
punctuated:
賢傳》紀之，其賢可知矣。士燮精核經傳，見稱名流；及爲交趾太守，爰致疆塲無事，民不失業。方之竇融保河西，何以過之耶？鄧盛事母至孝，矢聲尉曹；及覆竟左尚之獄，一以恩意感動，片言伏之。方之臯陶淑問，豈無其由耶？徐徴素行方直，不畏疆禦，爲督郵時，收致唐衡暴客，髠之郡市。蓋持節不撓，其英畧有足稱焉。養奮博通墳藉，一時名儒。當和帝時，條對陰陽水旱，無少牽合。蓋正色敢言，其大義有足取焉。夫是六子，咸漢才，咸出東京。無亦光武、明、章之烈，振作于上者有成效，而興起于下者無遺壤哉？
唐人雖置桂、容、邕三管，厥後藩鎭竊據，士無寧宇，故人才罕稱。惟趙觀文掇巍科，而以抗言謝歸，庶於見幾之君子乎？韋厥持使節而服生蠻，開擴化外；于向糾義兵而助高駢平定交趾，斯亦濶乎希矣。
有宋鼎建，南服文教易敷，士風益奮。方建隆
translation_en:
…Worthies, recording his deeds. His worthiness is thus evident. Shi Xie scrutinized the classics and their commentaries with precision and won acclaim among eminent scholars. When he became Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi, he brought peace to the frontier and enabled the people to pursue their livelihoods undisturbed. Compared with Dou Rong’s preservation of Hexi, how could the latter’s achievement surpass his? Deng Sheng served his mother with utmost filial devotion and established a reputation in the commandant’s office [?]. When he reviewed and concluded Zuo Shang’s case, he moved him entirely through kindness and goodwill, securing his submission with a few words. Surely there is reason to compare him with Gao Yao’s skillful questioning? Xu Zheng was consistently upright in conduct and unafraid of the powerful. While serving as an Inspector, he arrested Tang Heng’s violent retainers and had their heads shaved in the commandery marketplace. Unyielding in his integrity, he possessed outstanding ability and resourcefulness worthy of praise. Yang Fen was widely versed in ancient writings and was a celebrated Confucian scholar of his time. Under Emperor He, he submitted itemized responses concerning yin and yang, floods and droughts, without the slightest strained accommodation. Forthright and unafraid to speak, he upheld principles well worth commending. These six men were all talents of the Han, and all emerged under the Eastern Han. Was this not because the achievements of Emperors Guangwu, Ming, and Zhang produced effective encouragement from above, while the resulting response below left no region untouched?
Although the Tang established the three administrative jurisdictions of Gui, Rong, and Yong, military governors subsequently seized control. Scholars had no peaceful dwelling places, and consequently few men of talent won renown. Only Zhao Guanwen attained high distinction in the examinations, yet after speaking out boldly he took his leave and returned home. Was he not close to being a gentleman who discerned the first signs of change? Wei Jue bore an envoy’s credentials, brought the unassimilated Man peoples into submission, and extended rule into lands beyond the reach of civilizing influence. Yu Xiang rallied loyal troops and helped Gao Pian pacify Jiaozhi. Such men, too, were few and far between.
When the Song dynasty was established, literary and moral instruction spread readily through the southern territories, and the scholarly ethos grew still more vigorous. During the Jianlong era…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
初周渭召試時務受知藝祖即能誅縣吏
之奸弭監軍之叛減僞國稅筭之籍敭歴
中外聲績赫然可不謂奇士哉而教授廣
州獻本政書十三篇慨然有志復古時則
有若林勳焉張敬夫稱其人才卓然有以
也作牧三州躬操廉介惟以恩信結民夷
心時則有若蔣允濟焉朱元晦稱其遺愛
在人有以也覃光佃幼抱岐嶷著名御史
内肅朝儀外紓邊策其繫國安危若此王
===
世則早掇倫魁增光使節進憂國本退播
英聲其繫時輕重若此知昌化軍而請增
賓興之額減折納之輸者黃齊循良之績
也爲講讀官而疏陳謹獨之謨建脩武之
策者陶崇啓沃之功也若馮京三爲舉首
號名執政而中立之操始終不變所謂大
臣以道事君者京有之矣宋之人才於斯
爲盛洪惟我
國家
punctuated:
初，周渭召試時務，受知藝祖，即能誅縣吏之奸，弭監軍之叛，減僞國稅筭之籍，敭歴中外，聲績赫然，可不謂奇士哉？而教授廣州，獻《本政書》十三篇，慨然有志復古，時則有若林勳焉。張敬夫稱其人才卓然，有以也。作牧三州，躬操廉介，惟以恩信結民夷心，時則有若蔣允濟焉。朱元晦稱其遺愛在人，有以也。覃光佃幼抱岐嶷，著名御史，内肅朝儀，外紓邊策，其繫國安危若此。王世則早掇倫魁，增光使節，進憂國本，退播英聲，其繫時輕重若此。知昌化軍而請增賓興之額、減折納之輸者，黃齊循良之績也。爲講讀官而疏陳謹獨之謨、建脩武之策者，陶崇啓沃之功也。若馮京三爲舉首，號名執政，而中立之操始終不變，所謂大臣以道事君者，京有之矣。宋之人才，於斯爲盛。
洪惟我國家
translation_en:
…at the beginning of the Jianlong era, Zhou Wei was summoned for examination on current affairs and won the recognition of the dynastic founder. He then punished corrupt county clerks, quelled a rebellion by an army supervisor, and reduced the tax assessments registered under the former illegitimate regime. Serving in posts both at court and in the provinces, he gained an illustrious reputation for his achievements. Could he not be called an extraordinary man? There was also Lin Xun, who served as an instructor in Guangzhou and presented thirteen chapters of his Book on the Fundamentals of Government, earnestly aspiring to restore ancient institutions. Zhang Jingfu had good reason to praise his outstanding abilities. There was Jiang Yunji, who governed three prefectures, personally upheld integrity and strict principles, and sought only through kindness and trustworthiness to win the hearts of the common people and the indigenous peoples. Zhu Yuanhui had good reason to say that the affection he inspired endured among the people. Qin Guangdian [?] showed exceptional promise in childhood and became renowned as a censor. At court he enforced proper ceremonial conduct; beyond it he eased frontier difficulties through his policies [?]. Such was his importance to the security of the state. Wang Shize won first place in the examinations early in life and brought distinction to his diplomatic commissions. In office he concerned himself with the foundations of the state; in retirement his distinguished reputation spread. Such was his importance to his age. As administrator of Changhua Military Prefecture, Huang Qi requested an increase in the quota for candidates sponsored for the examinations and a reduction in payments commuted from taxes in kind: these were achievements of a conscientious and benevolent official. As a court lecturer, Tao Chong submitted memorials urging vigilance over one's conduct even in private and proposing measures to strengthen military preparedness: these were his contributions to enlightening the sovereign. As for Feng Jing, he placed first in the examinations three times and was celebrated as a chief councillor, yet his impartial principles remained unchanged throughout. Jing exemplified what is meant by a great minister who serves his ruler according to the Way. With these men, talent under the Song reached its flourishing height.
Reflecting reverently upon our dynasty…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承身任君師之責遐陬僻壤均沾教澤
賢才應運而生又豈往代所可倫擬哉今
觀黃驥以侍從使西域諭南交而停外夷
貢馬諸疏輒見嘉納自是陝右之民賴以
全安者衆矣王溥以藩司理冤獄禁侵占
而鑿庾嶺教車運諸法咸裨經濟自是廣
南之戶賴以蕃阜者多矣包裕討雲南之
夷圖爲經久而滇人悉心歸之至論其憲
度貞肅尤有蹇諤之風焉馮俊懲楊畢之
===
暴不避席寵而閩人闔戶倚之至攷其駕
馭土夷尤有威權之略焉張燦早列清華
晚躋樞筦而正心之教士人宗之志者稱
其詩章力儗古人非過也蔣昇歷官郡邑
晉秩上卿而窮理之學終身誦之志者稱
其言行無媿古人非過也吳廷舉勛猷氣
節足以起懦激頑疏歸東湖好學不倦稱
之者謂其才如干將鏌鉁志如長川逝河
節如堅松勁栢信矣屠楷雅量清操足以
punctuated: 列聖相承，身任君師之責，遐陬僻壤均沾教澤，賢才應運而生，又豈往代所可倫擬哉？今觀黃驥以侍從使西域、諭南交，而停外夷貢馬諸疏輒見嘉納，自是陝右之民賴以全安者衆矣。王溥以藩司理冤獄、禁侵占，而鑿庾嶺、教車運諸法咸裨經濟，自是廣南之戶賴以蕃阜者多矣。包裕討雲南之夷，圖爲經久，而滇人悉心歸之；至論其憲度貞肅，尤有蹇諤之風焉。馮俊懲楊畢之暴，不避席寵，而閩人闔戶倚之；至攷其駕馭土夷，尤有威權之略焉。張燦早列清華，晚躋樞筦，而正心之教，士人宗之。志者稱其詩章力儗古人，非過也。蔣昇歷官郡邑，晉秩上卿，而窮理之學，終身誦之。志者稱其言行無媿古人，非過也。吳廷舉勛猷氣節，足以起懦激頑，疏歸東湖，好學不倦。稱之者謂其才如干將鏌鉁，志如長川逝河，節如堅松勁栢，信矣。屠楷雅量清操，足以
translation_en:
…successive sage emperors have personally shouldered the responsibilities of ruler and teacher. Even remote corners and outlying lands have shared equally in their civilizing beneficence, and worthy talents have arisen in response to the age. How could earlier dynasties possibly compare?

Consider Huang Ji, who, as an attendant official, went on a mission to the Western Regions and conveyed imperial instructions to Nanjiao. His memorials requesting the suspension of tribute horses from foreign peoples repeatedly received favorable approval. Thereafter, many people of Shanyou owed their safety and security to these measures. Wang Pu, serving in the Provincial Administration Commission, redressed wrongful convictions and prohibited encroachment and seizure. His measures, including cutting a passage through Yuling and teaching transport by cart, all contributed to good governance. Thereafter, many households in Guangnan owed their growth and prosperity to them.

Bao Yu campaigned against the non-Han peoples of Yunnan, planning for lasting stability, and the people of Dian gave him their wholehearted allegiance. As for his upright and stern enforcement of laws and standards, he particularly displayed a spirit of fearless remonstrance. Feng Jun punished the brutality of Yang and Bi [?], undeterred by their reliance on powerful favor, and every household in Min looked to him for support. Examining his management of the indigenous non-Han peoples, one finds particular skill in exercising authority.

Zhang Can entered prestigious service early and later rose to a pivotal position in government; scholars took his teaching on rectifying the mind as their guide. The chroniclers’ praise that his poetry strove to emulate the ancients was no exaggeration. Jiang Sheng served successively in prefectural and county offices and rose to the rank of a high minister. Throughout his life he expounded the learning of investigating principle. The chroniclers’ praise that his words and deeds were worthy of the ancients was no exaggeration.

Wu Tingju’s achievements, counsels, spirit, and integrity were enough to rouse the timid and stir the obstinate. He memorialized requesting retirement to Donghu and remained tireless in his love of learning. Those who praised him said that his talent resembled the swords Ganjiang and Mozhen [?, probably Moye], his resolve a long stream or an onward-flowing river, and his integrity a sturdy pine or a strong cypress. Truly so! Tu Kai’s magnanimity and unsullied conduct were enough to…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
黜浮敦薄優游梓里以壽考終稱之者謂
其守身如蘧伯玉立朝如文潞公居鄉如
司馬君實信矣蔣冕休休有容由文學入
柄大政卒而受遺定策迎立
眞主銷危疑於未著奠
社稷於乂安者冕等二三大臣之功也稱之者
謂其德業文章如有源之水信知言哉夫
此數君子者樹休烈于當時垂芳聲于後
世炳炳烺烺較之漢唐宋諸臣遠過之矣
===
其諸一節一行之士播在記牒尤有未易
以枚舉者頃歲以來鴻材彙征內而秉衡
握軸外而仗鉞擁旄以及廊署岳牧布列
庶位者濟濟相望晉之履公卿輔弼之任
以翊
國家中興之治其所建樹將必與帝王名世
之佐相後先矣猗與盛哉詩曰思皇多士
生此王國王國克生維周之禎言才賢之
利於國也易曰雲從龍風從虎聖人作而
punctuated:
黜浮敦薄，優游梓里，以壽考終。稱之者謂其守身如蘧伯玉，立朝如文潞公，居鄉如司馬君實，信矣。蔣冕休休有容，由文學入柄大政，卒而受遺定策，迎立眞主，銷危疑於未著，奠社稷於乂安者，冕等二三大臣之功也。稱之者謂其德業文章如有源之水，信知言哉！夫此數君子者，樹休烈于當時，垂芳聲于後世，炳炳烺烺，較之漢唐宋諸臣，遠過之矣。
其諸一節一行之士，播在記牒，尤有未易以枚舉者。頃歲以來，鴻材彙征，內而秉衡握軸，外而仗鉞擁旄，以及廊署岳牧，布列庶位者，濟濟相望。晉之履公卿輔弼之任，以翊國家中興之治，其所建樹，將必與帝王名世之佐相後先矣。猗與盛哉！詩曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之禎。」言才賢之利於國也。易曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而
translation_en:
…to dispel frivolity and strengthen weak moral character. He lived at ease in his native place and died at an advanced age. Those who praised him said that in his personal conduct he resembled Qu Boyu, in service at court, Wen, Duke of Lu, and in life in his home community, Sima Junshi. This was indeed true. Jiang Mian was generous and accommodating. Through literary learning he rose to wield authority over the great affairs of government. Ultimately, he received the late emperor’s last commands, settled the succession, and welcomed and enthroned the true sovereign. That danger and uncertainty were dispelled before they became manifest, and that the altars of soil and grain were secured in peace, was the achievement of Jiang Mian and those few other great ministers. Those who praised him likened his virtue, accomplishments, and writings to water with a living source. How discerning their words were! These gentlemen established glorious achievements in their own day and left a fragrant reputation to later generations. Their brilliance shone forth; compared with the ministers of the Han, Tang, and Song, they far surpassed them.
As for men distinguished by a single act of integrity or exemplary deed, their deeds are scattered through the records, and they are especially difficult to enumerate individually. In recent years, men of outstanding talent have advanced into service together. At court they hold the balance of authority and direct the machinery of government; outside the capital they bear the battle-axe and command beneath their banners. Together with those serving in central offices and as regional governors, they fill the many posts, an impressive succession of worthy men. When advanced to the responsibilities of high ministers and chief advisers, to assist the state’s resurgent rule, their achievements will surely rank alongside those of the renowned assistants to emperors and kings through the ages. Ah, how splendid! The Book of Odes says: “August are the many worthy men, born in this royal kingdom. The kingdom can bring them forth: they are the auspicious sign of Zhou.” This speaks of the benefit that talented and worthy men bring to a state. The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and…”

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬物覩言人類之神於應也今
聖天子雍熈成化綱紀作人一時名賢際雲龍
之會而應彙征之期者蓋所在嚮風而承
德焉愚也生逢
唐虞之世上嘉臯夔之風竊願友天下之善
士又尚論古之人未敢以一方自限量也
敢以是爲明問復
第五問
彭啓忠
===
同考試官教諭陳 批時務策關繫最要是作以任
將達權爲主甚合機宜且議論鑿鑿可行足徵經濟
考試官教諭陳 批區畫精詳足占用世之學
考試官教授王 批籌畫切中機宜誠達時務者
御夷有常而任將爲急制勝有機而達權
爲要夫人之著能各不同也故爲將者有
偏全之技有攻守之才惟選擇而責成之
使專于其任焉斯則得統御之略矣夫兵
之爲勢無常形也故達權者有伸縮之相
punctuated:
萬物覩」，言人類之神於應也。今聖天子雍熈成化，綱紀作人，一時名賢際雲龍之會而應彙征之期者，蓋所在嚮風而承德焉。愚也生逢唐虞之世，上嘉臯夔之風，竊願友天下之善士，又尚論古之人，未敢以一方自限量也。敢以是爲明問復。
第五問
彭啓忠
同考試官教諭陳批：時務策關繫最要，是作以任將達權爲主，甚合機宜，且議論鑿鑿可行，足徵經濟。
考試官教諭陳批：區畫精詳，足占用世之學。
考試官教授王批：籌畫切中機宜，誠達時務者。
御夷有常，而任將爲急；制勝有機，而達權爲要。夫人之著能各不同也，故爲將者有偏全之技，有攻守之才。惟選擇而責成之，使專于其任焉，斯則得統御之略矣。夫兵之爲勢無常形也，故達權者有伸縮之相
translation_en:
…“and all things behold him.” This speaks of the marvelous responsiveness of humankind. Now our sage Son of Heaven brings harmonious prosperity and completes the work of transformation, ordering the realm and nurturing men of talent. The eminent worthies of our time encounter the auspicious conjunction of cloud and dragon and answer the call to advance together; wherever they are, they turn toward his influence and receive his virtue. Unworthy though I am, I have been born into an age like that of Tang and Yu, and esteem the example of Gao Yao and Kui. I humbly wish to befriend the good men of the world and also to consider the men of antiquity. I dare not confine my aspirations to a single region. I venture to offer this in reply to your discerning question.
Fifth Question
Peng Qizhong
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Policy essays on current affairs concern matters of the greatest importance. This essay centers on appointing generals and exercising discretion according to circumstances, closely fitting the needs of the situation. Its arguments are also sound and practicable, amply demonstrating competence in statecraft.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The planning is precise and thorough, sufficient to reveal learning suited to service in the world.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: The plans precisely meet the needs of the situation. This is truly someone who understands current affairs.
There are constant principles for managing the non-Chinese peoples, but appointing generals is the urgent task. Victory depends on opportunities, but understanding how to exercise discretion is essential. People differ in the abilities they display; thus, among generals, some possess specialized skills and others comprehensive abilities, while some have talents for attack and others for defense. Only by selecting them and holding them responsible for results, allowing them sole charge of their assignments, can one master the art of command. Military configurations have no fixed form; thus, those who understand how to exercise discretion alternate between expansion and contraction…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
仍有勦撫之相因惟隨時而運用之使萬
全不爽焉斯可幾安攘之圖矣為將者惟
其剛而弗審誇而無當也故於兵則易視
之其自許也則曰我熟夷地諳夷情也至
使當一隊守一障焉則進退維谷尺寸不
效矣若是者不早擇之可乎治兵者惟其
誕而寡謀泥而不通也故臨事則輕言之
其策敵也不過曰夷强可勦弱可撫也至
使臨大敵制大事焉則措置譸張經理失
===
據矣若此者不豫圖之可乎執事憤土猺
叛亂之久幸重臣
簡命之臨思文武將吏之佐詢必勝久安之畫
為一方計至審也愚生敢借前籌哉敬以
舊聞者陳焉夫嶺表之有蠻夷也其種落
非一類其窟宅非一隅其侵叛非一日其
詒罹非一方也然今之號最黠而禍最鉅
者莫若近省之土猺焉蓋其枕藉兩江連
亘融洛扼龍門之阿拒都狼之隘地至阻
punctuated:
仍，有勦撫之相因，惟隨時而運用之，使萬全不爽焉，斯可幾安攘之圖矣。為將者惟其剛而弗審，誇而無當也，故於兵則易視之。其自許也，則曰：「我熟夷地、諳夷情也。」至使當一隊、守一障焉，則進退維谷，尺寸不效矣。若是者，不早擇之可乎？治兵者惟其誕而寡謀，泥而不通也，故臨事則輕言之。其策敵也，不過曰：「夷强可勦，弱可撫也。」至使臨大敵、制大事焉，則措置譸張，經理失據矣。若此者，不豫圖之可乎？
執事憤土猺叛亂之久，幸重臣簡命之臨，思文武將吏之佐，詢必勝久安之畫，為一方計至審也。愚生敢借前籌哉？敬以舊聞者陳焉。夫嶺表之有蠻夷也，其種落非一類，其窟宅非一隅，其侵叛非一日，其詒罹非一方也。然今之號最黠而禍最鉅者，莫若近省之土猺焉。蓋其枕藉兩江，連亘融洛，扼龍門之阿，拒都狼之隘，地至阻
translation_en:
…follow one another, and suppression and pacification depend upon one another. Only by employing them as circumstances require, ensuring complete success without mishap, can one hope to realize a plan for securing peace and repelling incursions. Those who command troops are headstrong without being discerning, boastful without substance; hence they take warfare lightly. In their self-confidence they say, “I know the lands of the indigenous peoples well and understand their circumstances.” Yet when put in command of a detachment or assigned to defend a fortification, they find themselves unable either to advance or to retreat, achieving not the slightest result. With men like these, can we neglect to assess their fitness early? Those who direct military affairs are given to extravagant talk but lack plans, and cling rigidly to methods without adaptability; hence they speak lightly when confronting affairs. Their calculations concerning the enemy amount to no more than this: “When the indigenous peoples are strong, they can be suppressed; when weak, they can be pacified.” Yet when made to confront a formidable enemy and manage great affairs, their dispositions become confused [?], and their management loses its footing. In such cases, can we neglect to plan beforehand?
You, honored examiners, resent the long persistence of rebellion among the local Yao and welcome the arrival of a high minister selected and commissioned by the throne. You consider how civil and military officers might assist him and inquire into plans for certain victory and lasting peace. Your deliberations on behalf of this region are most thorough. Dare I, an ignorant student, presume to offer strategic counsel? I respectfully set forth what I have previously heard. As for the indigenous peoples beyond the Ling mountains, their tribes are of more than one kind, their lairs occupy more than one locality, their incursions and rebellions have continued for more than a single day, and the suffering they inflict extends beyond a single area. Yet among those now reputed most cunning and whose depredations are greatest, none surpass the local Yao near the provincial capital. They occupy the region of the Two Rivers, extend across Rong and Luo, command the bends at Longmen, and hold the passes at Dulang. Their terrain is exceedingly difficult…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也左連三鎮右達九寨背永寶綏靖之陰
達荔永藤峽之交穴至衆也往者抗王師
戕二將繼則掠省帑斃藩臣窺覬
靖邸侵竊縣治患至無巳也
聖天子軫念南顧而重臣握符矣計重糧餉至
內帑給儲矣然承制而專决一方建纛而總
握羣略者重臣之事也至運謀畫於帷幄
定進止於封郊宣恩威於燮伐奮勇力於
戰陣者文武諸吏之職也執事所謂欽承
===
===
威命而興師有期又云兵無常形而謀貴豫定
蓋率兵者將而兵勝以謀也制勝者謀而
謀成貴豫也兵志有之曰將者國之輔也
輔周則國强夫將必以周為輔矧今之土
猺地險而穴衆非可以一師一隊徑指而
直搗之者是所以分命諸將不可不擇之
精也又曰伐謀為上野戰為下夫兵之所
伐在謀矧今之土猺為患又至無巳非可
一朝一夕草薙而禽獮之者是所以相機
punctuated: 也。左連三鎮，右達九寨，背永寶綏靖之陰，達荔永藤峽之交，穴至衆也。往者抗王師，戕二將；繼則掠省帑，斃藩臣，窺覬靖邸，侵竊縣治，患至無巳也。聖天子軫念南顧，而重臣握符矣；計重糧餉，至內帑給儲矣。然承制而專决一方，建纛而總握羣略者，重臣之事也。至運謀畫於帷幄，定進止於封郊，宣恩威於燮伐，奮勇力於戰陣者，文武諸吏之職也。執事所謂欽承威命而興師有期，又云兵無常形而謀貴豫定，蓋率兵者將，而兵勝以謀也；制勝者謀，而謀成貴豫也。兵志有之，曰：「將者，國之輔也；輔周則國强。」夫將必以周為輔，矧今之土猺，地險而穴衆，非可以一師一隊徑指而直搗之者，是所以分命諸將，不可不擇之精也。又曰：「伐謀為上，野戰為下。」夫兵之所伐在謀，矧今之土猺為患又至無巳，非可一朝一夕草薙而禽獮之者，是所以相機
translation_en:
…To the left they connect with Sanzhen, and to the right they reach Jiuzhai; behind them lie the shaded sides of Yong, Bao, Sui, and Jing [?], and they extend to the junction of Li, Yong, and Teng Gorge [?]. Their lairs are exceedingly numerous. Formerly they resisted the imperial army and killed two commanders; subsequently they plundered the provincial treasury, killed a provincial official, coveted the residence of the Prince of Jing, and encroached upon and seized county seats. The troubles they cause have truly known no end.

The sagely Son of Heaven has been deeply concerned for the south, and a high minister now holds the command tally. Provisioning has been deemed so important that even the imperial treasury has supplied resources. Yet receiving imperial authority to make independent decisions throughout a region, and raising the command standard to direct all strategic plans, are the responsibilities of the high minister. As for devising plans within the command tent, determining advances and halts in the field, displaying imperial grace and might in pacification and punitive campaigns [?], and exerting courage and strength in battle—these are the duties of the civil and military officials.

You have spoken of reverently receiving the august command and fixing a date to mobilize the army. You have also said that warfare has no constant form and that plans must therefore be settled in advance. For commanders lead troops, but troops win through planning; planning secures victory, but successful planning depends upon preparation. A military treatise says: “The commander is the supporting pillar of the state; when that support is complete, the state is strong.” A commander must indeed provide complete support. All the more so with the local Yao today: their terrain is difficult and their lairs numerous. They cannot be directly approached and stormed by a single army or detachment. This is why, when assigning separate commands to the generals, one must select them with the utmost care.

It also says: “Attacking the enemy’s plans is best; fighting in the open field is inferior.” What an army should attack is the enemy’s plans. All the more so with the local Yao today, whose depredations have known no end: they cannot be mown down like grass or hunted down like beasts in a single day or night. This is why, in assessing opportunities…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
達權不可不計之深也且能道韜略者鮮
究其指趨喜談時事者弗裨於適用鳴劔
抵掌罕著伊吾之勳杜門思奮未効北平
之績不知吾方以蕩巢埽穴之責寄之也
而彼之非有建明者遂爾委之重寄可乎
謀在於勦者則謂秣馬犒師輕資匿影或
攻其不守或出其不虞靡不得志於夷者
也謀在於撫者則謂集我重兵壓彼境土
開布威信之令重加悔罪之恩夷亦有人
===
心者也不知彼方以聽招降附之辭詐我
也而我非有大懲創之者遂爾絡其詐中
可乎諸將不可不慎擇者然將得人則謀
必定矣謀定則審達權之略而明於行師
之始兵法所謂輔之周者雖計勝於未出
師之前可期也為謀不可不素定者然知
好謀則將斯得矣得將則因才智之長而
授機密之策兵法所謂攻其心者雖萬全
於既行師之後可必也人亦有言任相易
punctuated:
達權，不可不計之深也。且能道韜略者，鮮究其指趨；喜談時事者，弗裨於適用。鳴劔抵掌，罕著伊吾之勳；杜門思奮，未効北平之績。不知吾方以蕩巢埽穴之責寄之也，而彼之非有建明者，遂爾委之重寄，可乎？謀在於勦者，則謂秣馬犒師，輕資匿影，或攻其不守，或出其不虞，靡不得志於夷者也。謀在於撫者，則謂集我重兵，壓彼境土，開布威信之令，重加悔罪之恩，夷亦有人心者也。不知彼方以聽招降附之辭詐我也，而我非有大懲創之者，遂爾絡其詐中，可乎？
諸將不可不慎擇者，然將得人，則謀必定矣。謀定，則審達權之略，而明於行師之始。兵法所謂輔之周者，雖計勝於未出師之前，可期也。為謀不可不素定者，然知好謀，則將斯得矣。得將，則因才智之長，而授機密之策。兵法所謂攻其心者，雖萬全於既行師之後，可必也。人亦有言：「任相易
translation_en:
…and adapting to circumstances: these require profound deliberation. Moreover, those who can discourse on military strategy seldom fathom its purport, while those fond of discussing current affairs contribute little of practical use. They make their swords ring and clap their hands in animated discussion, yet seldom achieve exploits like those at Yiwu; they shut their doors and contemplate exerting themselves, yet have not matched the accomplishments at Beiping. They fail to understand that we are entrusting them with the responsibility of sweeping away the rebels’ lairs and clearing out their dens. If they have offered no sound proposals, can we simply entrust them with so weighty a charge?
Those whose plans favor suppression say that we should feed the horses and reward the troops, travel lightly and conceal our movements, attack where the enemy is undefended or appear where they least expect us; thus we shall invariably prevail over the non-Han peoples. Those whose plans favor pacification say that we should assemble a large force and bring pressure upon their territory, issue proclamations displaying our might and good faith, and generously extend clemency to those who repent of their crimes—for the non-Han peoples, too, have human hearts. They do not realize that the enemy is deceiving us with promises to heed our summons and submit. If we have not inflicted a severe chastisement upon them, can we simply become entangled in their deception [?]?
The commanders must indeed be chosen with care. Once suitable men have been obtained as commanders, plans will assuredly be settled. With plans settled, they will carefully consider strategies for adapting to circumstances and understand what to do at the outset of a campaign. This is what the military treatise means by an adviser whose assistance is comprehensive: we may thus expect to calculate victory even before the army sets out. Plans must indeed be settled beforehand. Yet if we understand the value of deliberation, suitable commanders will thereby be found. Having obtained commanders, we can give them confidential strategic instructions suited to their particular strengths in ability and intelligence. This is what the military treatise means by attacking the enemy’s heart: even complete success after the army has taken the field can be assured. There is also a saying: “Appointing a chief councillor is easy…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而任將難夫將之難知也然觀其年以知
其强勇試其言以考其智略其至要莫若
稽其行事驗其平生或累立戰功或曾經
陷陣昔人謂兵官非甞試之悉知其能者
則選將之術也若夫羸弱不可以服衆輕
率不可以諏謀其大致在於脂韋夤緣誇
談飾用聽其言則美施於用則疎昔人謂
兵不擇將以卒與敵者則任將之鑑也任
使旣稱謀猷旣周問罪於貫盈之夷發紓
===
===
夫人神之憤蠢玆土猺安能久逃鈇鉞也
是故曲道相伏險阨相薄至險不足虞也
何者昔者二馬之禍惟其識不遠而謀不
臧者也夫綿綿翼翼不測不克者師之律
也以曲道險阨之途而以無人之境視之
行不遠間諜止不定行幕經隘不搜竊伏
之奸紆道不匝住守之卒使猺突出以截
我也是豈素豫之將耶使其土著之夫結
之有素緝事之役待以殊恩分遣於數月
punctuated:
而任將難。夫將之難知也，然觀其年以知其强勇，試其言以考其智略，其至要莫若稽其行事，驗其平生。或累立戰功，或曾經陷陣，昔人謂「兵官非甞試之悉知其能者」，則選將之術也。若夫羸弱不可以服衆，輕率不可以諏謀，其大致在於脂韋夤緣，誇談飾用，聽其言則美，施於用則疎。昔人謂「兵不擇將，以卒與敵」者，則任將之鑑也。任使旣稱，謀猷旣周，問罪於貫盈之夷，發紓夫人神之憤，蠢玆土猺，安能久逃鈇鉞也？
是故曲道相伏，險阨相薄，至險不足虞也。何者？昔者二馬之禍，惟其識不遠而謀不臧者也。夫綿綿翼翼，不測不克者，師之律也。以曲道險阨之途，而以無人之境視之，行不遠間諜，止不定行幕，經隘不搜竊伏之奸，紆道不匝住守之卒，使猺突出以截我也，是豈素豫之將耶？使其土著之夫，結之有素；緝事之役，待以殊恩，分遣於數月
translation_en:
…but appointing generals is difficult. Though a general’s qualities are hard to discern, one may observe his age to judge his strength and courage, and test his words to assess his intelligence and strategic ability. Most essential, however, is to examine his deeds and scrutinize his past life. Some have repeatedly won distinction in battle; others have charged through enemy lines. The ancient saying concerning military officers—“unless one has tried them and thoroughly knows their abilities” [?]—expresses the method for selecting generals. The weak cannot command the obedience of their men, and the rash cannot deliberate on strategy. Such men generally resort to pliant flattery and cultivating connections, boastful talk and a show of competence. Their words sound fine, but when put to use they prove inadequate. The ancient saying, “To send troops without selecting their general is to give one’s soldiers to the enemy,” provides a warning for appointing generals. Once appointments are fitting and plans comprehensive, we can punish the barbarians whose crimes have reached their full measure and give vent to the indignation of men and spirits. How could these unruly local Yao long escape the executioner’s axe?
Thus, even where ambushes confront us along winding roads and fighting presses upon us at narrow passes, the greatest dangers need not cause alarm. Why? The disaster that formerly befell the two Ma commanders resulted simply from their lack of foresight and their poor planning. Sustained effort and orderly vigilance, being unfathomable and invincible: these are the rules governing an army. Yet they treated winding roads and narrow passes as though they were uninhabited territory. On the march they did not send spies far afield; at a halt they did not establish their field encampments securely [?]. When passing through defiles they did not search for concealed enemies, and along winding roads they did not station guarding troops all around. This allowed the Yao to burst out and cut off our forces. Were these generals who had prepared beforehand? If they had long cultivated ties with local inhabitants, treated those employed in gathering intelligence with exceptional favor, and dispatched them separately several months …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之先而申覘於臨發之期雖敵人動靜罔
不纖悉周焉行旌所至或布勇士於險巇
或陟高巘以瞭遠如亞夫然將幷崤澠之
伏兵而殲之也而反使之據險以扼我者
有是邪故曰是不素豫之將也往者巢穴
之盤惟其始之挫而終之餒者也夫嘽嘽
焞焞如霆如雷者師之法也以盤據紆迴
之區而以天造之險視之外覘之不先備
内應之不先圖出沒不知其所從虛實不
===
知其所措使猺堅壁以制我也是豈將之
善謀者邪使其内宅之窺得其地形外宅
之門得其險要多募敢死之士而懸以破
格之賞雖敵人之信息罔有毫髮遺焉分
道而進或犂賊巢於夾攻之頃或執巨魁
於懸購之下如班超然將指西域之名王
而俘之也而反使之恃險以持我者有是
邪故曰是不達權之將也諸猺之跳踉嶮
絕而輕越溪澗也其性則然也何者彼非
punctuated:
之先，而申覘於臨發之期，雖敵人動靜，罔不纖悉周焉。行旌所至，或布勇士於險巇，或陟高巘以瞭遠，如亞夫然，將幷崤澠之伏兵而殲之也。而反使之據險以扼我者，有是邪？故曰：是不素豫之將也。
往者巢穴之盤，惟其始之挫而終之餒者也。夫嘽嘽焞焞，如霆如雷者，師之法也。以盤據紆迴之區，而以天造之險視之，外覘之不先備，内應之不先圖，出沒不知其所從，虛實不知其所措，使猺堅壁以制我也，是豈將之善謀者邪？使其内宅之窺得其地形，外宅之門得其險要，多募敢死之士，而懸以破格之賞，雖敵人之信息，罔有毫髮遺焉。分道而進，或犂賊巢於夾攻之頃，或執巨魁於懸購之下，如班超然，將指西域之名王而俘之也。而反使之恃險以持我者，有是邪？故曰：是不達權之將也。
諸猺之跳踉嶮絕，而輕越溪澗也，其性則然也。何者？彼非
translation_en:
…in advance, and renewed reconnaissance just before departure, every detail of the enemy’s movements and dispositions would be thoroughly known. Wherever the army’s standards went, brave soldiers could be stationed at dangerous passes, or men could climb lofty peaks to observe the distance. Acting like Yafu, one could annihilate even troops lying in ambush at Xiao and Mian. Could one instead allow them to occupy difficult ground and block us? Thus I say: these were commanders who had made no preparations beforehand.
As for the former entrenchment of their lairs, this resulted simply from our initial setbacks and eventual loss of resolve. For an army’s proper method is to advance in imposing strength and blazing might, like thunderclaps and rolling thunder. Yet commanders regarded the winding terrain occupied by the enemy as naturally impregnable. They did not prepare external reconnaissance in advance or arrange support from within; they did not know where the enemy emerged and disappeared, or where its strengths and weaknesses lay. Thus they allowed the Yao to hold fortified positions and keep us in check. Were these commanders skilled in planning? Had they obtained knowledge of the terrain through spying within the dwellings, and of the strategic points through the approaches outside them [?], recruited many soldiers ready to brave death, and offered rewards beyond the ordinary rules, not the slightest scrap of intelligence about the enemy would have been missed. Advancing by separate routes, they could have swept away the rebels’ lairs in a converging attack, or seized their chief leaders through the offer of bounties. Acting like Ban Chao, they could have singled out renowned kings of the Western Regions and taken them captive. Could one instead allow the enemy to rely on difficult terrain to hold us off? Thus I say: these were commanders who did not understand how to adapt to circumstances.
The various Yao leap about on precipitous terrain and cross streams and ravines with ease: this is their nature. Why is this? They do not…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有棟宇之居衣屨之飾生而烙蹠履險若
飛而中國之足弗及之也彼狼兵者雖有
內屬之名實其侏離之類忍饑行鬭跳躍
射生素相類也以蠻夷攻蠻夷固中國之
形也然狼者懷野心者也非惟其頑之難
於敎練抑且悍之不便指麾且今之狼與
昔大相懸也異日者官帑之儲峙充而餉
犒之給賜厚是故土兵調至如歸以飽其
欲也今土兵之給旣微且薄矣土官又從
===
===
而朘削之故就調者非梟雄之兵而猶挾
驕蹇之氣也與我兵雜處也視戰勝則爭
我兵之前而善於搜捕視不勝則要求重
賞然後肯赴敵其氣盈而易衰可以一用
而不可再也近者於永安之役而知夫狼
果不可以純用也漢土兼制此自古破夷
之常法者非邪諸猺之不樂控制而便於
其黨也亦性然也何者彼非有上下之分
官長之素刀耕而食火種以生而中國之
punctuated:
有棟宇之居、衣屨之飾，生而烙蹠，履險若飛，而中國之足弗及之也。彼狼兵者，雖有內屬之名，實其侏離之類，忍饑行鬭，跳躍射生，素相類也。以蠻夷攻蠻夷，固中國之形也。然狼者，懷野心者也，非惟其頑之難於敎練，抑且悍之不便指麾。且今之狼與昔大相懸也。異日者，官帑之儲峙充，而餉犒之給賜厚，是故土兵調至如歸，以飽其欲也。今土兵之給旣微且薄矣，土官又從而朘削之，故就調者非梟雄之兵，而猶挾驕蹇之氣也。與我兵雜處也，視戰勝則爭我兵之前，而善於搜捕；視不勝則要求重賞，然後肯赴敵。其氣盈而易衰，可以一用而不可再也。近者於永安之役，而知夫狼果不可以純用也。漢土兼制，此自古破夷之常法者非邪？
諸猺之不樂控制而便於其黨也，亦性然也。何者？彼非有上下之分、官長之素，刀耕而食，火種以生，而中國之
translation_en:
…have no roofed dwellings or adornments of clothing and footwear. From birth their soles are seared [?]; they traverse perilous terrain as though flying, and the feet of those of the Central Realm cannot keep pace. As for the lang troops, although nominally subject to our rule, they are in fact of the same unintelligibly speaking kind. Enduring hunger, fighting on the march, leaping, and shooting game: in these they have always been alike. To attack barbarians with barbarians is indeed the strategic advantage of the Central Realm. Yet these lang troops harbor untamed ambitions. Not only does their obstinacy make them difficult to train; their fierceness also makes them difficult to command. Moreover, today’s lang troops differ greatly from those of the past. Formerly, government treasuries held ample reserves, and provisions and rewards were generous. Thus, when native troops were summoned, they came as though returning home, because their desires were satisfied. Now the native troops’ allowances are scant and meager, and the native officials further whittle them away. Consequently, those answering the summons are no fierce and valiant soldiers, yet they still carry an air of arrogance and insubordination. Serving alongside our troops, if they see victory at hand, they compete to get ahead of our soldiers and prove adept at searching out and capturing the enemy. If they see that victory is not forthcoming, they demand substantial rewards before consenting to engage the enemy. Their spirit swells but readily ebbs: they can be used once, but not a second time. The recent campaign at Yong’an showed that one truly cannot rely exclusively on lang troops. Is not the combined deployment of Han and native forces the established method of defeating the barbarians since antiquity?
That the various Yao groups dislike being controlled and feel at ease among their own people likewise arises from their nature. Why? They have neither distinctions between superior and inferior nor an established tradition of officials and leaders. They till with knives to obtain food and plant with fire to sustain themselves, while the Central Realm’s …

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
法弗加之也彼土司者雖有冠裳之形不
過羈縻之制佩刀帶劒以强爲威亦相近
也治蠻夷以不治亦一時之權也然土司
者非漢官也恐一時獲捍禦之利而終畢
有騷擾之虞且今之設土司因便利田宅
也異日者編氓之土田旣侵沒於猺手幸
其驅逐於我兵是故吾民之胥慶兾復其
故也今設爲土司將併其有矣夫并其故
而奪之是無辜者去猺蠻之害而復益以
===
===
水火之虐也故莫若棄其阻險者而畀於
土司其邇縣治者猶可畀吾民而俾之耕
種其勢則可以兩利而俱存吾民將德我
之曲全而不忍遠之也往者觀復脩荔之
事而知縣民之必不可棄也內華而外夷
此自古封域之大限者非邪昔之人有如
裴懷古之討歐陽倩也乃輕騎至壁而賊
眾迎降彼非徒恃一札之手書也蓋南蠻
之役誅止首惡先巳服其心矣况因其自
punctuated:
法弗加之也。彼土司者，雖有冠裳之形，不過羈縻之制，佩刀帶劒，以强爲威，亦相近也。治蠻夷以不治，亦一時之權也。然土司者，非漢官也，恐一時獲捍禦之利，而終畢有騷擾之虞。且今之設土司，因便利田宅也。異日者，編氓之土田旣侵沒於猺手，幸其驅逐於我兵，是故吾民之胥慶，兾復其故也。今設爲土司，將併其有矣。夫并其故而奪之，是無辜者去猺蠻之害，而復益以水火之虐也。故莫若棄其阻險者而畀於土司，其邇縣治者，猶可畀吾民而俾之耕種。其勢則可以兩利而俱存，吾民將德我之曲全，而不忍遠之也。往者觀復脩荔之事，而知縣民之必不可棄也。內華而外夷，此自古封域之大限者非邪？
昔之人，有如裴懷古之討歐陽倩也，乃輕騎至壁，而賊眾迎降。彼非徒恃一札之手書也，蓋南蠻之役，誅止首惡，先巳服其心矣。况因其自
translation_en:
…the laws of the Central Realm do not apply to them. Those native officials, though outwardly clad in official caps and robes, belong merely to a system of loose control. Wearing sabers and swords, they establish their authority through force and are much the same. Governing the barbarians by leaving them ungoverned is also an expedient for the moment. Yet native officials are not regular Chinese officials. I fear that, although they may provide an immediate advantage in defense, they will ultimately pose a risk of disturbance. Moreover, establishing native offices now involves the advantages afforded by fields and dwellings [?]. Previously, the registered commoners’ lands had been encroached upon and swallowed up by the Yao. Fortunately, our troops drove them out; thus our people rejoiced together, hoping to recover their former holdings. If native offices are now established, they will annex those possessions. To annex and seize their former holdings would mean that innocent people, freed from the harm inflicted by the Yao barbarians, would then suffer further cruelties like flood and fire. Thus it would be best to relinquish the rugged, inaccessible areas to the native officials. Land near the county seat could still be given to our people to cultivate. Such an arrangement could benefit both sides and preserve them together. Our people would be grateful for our solicitous protection and would be unwilling to become estranged from us. Looking at the earlier recovery of Xiu and Li, one sees that the county’s people must never be abandoned. To place the Chinese within and the barbarians without—is this not the great boundary governing territorial divisions since antiquity?
Among men of former times was Pei Huaigu, who campaigned against Ouyang Qian. He reached the enemy’s fortifications with light cavalry, and the rebel host came out to surrender. He did not rely solely upon a single handwritten letter. Rather, in his campaign against the southern barbarians, he confined punishment to the chief malefactors and had already won their submission in their hearts. All the more so, since, in response to their own…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
陳而亟赴之懷古其得破謀之算者與有
如岳飛之討曹成也盛夏興師而賀州以
平彼非有破敵之異術也蓋經畫旣具師
出不意先已破其膽矣况席累勝之威而
馳之飛其有達權之機者與執事謂韓雍
用永保之兵以殲夷脩荔也愚則曰雍玆
役兼兩京江廣之兵與土漢達官之衆也
其首破脩荔次及斷藤磨崖之烈于今賴
之雍其謀斷兼資之大將也夫執事謂王
===
守仁率田州之旅以蕩掃諸猺也愚則曰
守仁玆役兼用湖廣廣東之諸將而加之
永保址歸之士也其銜枚疾走八寨悉平
京觀之偉於今爲烈守仁其智勇具備之
儒將也夫此皆經畫之略豫審於其始而
區處之策克成於其終執事欲倣其已試
之明效則亦擇將定謀勦撫相因恩威並
濟而已矣善謀者潛於九地之下而發於
九天之上敵雖欲知之而不得所以知之
punctuated: 陳而亟赴之，懷古其得破謀之算者與？有如岳飛之討曹成也，盛夏興師，而賀州以平。彼非有破敵之異術也，蓋經畫旣具，師出不意，先已破其膽矣。况席累勝之威而馳之，飛其有達權之機者與？執事謂韓雍用永保之兵以殲夷脩荔也，愚則曰：雍玆役兼兩京江廣之兵與土漢達官之衆也。其首破脩荔，次及斷藤，磨崖之烈，于今賴之。雍其謀斷兼資之大將也夫！執事謂王守仁率田州之旅以蕩掃諸猺也，愚則曰：守仁玆役兼用湖廣廣東之諸將，而加之永保址歸之士也。其銜枚疾走，八寨悉平，京觀之偉，於今爲烈。守仁其智勇具備之儒將也夫！此皆經畫之略豫審於其始，而區處之策克成於其終。執事欲倣其已試之明效，則亦擇將定謀，勦撫相因，恩威並濟而已矣。善謀者潛於九地之下，而發於九天之上，敵雖欲知之而不得所以知之
translation_en:
…made their own representations, and he hastened to them. Had not Huai Gu grasped the calculations needed to defeat their designs? Consider also Yue Fei’s campaign against Cao Cheng: he mobilized his army in midsummer, and Hezhou was pacified. He possessed no extraordinary technique for defeating the enemy. Rather, his preparations were complete, and his troops appeared unexpectedly, having already broken the enemy’s courage. Moreover, he advanced swiftly with the imposing force of successive victories. Did not Yue Fei possess the knack of adapting to circumstances?

You say that Han Yong used troops from Yongshun and Baojing to annihilate the rebels at Xiuli. I would humbly reply that in this campaign Yong also employed troops from the two capitals and the Jiang and Guang regions, together with forces under native, Han Chinese, and Tatar officers. He first defeated Xiuli and then proceeded to Duanteng. The achievements commemorated in cliff inscriptions continue to benefit us today. Surely Yong was a great general endowed with both strategic judgment and decisiveness!

You say that Wang Shouren led troops from Tianzhou to sweep away the various Yao groups. I would humbly reply that in this campaign Shouren also employed the commanders of Huguang and Guangdong, supplementing their forces with men from Yongshun, Baojing, and Zhigui [?]. His troops marched swiftly with gags in their mouths to maintain silence, and all Eight Stockades were pacified. The imposing mound of enemy corpses remains a testament to his martial achievement. Surely Shouren was a scholar-general possessed of both wisdom and courage!

In all these cases, plans for conducting operations were carefully considered beforehand, and measures for settling affairs were successfully carried through in the end. If you wish to emulate their proven results, you need only select commanders and settle your plans, make suppression and conciliation support one another, and employ both benevolence and awe. Those skilled in strategy conceal themselves beneath the nine depths of the earth and strike from above the nine heights of heaven; although the enemy wishes to discern their plans, he cannot find the means to do so…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者也達變者畫於一時之宜而垂之爲千
百世之久睹其利而不至詒其害者也首
惡可誅也而種類之不可盡者開其歸附
而與其自新可也土司可置也而平衍之
可以居民者參之漢官以制其滋蔓可也
若風霆之迅震而繼之開明之日若雪霜
之栗烈而繼之和煦之春斯柔遠能邇蠻
夷率服之道也敢以爲進取之助何如
punctuated: 者也。達變者，畫於一時之宜，而垂之爲千百世之久，睹其利而不至詒其害者也。首惡可誅也，而種類之不可盡者，開其歸附而與其自新可也。土司可置也，而平衍之可以居民者，參之漢官以制其滋蔓可也。若風霆之迅震，而繼之開明之日；若雪霜之栗烈，而繼之和煦之春。斯柔遠能邇、蠻夷率服之道也。敢以爲進取之助，何如？
translation_en: …such is the case. Those who understand changing circumstances devise plans suited to the needs of the moment and leave them to endure for hundreds and thousands of generations, ensuring that their benefits are seen without bequeathing their harms. The chief malefactors may be executed, but their peoples cannot be exterminated: it is appropriate to open a path for their submission and allow them to reform themselves. Native officials may be appointed, but in level, open areas suitable for settlement, it is appropriate to intersperse Han officials among them to restrain the expansion of their power. Let the swift onslaught of wind and thunder be followed by bright, clear days; let the bitter severity of snow and frost be followed by the gentle warmth of spring. This is the way to conciliate those afar, win over those nearby, and bring the Man and Yi peoples into submission. I venture to offer this as an aid to your undertaking. What do you think?

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
隆慶庚午秋八月廣西鄉試
事竣御史李良臣率諸大夫
若執事勸饗諸士工歌鹿鳴
繼之南山諸什將馳賢書貢
天府顧冦以執事宜序末簡序曰
始冦膺聘檄道衡山也則前
===
睹九嶷諸峰邏迤横亘踰永
而南狀若奔驥望之嘆曰兹
其爲嶺粤之始鍾也夫既入
境清湘縈帶文嶂矗空遶以
三江峙以八桂巉絶明秀寰
中罕儷聳然異之曰玆其爲
天地之奥區也夫既鎖院畢
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

隆慶庚午秋八月，廣西鄉試事竣，御史李良臣率諸大夫若執事，勸饗諸士。工歌《鹿鳴》，繼之《南山》諸什。將馳賢書貢天府，顧冦以執事宜序末簡。序曰：

始冦膺聘檄，道衡山也，則前睹九嶷諸峰邏迤横亘，踰永而南，狀若奔驥。望之嘆曰：「兹其爲嶺粤之始鍾也夫！」既入境，清湘縈帶，文嶂矗空，遶以三江，峙以八桂，巉絶明秀，寰中罕儷。聳然異之曰：「玆其爲天地之奥區也夫！」既鎖院畢
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the gengwu year of Longqing (1570), the Guangxi Provincial Examination concluded. Censor Li Liangchen led the assembled officials and examination staff in exhorting and feasting the candidates. The musicians sang “Deer Calling” (Lu ming), followed by “Southern Mountain” (Nan shan) and other odes. As the list of worthy men was about to be dispatched to the imperial capital, he turned to me, Kou, considering that, as a member of the examination staff, I should write a postface on the closing pages. The postface reads:

When I, Kou, first received the written invitation to serve and traveled by way of Hengshan, I saw ahead the peaks of Jiuyi winding and stretching across the landscape. Extending south beyond Yong, they resembled galloping steeds. Gazing at them, I sighed: “Surely this is where the vital energies of Ling-Yue first gather!” Once I entered the territory, the clear Xiang River wound like a girdle, and patterned mountain walls towered into the sky. Encircled by the Three Rivers and flanked by the Eight Cassia Trees, the landscape was precipitous, luminous, and beautiful, with few equals under heaven. Awestruck by its singularity, I said: “Surely this is a secluded treasure of Heaven and Earth!” Once we had been locked into the examination compound and completed…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
試閱其文詞根極理要弗驚
葩藻七篇論對言人人殊咸
稽傳註明性術也肅然三復
之曰玆其大羹玄酒之遺敦
尚典雅而緣以辭采者夫何
粤西産才若是富也往讀王
制稱天子之田南不盡衡山
===
然則粤西者固三代之所不
能仁太樸眞元渾淪而未斲
詩書禮樂湮鬱而未伸者與
夫
天地泰而羣賢生
聖人作而萬物覩神龍襄首則雲
氣追隨威鳳呈苞則珍禽蘩
punctuated:
試，閱其文詞，根極理要，弗驚葩藻。七篇論對，言人人殊，咸稽傳註，明性術也。肅然三復之曰：「玆其大羹玄酒之遺，敦尚典雅而緣以辭采者夫！何粤西産才若是富也？」往讀《王制》，稱天子之田南不盡衡山。
然則粤西者，固三代之所不能仁，太樸眞元渾淪而未斲，詩書禮樂湮鬱而未伸者與！夫天地泰而羣賢生，聖人作而萬物覩。神龍襄首，則雲氣追隨；威鳳呈苞，則珍禽蘩
translation_en:
…the examination. Reading their compositions, I found them rooted deeply in essential principles, without startling floral ornament [?]. Across the seven essays and responses, each candidate expressed himself differently, yet all consulted the commentaries and annotations and elucidated the principles of human nature. With reverence I read them over three times and said: “Surely these preserve the legacy of the unseasoned broth and the plain water of ancient ritual: they esteem classical refinement and adorn it with literary elegance! How is it that western Yue produces talent in such abundance?” I once read in the Royal Regulations that the Son of Heaven’s domain did not extend southward to encompass all of Hengshan.
Thus western Yue was indeed a place to which the Three Dynasties could not extend their benevolent influence. Its pristine simplicity and original vitality remained whole and uncarved; the traditions of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music lay submerged and had yet to unfold. When Heaven and Earth are in harmony, worthy men arise in multitudes; when a sage appears, all things come into view. When the divine dragon raises its head, clouds follow in its wake; when the majestic phoenix displays its plumage [?], rare birds abound…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
集氣之相感遐邇悉通也乃
粤西人士入唐抵宋始蒸蒸
出而特盛于我
國家熈皞之朝無亦山川有待
人事聿興氣與運符道因時
顯者與爾諸士玆以言進也
言者達心之器而致用之階
===
也自昔名世之英篤弼之佐
率以言顯唐虞之盛則有若
禹皐之矢謨殷商之興則有
若伊傅之對命成周之際則
有若尚父獻書箕子陳疇數
聖賢者誦言以明心奮身以
致主然言之罔不劇事情而
punctuated:
集，氣之相感，遐邇悉通也。乃粤西人士，入唐抵宋，始蒸蒸出，而特盛于我國家熈皞之朝，無亦山川有待，人事聿興，氣與運符，道因時顯者與？爾諸士玆以言進也，言者達心之器，而致用之階也。
自昔名世之英、篤弼之佐，率以言顯。唐虞之盛，則有若禹皐之矢謨；殷商之興，則有若伊傅之對命；成周之際，則有若尚父獻書、箕子陳疇。數聖賢者，誦言以明心，奮身以致主，然言之罔不劇事情而
translation_en:
…gather together: through the mutual resonance of vital forces, far and near are all connected. Only from the Tang through the Song did men of learning in western Yue begin to emerge in growing numbers; they have flourished especially under the radiant and harmonious rule of our dynasty. Might it be that these mountains and rivers were awaiting their time, that human endeavors have now arisen, that vital forces accord with the course of destiny, and that the Way manifests itself as the times permit? You scholars now seek advancement through your words. Words are the means of conveying the heart’s intent and the steps toward practical service.
From antiquity, outstanding men renowned in their age and steadfast assistants to their rulers have generally attained distinction through their words. In the flourishing age of Tang and Yu, there were Yu and Gao Yao setting forth their counsels; at the rise of Yin-Shang, there were Yi Yin and Fu Yue responding to royal commands; in the time of Cheng Zhou, there were Shangfu presenting a document and Jizi expounding the categories of the Great Plan. These sages and worthies spoke to make their hearts’ intentions clear and exerted themselves to bring their rulers to perfection. Yet their words invariably probed the realities of affairs [?] and…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
厎績用裨賛襄而潤皇猷者
也故行業著于當世聲稱浹
乎于玆今之談者則云虞夏
商周之士之進也或以事舉
或以德庸或云夢協或云卜
徵匪專之于言誠是也我
國家令制聚士而甄陶諸學宮
===
稽行於有司而賓興之於三
歲蓋非徒曰以試得之以言
揚之爾也顧視虞夏商周之
辨才有同符焉者今諸士之
自獻其言也述虞夏叙商周
舍性術弗陳外傳註弗演鏘
然可觀矣然言華也行實也
punctuated:
厎績用，裨賛襄而潤皇猷者也。故行業著于當世，聲稱浹乎于玆。今之談者則云：「虞夏商周之士之進也，或以事舉，或以德庸，或云夢協，或云卜徵，匪專之于言。」誠是也。
我國家令制，聚士而甄陶諸學宮，稽行於有司，而賓興之於三歲。蓋非徒曰以試得之，以言揚之爾也。顧視虞夏商周之辨才，有同符焉者。今諸士之自獻其言也，述虞夏，叙商周，舍性術弗陳，外傳註弗演，鏘然可觀矣。然言華也，行實也。
translation_en:
…brought practical achievements, aided the work of governance, and enriched imperial policies. Thus their conduct and accomplishments were renowned in their own age, and their reputations have spread down to the present. Those who discuss the matter today say: “When scholars advanced under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, some were recommended for their service, others employed for their virtue; some were said to accord with dreams, others to be confirmed by divination. Advancement did not depend exclusively upon words.” This is indeed so.
Under our dynasty’s admirable regulations, scholars are assembled and cultivated in the schools; their conduct is examined by the responsible officials, and every three years they are honored as guests and recommended for advancement. It is certainly not simply a matter of selecting them through examinations and advancing them through their words. Compared with the discernment of talent under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, this follows the same principles. Now, when these scholars present their writings, they recount Yu and Xia and describe Shang and Zhou. They set forth nothing apart from the cultivation of moral nature [?] and expound nothing beyond the commentaries and annotations. Their words ring out resoundingly and are worthy of admiration. Yet words are the blossom; conduct is the fruit.

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸士者如其攄心以發言言心
罔弗孚卽行以稽言言行罔弗
成矣玆尅以是爲諸士望之
也夫士而不以禹臯伊傅箕
望之業待其身匪善致身者
也士而不以虞夏商周之盛
事其君匪能致君者也諸士
===
行矣將以言對
大廷揚敷納明烈訓者繼自今
若曰
明盛間值川岳匪虛旣已應毓秀
而慶遭逢也所持以終身者
惟敏顧于言弗懈於行用是
無忝昔人不媿賢科已矣抑
punctuated:
諸士者，如其攄心以發言，言心罔弗孚；卽行以稽言，言行罔弗成矣。玆尅以是爲諸士望之也。夫士而不以禹臯伊傅箕望之業待其身，匪善致身者也；士而不以虞夏商周之盛事其君，匪能致君者也。
諸士行矣，將以言對大廷，揚敷納明烈訓者，繼自今。若曰：「明盛間值，川岳匪虛，旣已應毓秀而慶遭逢也，所持以終身者，惟敏顧于言，弗懈於行。用是無忝昔人，不媿賢科已矣。」抑
translation_en:
…If you gentlemen express your hearts in your words, your words and hearts will invariably accord; if you examine your words against your conduct, your words and deeds will invariably fulfill one another. This, then, is what I expect of you. A scholar who does not hold himself to the achievements of Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, Jizi, and Lü Wang does not know how to fulfill his own potential. A scholar who does not serve his ruler with the flourishing ages of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou as his standard cannot bring his ruler to greatness.
Go forth, gentlemen! You will answer with your words in the great imperial court. From this time onward, it will fall to you to carry forward the illustrious instruction concerning the presentation and reception of words [?]. You might say: “We have encountered an enlightened and flourishing age; the mountains and rivers have not nurtured talent in vain. Having answered to their nurturing of outstanding men, we rejoice in this fortunate encounter. What we must uphold throughout our lives is simply to attend diligently to our words and remain unremitting in our conduct. Thus may we bring no dishonor upon the men of old and prove worthy of this examination for the selection of worthy men.” Yet…

title: 隆慶四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
愚竊尚有懼焉顧茲文章桂
嶺之巉絕而亦有夷酋異物
之竊為憑依也清湘三水之
明秀而亦有炎風蒸嵐之因
以時作也諸士者間或有言
馳于心行違于始則醇駁且
不相掩他日人將訾之其於
===
明盛之值川岳之鍾胥有負焉則
使斯錄也不幾為弗信之書
與故冠之願與諸士勗之也
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教
諭陳冠謹序
punctuated:
愚竊尚有懼焉。顧茲文章，桂嶺之巉絕，而亦有夷酋異物之竊為憑依也；清湘三水之明秀，而亦有炎風蒸嵐之因以時作也。諸士者間或有言馳于心、行違于始，則醇駁且不相掩。他日人將訾之，其於明盛之值、川岳之鍾，胥有負焉。則使斯錄也，不幾為弗信之書與？故冠之，願與諸士勗之也。
浙江溫州府樂清縣儒學教諭陳冠謹序。
translation_en:
…I, in my ignorance, privately still have some apprehension. Consider this literary brilliance [?]: the Guiling mountains are steep and lofty, yet tribal chieftains and strange creatures also secretly find refuge there; Qingxiang and Sanshui are clear and beautiful, yet scorching winds and steaming mountain mists also arise there from time to time. If some among you gentlemen should let your words outrun your convictions, or your conduct depart from your original intentions, then purity and impurity will not conceal one another. In days to come, people will reproach you, and you will have failed both the enlightened and flourishing age you have encountered and the gifts bestowed upon you by its rivers and mountains. Would this not make this record almost an untrustworthy book? Therefore I place these words at its head, wishing to join you gentlemen in mutual exhortation.
Preface respectfully composed by Chen Guan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
